title: BREAK, BREAKATPOINT and JOIN: leave objects on locked layers alone (fixes #727)
author: atmikshetty
body:
Fixes #727.

BREAK, BREAKATPOINT and line/arc/polyline JOIN removed their source objects and added the replacements without checking the source layer's lock, so a line on a locked layer could be cut or merged into an unlocked polyline. ERASE, MOVE, TRIM, FILLET, EXPLODE and the ellipse/spline JOIN already refuse in that case; these now do too.

## Changes
- **BREAK / BREAKATPOINT** (`break_entity`, which the JSON command, the interactive prompts and the command line all use): refuses an object on a locked layer with "The object is on a locked layer.", the wording FILLET uses. Covers lines, arcs, circles and polylines.
- **JOIN** (`modify::join`): refuses when any selected object is on a locked layer with "An object is on a locked layer.", the wording the ellipse/spline JOIN uses, so a locked/unlocked pair keeps its locked original in either order.
- The drawing is left exactly as it was when a request is refused; nothing changes for unlocked layers.

## Testing
- Reproduced first: the five new tests in `crates/engine/tests/break_join_locked_layers.rs` failed on `main` (the locked edit succeeded and replaced the source) and pass now. They cover BREAK and BREAKATPOINT on a locked line by handle and by selection, BREAK on a locked arc and circle, JOIN of locked lines and of a locked/unlocked pair in both orders, and interactive BREAK / JOIN reporting the refusal on the command line. Each also checks the same edit works once the layer is unlocked (BREAK also undoes and redoes).
- `cargo test --workspace`: 1664 passed, 0 failed (1659 before, +5 new).
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, test, assets, layers, wasm).
- In the app on macOS, through the control channel: with a line pair and an arc on a locked layer, BREAK, BREAKATPOINT and JOIN (JSON and typed at the command line) were all refused and the drawing was unchanged; the same commands on an unlocked layer joined two lines and broke a polyline and an arc; after unlocking the layer, BREAK…

title: Property-based and hostile-input tests for geometry numerics (gaps.md S6)
author: Lion-1209
body:
Closes the S6 row of `docs/gaps.md`: property-based and fuzz tests for geometry, where hostile-input tests so far covered parsing only. `geometry-parity.md` §Tests also called for a known-answer suite at large coordinates.

**How it works** — `crates/geom/src/property_tests.rs`, a deterministic xorshift64* generator (no new dependency, following the hand-rolled `Rng` precedent in the CLI) driving a few thousand cases per property. The whole suite runs in ~0.03 s; every seed is fixed, so nothing is flaky.

**Properties**

- line/line: hits lie on both lines, parameters reproduce the point, operands are symmetric, finite results agree with the infinite parameters
- line/circle, circle/circle: hits lie on both curves, results are symmetric, properly crossing circles match the closed form (x = (d²+r1²−r2²)/2d, h = √(r1²−x²))
- segments: extension only adds hits
- closest points: idempotent, perpendicular inside the segment, endpoints outside
- arcs (`at`/closest/from_3_points): endpoints and sampling consistent at radii 1e-6…1e6; three-point arcs keep `{start, end} = {p1, p3}`, contain p2, and match the circumradius closed form; collinear inputs rejected
- bounds and vector identities
- **known answers at 1e6–1e7 coordinates** hold to 1e-9 relative (line/circle through the centre, crossing lines, circle pairs) — the large-coordinate part of the §Tests ask

**Hostile inputs** (NaN, ±inf, ±0, subnormals, 1e300, raw f64 bit patterns): no panics anywhere; the guarded functions (`line_circle`, `circle_circle`) return only finite hits or none. `line_line_infinite` can return non-finite points for non-finite inputs — upstream callers guard (`refuse_non_finite`), so the suite asserts only no-panic there.

**One semantic note found while writing these**: `Arc::from_3_points` returns start/end swapped relative to (p1, p3) when p2 lies on the clockwise side — that is correct DXF behaviour (arcs are stored CCW), now pinned as a property test so it stays deliberate.

**Checks**: `ca…

title: Constraint point names: `s2` names segment 2, as documented
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #710.

`Sub::parse` documents `s2` / `seg2` / `segment2` for a segment, but the prefix list had no `s`, so `s2` came back `None`. It now ends `segment, seg, s, v`:

- `s` comes after `seg` and `segment`, so those still match first;
- a bare `s` is still `Start`, matched as a whole word before the prefixes.

Validation:
- `crates/doc/tests/sub_segment_alias.rs` (the issue's test plus an unknown-name check) fails on main at `s2` and passes here. Putting `s` before `seg` makes it fail at `seg2`.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-doc` passes.
- The engine's constraint tests pass (`constraint_geometry`, `constraint_infer`, `cmd::constraints`).
- clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: POLYGON: a typed radius of zero or less, or a radius point on the centre, is refused and asked again
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #720.

At the interactive radius prompt, POLYGON took a typed radius straight to `polygon_typed_radius_point` and a clicked point straight to `polygon_vertices`. With `0`, a negative value or the centre itself, it drew a polygon whose vertices all coincide. The JSON path already refuses these through `size_param`. The prompt now answers "Value must be positive and nonzero." (what CIRCLE says in the same case) and stays open for another radius.

Validation:
- `polygon_radius_must_be_positive` in `tests/draw_prompts.rs` covers `0`, `-5` and `0,0` in both inscribed and circumscribed mode. It checks that no entity is added, that the message is logged, that the prompt stays open, and that a following `2` draws one closed polyline. It fails on main.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine` passes, clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

Left as it is: in Edge mode the prompt still accepts two identical endpoints, which the JSON path refuses. Happy to send that separately.

title: HATCH: a pattern name with no definition is refused instead of drawn as ANSI31
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #722.

`hatch` through JSON stored any `pattern` name. `patfile::lines_for` finds nothing for an unknown name, so the hatch was drawn as ANSI31 while still carrying the made-up name. The prompt and HATCHEDIT already refuse such names. `run_hatch` now does the same check after `patfile::load_param` (so `patternText` / `patternFile` patterns count) and returns `unknown pattern NAME`.

- SOLID is in the library, so it is still accepted.
- Gradients go through `run_gradient`, which is untouched.

Validation:
- `json_hatch_refuses_an_undefined_pattern`:
  - `NOPE` is an error and leaves only the rectangle;
  - `ansi31` and `SOLID` still hatch.
  - It fails on main (`unwrap_err` on an `Ok`).
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine` passes, `lin_pat_files` included (the user-pattern case), and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: Plot dialog: match the familiar sectioned print layout
author: cyfung1031
body:

title: JOIN: an elliptical arc named twice is one object, so the joined result stays
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #725.

`join_curves` keeps the first handle as the source and removes every later one after merging it. When the source handle is named again (`[a, a]` or `[a, a, b]`), the "later" copy is the source itself, so the joined result was deleted. The handle list is now deduplicated, in order, before joining:

- `[a, a, b]` joins like `[a, b]`;
- `[a, a]` is refused like `[a]`, with the existing message.

Validation:
- `join_names_an_elliptical_arc_twice_without_losing_it` in `tests/modify_curves.rs` fails on main: `[a, a]` succeeds, and `[a, a, b]` leaves no entity behind. It passes here.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

The fix sits in `join_curves`, so `modify.rs` stays untouched (#730 edits the start of `join()`). The polyline path has the same issue with a repeated line handle (`[l, l]` turns the line into a degenerate closed polyline). I'm happy to send that separately once #730 is in.

title: HATCHEDIT: choosing SOLID on a gradient hatch makes it a plain solid fill
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #721.

HATCHEDIT cleared the gradient only when the new pattern wasn't SOLID (`h.gradient = None` sat inside `if !h.solid`). Choosing SOLID on a gradient hatch kept the gradient, so it still rendered as one. Any explicit `pattern` now clears it. An edit without `pattern` (scale or angle only) keeps the gradient as before, which the existing test already covers.

Validation:
- `hatchedit_solid_replaces_gradient` (next to `hatchedit_pattern_replaces_gradient`) fails on main and passes here. It checks the same handle, `solid`, no gradient, and unchanged boundary loops.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: Geometry: param_at_length checks spline validity before clamping to the domain
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #704.

`param_at_length` clamped `from` to the knot domain before checking `is_valid()`. With an inverted domain, or a NaN bound, `f64::clamp` panics ("min > max, or either was NaN"). The validity check now runs first. On an invalid spline the function returns what its existing fallback returns: `from` when it's finite, otherwise the domain start. `lengthen_spline` already guards upstream, so this only hit direct library callers.

Validation:
- `param_at_length_on_invalid_domain_does_not_panic` (inverted knots, and a NaN bound) panics on main and passes here.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-geom` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: Dimensions: a jogged radius with a NaN or infinite radius draws no lines instead of panicking
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #712.

The jogged radius dimension clamps the jog position with `.clamp(0.0, r)`. With a NaN radius (a non-finite definition point) that panics. When the radius isn't finite the dimension now keeps its text, which `linear_text` already sanitises, and draws no lines or arrow. That matches how `jog_line` and `cut` in the same file skip geometry for non-finite values. Finite results are unchanged.

Validation:
- `jogged_radius_with_nan_radius_draws_no_lines` has a finite control (the 4-point polyline to the override centre) and a NaN case with no lines or fills. It panics on main and passes here.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-render` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

An infinite radius is treated the same way (it used to produce infinite geometry).

title: MTEXT: annotative scaling and SCALE on multileader text scale the text width and columns too
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #708, fixes #709.

The same omission in two places: MTEXT column settings weren't scaled along with the text.

- **#708, annotative scaling:** `anno_scaled` scaled height and width but not the columns, so a 2:1 annotation scale left the column height and gutter at 1:1. It now calls `MTextColumns::scale`, for MText and for multileader text in the same function.
- **#709, SCALE on a multileader:** the MLeader branch of the transform scaled only `text.height`. It now also scales `width` and the columns, as the MText branch already does.

Validation:
- #708: `annotative_mtext_columns_follow_the_scale` (`tests/annotative.rs`) follows the issue's steps and checks EXTMIN/EXTMAX. On main it gets `[0, -20, 0]` instead of `[0, -40, 0]`.
- #709: `scale_scales_multileader_text_width_and_columns` (`tests/mtext_columns.rs`). On main it gets width 10 instead of 20.
- Undoing any one of the four additions fails a test.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-doc -p cadcraft-engine` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: Plot: model-space PNG and SVG plots honour fit: false without a scale, at 1:1 like PDF
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #713.

In model space, `plotter::fit_scale` returned early only for an explicit `scale`. With `fit: false` and no scale it still fitted the drawing to the sheet, while the PDF plotter plots 1:1. `fit_scale` now uses the PDF's `plot_scale` (made `pub(crate)`), so PNG and SVG follow the same rule and the duplicated logic goes.

Validation:
- `tests/plot_model_png_scale.rs` plots a 100 mm line on A4 at 100 dpi and measures the ink in mm. It decodes the PNG with `miniz_oxide`, which is already a dependency. The cases:

  | options | ink |
  |---|---|
  | `fit: false` | 100 mm |
  | `fit: false, scale: 1` | 100 mm |
  | `scale: 0.5` | 50 mm |
  | `fit: true` | 287 mm |
  | fit omitted | 287 mm |

  On main, `fit: false` gives 287.02 mm, the value in the issue.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-io -p cadcraft-engine` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

Not touched: layout PNGs with `fit: false` still ignore an explicit `scale`, which the PDF honours since #490. Happy to follow up.

title: Extents: count the visible attributes of a reference to a missing block
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #707.

Extents of a block reference whose definition is missing returned `Bounds2::EMPTY` straight away (`let … else { return }`). That skipped its attributes, although the comment there says "Attributes below still count". The block geometry and array matrix now sit in an `if let Some(blk)`, and the attribute loop runs either way. The insertion point still doesn't count, as before.

Validation:
- `visible_attributes_of_a_missing_block_still_count` checks that a reference with a missing definition has the same bounds as one with an empty definition. Controls: with no attributes, and with an invisible attribute, the bounds stay empty. It fails on main (`!missing.is_empty()`).
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-doc -p cadcraft-engine` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: Select: pick a SOLID inside its fill, not its bounding rectangle
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #718.

`entity_distance` treated a SOLID as filled across its whole bounding rectangle. So clicking the empty corner of a triangular SOLID picked it. SOLID is now out of that list: a click counts as inside only when the polygon the renderer fills (`Prim::Fill`) contains it, via `point_in_polygon`. Clicks near the edge still pick it within the aperture as before.

Validation:
- `solid_interior_tests::pick_in_triangular_bbox_but_outside_fill_does_not_select`, aperture 0.25:
  - (9,9), in the box but outside the triangle: `None`. On main it's `Some`.
  - (2,2), inside: `Some`.
  - (5.1,5.1), just outside the hypotenuse but within the aperture: `Some`.

  Dropping the inside rule fails (2,2).
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

Solid hatches still pick by bounding box (same issue for non-rectangular hatches with islands); I left them for a separate PR.

title: View: refuse a view that maps to an infinite viewport view, keeping the viewport
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #714.

With an active viewport, `store_view` mapped the requested view into the viewport and saved it without checking. A huge `view.set` (height 1e308) stored `NaN` centres and an infinite height in the viewport. `set_view` already refused unusable views, so its check moved into a small `usable_view` helper:

- `store_view` refuses a mapped view that isn't finite or has height ≤ 1e-12, and leaves everything unchanged. This covers locked and unlocked viewports.
- `set_view` records view history only when the view was stored.
- `view.set` returns "the view is too large to show. Nothing was changed".

Validation:
- `a_view_too_large_for_the_viewport_is_refused_and_keeps_the_viewport` (`tests/zoom_viewport.rs`): the command errors, the viewport stays identical and finite, and a sane height afterwards still applies.
  - On main the command succeeds and stores `NaN, NaN, inf`.
  - "Error but state written" and "state kept but no error" each fail the test.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine` passes, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` is clean, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

`Session::set_view` now returns `bool`. Its other callers (zoom and pan commands, named views, layouts) ignore it: an unusable view is simply not applied, as before. If you'd rather `view.set` stay silent too, it's one line.

title: Plotting: honor model-space center and X/Y offsets
author: cyfung1031
body:

title: Hatch and Gradient dialog (create and edit)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Adds a **Hatch and Gradient dialog** with two modes: **create** and **edit**. This closes the "no hatch dialog" part of gaps.md F13.

## What it does
- **Create mode.** Opens on `HATCH`/`H`/`BH` and `GRADIENT`/`GD` typed with no parameters, and from Draw ▸ Hatch…/Gradient… and Tool Sets.
  - Pattern tab: swatch picker (the existing one), angle, scale.
  - Gradient tab: colour 1 and 2, shape (linear, cylinder, curved, spherical, hemispherical), inverted, centred, angle.
  - Hatch origin: current, a clicked point, or a corner or centre of the extents.
  - Boundaries: Add: Pick points / Add: Select objects, a count, and Clear.
  - Options: associative, create separate hatches, island detection.
- **Edit mode.** Opens on `HATCHEDIT`/`HE`, Modify ▸ Object ▸ Hatch…, right-click Hatch Edit, or **double-clicking a hatch**. It shows the first selected hatch, and OK sends only what changed to every selected hatch. With no hatch selected, it asks for one first.
- `-HATCH` and `-HATCHEDIT` keep the command-line prompts. **Calls with JSON parameters never open the dialog**, so scripts, the CLI, the control channel and MCP behave as before.
- New `HPDLGMODE` (header/SETVAR, 0 or 1, default 1). With 0, HATCH and GRADIENT stay on the command line.

## How it works
The dialog never edits the drawing itself.
- Picking follows the Plot dialog's "Window <" pattern. The dialog hides, a new helper command `hatchpick` collects the picks into `Session::hatch_picks`, and the dialog comes back.
  - `hatchpick` modes: Points / Objects / oRigin / Hatch. It is `noundo`, has no menu entry, and has a JSON form `{points?, handles?}` that is checked the same way as the prompts.
- OK runs **one** `hatch`, `gradient` or `hatchedit` call.

Engine changes:
- HATCH and GRADIENT accept `points` and `handles` **together**: one hatch (or one per pick with `separate`), one undo step.
- GRADIENT takes `name` (checked against the shapes the renderer draws; unknown names are refused) and `centered`.
- HATCHEDI…

title: Plot to system printers on macOS and Linux through CUPS (#670 step 2)
author: aldozar
body:
Step 2 of #670: system printers on macOS and Linux, through CUPS. Builds on the Plot dialog from #673.

## Changes
- **Printers as devices.** The CUPS destinations (`lpstat -e`) are listed after the built-in PDF/PNG/SVG devices, each with the papers and printable areas of its PPD (`PageSize`, `PaperDimension`, `ImageableArea`, `DefaultPageSize`; borderless variants named as such). A destination without a readable PPD is left out. The list is cached for a few seconds.
- **Printing.** PLOT to a printer renders the PDF the PDF plotter already writes for that paper and sends it to `lp -d NAME -n COPIES -o PageSize=KEY -o print-scaling=none -o fit-to-page=false -` (PDF on stdin), so the plot's scale reaches the paper unchanged. The reply is the job id. EXPORTPDF to a printer device still writes the PDF.
- **Landscape on portrait media.** Printers feed portrait sheets and macOS doesn't turn a landscape PDF page by itself, so a landscape plot printed sideways. The PDF option `portraitMedia` draws each landscape sheet a quarter turn on a page of the paper's portrait size (no link annotations on turned pages); PLOT sets it for printers only. Saved PDFs are unchanged.
- **Plot dialog.** With a printer chosen, OK prints straight away (no file dialog) and a *Number of copies* field appears; the command line reports the job.

title: cadcraft-cli mcp: --lazy and --launch for MCP clients that start before the app
author: aldozar
body:
MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Claude Code…) start their servers when they start, usually before CADCraft is open, and `cadcraft-cli mcp --connect HOST:PORT` refuses to start then, so the client shows the server as failed until it is restarted.

## Changes
- `--lazy`: the bridge starts anyway and reaches the app at the first tool call (the existing reconnect path). Until the app answers, each call fails with a message saying how to open it (`--control PORT` or `CADCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT`).
- `--launch` (implies `--lazy`): at a call that finds nothing listening, open CADCraft with that control port (`open -a CADCraft --args --control PORT` on macOS; elsewhere the error says how to start it) and wait up to 30 s for it.
- Neither falls back to a headless session (#103): without `--connect` both are errors.
- Usage text and `docs/mcp.md` show a client config with `--launch`.

## Testing
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass.
- New tests: argument parsing (`--lazy`/`--launch` need `--connect`); a lazy bridge to a free port initializes, lists the UI tools, fails a call with the how-to-open message, and reaches a listener that starts afterwards.
- By hand on macOS with Claude Code and Claude Desktop: with CADCraft closed, the first tool call opened it with the control port and drew into it.

## How this was made
Investigated, written and tested by Claude Code (an AI coding agent) at the request of @aldozar. Happy to adjust anything.

title: MCP: render one area of the drawing, and read its texts (find_text)
author: aldozar
body:
Two MCP gaps that show on real drawings: a construction-permit set drawn as many sheets side by side in model space renders as one image where nothing can be read, and an agent has no cheap way to find room names, sheet numbers or notes without pulling all the geometry.

## Changes
- **`render {window}`**: `[[x0,y0],[x1,y1]]` renders just that area — one sheet or one room. Without a size the image is 1600 px wide with the window's shape. Both the app's and the headless `ui.render` take it; the display list is built for that view only. `raster::View::of_window` sizes it.
- **`find_text`** (new engine command `texts`, read-only): the readable text of TEXT, MTEXT (formatting removed with `plain_mtext`), block attributes and multileaders, each with its text, insertion point, height, rotation, style, layer and handle; filtered by `contains` (any case), `layer` and a `window` around the insertion points; paged (`limit` default 200, `offset`). FIND selects and can replace; this only reports.
- `docs/mcp.md` lists both; "Query Texts" is translated in the catalogs.

## Testing
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass.
- New MCP test: texts by content, layer and window, an MTEXT with formatting codes comes back plain, and a windowed render has the window's shape (1600 × 800 for a 2:1 window).
- On a real 39,600-object permit set (15 sheets of 90 × 59.4 at 1:100): `find_text` returned all 5,861 texts in 0.02 s, which was enough to list each sheet's number from the texts inside its frame; one sheet rendered at 2400 × 1584 in 0.5 s, fully legible.

title: Follow the operating system's animation setting; add View ▸ Accessibility ▸ Animation Effects
author: JeremyYao
body:
## The problem

With Windows set to show no animations (Settings ▸ Accessibility ▸ Visual effects ▸ Animation effects: off), CADCraft still animated: dialogs such as Layer Properties Manager, Blocks, About and Page Setup Manager faded in, the File … Help menus faded in, and wheel input glided.

None of that motion is CADCraft's own. It is egui's defaults, and nothing asked the operating system:

- Windows, menus, tooltips and popups fade in over `Style::animation_time` (0.2 s); collapsing sections and scroll bars animate over the same time.
- Scroll areas glide to a scroll target (`Style::scroll_animation`).
- egui spreads each mouse-wheel notch over several frames, for scrolling and for ⌘/Ctrl+wheel zoom. It has no switch for this.

Plain wheel zoom over the drawing was already fixed by #692 (in 0.6.0): it zooms a whole notch in the frame it arrives. A 0.5.0 install still shows the old
                                                                                                               ## What changes

- **Animation effects follow the OS by default.** When the OS shows no animations, dialogs, menus and tooltips appear at once, collapsing sections and scroll bars change at once, wheel scrolling in lists moves a whole notch per frame, and ⌘/Ctrl+wheel zoom (a touchpad pinch on Windows) reaches its zoom in one step. A change to the OS setting is picked up while CADCraft runs.                                                                                        - **View ▸ Accessibility ▸ Animation Effectsg** (the default), **On** and **Off**, builtlike View ▸ Interface Theme. Options ▸ Display has the same choice. The choice is saved with the other interface preferences, and Reset Palettes keeps it.                                                                      - **Where the OS answer comes from** (`apps/s.rs`, `apps/cadcraft-web`):

  | Platform | Source |                                                                                          |---|---…

title: POLYGON: an Edge second endpoint on the first is refused and asked again (follow-up to #735)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Follow-up to #735.

In POLYGON's Edge mode, picking the second endpoint of the edge on top of the first was accepted: `polygon_from_edge` got two identical points and the command added a closed polyline whose vertices all sit on that point. The JSON form already refuses this ("edge endpoints must differ"). The interactive machine now refuses a second endpoint that coincides with the first, with the same message ("Edge endpoints must differ."), before the point is stored, so the prompt stays at "Specify second endpoint of edge" and the next distinct point draws the polygon. It uses the same `near(.., 1e-12)` test as the JSON path.

Validation:
- `polygon_edge_endpoints_must_differ` (`tests/draw_prompts.rs`) types `polygon 4 e 1,1 1,1`, checks that nothing is added, the message is logged and the prompt is still open, then finishes with `3,1`. On main it fails with one polygon added (`left: 1, right: 0`).
- Removing the check makes the test fail again.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test draw_prompts --test json_param_validation` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: CIRCLE: a radius point on the centre is refused and asked again (follow-up to #735)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Follow-up to #735.

CIRCLE already refuses a typed radius of zero ("Value must be positive and nonzero.") and asks again, but a radius point picked on the centre went through: the distance is 0 and the command added a zero-radius circle (and stored 0 as the CIRCLERAD default). The same happened with the Diameter option. In the centre-radius mode the machine now refuses a second point that coincides with the centre with the same message, before the point is stored, so the radius prompt stays open and a valid value or point finishes the circle on the same centre.

Validation:
- `circle_radius_point_on_the_centre_is_refused` (`tests/draw_prompts.rs`) covers `circle 2,3 2,3` and `circle 2,3 d 2,3`: nothing is added, the message is logged, the prompt stays open, and typing `4` then gives a circle centred on 2,3 (radius 4, or 2 with Diameter). On main it fails with a circle added (`left: 1, right: 0`).
- Removing the check makes the test fail again.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test draw_prompts` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: Hatch: a view covering a pattern hatch leaves its lines exactly as they are
author: SBaksa
body:
`normal_zoom_pattern_is_unchanged` (added in #638) fails on Windows on main: with a view covering the whole hatch, an ANSI31 line that passes through a boundary corner starts at `(-3.1e-16, -3.1e-16)` instead of `(0, 0)`.

With a view, `Family::sweep` cut each span to the view's extent intersected with the boundary's. Spans already lie within the boundary. The boundary extent comes from rotating the corners directly, while a span end is interpolated along an edge, so at a corner the two differ by a rounding error and the cut moved the end. MSVC's sin/cos round differently from glibc's and macOS's, which is likely why only Windows saw it. Spans are now cut to the view's extent only, so the same lines come out with or without a covering view.

`cargo xtask ci` passes on Windows (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm). I haven't run it on macOS or Linux; the change only drops a redundant clip, so behaviour there should be unchanged.

title: Select: pick a solid hatch inside its fill, islands left out, not its bounding rectangle (follow-up to #747)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Follow-up to #747.

Picking a solid hatch counted any point inside its bounding rectangle as a hit (`entity_distance` sets the distance to 0 for "filled" kinds when `entity_bounds` contains the point). So clicking the empty corner beside a triangular hatch, or inside an island the fill leaves empty, selected the hatch. It is the same defect #747 fixes for SOLID. A solid hatch is now hit inside the region the renderer actually fills: the loops `fill_loops` returns for its island style, with odd parity. `fill_loops` was `pub(crate)` in `cadcraft-render`; it is now public and re-exported as `hatch_fill_loops`, so picking and drawing use the same loops. Points near the boundary still pick through the aperture, as before.

Validation:
- `solid_hatch_is_picked_inside_its_fill_not_its_bounding_rectangle`: a triangular solid hatch is not picked in the empty corner of its bounding rectangle, but is picked inside the fill and near the hypotenuse. On main the empty corner picks it.
- `solid_hatch_island_follows_the_island_style`: with the normal style a point inside the island doesn't pick the hatch (on main it does), and with the ignore style, which fills over the island, it does. Parity over the raw loops, or "inside any loop", each fail this test.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib select::` and `cargo test -p cadcraft-render --lib hatch` pass, and clippy (`-p cadcraft-render -p cadcraft-engine`) and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: Draw object transparency on screen, in exports and in plots
author: EP995LAB
body:
Transparency has been read and round-tripped since #132/#174/#225 (entity group 440, layer
xdata, ByLayer/ByBlock) but nothing drew it: a red SOLID hatch at 0, 50 or 90 % hid the line
under it, and the PNG and PDF outputs were byte-identical.

## Changes
- Display lists carry each object's effective transparency, clamped to 0–90: its own, its
  layer's when ByLayer (layer 0 in a block: the reference's layer), the block reference's when
  ByBlock, through nested blocks; attributes use their own (from their definition). Worked out
  only when `render::Options::transparency` is on, from the layer the property lookup already
  found. Each primitive blends on its own, as AutoCAD does: observed black-box in AutoCAD 2027
  with a synthetic drawing (two thick crossing polylines inside one block reference at 50 %, and
  two separate ones on a 50 % layer), the crossings come out darker in both cases, on screen and
  in a PDF plotted with "Plot transparency" on.
- Screen: the GPU canvas blends premultiplied alpha (the shader linearises it correctly), and
  so do the CPU fallback, `ui.render` and the GPU drag of selected objects. TRANSPARENCYDISPLAY
  controls it and now starts on: AutoCAD's initial value is 1
  (https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-Core/files/GUID-0908F1AC-D122-4B3D-A17C-8705D03A0D0C.htm).
  Rubber bands and rebuilt copies (which carry the current layer's properties) stay opaque.
  PNG and SVG exports of the drawing draw transparency.
- Plots: "Plot transparency" page setup option (`pagesetup {plotTransparency}`, checkbox in the
  Page Setup Manager and the Plot dialog), `plotTransparency` on PLOT/EXPORTPDF/PREVIEW, and
  PLOTTRANSPARENCYOVERRIDE (0 never, 1 the setting, 2 always). PDF gets `/ExtGState` alpha
  (`/CA`, `/ca`) with every transparent primitive stroked on its own; PNG plots blend; SVG uses
  `opacity`. Off by default; plots without it are unchanged byte for byte.

title: DXF/DWG: write the Model layout's plot type as extents, not "Layout information"
author: EP995LAB
body:
How it was found: a DXF saved by CADCraft opened in AutoCAD 2027 (black-box, with a synthetic
drawing) showed the Plot dialog for Model with an empty "What to plot", no preview and no plot
scale, and Extents could not be chosen.

The Model LAYOUT object was written with the default page setup, whose "layout" plot area is
PLOTSETTINGS group 74 = 5, "Layout information" (DXF Reference,
https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-1113675E-AB07-4567-801A-310CDE0D56E9.htm),
at a 1:1 standard scale (75 = 16). Layout information means nothing for model space.

## Changes
- The Model layout is written as CADCraft plots model space: drawing extents (74 = 1), scaled to
  fit (75 = 0). That is PLOT's default for Model (no plot area: the extents; `fit` defaults on for
  model space), the Plot dialog's starting setting for Model, and PREVIEW's. Paper-space layouts
  are unchanged (74 = 5).
- DWG saves go through the same writer, so they carry it too. The reader already ignores the
  Model layout's plot settings, so files from other programs are unaffected.
- docs: file-format-parity.md revision history.

## Testing
- `crates/io/tests/model_layout_plot_type.rs`: the written DXF has Model 74 = 1 / 75 = 0 and the
  layouts 74 = 5 / 75 = 16; a DWG save read back through the bridge has Model 74 = 1. Both fail
  on main (Model 74 = 5).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.
- Checked in AutoCAD 2027: a synthetic drawing saved with this branch opens with "What to plot:
  Extents" and "Fit to paper" set in the Plot dialog for Model, the preview shows the drawing,
  and it plots to PDF.

## Not included
- The Model layout's paper stays the default (ANSI A) while PLOT uses A4 for metric drawings.
- The PLOTSETTINGS "ModelType" flag (1024) is not set on the Model layout; whether it matters
  wasn't observed.

  can't carry a user's own plot settings yet.

title: Interface fonts for the scripts of the names shown, on top of install_fonts (follow-up to #732)
author: SBaksa
body:
Follow-up to #732, rebuilt on #861's `theme::install_fonts` as asked there.

Since #513 / #861 every interface loads CJK faces whatever its language, and the Korean or Arabic interface adds its own script. Names the interface shows can still need a script the language's fonts don't cover: a **Korean layer name in an English interface**, a **Thai, Devanagari, Arabic or Hebrew** drawing, layer, layout or block name. Those showed boxes. (On this Windows machine, a Korean layer name in the English interface does: the CJK fonts found don't carry Hangul.)

- `theme::install_fonts_for(ctx, language, names)`: `install_fonts` (unchanged, it calls this with no names), then a face for each of `names`' scripts that isn't covered, found the way drawing text finds one (`cadcraft_fonts::ttf::fallback_for`). Hangul counts as covered in the Korean interface or when the CJK font has it, Arabic in the Arabic one.
- Faces are looked for **off the UI thread** and kept for the process, so showing a script again never re-reads a file and egui shares the cached `Arc`s. `theme::fonts_generation()` changes when faces are ready, and the app installs again.
- `CadApp::name_scripts` scans drawing titles and their layers, layouts and blocks, again only when a drawing changes, opens or closes (a fingerprint of the open drawings).
- Not changed: the CJK and language faces `install_fonts` loads (still read when it runs, as on main).

**Tests**
- `theme::tests::scripts_of_names`: each script's characters, mixed names, Latin and CJK need nothing extra.
- `tests::a_layer_name_brings_the_font_its_script_needs`: an English interface and a Latin-named drawing whose layer is renamed to Korean. The scan finds Hangul, the layer name's glyphs are in the fonts (when this machine has a Hangul font), a frame without changes doesn't rescan, and renaming it back drops the need. With the name faces disabled, the glyph check fails here, so it's this change that shows the name.

title: Active viewport: redraw while panning and zooming inside it, without rebuilding the layout (fixes #688)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #688.

**Bug:** Inside an active MSPACE viewport, middle-drag, trackpad pan and wheel or pinch zoom change the viewport's view through `set_view_quiet`, which makes no new revision. The layout's display list draws model space through each viewport and was cached on (drawing, revision, zoom band), so it kept showing the old view until a command such as ZOOM rebuilt it: the viewport froze, or appeared to ignore the zoom.

**Fix:** The active viewport's contents are now drawn apart from the layout's list, the way model space itself is drawn:

- They are built once for an area around the viewport, with half its larger side as margin.
- Each frame they are moved and scaled to the current view on the GPU, under the layout's own objects.
- They are rebuilt when the drawing changes, when the zoom has moved 2x from the built view, when the view leaves the built area, and once a zoom comes to rest (so dash lengths and curve detail follow the viewport's scale).

**Clipping:**

- Rectangular viewports clip with the scissor rectangle.
- A clipped viewport's outline is drawn into a stencil buffer as a triangle fan that flips a bit (even-odd, the same rule as the CPU clip), and its contents draw only where the bit is set. The native window now requests an 8-bit stencil buffer, and every canvas pipeline names its format.
- Without a stencil buffer (the CPU canvas, the web runner), a clipped viewport's contents stay in the layout's list, whose cache now follows the viewport's view.

**Render:**

- `Options::skip_viewport` leaves a viewport's contents out of a layout.
- `viewport_content` builds them for any area.
- Viewport contents are built on all cores, like model space: 130 ms → 37 ms for 70,000 polylines.

**Measured** (70,000 polylines, release): a pan step inside the viewport takes about 1 ms. Rebuilding the layout every frame takes about 140 ms per frame. After panning, rectangular and circular viewports match a REGEN at the same view pixel for pixel.

**Tests:**

- `c…

title: Active viewport highlight: selection on the GPU, hover cached apart, kept inside a clipped outline
author: SBaksa
body:
Follow-up to #769, which it builds on. Until #769 is merged this branch also contains its commit, so please review only the last commit, be5ef69.

Inside an active MSPACE viewport, the selection highlight (#695 cached its geometry per zoom band) is still drawn as dashed egui shapes on the CPU every frame. With 7,000 polylines selected that is about 8-13 ms per frame, even with the view still. Its geometry is also cached together with the hovered object, so moving the cursor over objects tessellates the whole selection again.

**Changes** (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`):

- The selection and the hover each have their own cache (`VpHighlight`), rebuilt only when the drawing, the objects or the 2x zoom band change. #695's banded tolerance is kept.
- The selection goes through the GPU highlight path model space already uses (`draw_highlight_gpu`, sharing its layer; the viewport list's generations carry the high bit so the two lists never share a mesh key). The hover, a single object, stays on the CPU as in model space.
- In a clipped viewport the selection is kept inside the outline with the stencil mask from #769 (`Stencil::Inside`). Before, it was only cut to the outline's bounding rectangle.

**Measured** (7,000 polylines selected inside a layout viewport, release): canvas drawing went from about 8-13 ms to about 0.1 ms per frame.

**Tests:**

- `viewport_highlight_is_tessellated_once_per_selection_and_zoom_band`: the selection isn't rebuilt by repeated frames, zooming within the band or the hover moving. It is rebuilt finer past the band, and when the selection changes.
- `gpu_viewport_stencil.rs`: through the canvas pipelines, a highlight drawn with `Stencil::Inside` after a circular mask stays inside the circle.

`cargo fmt`, workspace clippy, `xtask layers` and `xtask wasm` pass, as do all `cadcraft-ui-egui` tests.

title: TRIM: a pick after a closed polyline's last cut keeps only the complementary run (#726)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #726

## Cause

`trim_polyline` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs`) works on arc-length positions along the outline. For a closed polyline it keeps the complementary run from the cut after the pick (`hi`) around to the cut before it (`lo`). When no cut lies past the pick, `hi` falls back to the first cut plus the perimeter, and the run was then taken as `[hi - perimeter, lo + perimeter]` on a doubled copy of the outline. The first bound is already wrapped, the second is not, so the run covered one extra full circuit: in the issue's 4 x 4 square, the vertices `(2,0), (4,0), (4,4), (0,4), (0,0), (4,0), (4,4), (2,4)` (length 24 instead of 8), with the picked left edge still in the drawing. Picks before the first cut (across the stored start vertex) and between the two cuts were fine, which is why the result depended on where the polyline's first vertex was stored.

## Fix

When `hi` was the wrapped fallback, the run is `[hi - perimeter, lo]` (the stretch from the first cut to the last cut before the pick); otherwise it is `[hi, lo + perimeter]` as before. A single cut still leaves the whole outline opened at that point, as before (guarded, with a test).

## Verified

Issue steps on `main` (`rectang` 0,0-4,4, `line` x=2, `trim` pick (0,2)) against this branch:

| | stored result |
|---|---|
| `main` | open, 8 vertices `(2,0),(4,0),(4,4),(0,4),(0,0),(4,0),(4,4),(2,4)` |
| this branch | open, 4 vertices `(2,0),(4,0),(4,4),(2,4)` (length 8), picked edge gone |

New `crates/engine/tests/trim_closed_polyline.rs`. The first three below fail without the fix and pass with it (checked by running them on unchanged `main` code); the others pass before and after as controls:

- `a_pick_after_the_last_cutting_edge_keeps_only_the_complementary_run` (picks (0,2), (0,4), (1,4))
- `the_stored_start_vertex_does_not_change_the_result` (the square stored from each of its four corners, three picks each)
- `a_closing_arc_is_dropped_with_the_picked_piece` (closing semicircle; picking th…

title: Constraints: an arc solved with a negative radius is stored turned half a turn, so its points stay put
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #703.

The solver has no sign restriction on an arc's radius, and a coincidence at an arc's midpoint can converge with a negative one: every point of the arc is then `center + r * (cos a, sin a)` with `r < 0`, i.e. opposite its angle. The write-back stored `|r|` with the same start and end angles, which moves the arc's points to the other side of the centre, so `add` and `solve` returned success with the constraint unsatisfied (residual 2 in the issue's fixture). When the solved radius is negative the arc is now stored with `|r|` and both angles turned by π, which describes the same points.

Validation:
- New `arc_solved_with_a_negative_radius_keeps_its_points` in `crates/constraints/src/tests.rs`: the issue's semicircle fixture and its asymmetric one, each through `add` and through `solve`, checking `all_satisfied` right after the first operation and a positive stored radius. On main it fails through both entry points with the residual from the issue (2.0000000047369513).
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-constraints --lib tests::`, `--test dof`, `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test constraint_geometry`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-constraints --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Geometry: fit splines with too many points use them as control points instead of a dense solve
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #702.

Interpolating fit points builds a dense n x n matrix and clones it for the second coordinate, with no upper bound on n, and every fit path reaches it (the SPLINE command, SPLINEDIT refits, DXF splines that only carry fit points). `open_fit` and `closed_fit` now skip interpolation above `MAX_INTERP_POINTS` (4,096) and use the fit points as control points, which is the fallback both already use when the solve fails; the approximation path was already limited to 300 points. 4,096 keeps the two matrices around 270 MB and stays above the 4,001 fit points of a 500-turn helix, the largest fit our own code builds, so helices still interpolate.

Validation:
- New `too_many_fit_points_are_not_interpolated` in `crates/geom/src/spline_fit.rs`: 4,097 fit points give the control-point spline, open and closed, and a small fit still passes through its points. It fails on main (the open curve's control points come from the solve), and removing only the closed-curve check fails it too.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-geom --lib spline_fit`, `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test helix`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-geom --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Autosave: a write that failed is tried again without another change
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #717.

`Autosaver::plan` records a drawing as autosaved when it dispatches the write job, and the background worker only logged a failure, so an unchanged drawing whose write failed (for example because the autosave folder's path was taken by a file) was never written again, even after the folder became writable. The worker now returns whether the file was written; the reaping step that `tick` already ran (now `Autosaver::reap`) joins finished workers and, on a failure or a panicked worker, stops counting the drawing as autosaved, so the next plan restarts its SAVETIME clock and retries one interval later without needing another edit. A thread that cannot be spawned is handled the same way. A successful write is still not repeated for an unchanged drawing.

Validation:
- New `a_failed_autosave_is_tried_again_without_another_change` in `crates/engine/tests/autosave.rs`: fails on `main` (the drawing is never re-armed), passes with the fix; it also checks that a successful write is not repeated
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test autosave` and `--test drawing_recovery_command`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo check -p cadcraft-ui-egui`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- Tested on macOS (Apple silicon)

title: Selection: rebuild the spatial index when a layer used inside blocks is hidden or shown
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #716.

An insert's bounds leave out block contents on layers that are off or frozen, but the spatial index's context check (`same_context`) only compared the block table, dimension styles, DIMSCALE and the annotation scale. Turning such a layer off changes neither the space nor the block table, so the cached index kept the insert's old, larger bounds and a window that now fully contains its visible geometry missed it. The index now also records the names of the hidden layers and is rebuilt (with its chunks re-measured) when that list changes; layer renames and deletions are caught the same way.

Validation:
- New `index_follows_layer_visibility_inside_blocks` in `crates/engine/src/spatial.rs`, on the issue's drawing (block with a radius-1 circle on 0 and a radius-50 circle on HID, more than 256 entities): after turning HID off the old index no longer matches, an incremental rebuild measures the insert like a fresh one, and the small window selects it. It fails on main and passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib spatial`, `--lib select`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: SPLINE: cap programmatic control points like spline.cv
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #719.

The JSON `spline` command's `control` branch only checked for at least two points, so any number of control points went on into `Spline::from_control` and its knot vector. `spline.cv` already refuses more than `MAX_GEN` (20,000) control points; `spline` now applies the same cap with the same message, before the spline is built, so an oversized request is an error and nothing is added to the drawing.

Validation:
- New `programmatic_spline_control_count_is_limited` in `crates/engine/tests/spline_degree.rs`: 20,001 control points are refused and the drawing stays empty, 20,000 still draw. It fails on main and passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test spline_degree`, `--lib spline`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: HATCHEDIT: refuse an explicit bad scale or angle before editing anything (#724)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #724

## Cause

`run_hatchedit` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/hatch/edit.rs`) read `scale` and `angle` leniently in `properties`: a non-positive or non-numeric `scale` and a non-numeric `angle` were silently skipped. The request still went through, so it returned `changed: 1`, added a Hatch Edit undo step (which cleared the redo history and bumped the revision), applied its valid companion property (`{"scale": 0, "angle": 45}` set the angle) or recreated the boundary (`{"scale": 0, "recreate": "polyline"}`). `HATCH` already refuses a non-positive scale through `size_param`, and the interactive Properties prompt keeps asking.

## Fix

`run_hatchedit` now validates the two numbers first, before any lookup or edit:

- `scale` goes through the same `size_param` rule `HATCH` uses (absent or null: leave it; otherwise a finite number above zero).
- `angle` (degrees): absent or null leaves it; otherwise it must be a finite number. Zero and negative angles stay valid.

The error names the property (`` `scale` must be positive ``, `` `angle` must be a number of degrees ``), the command errors out as any other bad parameter, and nothing in the drawing or its history changes.

## Verified

The issue's fixture (rectangle, hatch, one undone circle so one redo entry exists), `hatchedit` with each bad request, on `main` and on this branch:

| request | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `{"scale": 0}` | success, `changed: 1`, undo step added, redo cleared | error naming `scale`, drawing, undo, redo and revision unchanged |
| `{"scale": -1}`, `{"scale": "x"}`, `{"angle": "x"}` | same | error, unchanged |
| `{"scale": 0, "angle": 45}`, `{"scale": 2, "angle": "x"}` | the valid half applied | error, nothing applied |
| `{"scale": 0, "recreate": "polyline"}`, `{"angle": "x", "recreate": "polyline"}` | boundary created | error, no boundary |

New `crates/engine/tests/hatch_numeric_validation.rs`:

- `bad_scale_or_angle_is_refused_and_changes_nothing` (all eight requests above; compar…

title: Extents: cache block bounds per depth so a deep visit can't hide a shallow reference
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #706.

`bounds_in` cached block bounds by name only. When a block was first reached through a chain deep enough to hit `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH`, its truncated (empty) bounds went into the cache, and a later direct reference to the same block reused them, so the drawing's extents came out empty and Zoom Extents fell back to the limits. The cache key is now (name, depth): a deep visit can no longer stand in for a shallow one, and the work stays bounded at one pass per definition per depth.

Validation:
- `deep_block_visit_does_not_hide_a_shallow_reference` (crates/doc/src/tests.rs): fails on main (extents empty when the deep path comes first), passes here; it also checks the other child order, the shallow-only control, and that the deep path alone still contributes nothing
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-doc --lib tests::`, `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-doc --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Engine: NEW and OPEN end a command left running in the previous drawing
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #715.

A programmatic NEW or OPEN (`Session::execute`) made another drawing current while an interactive command such as LINE was still waiting for input. The command kept running in the new drawing, and when it finished it pushed its undo snapshot, which holds the first drawing, onto the new drawing's undo stack, so undo there brought the other drawing back. `Session::new_drawing` and `Session::open_drawing` now end a running command before the new drawing becomes current, the same thing CLOSE and `document.switch` already do and that starting NEW from the command line did. The command's undo step lands in the drawing it started in. This covers blank NEW, NEW from a template, OPEN and RECOVER, since all of them go through these two functions. With no command running nothing changes, and the previous drawing keeps its selection.

Validation:
- New `crates/engine/tests/new_open_end_command.rs`: NEW and OPEN with LINE pending fail on `main` (the command survives the switch) and pass with the fix; they check that undo in the new drawing leaves it as created and that the first drawing's own undo removes its segment. A third test checks that NEW with no command running keeps the previous drawing's selection
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine` for `--test new_open_end_command`, `templates`, `drawing_recovery_command`, `transparent`, `undo_control`, `undo_count`, `autosave`, `clipboard`
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-ui-egui --lib closing`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Keep the ACIS geometry of 3D solids, regions and bodies on save (ACDSDATA)
author: aldozar
body:
From AutoCAD 2013 on, a 3DSOLID, REGION or BODY doesn't carry its ACIS geometry: the binary SAB lives in the file's data store section (`ACDSDATA`), one `ACDSRECORD` per entity bound by a 320 handle. CADCraft kept those entities (as unknown entities, with their handles) but dropped the section, so a drawing saved as DWG or DXF had empty solids — and the save reported them as "not saved", blaming the DWG writer. acadrust's DXF reader already attaches `ACDSDATA` records to their entities and its DWG writer writes them, so the section only had to be kept.

## Changes
- doc: `Foreign::data_store` keeps the section's groups as read; `data_store_entities()` lists the entities it has records for.
- io: the reader keeps the section; the writer puts it back for files of 2013 and later — and in the DXF the DWG bridge converts — leaving out the records of entities that are no longer written. Nothing is written for older files, or when no record's entity remains.
- engine: `not_saved_as(d, version)`: from 2013 a solid, region or body with a data store record isn't reported as lost. SAVE/SAVEAS and `document.bytes` pass the version being written; older targets still report them.

## Testing
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass.
- New io tests (synthetic SAB data): the section survives a DXF save; a deleted solid's record goes; no section for R2000 or once no solid remains; DWG → read back keeps every solid's bytes. New engine test for the version-aware report.
- On a real 39,600-object permit set with 625 3D solids and 2 regions, DWG → CADCraft → DWG: all 627 bodies keep byte-identical SAB (before: none), and the save no longer warns.

## How this was made
Investigated, written and tested by Claude Code (an AI coding agent) at the request of @aldozar. Happy to adjust anything.

title: Write an unedited dimension's block as it was read
author: aldozar
body:
Saving regenerated every dimension's anonymous `*D` block, including dimensions read from another program's file and never touched. Their definition points went, and other programs then showed CADCraft's drawing of each dimension rather than their own (for instance, a dimension line split around its text came back as one line).

A dimension still linked to the block it was read with (`Dimension::block`) hasn't changed since: every edit drops the link (grips, MOVE/ROTATE/SCALE through `EntityKind::transform`, DIMEDIT, properties, text overrides…), and the screen already draws that block while the link is there. Its block is now written as read, under its name and with its entities' handles. Edited and new dimensions are generated as before.

## Testing
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass, including the existing #495 tests that require reopen-and-save to be byte-stable.
- New test: a dimension whose block holds geometry CADCraft never generates (a circle, a definition point) keeps it, entity for entity, through DXF and DWG; once edited it is regenerated.
- On a real permit set with 1,013 dimensions, DWG → CADCraft → DWG: every dimension's block geometry matches the original (before: none did).

## How this was made
Investigated, written and tested by Claude Code (an AI coding agent) at the request of @aldozar. Happy to adjust anything.

title: Don't give entities made while reading handles the file still uses
author: aldozar
body:
Another program's file can name a `$HANDSEED` below handles it uses (a DWG read through the bridge did: its seed was under the handles of its dimension blocks). The faces a polyface mesh becomes are numbered from the seed while reading, so they could take handles of records further on in another list (another block, or model space); within one list duplicates were already renumbered. A DWG keeps one object per handle, so saving lost the duplicates — 15 of a block's 16 mesh faces in a real permit set.

## Change
Before entities are read, every handle (5/105) another program's file uses is reserved (`bump_handseed`). A file CADCraft wrote names its own next handle (#495), above which its rebuilt records are numbered, so it is left to that and reopen-and-save stays byte-identical.

## Testing
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass, including the #495 byte-stability tests.
- New test: a polyface mesh in a block and model-space lines holding the next handles, under a low `$HANDSEED`. Without the change it fails with duplicate handles; with it every handle is unique, the file's own handles stay with their entities, and nothing is lost through a DWG.
- On the real permit set: the block keeps all 16 faces after DWG → CADCraft → DWG (before: 1).

## How this was made
Investigated, written and tested by Claude Code (an AI coding agent) at the request of @aldozar. Happy to adjust anything.

title: MTEXT: Exactly line spacing keeps the pitch when a line has taller text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #711.

The Exactly/At least flag was stored and round-tripped, but `layout_mtext_entity` never passed it to the layout, and `MTextParams` had no field for it, so both styles stepped each line by its own tallest character. `MTextParams` now carries `line_spacing_exact`; with it set, the plain layout and the paragraph/column layout step every line after the first by the entity height (times the spacing factor) instead of the line's max height. At least is unchanged. The first line still sits at its own cap height, so a tall first line isn't clipped above the insertion point; happy to switch if you'd rather that use the entity height too.

Validation:
- `mtext_exact_spacing_ignores_taller_lines` (render): fails on main (Exactly gives the same 6-unit block as At least for `A\P{\H2x;BB}\PCC`, expected 13/3), passes here; covers the plain and `\p` paragraph layouts, factor 2, and uniform lines being equal in both styles
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-fonts --lib mtext`, `cargo test -p cadcraft-fonts --test mtext_paragraphs`, `cargo test -p cadcraft-render --lib mtext`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-fonts -p cadcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Geometry: spline arc length converges on tight bends, so LENGTHEN shortens to the target
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #705.

Spline arc length used a fixed rule, five-point Gauss on four panels per knot span. On a span that bends sharply that isn't converged: the issue's cubic measured 26.6305 against a true 26.7081. The inverse (`param_at_length`) bisects with differently placed panels, so its own error didn't match the measure's, and LENGTHEN came out 0.137 long in every mode. Each panel now halves until the two halves agree with the whole (relative 1e-13, at most 12 levels deep), and both the measure and the inverse go through it, so both are accurate and agree with each other. Ordinary curves converge at the first check, so the extra cost is one extra pair of Gauss evaluations per panel. Panels that don't converge stop at the depth cap. Happy to switch to an absolute tolerance or a different depth if you prefer.

Validation:
- `nurbs::tests::spline_arc_length_on_a_tight_bend`: fails on main (length 26.6305 vs 26.7081), passes here; it also checks the inverse forwards and backwards at 25/50/90%
- `shortening_a_tightly_bent_spline_reaches_the_requested_length` (engine, Total/Delta/Percent): fails on main, passes here; the retained piece stays on the original curve
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-geom --lib nurbs`, `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test modify_curves`, `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-geom -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: LINE: resolve deferred TAN first point with typed @distance<angle
author: william-wwh
body:
Fixes #779.

## Summary

`LINE`'s first point may be a deferred TAN snap (#168). When the next point
is typed as `@distance<angle`, `Session::typed` parses the point and discards
the original text, so `LineM` falls back to `resolve_deferred(Deferred, Point)`
— a tangent from the typed point to the circle — which is the opposite
geometry from what the user asked for, and drifts because `p` is derived from
a stale `last_point`.

## Fix

`Session` gains `last_polar: Option<(f64, f64)>`.

- `typed()` records `(distance, angle)` when the input parses as
  `@distance<angle`.
- `LineM::input` consumes it (via `.take()`) when the first point is a
  deferred TAN, computing the exact tangent point from the direction and
  drawing the exact segment.
- `start()` clears it so no command inherits a stale value.

The `Input` enum is left untouched: CodeGraph impact analysis shows adding a
variant would affect 443 symbols across the engine, the UI and every test
file — disproportionate to the bug.

## Nature of the fix

Targeted fix for `LINE` + deferred TAN first point + typed `@d<a`. The
tangent point is determined by the direction alone, and the segment matches
the typed length and angle. Other commands that later want deferred snaps
plus typed polar input (`PLINE`, `XLINE`, …) can reuse `Session::last_polar`
in their own `input`.

## Tests

- New `line_deferred_tangent_with_typed_polar`: asserts the start lies on the
  circle, the length is exactly 150, the direction is exactly 218°.
- All existing tests pass (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine`, 245 + integration).

title: Zoom Window: the opposite corner ignores ortho, so the window stays a rectangle
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #787.

The opposite-corner prompt of ZOOM Window carries the first corner as its `base`, and `snap_cursor` applies ortho to any prompt with a base, so with ORTHOMODE on the second corner was pulled onto the horizontal or vertical through the first one and the window collapsed into a line. The prompt now marks that base as a window corner (`Prompt::corner`, passed through `CursorQuery::corner`): ortho skips it, both for the cursor and for a distance typed at the prompt. The base itself stays, so Dynamic Input still reads the second corner relative to the first, and object snaps still work. I scoped it to ZOOM Window as the issue asks; the same flag could go on RECTANG and the W/C selection modes if you want those to behave the same way, happy to add them here or in a follow-up.

Validation:
- `zoom_window_ortho`: fails on main (corner snapped to `(10, 0)` instead of `(10, 4)`), passes here; it also checks that a LINE rubber band still follows ortho
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test zoom_window_ortho --test snap_tracking --test temp_tracking --test isometric --test followups_626 --test drafting_spacing --test zoom_keywords`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine -p cadcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: In-place MTEXT editor with formatting toolbar and ruler (#532, F9)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #532

## Problem
MTEXT text was typed in a dialog window: no formatting toolbar on the canvas and no ruler for indents and tabs (gaps.md F9).

## Changes
- `engine::mtext_edit`: `Formatted` model of MTEXT contents (plain text, a format per character, `\p` properties per paragraph). Parses and writes `\f \H \C \c \L \O \p \P`, keeps other codes (`\S`, `\A`, `\N`, ...) as opaque atoms so nothing is lost. Ops: toggle bold/italic/underline/overline, font, height, colour, indents, tab stops, lists. Typing keeps formats via a diff of the edited text.
- `Interactive::editing_mtext` (MTEXT machine, forwarded by the panic guard) tells the UI where the box is.
- `ui-egui/mtext_editor.rs` replaces the dialog: text box placed at the MTEXT location/width, toolbar (font, height, B/I/U/O, colour, alignment, lists, tab, degree/plus-minus/diameter) and a ruler (drag first-line and left indent markers, click to add a tab stop, right-click to remove). Ctrl+Enter/OK finish, Esc/Cancel abort.
- Ukrainian and German strings, gaps.md F9 row narrowed.

## Limits
New MTEXT only (no DDEDIT/MTEDIT of existing text yet). The box does not lay text out by indents, tabs, columns or font weights while typing (bold shows wider, overline is not drawn); attachment point and columns are still set by the MTEXT options before the text. Atoms show as placeholder glyphs. Listed in gaps.md F9.

- UI test: editor opens only at MTEXT text entry, typing reaches the model, finished contents land in the drawing.

title: Geometry: keep vector midpoints finite at coordinate extremes
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
`Vec2::mid` subtracts the endpoints before halving, so opposite-sign coordinates such as `-1e308` and `1e308` give an infinite midpoint. Line midpoint snaps, dimension associations and 2-point circle centers use it. #400 fixed the same overflow in `Bounds2::center`; this fixes the vector helper.

Use `f64::midpoint` for each coordinate. It is correctly rounded and gives the same result whichever endpoint comes first, so ordinary coordinates can change in the last bit (0.1 and 0.7 now give 0.39999999999999997, the nearest double to their midpoint, instead of 0.4). The regression test covers opposite-sign extremes, large same-sign coordinates, the smallest positive subnormal, and reversed endpoints.

## How it was tested

- New test on unchanged main: `cargo test -p cadcraft-geom midpoint_handles_finite_coordinate_extremes` fails with `(inf, -inf)` instead of `(0, 0)`.
- With the fix: `cargo test -p cadcraft-geom` passes (67 tests), and the tests of the crates that call `Vec2::mid` (doc, engine, constraints, render) pass.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes: fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, workspace tests, assets, layers, wasm.

title: Add a Nix flake (NixOS, GNOME and Hyprland)
author: untypequicode
body:
## What

Adds `flake.nix` and `nix/package.nix` so that `nix build`, `nix run` and an overlay give a source-built cadcraft and cadcraft-cli on NixOS, modelled on the existing LightCraft flake.

- `Cargo.lock` drives the dependencies (git sources through `cargoLock.allowBuiltinFetchGit`), so there is no `vendorHash` to maintain. The version comes from `[workspace.package]`.
- Installs the desktop file, hicolor icons, MIME types and AppStream metadata from `packaging/linux/`, validated at build time (`desktop-file-validate`, `appstreamcli`).
- Wayland and X11: the binaries are wrapped so the libraries winit/wgpu/rfd `dlopen` are found on NixOS — `libwayland-client`, `libxkbcommon` (incl. x11), the X11 libs, the Vulkan loader, `libEGL` and `libdbus` (xdg-desktop-portal file chooser). It runs natively on Wayland under GNOME and Hyprland, with X11/XWayland as fallback. Hyprland needs a portal backend for the file dialogs (`xdg.portal.extraPortals = [ pkgs.xdg-desktop-portal-gtk ]`); this is noted in `nix/package.nix`.
- The fonts from `storytold/craft-fonts`, where the app embeds them, are a pinned non-flake input at the revision the release workflow uses.
- Also: `overlays.default`, `apps.default`, a dev shell, `nix fmt` and a formatting check.
- `doCheck` is off: the suite needs corpora and a GPU the sandbox cannot provide (`cargo xtask ci` stays the gate); it can be turned on with `overrideAttrs`.

No Rust, packaging or CI file is touched.

## Testing

`nix build .#cadcraft` builds both binaries and passes the desktop-file and AppStream validation, on NixOS.

title: BOUNDARY: cap point list and aggregate output per call (#723)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #723

## Problem

author: flyboy-byte

Typing `ORTHOMODE`, `PICKADD` and the like at the command line returned "unknown command". `Session::start` now falls back to SETVAR with the name already entered when the text isn't a command but is a known variable. title: ACAD_TABLE: readable cell text from AutoCAD files (cell height, style scale, MTEXT)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #802

Analysis of the causes by @LiteS1de (Artem Pedenko) in the issue; this is an independent implementation.

## Problem
ACAD_TABLE entities from AutoCAD files rendered their cell text about 0.18 units high (a dot on a metric sheet), and MTEXT codes in cells were drawn literally.

## Changes
- `dxf_read`: a table without CADCraft xdata (another writer) has no scale of its own; once table styles are read its `text_height` is resolved to its style's height, so cell style heights apply unscaled (scale 1).
- `TableCell::text_height: Option<f64>`: read from DXF 140 in the cell record, ignoring a 140 inside the `301 CELL_VALUE` ... `304 ACVALUE_END` block (a numeric value there). Written back by `dxf_write`; non-finite or non-positive values are dropped.
- `render::table`: the cell height overrides the cell style height and scales with the table like it; cell content is laid out with `layout_mtext_with` (cell alignment numbers are MTEXT attachment points), so `\P`, `{\Q15;...}`, `\F...;`, `\W1;` work.

## Limits
Not addressed (also listed in the issue): merged cells from AutoCAD files, block cells, cell text style override, wrapping to the cell width, per-run MTEXT colours (cell colour is used), and the DWG path (acadrust writes 140 from the cell style).

## Test plan
- io: foreign table reads cell 140 (outside the value block only), resolves table height to the style's, round-trips the cell height; hostile 140 values added to `hostile_extension_data_never_panics`.
- render: cell height overrides the style and scales with the table.
- `cargo test` doc/io/render/engine and clippy -D warnings on touched crates pass (full `xtask ci` not run).

title: Geometry: param_at_length validates the spline before clamping to its domain (#704)
author: mroxso
body:
## What

`Spline::param_at_length` clamped a finite `from` parameter to `domain()` **before** checking `is_valid()`. An invalid spline can carry reversed domain bounds (`knots[degree] > knots[control.len()]`), and `f64::clamp` asserts `min <= max` — so a direct public API call on such a spline panicked instead of reaching the method's documented non-panicking invalid-input fallback.

Fixes #704.

## Change

- `crates/geom/src/nurbs.rs`: check `is_valid()` first; for an invalid spline return `from` when finite, else `domain().0` (no clamp, so no panic). Valid-spline behaviour is unchanged — for a valid spline the knots are non-decreasing and `degree < control.len()`, so `lo <= hi` and the clamp is safe.
- Regression test `param_at_length_never_panics_on_invalid_domain`: a reversed-domain spline (`knots = [0.0, 2.0, 1.0, 1.0]`, `domain() == (2.0, 1.0)`) and an empty spline; also covers `length_between`/`length` on the invalid spline. Verified the test panics on the pre-fix code and passes after.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p cadcraft-geom`: 67 passed.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers all ok. The wasm step fails in this environment for an unrelated reason (no rustup / `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target not installed — it fails identically on clean `main`); the change is plain Rust in the L0 geom crate with no target-specific code.

title: REFEDIT, REFSET and REFCLOSE: edit block references in place
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #813

## Problem
gaps.md F2: block and xref references could not be edited in place (REFEDIT, REFSET, REFCLOSE missing). XCLIP is not part of this (see #728).

## Changes
- `REFEDIT` (handle/name, optional `objects` subset): hides the picked reference, puts the block's objects into the drawing where the reference shows them (the working set), the rest of the block as faded copies. Everything else is locked (`is_locked`, and `after_command` undoes any command that touched something outside the working set). Objects drawn while editing join the working set.
- `REFSET` `{add, remove}`: adds drawing objects or faded block objects to the working set, or returns objects to the block (edits kept). Prompt machine with Add/Remove.
- `REFCLOSE` `{option: save|discard}`: writes the working set back into the block definition (all other references update) or discards. A save that would make the block contain itself is refused and the edit stays active. Prompt machine with Save/Discard.
- State is `Drawing::refedit` (in the doc crate), so undo/redo move copies and state together. Files are written from `Drawing::committed()` (DXF/DWG/autosave never hold half an edit); an explicit SAVE is refused until REFCLOSE; BLOCK may not redefine the block being edited. The state ends with its document, so closing or opening another drawing leaves nothing inconsistent.
- Menu entries under Tools > Xref and Block In-place Editing, translations in all 8 languages, gaps.md F2 and ROADMAP updated.

## Limits (left)
- Xrefs are refused with a message (writing the source drawing back is not available; XOPEN opens it).
- No nested-reference picking, no dimmed look or banner for the locked drawing in the UI (command line / JSON only), attributes of other references are not synchronised (ATTSYNC). References must be scaled equally in X and Y.

title: Block Editor: BEDIT, BSAVE, BSAVEAS and BCLOSE for static blocks
author: codyvogt
body:
Part of #185 (gaps.md row 4 / F3)

## What this is
A first, deliberately simple Block Editor: open a normal (static) block, edit it with the ordinary commands, save it back, and every reference in the drawing updates. It is the base the dynamic-block work in #185 needs. No parameters, actions or authoring palettes yet (see Next steps).

## Changes
- **BEDIT** `{name? | handle?}` opens a block definition in the drawing's own tab, with its base point at the origin. With one block reference selected it opens that block directly. Otherwise it prompts for a name, a picked reference, or `?` to list blocks. It is in Tools > Block Editor, the Block tool set's Block Editor button (enabled now) and the right-click menu of a selected block reference.
- **BSAVE** writes the objects back into the definition. It is one undo step in the drawing, and every reference updates.
- **BSAVEAS** `{name, replace?}` saves under a new name (keeping the block's base point) and then edits that block.
- **BCLOSE** `{save?}` returns to the drawing. Interactively it asks "Save changes to block?" when there are unsaved changes.
- **BLOCKEDITOR** sysvar (read-only). `blockEditor` added to the drawing info and the document list.
- **State** (`crates/engine/src/blockedit.rs`): while the editor is open, `DocState::doc` is the editor's drawing. The drawing waits untouched in `DocState::block_edit` with its undo history, selection and views, and BCLOSE puts it back. Because nothing else can change the drawing meanwhile, saving needs no merge and handles can't collide. Objects left unchanged are written back exactly, so no coordinate drifts by `x - base + base`. Table changes made in the editor (layers, styles) apply to the drawing, as in AutoCAD.
- **Files:**
  - SAVE/QSAVE write the drawing outside the editor (`DocState::drawing()`), without block changes that haven't been saved into the block yet.

title: Fix polyline offset arc bulge after joining moved endpoints (#817)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #817.

Offsetting a polyline whose arc meets a line at a corner (for example a circle trimmed and joined to a polyline) drew a wrong curve on the arc part.

`offset_polyline` offsets each segment, then moves each segment's start to where it meets the previous one. On an arc this moves the start (and the end) along the offset circle, but the vertex kept the bulge of the original, unmoved arc. A bulge describes an arc by its chord, so the same bulge on a shorter or longer chord gave a circle with a different centre and radius. The code already had a comment saying the bulges should be recomputed there.

The fix first collects all joined start points, then computes each arc's bulge from the sweep between its joined start and end around the arc's own centre (counter-clockwise or clockwise as the arc runs). Lines and tangent joins, where the endpoints do not move, give the same result as before.

Test: `offset_polyline_arc_bulge_follows_joined_endpoints` offsets a line followed by a semicircle inward by 1 and checks that the arc in the result still has the original centre (10, 5) and radius 4. Without the fix the old bulge on the shortened chord moves the centre.

title: Render tests: compare hatch LOD segments within a tolerance (fixes a Windows failure on main)
author: mattlafy
body:
## What

`crates/render/src/tests.rs`: `normal_zoom_pattern_is_unchanged` compared `pattern_lines` output
against the full-detail result with exact `assert_eq!`. It now compares through a small
`assert_same_segments` helper: the number of segments and points per segment must still match
exactly, and each point within `1e-9`. Test-only; no production code changes.

## Why

The test fails on a clean `main` (00c7613, and since #638 introduced it) on Windows
(x86_64-pc-windows-msvc). With ANSI31 one pattern line's clipped start point comes out as
`(-3.14e-16, -3.14e-16)` on one path and `(0.0, 0.0)` on the other — the same corner, differing
only by floating-point noise from code generation. The level-of-detail logic is correct; the
assertion was stricter than the property it states ("the level of detail changes nothing"). This
makes `cargo xtask ci` red for any Windows contributor before they've changed anything.

## How tested

- On upstream/main 00c7613, Windows 11: `cargo test -p cadcraft-render normal_zoom` fails (ANSI31,
