title: DXF: write viewport frozen layers as group 341 layer handles too
author: mattlafy
body:
## What

Follow-up to #98: #150 made viewport frozen layers survive CADCraft's own save and reopen, through its `VPFROZEN` xdata. Other programs don't read that xdata, so this writes the standard group too.

A layout VIEWPORT's per-viewport frozen layers (VPLAYER / `frozen_layers`) are now also written as
the standard DXF group 341 — one soft pointer per frozen layer to its LAYER table record handle —
alongside CADCraft's existing `1001 CADCRAFT` / `1000 VPFROZEN` xdata. The reader falls back to 341
when the xdata is absent.

- **Writer** (`crates/io/src/dxf_write.rs`): the LAYER record handles are remembered as the table
  is written; each VIEWPORT emits its 341 groups after 90/340 and before the xdata. A frozen name
  with no LAYER record is skipped for 341 only (the xdata still carries it, so nothing is lost on
  a CADCraft round trip).
- **Reader** (`crates/io/src/dxf_read.rs`): the CADCRAFT xdata still wins. A VIEWPORT without it —
  i.e. a file from another program — resolves its 341 handles through the LAYER records' group-5
  handles; unknown handles are ignored and the 341 order is kept.
- `docs/file-format-parity.md`: VIEWPORT row and revision history.

## Why

Per-viewport layer freezing is how a sheet shows different content in different viewports
(plan vs. RCP vs. furniture layout of the same model). Until now it was saved only in CADCraft's
private xdata, which every other program ignores, so a CADCraft-saved DXF opened in any third-party
viewer showed every layer in every viewport — the sheet looks wrong outside CADCraft even though
CADCraft reads it back correctly. Group 341 is the DXF Reference's own field for this list, so
this is a file-format fidelity fix (docs/gaps.md FF1 territory: what other programs see in our
saves), and it also lets CADCraft read per-viewport freezing from DXFs written by other programs,
which it currently drops.

title: Extension slots: application-keyed JSON on entities, layers and the drawing, round-tripped through DXF
author: mattlafy
body:
## What

```rust
pub type Extension = BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>; // keyed by application name
```

and `pub ext: Extension` on `Common` (every entity), `Layer` and `Drawing`. Serde `default` +
`skip_serializing_if = is_empty`, so every existing serialized form is byte-for-byte unchanged while
a slot is empty. No command reads or writes `ext`; it is data that travels with its object.

- **Copies carry it** — COPY, MIRROR, ARRAYRECT, OFFSET, ROTATE copy, COPYCLIP/PASTECLIP clone the
  entity, so the slot comes along; an associative array keeps it on the objects it moves into its
  source block.
- **Undo/redo restore it** through the existing `Arc<Drawing>` snapshots.
- **DXF round-trips it** (`crates/io/src/dxf_ext.rs`, `dxf_write.rs`, `dxf_read.rs`):
  - entity/layer key `K` → xdata under its own registered APPID `K`, shaped like the existing array
    xdata: `1001 K`, `1000 EXT`, `1002 {`, the JSON split into ≤240-byte `1000` strings, `1002 }`;
    spliced at the end of the entity's own record, before any VERTEX/ATTRIB/SEQEND;
  - `Drawing.ext` → one named-object-dictionary XRECORD `CADCRAFT_EXT_<key>` per key;
  - keys that aren't valid symbol names, or equal (any case) to CADCraft's own APPIDs, are skipped
    on write; keys equal but for case keep the first.
- `docs/file-format-parity.md`: foreign-data row and revision history.

## Why

CADCraft is headless-first (CLI, MCP, control channel, crates usable on their own), which makes it
attractive to embed: a program can build on `cadcraft-engine` and get AutoCAD-compatible editing,
undo and DXF/DWG for free. What such a program can't do today is attach its own *typed* data to
CADCraft objects. A side table keyed by handle goes stale on every COPY, MIRROR, array, clipboard
paste and undo, and is lost on save. `ext` puts the data on the object, so the engine's existing

title: Fix active layout viewport display staying static during pan and zoom (#822)
author: GJoe2
body:
Fixes #822

### Summary
In layout tabs (Paper Space), panning or zooming inside an active model-space viewport (`MSPACE`) caused selection/rollover highlights to move, but the underlying drawing geometry inside the viewport remained completely frozen until the user manually ran `REGEN`.

### Root Cause & Relation to #687 / PR #695
In model space, the GPU shader translates the mesh dynamically using uniform offset `mesh_origin - view_center`. In paper space, model entities viewed through a viewport cannot use that single global translation; they are clipped to the viewport rectangle and mathematically transformed into paper sheet coordinates by `cadcraft_render::build`, baking their geometry into `app.canvas.list`.

When panning or zooming in an active viewport, `DocState::store_view` modified the viewport entity's `view_center` and `view_height` inside the document store in place, but **never bumped `self.revision`**. Because `self.revision` did not change, `ensure_list` assumed nothing changed and exited early every frame. The GPU continued rendering the stale display list at sheet coordinates.

PR #695 cached active viewport highlights (`app.canvas.vp_hl`) per zoom band. Because highlights use the viewport model view transform `xf` directly, they moved with pan and zoom, which made the underlying frozen drawing even more noticeable.

### Fix
1. In `DocState::store_view` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`): bump `self.revision += 1;` when an unlocked active viewport's `view_center` or `view_height` changes.
2. In `run_mspace` and `run_pspace` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/layout.rs`): bump `st.revision += 1;` so entering/exiting model space in a layout tab immediately triggers a fresh display list.
3. In `ensure_list` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`): incorporate `st.space` in the display list key so layout switches invalidate cleanly.
4. Added unit test `pan_and_zoom_in_unlocked_viewport_bumps_revision` (`crates/engine/tests/zoom_viewport.rs`).
5. Added integration test `pan_i…

title: Fix double-clicking layout viewports creating persistent selection rectangle (#823)
author: GJoe2
body:
Fixes #823

### Summary
Double-clicking inside a viewport to enter `MSPACE` or on the paper sheet outside to enter `PSPACE` caused a persistent green (crossing) or blue (window) selection rectangle to stick to the mouse cursor as if picking the second corner of a selection window.

### Root Cause
In egui, a double-click is delivered across frames as:
- **Click 1**: `i.pointer.primary_clicked()` is `true`, while `i.pointer.button_double_clicked()` is `false`. When clicked over empty space on paper, `Session::idle_click` initiated a window selection:
  ```rust
  self.pending_window = Some(PendingWindow { corner: p, during_command: false });
  ```
- **Click 2**: Both `primary_clicked()` and `button_double_clicked()` are `true`. The viewport double-click handler in `canvas.rs` ran `app.run("mspace", ...)` (or `pspace`) and immediately executed an early `return;`.

Because of the early `return;`, click 2 never reached `idle_click` to consume or cancel the window selection. Neither `canvas.rs` nor `run_mspace`/`run_pspace` cleared `pending_window`. This left `pending_window` active with its corner at the double-click position (in paper units), and subsequent mouse movements drew a crossing/window selection box between that stored corner and the active cursor.

### Fix
1. In `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`:
   - In the viewport double-click handler, explicitly reset `app.session.pending_window = None;` and `app.canvas.drag_window = false;`.
   - Before click handling, if `dbl_primary` is `true`, reset `pending_window` and `drag_window` and suppress `pressed_primary` dispatch (`pressed_primary && !picked && !dbl_primary`) so double-clicks on empty canvas never open a selection window.
2. In `crates/engine/src/cmd/layout.rs` (`run_mspace`, `run_pspace`) and `crates/engine/src/cmd/view.rs` (`run_layout_set`): explicitly clear `s.pending_window = None;` so space/viewport switches never leave an orphaned selection window.
3. Added integration test `double_click_viewport_does_not…

title: Ctrl+Z / U during LINE removes only the last segment (#750)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #750

## Problem
Ctrl+Z (and the U command / menu) while LINE was running ended the command and then undid the whole chain, so ~10 drawn segments vanished at once. AutoCAD removes only the last segment, like the `Undo` keyword at the "Specify next point" prompt.

## Changes
- `Session::start` (UI shortcut, menu, command line `u`/`undo` as a command): if `u`/`undo` is invoked while the current prompt offers an `Undo` keyword, it is routed to that keyword; the command keeps running. Applies to every prompt machine that offers Undo (LINE, PLINE, SPLINE, 3DPOLY, MLINE ...).
- Fallback unchanged: no Undo keyword (TEXT, first point of LINE ...) ends the command, then undoes.
- `engine.execute("undo")` (JSON/MCP/scripts) unchanged; `programmatic_undo_during_a_command_ends_it_first` still passes.

## Limits
Any prompt with an `Undo` keyword gets the routing, including selection prompts (the keyword there undoes the last selection step).

## Test plan
- New: `undo_during_line_removes_the_last_segment_and_keeps_line_running` (3 segments -> 2 -> 1, LINE still running, continues), `undo_during_a_command_without_undo_keyword_ends_it_and_undoes`.
- cadcraft-engine tests and clippy -D warnings pass.

title: fix(dxf): MTEXT direction ignores the embedded object's insertion point (#667)
author: iHateStupidPeople
body:
Fixes #667.

**Cause.** An R2018+ MTEXT can carry an embedded object (group 101) that repeats its geometry with other meanings: there, 10 is the X-axis direction and 11 the insertion point. AutoCAD writes one for MTEXT with column settings, and the DWG bridge (acadrust's DXF writer) does too. The MTEXT reader took the first group 11 anywhere in the entity as the direction, so such text turned towards its own insertion point: each label tilted by the angle from the origin to where it sits, as in the issue's screenshot.

**Fix.** Read 11/21 and the fallback 50 from the MTEXT's own groups only (`mtext_dxf::before_columns`, which already stops at group 101 and was used for the 50 fallback).

**Tests.** `crates/io/tests/mtext_embedded_object.rs` adds an embedded object as AutoCAD writes it to an unrotated and a rotated MTEXT. Both tests fail before the change and pass after it. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-io --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test -p cadcraft-io` pass. The test DXF is synthetic; no AutoCAD-produced file is used or committed.An R2018+ MTEXT can carry an embedded object (group 101) in which 10 is the
X-axis direction and 11 the insertion point. AutoCAD writes one for MTEXT with
column settings, and so does the DWG bridge. The reader took the first group 11
anywhere in the entity as the direction, so such text turned towards its own

title: Canvas: every click places a point while drawing, however fast
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #815.

Two ways a fast click got lost in LINE/PLINE (and any other point prompt). egui only counts a click if the button comes up within 6 points of where it went down; when you're already moving to the next point as you click, it becomes a drag and no point is placed. And eframe hands over all the input since the last frame at once, so two clicks that land in one slow frame show up as a single `primary_clicked()`, and only the last one placed a point. Now, while a command asks for a point, a drag that ends on the canvas places the point where the button came up, and earlier releases in the same frame each place their own point (snapped as usual) before the last one goes through the normal click path. Selection prompts, pending windows and realtime zoom are left as they were. The sliding click uses the release position, like ordinary clicks do now; happy to switch to the press position if you'd rather.

Validation:
- `rapid_clicks::two_clicks_within_one_frame_place_two_points`: fails on main (1 line instead of 2), passes here
- `rapid_clicks::a_click_made_while_the_mouse_moves_still_places_the_point`: fails on main (no line), passes here
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-ui-egui --test context_menus --test context_menu --test docking_workflows --test options_followups --test shared_controls --test measure_distance_snapping`, `--lib canvas::`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

The full selection is preserved, including PICKADD=0 and PICKFIRST=0. Snapping and Ortho apply, locked layers remain protected, and Escape or loss of window focus cancels. Grips and modified clicks keep their existing behavior, and dragging empty space still selects by window.

title: Fix Intel Mac crash: probe Metal shader language version support
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes crashes on Intel Macs where all ArtCraft apps fail to launch with `Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'`.

The wgpu Metal backend was choosing MSL version purely from OS version, but legacy Intel GPUs have older Metal compilers that reject newer MSL versions.

## Solution

Vendors wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with the patch from gfx-rs/wgpu#10592:
- Probes the Metal compiler at adapter creation by compiling a test kernel
- Steps down from OS-selected version until compiler accepts it
- Modern Macs: tries Metal 3.2 → succeeds immediately
- Legacy Intel Macs: tries 3.2 → 3.1 → ... → 2.4/2.3 until one works

## Issues Fixed

Fixes storytold/photocraft#1859
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2126  
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2190

## Testing

- ✅ Compiles on macOS
- ✅ Passes clippy
- ⚠️ Untested on real Intel Mac hardware (awaiting community testing)

## Notes

The vendored wgpu-hal will be removed once upstream releases the fix and ArtCraft can bump to that version.

---
— sent on behalf of @mjohnson7cd by Claude Code

## What this is
The first step toward using AutoCAD dynamic blocks in CADCraft: **read** a dynamic block's parameters and actions into a typed model. Nothing is applied to references yet. Since #528 the data has been kept and written back as foreign objects, but nothing could read it.

title: Improve large-drawing performance and responsiveness
author: PedroGuille
body:
Large drawings are sluggish because cursor movement repeats geometry calculations, small edits rebuild the entire model, and file decoding blocks the desktop interface. This change reduces that repeated work through geometry caching, incremental rendering, indexed entity access, and background file loading.

The implementation covers the following areas:

1. **Cached cursor hit testing**

   Reuses the geometry used to determine which object is under the cursor, including patterned hatches and expanded block geometry. A spatial index searches the cached segments for the closest match. Lines and points use direct distance calculations without allocating tessellated geometry.

   The cache is bounded and invalidated when the drawing or relevant font settings change. The first query still builds the required geometry; subsequent cursor movements benefit from reuse.

2. **Less work during intersection snapping**

   Filters out finite segments whose padded bounds cannot intersect the cursor’s snap aperture before running the more expensive intersection calculations. This particularly helps tessellated curves such as ellipses and splines.

   Apparent Intersection retains the segments needed for extended intersections. Candidate ordering and snap scoring continue to follow the existing behavior.

3. **Incremental model rendering and GPU buffer reuse**

   Caches model geometry by the document’s copy-on-write entity chunks. A small edit rebuilds affected chunks while reusing unchanged geometry.

   GPU mesh conversion and buffer uploads also reuse unchanged parts. The vertex origin remains stable across compatible edits, preventing an extents change from unnecessarily invalidating every buffer.

   Wipeout barriers remain part of the complete drawing’s render order, preserving the grouping of fills, lines, and wide lines across chunk boundaries.

4. **Conservative off-screen geometry culling**

   Skips tessellation for supported model entities that are safely outside the…

title: Desktop: a bare --control keeps the CADCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT port
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #844.

A bare `--control` (as the last argument) passed `None` to `control_port_from`, which returned `None` early and overwrote the port already read from `CADCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT`, with nothing in the log. The `--control` arm now goes through a small `control_flag` helper: with no value it keeps the variable's port and logs a warning (saying which port it uses, or that the channel is off); with a value it behaves as before, so `--control PORT` still wins over the variable. One line in `docs/control-protocol.md` states the precedence. I went with keeping the env port rather than only warning, since that's what the env var asked for; happy to switch to warn-and-off if you prefer.

The `--control some/file.dxf` case from the issue is left as is: it already logs a warning, and treating a non-number as "no port given" would change what the flag means.

Validation:
- `tests::control_without_a_port_keeps_the_environment_port`: fails on main (`left: None, right: Some(47321)`), passes here

title: Control channel: control.methods lists the methods, ping answers
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #843.

The only way to learn the control channel's top-level methods was `docs/control-protocol.md`; `help`, `methods`, `ping` and friends all got `unknown method`. Both the app (`control.rs`) and the headless backend (`cadcraft-cli mcp`) now answer `control.methods` with the methods they actually serve, each as `{method, params, description}` (headless lists only its subset), and `ping` with `"pong"`. An unknown method's error now reads ``unknown method `help`; `control.methods` lists them (docs/control-protocol.md)``. Both new methods are added to the doc table and to the MCP bridge's read-only list, so they are resent after a lost reply. The list is a plain table next to `handle`. A test keeps it equal to the doc table and calls every listed method to make sure it is dispatched, so the two can't drift silently. I kept the names the issue suggested (`control.methods`, `ping`); happy to switch to `help` or to a different `ping` reply.

title: Dynamic block references: custom properties in Properties (stacked on #838)
author: codyvogt
body:
Part of #185. **Stacked on #838** (dynamic block reader): the first commit is #838's; review the last one. I'll rebase once #838 merges.

## What this is
Select an AutoCAD dynamic block reference in CADCraft and Properties shows what AutoCAD shows: the dynamic block's name (not its anonymous `*U12` block) and a **Custom** section with its visibility state, lookup value, distances and positions. Read-only for now; changing values is the next PR.

## Changes
- **`dynblock::reference(drawing, insert)`**:
  - A changed reference's extension dictionary leads to `AcDbBlockRepresentation`. Its `AcDbRepData` points at the dynamic block's BLOCK_RECORD, and `AppDataCache ▸ ACAD_ENHANCEDBLOCKDATA` holds one XRECORD per parameter graph id with the value in block units (a state or lookup name, a point, or a two-point parameter's points).
  - A reference to the dynamic block itself has the block's own values.
- **`dynblock::custom_properties(drawing, insert)`**, in parameter order, only parameters with "show properties" on:
  - Visibility state, with the state names as choices.
  - Lookup value, worked out from every lookup table that sets it: the row whose input cells match the current values (numbers compared as numbers), or the tables' "no match" name (`Custom`) when none matches or they disagree. Empty tables are ignored; choices are the lookup values.
  - Distances and point positions (`Position1 X`/`Y`) in drawing units: block units × the reference's scale, positions relative to the base point, formatted with LUPREC. A distance with a value list lists them as choices.

title: Multiline attributes: read, draw and save their text (they were lost on save)
author: codyvogt
body:
## Problem
Multiline attributes from AutoCAD drew nothing in CADCraft, and **saving the drawing lost their text**. A multiline attribute (DXF attribute type 2, or 4 for a definition) keeps its text as embedded MTEXT after its own groups (`101 Embedded Object`), and its own group 1 is empty. CADCraft read only the own groups, so the text was empty on screen and was written back empty.

Found with a company dynamic block (part of #185 testing): its LOCATION label is a multiline attribute. AutoCAD shows the label; CADCraft showed a blank box, and a CADCraft save removed it from the file.

## Changes
- **Model:** `Attrib::multiline` keeps the multiline text, and `text.value` holds its plain text. ATTEDIT, -ATTEDIT, BATTMAN, extraction and the rest keep working on the value. An edited value replaces the formatted contents (`Attrib::multiline_text`; `mtext_literal` escapes braces, backslashes and line breaks).
- **DXF read:** ATTRIB and ATTDEF are split at the marker. The embedded groups are read with the MTEXT entity parser, now a shared `mtext_from`.
- **Drawing:** a multiline attribute is drawn as multiline text, and ZOOM Extents counts its box.
- **DXF write:** for 2007 and later (when multiline attributes appeared), the attribute type (2/4), alignment point and embedded MTEXT. Only values that differ from unrotated text go in the embedded object, as AutoCAD writes it. Earlier versions get one line of text.
- **Placement:** INSERT and ATTSYNC give references the definition's multiline text placed with them. MOVE/ROTATE/SCALE/MIRROR, Properties rotation and scale, annotative scaling and FLATTEN carry it.
- docs: file-format-parity TEXT/ATTRIB row, gaps.md F17.

## Overlap
- **#834** fixes MTEXT direction being read from an embedded object (#667) on the same lines this PR moves into `mtext_from`. The second commit applies the same fix there, so the two agree. Whichever lands second has a trivial conflict, and I'll rebase if this one is second.

title: AutoLISP: load and run .lsp routines (fixes #758)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #758.

CADCraft runs AutoLISP routines: `.lsp` files load with APPLOAD, `(load)` or by dropping them on the window; `(defun c:NAME …)` defines commands; `(expression)` and `!variable` work at the command line. Details: `docs/autolisp.md`.

**Interpreter** (`crates/engine/src/lisp/`):

- A reader for `.lsp` source: lists, dotted pairs, `'` quoting, strings with escapes, both comment styles. It keeps its own stack, so hostile nesting is an error, not a crash.
- An explicit-stack evaluator. Nothing recurses on the Rust stack, so a routine can stop in the middle (`getpoint` waiting for a click, `pause` inside `command`) and carry on when the input arrives, on one thread as the web build needs. Deep recursion is the error "internal stack limit reached". Long loops run a slice per frame, so the window stays live and Esc stops them.
- AutoLISP semantics: 32-bit wrapping integers, dynamic scope for arguments and locals, `*error*`, `vl-catch-all-apply`, reals printed with six significant digits, AutoLISP's error wording.
- About 200 built-ins: the forms, numbers, lists, strings, `wcmatch`, geometry, output, files, `apply`/`mapcar`/`eval`/`vl-sort` and friends, `get…` input with `initget`, `command` (with `pause`, a command left open for the next call), `getvar`/`setvar`, `entget`/`entmake`/`entmod`/`entdel`/`entlast`/`entnext`/`handent`, `ssget` (modes X, L, P, I, W, C, F, WP, CP, user selection; filters with wildcards and `-4` operators) and the `ss…` functions, `tblsearch`/`tblnext`, `rtos`/`angtos`/`distof`/`angtof`.

**At startup:** `acad.lsp` (once per session, or into every drawing with `ACADLSPASDOC` = 1) and `acaddoc.lsp` (into every drawing opened or created) load from CADCraft's support folder (`<settings>/support`, created at first start), then `S::STARTUP` runs if they define it. `(autoload "file" '("CMD"))` makes commands that load their file on first use; `(load)` also looks in the support folder. A drawing's own folder is never searched for startup files…

title: Engine: run the post-command passes from one place
author: mattlafy
body:
## What

After a command, three passes tidy the drawing so their edits land in that command's undo step:
group membership is pruned (`cmd::groups::after_command`), constraints are inferred, purged and
re-solved (`cmd::constraints::after_command`), and associative dimensions and hatches follow their
sources (`assoc::after_command`). They were called as a block of three lines in two places —
`Session::execute` (programmatic and MCP/control-channel commands) and `Session::finish`
(interactive commands) — each with its own argument expressions.

Both now call one private method:

```rust
/// The post-command passes, in order, run after every command ...
fn after_command(&mut self, before: Option<&Arc<Drawing>>, uid: Option<u64>, ok: bool) {
    cmd::groups::after_command(self, before);
    cmd::constraints::after_command(self, before, ok);
    assoc::after_command(self, before, uid);
}
```

## Why

The two call sites had already drifted in their arguments, and nothing tied them together: the
next pass (or a change to an existing one) has to be made in both, and missing one gives a bug that
only shows on one path — e.g. a typed command behaving differently from the same command over MCP.
With the passes listed once, the order and the set are the same on both paths by construction, and
the doc comment on the method is the one place that says what runs after a command.

Two open PRs show the cost of the current layout: #818 (REFEDIT) adds a fourth pass and has to add it at both call sites, and #824 (Block Editor) changes the three-pass block at one of them. With the passes listed once, each becomes a one-line change in one place. Whichever lands first, this rebases onto it trivially, or it can go after them.

## No behaviour change

Each path passes exactly what it passed before:

| | `before` | `uid` | `ok` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `execute` | the drawing the command started from | the document it started in | `spec.undoable && result.is_ok()` |
| `finish` | `run.before` | `…

title: Open damaged DWGs partially and say what was left out (acadrust 0.6.4, #800)
author: aldozar
body:
Closes #800.

**What changes**
- acadrust goes to 0.6.4, and DWG is read in its failsafe mode (`DwgReadOptions::failsafe()` + `read_with_stats()`). When one object record can't be decoded, the reader skips it and opens the rest. Before, the whole file failed to open.
- A partial read is never presented as a complete one. The skipped records go into a new `Drawing::read_notes` (never saved), counted by type, for example: `DWG: 18 of 52005 object records couldn't be read and were left out (type 55 × 12, VX_TABLE_RECORD × 6); saving over the original file would lose them`. OPEN echoes the note on the command line and returns it as `warnings`, and the app shows it in the status bar.
- Failsafe applies only to individual records. If the objects stream itself can't be read (damaged header or section map, or not a DWG at all), the file still fails to open with the reader's message.
- **0.6.4 test failures, fixed.** acadrust 0.6.4 writes a merged table cell's anchor with `173=0` plus the span (175/176), and sets `173=1` only on the cells the merge covers. The DXF reader now takes a merge from the span alone. Unknown records that the DWG writer can't write back (no raw data, or from another DWG version) are dropped before writing, instead of failing the save.

**Why it matters now:** a real 5 MB AutoCAD 2018 construction drawing set opens with 0.6.3. With 0.6.4's default (strict) reader it fails outright (`Skipped corrupt table record … type_code=71`), because of 18 damaged obsolete table records. With this PR it opens with all its content and the note above. The 0.6.4 bump needs the failsafe read.

**Tests**
- New `damaged_dwg_opens_partially_and_says_what_it_left_out`. It damages bytes across a 200-line R2000 DWG. Every copy that still reads either reads whole or carries the note, and at least one reads partially. An undamaged file has no notes.
- Checked by hand: 8 real DWGs (100 KB to 5 MB). Seven open with no notes; the one above opens with its note.
- `cargo xtask ci`:…

title: Dynamic block references: change the visibility state (stacked on #853)
author: codyvogt
body:
Part of #185. **Stacked on #853** (itself on #838): review the last commit. I'll rebase as those merge.

## What this is
The first property CADCraft can **change** on an AutoCAD dynamic block reference: its visibility state. Pick a state in Properties ▸ Custom (now a dropdown), or call `blocks.reference.set {handle, name, value}`. A lookup value whose tables set only visibility states can be picked too. One undo step.

## How a change is made (as AutoCAD makes it)
Observed in a drawing AutoCAD wrote with changed references of a company dynamic block (kept local):
- **New anonymous block.** A changed reference shows an anonymous block that keeps all the dynamic block's objects and flags the hidden ones invisible (group 60). CADCraft makes a new one from the reference's current block with the chosen state applied. Objects are matched to the dynamic block's by their `AcDbBlockRepETag` element tags, which AutoCAD writes on both. The old anonymous block is removed when nothing else uses it.
- **Link data:**
  - The new block's record gets `AcDbBlockRepBTag`, naming the dynamic block's record.
  - Copied objects keep their element tags.
  - The reference's `AcDbBlockRepresentation ▸ AcDbRepData` (pointing at the dynamic block) and `AppDataCache ▸ ACAD_ENHANCEDBLOCKDATA` hold the value. An existing value record is updated. A new one copies another reference's record for the same parameter when the drawing has one, else a minimal record. The representation is created when the reference had none.
- **Attributes:** an ATTRIB whose definition the state hides is now written hidden (60). It was never written before, so a save could show hidden attributes again in AutoCAD.

## Not yet (refused with a message, nothing changes)
Distances, positions, and lookups whose tables set them. AutoCAD runs those through the actions: in the observed drawing, switching to the "Label" state also ran a lookup that set a distance, and the stretch actions shrank the label's box. That's the next PR…

title: CJK text: big-font cells in SHX text, CJK interface fonts in every language (#674, #513)
author: aldozar
body:
Addresses #674 and #513.

**Drawing: CJK text in SHX styles (#674).** Drawings from China and Japan nearly always put their text in an SHX style with a big font, such as `txt.shx` plus a GB or JIS big font. CADCraft doesn't read big fonts, so it drew those characters from an installed fallback font, scaled by that font's *Latin cap height*. That made each character about 1.3× (Chinese, Japanese) to 1.5× (Korean) too wide and about 1.2× too tall. Labels then ran past their space and over neighbouring text, which matches the "character spacing / broken formatting" in the report.

Now a wide East Asian character (CJK ideographs and punctuation, kana, Hangul, fullwidth forms) in stroke-font text fills a square cell from the baseline to the text height, scaled by the width factor, as a big font's characters do. Latin text and other fallback characters are unchanged. A line also no longer ends with the stroke font's letter gap after a fallback glyph.

Measured at height 1 on macOS:

| text | before: width, y range | after |
|---|---|---|
| 中 | 1.04, −0.09…1.09 | 1.00, 0.05…0.95 |
| 文字 | 2.34, −0.08…1.11 | 2.00, 0.06…0.97 |
| 한글 | 2.53, −0.09…1.18 | 2.00, 0.06…0.96 |

Synthetic check (rendered with `cadcraft-cli convert`): TEXT of height 3 in Chinese and Japanese, each drawn inside a 3·N × 3 box (the footprint N characters have with a big font), now fills its box exactly.

**Interface: CJK names show as boxes (#513).** The interface loaded a CJK font only when the interface language was Chinese. Japanese or Chinese file, layout and layer names therefore showed as boxes in every other language. A CJK font now always comes after the Latin one, so Latin text keeps its look:
- A Japanese font comes first (Hiragino, Yu Gothic/Meiryo, IPA) unless the interface is Chinese.
- Then the existing Chinese font.
- A craft-fonts face embedded in the build comes last, for systems without any CJK font and for the web build.

The name overlapping the tab's close button was already fixed on…

title: Recent files: the Start page and File ▸ Open Recent list the drawings opened last
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #858.

CADCraft never kept a list of opened files: the Start page always showed "There is nothing here yet." and the File menu had nothing to show either. Every drawing opened from a path (Open..., a dropped file, the command line arguments, Recover) is now remembered, newest first and at most 9 like AutoCAD's default. The Start page lists them under Recent (name, folder underneath, full path on hover) and opens one on click; File ▸ Open Recent lists them after Open... with a Clear Recent Files item at the end. The list is saved with the other preferences (`recentFiles` in `cadcraft.prefs`), so it survives a restart, and it's recorded on open, so a drawing doesn't need to be saved to appear. On macOS the native menu is built once, so its Open Recent submenu is rebuilt when the list changes.

Choices that are easy to change: the menu shows file names only (the Start page shows the folder too), and opens through the control channel (`app.open`) or JSON `open` calls aren't recorded, only opens a person does. Happy to switch either.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-ui-egui --test recent_files`: both tests fail on main (empty list; Start page shows "There is nothing here yet."), pass here
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-ui-egui --lib i18n::` (Ukrainian strings for the two new labels)

title: Viewport scale list: add engineering scales for imperial drawings
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #851.

The status bar scale list for imperial drawings only had the ratio and architectural sets, so civil/site scales like 1" = 20' (1:240) could only be reached with `ZOOM 0.0041667XP`. This adds an `ENGINEERING` list next to `ARCHITECTURAL` in `vpscale.rs` (1" = 10', 20', 30', 40', 50', 60', 100', i.e. 1:120 to 1:1200) and appends it to the imperial scales, so it shows up in the popup and a viewport already at one of those scales gets the named label instead of `1:240`. Labels follow the `1" = 10'-0"` form AutoCAD uses in its default scale list; happy to switch to the shorter `1" = 10'` if you prefer.

I left out the "Custom..." entry from the suggested fix: it needs a text input inside the popup and parsing of both `1:240` and `1"=20'`, which felt like a separate change. Glad to follow up with it if you want it.

title: Double-click on text, mtext or an attribute definition starts TEXTEDIT on it
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #842.

The canvas only handled double-click for paper-space viewports, so double-clicking text did nothing. title: DXF: read every ENTITIES section, not only the last
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #865.

`recover01.dxf` splits its entities over several `ENTITIES` sections, with stray header variables and `ENDSEC`s between them, a few empty `ENTITIES` sections and no `EOF`. The tag reader and the section splitter already cope with all of that. The problem was in `dxf_read::read`: each `ENTITIES` section *replaced* the entities collected so far, so only the last section counted (the 5 LINEs in the report). It now appends them, the same way `BLOCKS` and `OBJECTS` already accumulate across sections. With the fix, `cadcraft-cli info recover01.dxf` reports 1,441 LINE and 63 TEXT, 1,504 entities, which matches ezdxf's recover mode.

I didn't add a warning or a non-zero exit code: in this file nothing is skipped any more, so there's no loss left to report. Happy to add a count of skipped records separately if you'd like one.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-io --test split_entities_section` (new): fails on main (`left: (0, 0, 0)`, the empty last section wins), passes here
- `cadcraft-cli info recover01.dxf`: `"entityCount": 1504` (`Line: 1441`, `Text: 63`)
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: Properties palette: numeric fields take feet and inches, show lengths in the drawing's units, and report what they can't read
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #849.

The Properties palette read every numeric field with `str::parse::<f64>()`, so `3'` or `3'6"` didn't parse and the edit was dropped without a word. The fields now go through `units::parse_distance`, the same parser the command line uses for numbers (`36`, `3'`, `1'6 1/2"`, `6 1/2`). Length fields (coordinates, length, radius/diameter/circumference, text height, widths, thickness, and the read-only deltas/positions) are shown with `format_distance` in LUNITS/LUPREC, so an Architectural drawing shows `3'-6"` instead of `42.0000`. Angles, scales, width factor, area and linetype scale keep their plain decimal display. When a field can't be read, the command line says so ("Not a number or distance: abc") and the field goes back to its value. The new message is in all eight catalogs; happy to drop the non-Ukrainian ones if you'd rather have native speakers add them.

title: DXF: associative hatches in blocks keep their boundary; boundaries carry the hatch reactor
author: codyvogt
body:
## What

Saving a drawing broke the link between an associative hatch **inside a block** and its boundary:

- the hatch was written with `97 0` (no source objects), because the writer only looked for sources in model and paper space;
- the boundary object was written without its `{ACAD_REACTORS 330 <hatch>}` group, anywhere (model space too).

AutoCAD writes the link both ways. Without the reactor, the hatch no longer follows its boundary there. Found while testing dynamic blocks in AutoCAD: after a CADCraft save, stretching a dynamic block in AutoCAD moved the outline but left the solid fill behind.

## Change

- `hatch_reactors(d)`: for each associative hatch, its source objects in the same space or block → the hatch.
- `common_x` writes those as the entity's `ACAD_REACTORS` (alongside the DIMASSOC reactor of associative dimensions).
- The hatch writes the sources that carry it as a reactor. A source in another space or block is no longer written: AutoCAD keeps a hatch and its boundary in the same owner.

## Tests

`hatch_assoc_roundtrip::a_hatch_in_a_block_keeps_its_boundary_and_the_boundary_its_reactor`:
- the boundary in a block gets the reactor;
- the hatch writes `97 1 / 330 <boundary>`;
- a model-space hatch pointing into the block writes `97 0`;
- the sources survive DXF and DWG round trips.

The test fails without the fix. `cargo test -p cadcraft-io` and `-p cadcraft-engine --test hatch_assoc` pass; clippy `-p cadcraft-io --no-deps` is clean.

(`cargo clippy` on rustc 1.95 also flags `nonminimal_bool` in `crates/geom/src/nurbs.rs:460` on main; that's unrelated and left alone.)

title: DXF: count the records the reader can't place; info reports them, convert warns
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Follow-up to #869, as asked there: the DXF reader now counts the records it can't place, by the section they came from, instead of dropping them silently.

What counts as skipped:
- `ENTITIES` and block bodies: a `VERTEX` or `ATTRIB` with no `POLYLINE`/`INSERT` before it, a `HATCH` with no boundary data, a polyface/polygon mesh with no usable faces
- `BLOCKS`: a record outside any `BLOCK` ... `ENDBLK`
- `(no section)`: a record between an `ENDSEC` and the next `SECTION`

End markers in the wrong place (`ENDSEC`, `ENDBLK`, `SEQEND`, `EOF`) hold nothing and aren't counted. Unknown entity types aren't counted either: they're already kept and written back.

`info` (that is, `drawing.inspect`, so MCP gets it too) has a new field, always there:

```json
"skipped": { "count": 2, "sections": { "(no section)": 1, "ENTITIES": 1 } }
```

and `{ "count": 0, "sections": {} }` for an intact file. `convert` prints one line to stderr when the count isn't zero, before writing:

```
damaged.dxf: 2 records could not be read and are left out (ENTITIES: 1, (no section): 1)
```

The exit code doesn't change. The count is kept on the `Drawing` (`skipped_records`), next to `hidden_objects`, and is never written to a file.

`recover01.dxf` reports `count: 0`, so the stray `ENDSEC`s and header variables in that file don't produce noise.

Tests:
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-io --test skipped_records` (new): one synthetic file with every case above plus the stray markers. On main it doesn't compile (no field); here it passes. Dropping any one counting site, or counting `SEQEND`/`ENDBLK`/`EOF`, makes it fail.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-cli --test skipped_records` (new): `info` JSON and the `convert` warning on a damaged file, zero and no warning on `sample floorplan`. On main: `left: Null`.
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-doc -p cadcraft-io -p cadcraft-engine -p cadcraft-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: docs: clarify control protocol command dispatch (#845)
author: Zaxaerith
body:
## Summary
Clarify how the JSON control protocol dispatches engine commands, and document the existing `command` alias.

## Problem
Engine command ids such as `open` and `document.bytes` can be mistaken for top-level protocol methods, especially since `drawing.inspect` supports both entry points. Sending either command id as `method` produces an unknown-method error.

## Changes
- Distinguish top-level protocol methods from the catalog returned by `engine.commands`, including the desktop catalog's UI commands.
- Explain `engine.execute` with the command id in `params.command` and command arguments in `params.params`.
- Document `command` as an alias with the same parameters and result.
- Add complete JSON-line requests for inspection, command discovery, opening the repository's sample drawing, and retrieving DXF bytes, including an alias example.
- Explain unknown-method errors, the `app.open` convenience method, and the relevant MCP tool mappings.

Only `docs/control-protocol.md` is changed; runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Validation
- `git diff --check` passed.

title: Embed craft-fonts by default via .cargo/config.toml [env]
author: sblount2025-design
body:
A plain `cargo build --release` from a clean clone silently produces a CJK-blind binary. build.rs warns and carries on:

```
warning: no craft-fonts embedded: Chinese and Japanese text will render as empty
boxes. Clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts next to this repo and
rebuild with CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts
```

With craft-fonts already cloned beside the repo exactly as the warning asks, the build *still* needs `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` passed by hand on every invocation. A build-time requirement that lives only in a warning is one that gets forgotten, and then comes back as a bug report about missing glyphs.

This adds it to `.cargo/config.toml`:

```toml
[env]
CRAFT_FONTS_DIR = { value = "../craft-fonts", relative = true }
```

**This is not a new convention — it mirrors `deckcraft/.cargo/config.toml`, which already ships this exact block.** The other craft apps that read `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` don't, which is the inconsistency this closes.

Properties:

- `relative = true` resolves against the repo root, so no absolute path is committed.
- No `force`, so a `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` already in the environment still wins for a one-off build against a different font set.
- If craft-fonts is **not** cloned beside the repo, behaviour is unchanged — build.rs warns exactly as it does today.
- The existing `[alias]` entry is untouched.

## Verification

Built with the variable explicitly removed from the environment, so only the config could supply it:

```
env -u CRAFT_FONTS_DIR cargo build --release
```

The crate recompiled and the "no craft-fonts embedded" warning did not appear. Tested on macOS (Apple silicon), Rust 1.99.0, against craft-fonts at its current main.

title: Attributes keep Verify, Preset and Lock position (stacked on #854)
author: codyvogt
body:
**Stacked on #854** (multiline attributes); the first two commits are #854's. Only the last commit is new here.

## What

Saving a drawing dropped three attribute modes AutoCAD keeps:

- **Verify** and **Preset** (ATTDEF/ATTRIB flags 4 and 8);
- **Lock position** (group `280` after the tag, DXF 2007 and later).

Found while testing dynamic blocks in AutoCAD. After a CADCraft save the attributes were no longer locked, so AutoCAD let an attribute be dragged out of its reference, and the block's stretch and move actions stopped carrying the attributes along.

## Change

- `Attrib.modes: AttribModes { verify, preset, lock_position }` (serde-defaulted, skipped when default).
- The DXF reader takes the flags from 70, and Lock position from the `280` after the tag. A `280` before the tag is the subclass version.
- The writer follows AutoCAD's layout: subclass version `280 0` (2010+), then prompt, tag, flags with 4/8, alignment, then `280` Lock position (2007+). The DWG bridge reads the same layout, so it reaches DWG files too.
- INSERT and ATTSYNC give a reference's attributes their definition's Lock position. Verify and Preset stay on the definition, as AutoCAD saves them.

INSERT doesn't act on Verify or Preset yet (asking twice, or not asking). That's left for later; this PR only keeps the modes in files.

## Tests

- `io/tests/attrib_modes.rs`:
  - every mode round-trips through DXF 2018 and DWG;
  - the written groups match AutoCAD's order;
  - DXF 2000 keeps the flags;
  - a `280` before the tag is not read as Lock position.
- `engine/tests/attrib_modes.rs`: INSERT carries Lock position (only) to the reference.
- The doc and io suites pass.
  - render: only `normal_zoom_pattern_is_unchanged` fails, as on main on Windows.
  - engine: the attribute and block tests pass.
- Clippy `--no-deps` shows nothing in changed code. rustc 1.95's clippy flags existing `collapsible_match`/`nonminimal_bool` spots on main.

title: Dynamic block references: distances, positions, stretch and move actions, lookups both ways (stacked on #860)
author: codyvogt
body:
Part of #185. **Stacked on #860** (on #853, on #838): review the last commit. I'll rebase as those merge.

## What this is
Dynamic block references' **distances and positions** can be changed. A change runs the **stretch and move actions** that follow it, the way AutoCAD evaluates them, and **lookup tables now run both ways**.

## Changes (`dynblock::set_property`)
- **Distances** (linear parameters): the typed value (drawing units, ÷ the reference's scale) snaps to the value set (nearest listed value, increment from the minimum, minimum/maximum). Zero or negative is refused. The end point moves along the parameter, or both points from the midpoint when the parameter's base location is the midpoint (group 177).
- **Point positions** ("Position1 X"/"Y"), relative to the block's base point.
- **Actions:** each stretch or move whose connections follow a changed parameter moves by that parameter's change (`EndXDelta`/`EndYDelta`, `BaseXDelta`…, `XDelta`/`YDelta`) × its multiplier, turned by its angle offset.
  - A stretch moves an object's listed vertices (lines, polylines) or the whole object.
  - A parameter in the action's selection is **carried along**: its points inside the stretch frame move. Its own actions don't fire, as with chaining off.
  - Associative hatches whose loop is one closed polyline refill from it after the stretch.
  - The reference's attributes move with their definitions, through the reference's transform.
- **Lookups:** a lookup value sets every table's inputs (visibility states and distances). A changed input (a visibility state or a distance) gives its table's lookup value, which then sets the lookup's other tables' inputs. This is what AutoCAD did in the observed drawing: setting the label's visibility to "Label" also set its lookup to "2" and shrank its box through the distance the lookup sets.

A selected dynamic block reference shows its **grips** and they can be **dragged**, as in AutoCAD:

title: Save xref layer overrides with the host, in DXF and DWG
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #886.

Reading already did the right thing: an `xref|layer` record in the host wins over the xref's own layer when the xref loads. Saving never wrote one, though. `dxf_xref::saved_view` dropped every xref-dependent symbol before writing, layers included, and the DWG save goes through the same DXF tags, so both formats lost the host's colour and freeze. The xref's layers are now kept and written as xref-dependent LAYER records, with group 70 bits 16 and 32 ("externally dependent on an xref" and "resolved", [DXF Reference, LAYER](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-D94802B0-8BE8-4AC9-8054-17197688AFDB.htm)). #530 left these records out on purpose (matching VISRETAIN = 0), so this changes that choice: the host now keeps the overrides, as the report expects. `$VISRETAIN` itself is still not written to the header.

The `xref|` linetypes those layers use are saved too, with the same flags. Without them a DWG has nothing to point the layer at, so `acadrust` falls back to Continuous. The test caught this: a dashed xref layer came back Continuous after a DWG round trip. The DXF Reference says the linetype of these layers is always written as CONTINUOUS in DXF. I kept the real name instead, because otherwise reopening would replace the xref's linetype with Continuous. Happy to switch if you'd rather follow the reference to the letter. Other `xref|` symbols (blocks, text/dim/multileader/table styles) are still not saved.

Validation:
- `xref_layer_overrides_survive_save_and_reopen_in_dxf_and_dwg` (engine): attaches a real xref, sets colour 252 on `site|Walls` and freezes `site|Doors`, saves, then reopens as DXF and as DWG. On main, `site|Walls` comes back as the xref's red (`Index(1)`). It passes here, and the dashed linetype of `site|Doors` survives as well.
- `xref_layers_are_saved_as_dependent_layer_records` (io): the written LAYER record has flags 1|16|32, the host's own layers have no xref bits, and the colour/freeze read back.

title: Xdata travels with its object: COPY, MIRROR, ARRAY and paste keep other applications' xdata
author: mattlafy
body:
## The problem

CADCraft keeps other applications' extended data (xdata) since #528: the reader holds it raw in
`Drawing.foreign.entities`, keyed by the entity's handle, and the writer puts it back. That
survives open → save, but not editing. A copy gets a new handle, so the side table has nothing
for it:

- COPY a door tag that carries a hyperlink (`PE_URL` xdata) and the copy has no link — not in the
  saved DXF/DWG, not in the PDF plot's links;
- COPY, MIRROR, a non-associative ARRAYRECT, PASTECLIP: every third-party application's
  tags (Civil, MEP, title-block tools, …) stay on the original only.

In AutoCAD, xdata is part of the object: every copy has it.

## The change

Entity xdata moves from the side table onto the entity, as `Common::xdata: Vec<RawTag>` (the same
raw groups as before: whole applications from their `1001` on). Every command that copies an
entity already clones its `Common`, so all copy paths now keep it with no per-command code; undo
and redo restore it through the existing drawing snapshots.

- `cadcraft-doc`: `Common::xdata` (serde `default`, skipped when empty, so serialized entities are
  unchanged unless they carry xdata). `ForeignExtra::xdata` remains for table records and blocks.
- `cadcraft-io` `dxf_raw.rs`: the reader puts each entity's xdata on the entity instead of in
  `foreign.entities` (and still notes its handle references, so `1005` groups are remapped on save
  as before); the writer takes it from the entity. APPID records are added for copies the same way.
- `cadcraft-io` `pdf.rs`: hyperlinks for the PDF come from the entities, so a copied hyperlink is a
  link in the plot too.
- `cadcraft-engine` EXPLODE: the pieces of an exploded object are new objects and don't inherit its
  xdata (a block reference's pieces are copies of the block's objects and keep theirs, as before).
- `docs/file-format-parity.md`: the foreign-data row says so.

Out of scope here (a follow-up): MOVE/ROTATE/SCALE/MIRROR transforming the world-space gr…

title: STRETCH: polygon and fence selection
author: NakaSato
body:
STRETCH printed "Polygon and fence selection are not available yet" for `CP`, `WP` and `F` at "Select objects" (gaps.md F1). This makes them work.

## What changes

- **`CP` / `WP`**: a crossing or window polygon (Enter closes it). The polygon marks the area whose vertices move, the same way a crossing window does.
- **`F`**: a fence. It marks no area, so the objects it crosses move whole, like objects picked one at a time.
- **`BOX`** works too, and `Undo` takes back the last polygon or fence point.
- The polygon or fence is drawn as a rubber band while its points are placed.
- **JSON form**: `stretch` takes `polygon` or `fence` in place of `window`. Both are capped at the selection modes' point limit and refuse non-finite points.

STRETCH reuses the existing `SelectMode`, `select_polygon` and `select_fence` from `select.rs`; the only change there is making `MAX_MODE_POINTS` `pub(crate)`.

## Testing

- `crates/engine/tests/stretch_select.rs`: six tests covering CP, WP, fence, Undo and too-few-points, the JSON form with a locked layer, and hostile input (`hostile_polygon_and_fence_never_panic`).
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).
- Run in the desktop app over the control channel: the CP rubber band draws and closes; a CP stretch moved only the vertices inside the polygon; a fence moved the crossed line whole. WP was checked by the automated tests only.

## Note for review

That a fence moves objects whole is my reading of AutoCAD's STRETCH (only crossing selections mark a stretch area); it was not checked against the running reference app.

`docs/gaps.md`: F1 narrowed, revision history line added.

title: Fonts: use the TrueType typeface from a style's xdata and find families by first word
author: asimfali
body:
AutoCAD stores a TrueType text style's family in the style's `ACAD` xdata (`1000 GOST type A`, `1071` flags) and leaves the font file name (group 3) empty. CADCraft only read group 3, so every such style fell back to the default font. In the drawing I tested (an electrical schematic) the two styles that carry almost all of its text were affected.

Two changes:

- `style_font` (`io/dxf_read.rs`): a style with no font file takes the typeface from its `ACAD` xdata. A style that has a font file keeps it.
- Family lookup (`fonts/ttf.rs`): `by_family` only considered files whose stem shares at least 5 characters with the family name, so `GOST type A` never found `GOST.TTF` (the stem shares 4). When that finds nothing it now also checks files whose stem starts with the family's first word (at most 24 files, so the lookup stays bounded).

Validation:
- `style_without_a_font_file_uses_the_xdata_typeface` (io): a style with an empty file and `ACAD` xdata gets the family, one with a file keeps the file, one with neither stays empty.
- `a_family_is_looked_for_in_files_starting_with_its_first_word` (fonts): candidate selection for `GOST type A`, the first-word length limit and the cap on files loaded.
- Rendered the real drawing before and after with the installed GOST fonts: the title block text goes from the fallback font to GOST type A and fits its cells.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm). Also built and run on Windows (debug build).

title: MTEXT: paragraph indents and tab stops are in drawing units
author: asimfali
body:
Paragraph indents and tab stops in MTEXT contents (`\pi`, `\pl`, `\pr` and the `t` tab stops of `\p`) were laid out as multiples of the text height. AutoCAD writes them in drawing units. A real AutoCAD file has `\pi27.485;ABC-123.00.000 E3` on 6-high text in a 120-wide box: read as text heights that is a 165-unit first-line indent, so the first line disappeared and only the last word was drawn, at the left edge. `\pi4.8634;ABC «Name»` (4.67 high, 50.2 wide) wrapped onto two lines for the same reason. In AutoCAD both are one line and fit their cells.

Changes:

- `fonts/mtext/para.rs`: indents (`i`, `l`, `r`) and tab stops (`t`) are drawing units. Space before/after (`b`, `a`) and the default tab interval are unchanged (still text heights); I had no evidence for those.
- The JSON `mtext` parameters `indent`, `firstIndent`, `rightIndent` and `tabs` therefore are drawing units too, since they are written straight into the `\p` code. A list's default hanging indent was 3 and is now 3 text heights (in drawing units), so lists look the same for any height. This is a change to the meaning of those parameters; happy to adjust if you'd rather keep them in text heights and convert.

Validation:
- New `indents_are_drawing_units` (fonts): a `\pi4.8634;` paragraph in a 50.2-wide box stays on one line.
- `json_columns_and_lists` (engine) now passes `height: 1` so its expected `\pxi-3,l3,t3` codes are unchanged.
- Rendered the real drawing before and after: the title block cells that use these indents now match AutoCAD.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm).

title: PDFBOOK: plot sheet frames in model space into one PDF per row of frames
author: asimfali
body:
Adds `PDFBOOK` ("Sheet Books to PDF...", File menu, Ctrl+Shift+P): drawings that hold several sheets side by side in model space, each marked by a frame polyline, are plotted into one PDF per row of frames.

How it works:

- Closed polylines in model space whose height is `frameHeight` (default 297 mm) are sheet frames. `unit` (mm per drawing unit, default 1) scales drawing units to millimetres.
- Frames are grouped into rows by their lower edge (bottom to top) and sorted left to right inside a row. Each row becomes one book (one PDF), each frame one page.
- Each page is the frame window plotted without margins on the ISO/ANSI paper the frame matches (either orientation, 0.5 mm tolerance), so a frame fills its page exactly. Frames of another size are skipped and counted in `skipped`.
- Output names: the drawing's file name split at `^` gives one book name per row (`Plan^Spec.dwg` → `Plan.pdf`, `Spec.pdf`); `names` overrides, extra rows are numbered after the drawing. `path` chooses the folder and base name; without any path the books come back as base64.
- Behind it, the `plot` hook takes `pages: [{window, paper, landscape}]` and `pdf_sheets` is now a thin wrapper around a new `pdf_items`, which plots each page with its own options.

It comes from a workflow where one drawing holds several sheets and each row must be sent as a single PDF; I use it for electrical schematics. The frame height convention is a parameter, not hard coded.

Validation:
- `pdfbook_collects_frames_into_one_pdf_per_row` (engine): frames drawn out of order land left to right, A4 portrait and A3 landscape are recognised, two rows give two files named from `a^b.pdf`, a stray rectangle is ignored, and a drawing without frames is an error.

title: Zoom and pan regenerate in the background instead of freezing the window
author: Lufftre
body:
## Problem

Zooming or panning a moderately heavy drawing froze the window. On a real architect's DWG (12k entities, 83 hatches, 1,031 block references; about 340k display primitives) every 2x zoom step blocked the UI for **2–4.5 s**. The GPU was not the bottleneck: a still frame takes under 5 ms. The time went into rebuilding the display list, converting it to vertex data and creating GPU buffers, all on the UI thread, at every zoom band or pan out of the built area.

## Change

**Background rebuilds** (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas/rebuild.rs`). When only the view asks for a new list (new zoom band, pan out of the built window), the canvas keeps drawing the current list, scaled by the view uniform, while a worker thread builds the list, converts it to vertex data and creates the wgpu buffers. The frame that swaps it in only swaps buffers. Edits, the first build and the web build (no threads) still rebuild synchronously, so a change is never drawn late.

**Cancellation.** `cadcraft_render::Options` gains `cancel: Option<Arc<AtomicBool>>`. A set flag stops the build at the next entity (block contents included) and the hatch sweep at its next pattern line. Dropping the canvas's `Job` sets it, so a view that needs a different list cancels the build in flight and starts its own. A long scroll through many bands builds only for where it stops.

**`ZOOM` no longer calls `touch()`.** It changes the view, not the drawing; the bumped revision made every typed zoom a full blocking rebuild (wheel zoom never did). `REGEN`, `REGENALL` and layout switches still touch.

**Agents:** `ui.screenshot` waits (up to 6 s) for a background rebuild so it captures the new view; `ui.inspect` → `perf.building` reports one in flight.

## Measurements (M-series Mac, the DWG above)

Worst UI stall per zoom step, measured as control-channel ping round trips (handled on the UI thread):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Zoom one band | 2–4.5 s | 26–64 ms |
| Fast scroll through 8 bands (a step ev…

title: Read the drawing's WIPEOUTFRAME from its WIPEOUTVARIABLES object
author: asimfali
body:
AutoCAD stores the wipeout frame setting in the drawing's `WIPEOUTVARIABLES` object (group 70: 0 = frames hidden, 1 = shown; DXF name `WIPEOUTVARIABLES`, class `AcDbWipeoutVariables`). CADCraft never read it, so every drawing used the default (frames shown) and masks were outlined. In the file I tested, a numbered circle masks the wires behind it with a diamond-shaped wipeout; AutoCAD shows only the circle (frames off in the drawing), CADCraft also drew the diamond.

`io/dxf_read.rs` now reads the object's group 70 (0 to 2) into the `WIPEOUTFRAME` setting. DWG files go through the same path (the object comes out of the DWG bridge as `WIPEOUTVARIABLES`). Nothing is written back differently: the object is still round-tripped as before.

Validation:
- `wipeoutvariables_sets_the_frame_flag` (io): 0, 1 and 2 are read, no object keeps the default, an out-of-range flag is ignored.
- Rendered the real drawing before and after: the diamond is gone, the circle and the masking of the wires behind it are unchanged.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm).

title: MTEXT: take the contents from the ACAD_MTEXT_2008_RT XRECORD when there is one
author: asimfali
body:
AutoCAD keeps an MTEXT's real contents in an `ACAD_MTEXT_2008_RT` XRECORD of the entity's extension dictionary, and writes an approximation for older readers in the entity itself. For centred paragraphs the entity holds an indent computed to centre the text (`\pi4.8634;...`) while the XRECORD holds the real thing (`\pxqc;...`, centred). AutoCAD shows the XRECORD's contents (the Properties palette shows `\pxqc;...` for such text). CADCRAFT showed the entity's, so text that is centred in its cell in AutoCAD came out left aligned (title block cells, labels under a terminal row).

`io/dxf_read.rs`: while reading the objects it now records the owner of each dictionary (`dict_owner`, the MTEXT whose extension dictionary it is) and, after the entities are placed, replaces the contents of every MTEXT that has an `ACAD_MTEXT_2008_RT` XRECORD with the XRECORD's text (groups 1/3, capped like the other xrecord reads). Entities in model space, layouts and block definitions are covered. MTEXT without such an entry is untouched.

One limitation, so you can decide whether it matters: the XRECORD stays in the drawing as a foreign object, so if such an MTEXT is edited in CADCraft and saved, AutoCAD may still show the old XRECORD text. I did not touch the write side here; dropping or updating the entry when the contents change would be the follow-up.

Validation:
- `the_2008_rt_contents_replace_the_entity_contents` (io): an MTEXT with the dictionary entry takes `\pxqc;ABC` instead of `\pi4.86;ABC`, an MTEXT without one keeps its contents.
- Rendered the real drawing before and after: the cells that were left aligned are centred, matching AutoCAD.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm).

title: Read the vertical justification of ATTRIB and ATTDEF from group 74
author: asimfali
body:
For ATTRIB and ATTDEF, group 73 is the field length and the vertical justification is group 74. `text_from` read `73` first and fell back to `74` only when 73 was missing, so an attribute with `73 = 0` and `74 = 2` (justified middle) was read as baseline-aligned. A numbered symbol (an attribute with horizontal 1 / vertical 2 at the circle's centre) therefore drew its number with the baseline on the centre, above the middle of the circle. The DWG bridge writes both groups on every attribute, so this hit every DWG attribute with a non-baseline vertical justification.

`io/dxf_read.rs`: `text_from` now takes a flag; TEXT uses 73, ATTRIB and ATTDEF use 74 (the writer already did it this way).

Validation:
- `attribute_vertical_justification_is_group_74` (io): an ATTDEF and an ATTRIB inside an INSERT with `73 = 0` and `74 = 2` read as `VAlign::Middle`.
- Rendered the real drawing before and after: the numbers are centred in their circles, as in AutoCAD.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm).

title: Editing an imported table larger than TABLE creates keeps all its rows and columns
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #915.

Every table edit goes through `normalize` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs`, which clamped the grid to the TABLE command's creation caps (2000 rows, 200 columns). Those caps are there for hostile parameters when creating a table, but the DXF reader accepts larger tables (up to its 1M-cell budget), so one `table.set` on an imported 2001×1 table quietly dropped the last row, as PierrunoYT spotted. `normalize` now keeps the table's own rows and columns. It still needs a bound, since it allocates the grid, so it uses the reader's 1M-cell budget and refuses the edit with an error above it, leaving the table untouched instead of cutting it. TABLE, insert row/column and CSV linking keep their 2000/200 caps as before; happy to switch to a different budget if you'd rather.

Validation:
- `table_large_edit::editing_a_large_imported_table_keeps_every_row_and_column` (2001×1 and 1×201 with a sentinel in the last cell, edit A1, undo/redo): fails on main (`left: (2000, 1, 2000)`, `right: (2001, 1, 2001)`), passes here
- `table_large_edit::a_table_past_the_cell_budget_is_refused_unchanged`: new behaviour; fails if the budget check is removed
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test table_large_edit --test table_formulas --test table_breaks --test table_styles`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

TABLEEXPORT (`table_csv`) still exports at most 2000 rows and 200 columns of a larger table. I left it alone to keep this change to editing, and can follow up if you want it covered too.

title: JOIN takes an open polyline whole, so a partly chained one no longer loses its other segments
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #914.

`join()` flattened every selected open polyline into its segments and chained those one by one, then removed every entity that had contributed at least one segment. A line meeting a polyline at an interior vertex could pick up one half of it, and the other half went away with the original polyline. JOIN now chains each source entity as one piece: an open polyline attaches by its own endpoints, reversed when needed, or stays out of the chain untouched. That matches AutoCAD, which joins polylines end to end and never splits one, and it completes what #148 started for #86: only entities fully inside the result are removed. Thanks @PierrunoYT for the clear write-up.

Validation:
- `join_takes_a_polyline_whole_or_leaves_it` (both selection orders, plus a whole polyline joined by its end): fails on main (`line first: true: the polyline's far segment is gone`), passes here
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib join`, `--test break_join_locked_layers --test pedit_splinedit --test modify_curves`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: MTEXT: keep leading and repeated spaces; read a caret-I in the contents as a tab
author: asimfali
body:
Two differences from AutoCAD in the MTEXT layout, both seen in a bill-of-materials table whose cells are single MTEXT objects.

**Spaces.** The layout dropped the spaces that start a paragraph's first line and collapsed a run of spaces into one. AutoCAD keeps both. A quantity column is typically right aligned with leading spaces (`'              12'` in a 31.8-wide box): CADCraft drew the number at the left edge of its box, AutoCAD where the spaces put it. Now:
- spaces that start a paragraph's first line keep their width,
- every space of a run counts (previously only one did),
- a soft-wrapped line still drops its leading spaces, as before.
This is done in both layout paths (`mtext.rs`, and `mtext/para.rs` for contents with `\p` codes or tabs).

**Caret-I as a tab.** In MTEXT contents `^I` is a tab for AutoCAD. DXF files encode a tab that way and the DXF reader already decodes it, but the DWG bridge escapes the caret (`^ I`), so the two characters `^I` arrived in the contents and were drawn as text in front of the label. `layout_mtext_with` now reads `^I` as a tab.

Validation:
- `spaces_keep_their_width_and_a_caret_i_is_a_tab` (fonts): leading spaces and runs widen the text, a wrapped line drops its leading spaces (`["AAAA", "BBBB"]`), `^I` lays out like a tab character, and the paragraph path (`\pxql;`) behaves the same.
- Rendered the real drawing before and after: the `^I` characters are gone and the quantity column lines up with its cells.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm).

title: DXF/DWG: keep extrusion directions on save (lines, points, tilted 2D objects)
author: Lufftre
body:
## Problem

Saving a drawing dropped every entity's extrusion direction (group 210). Three separate effects:

- **LINE and POINT** points are world coordinates; their extrusion says which way their thickness runs. The reader kept it, the writer never wrote it. Lines with thickness came back pointing the wrong way.
- **2D objects in a tilted plane** (elevations drawn in a vertical plane, extrusion `(0,-1,0)`): circles, arcs, ellipses, lightweight polylines, block references, solids and traces were written without their extrusion, so in AutoCAD they landed flat in the XY plane. That is real geometry damage, invisible in CADCraft's plan view.
- **Mirrored objects** (`(0,0,-1)`, what MIRROR leaves): the reader turns them into world coordinates (#277) but kept the extrusion on the object, a plane the geometry no longer has. The drawing read and the same drawing saved and read back differed.

Found by comparing a real 11 MB AutoCAD drawing (kitchen elevations, 12k entities) with itself after a save, object by object: **1,749 objects lost their extrusion**.

## Change

**Writer** (`crates/io/src/dxf_write.rs`): `tilted(e)` returns an entity's extrusion when it is not the default; `extrusion()` writes it.
- LINE and POINT: written as is.
- Circle, arc, solid, trace: the reader converted their points OCS → WCS, so the writer converts them back (`to_ocs`, the transpose of the orthonormal arbitrary-axis frame) before writing 210.
- Arc angles, ellipse parameters and polyline x/bulges, which the reader turns round for a negative-z extrusion, are turned back.
- Block references: a tilted one is kept as read (in its OCS), so only 210 is added.

**Reader** (`crates/io/src/dxf_read.rs`): `folds_extrusion` resets the extrusion to `(0,0,1)` after a mirrored `(0,0,-1)` OCS was turned into world coordinates (circles, arcs, ellipses, LWPOLYLINE and R12 2D POLYLINE, text, mtext, attribute definitions, block references, dimensions, solids, traces, hatches). A tilted extrusion, which is no…

title: fix(dxf): read every MTEXT group from its own groups, not the embedded object (follow-up to #834)
author: iHateStupidPeople
body:
Follow-up to #834, addressing the review there: thanks for catching it.

**Cause.** An R2018+ embedded object (group 101) reuses MTEXT's codes for other values: 10 the direction, 41 the defined height, 71 the column type, 44 the column width, 73 the auto-height flag. #834 read only 11/21 and 50 from the MTEXT's own groups; the rest were read across the whole entity and came out right only because AutoCAD writes the MTEXT's own value first. 44 and 73 are optional, so an MTEXT without its own line spacing took the column width as its line spacing factor.

**Fix.** `mtext_from` reads every group from the MTEXT's own groups (`mtext_dxf::own`, now `pub(crate)`), contents included. 50 is still read from `before_columns`, since after the column type it is a column height. Multiline attributes pass only the groups after their marker, so they are unaffected.

**Tests.** `optional_groups_left_out_are_not_taken_from_the_embedded_object` removes the MTEXT's own 44 and 73 and checks line spacing, insertion point, height, width and attachment. It fails before the change (line spacing 6.0, the column width) and passes after. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-io --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test -p cadcraft-io` (292 tests) pass.

title: Properties: describe and set every text, mtext and dimension property (engine side of the palette rows)
author: Slopapalooza
body:
Engine side of the Properties palette's text, mtext and dimension rows (new gaps.md row U14). The palette switches to these rows in a follow-up PR.

**Rebased onto main at `0b32c2e` (2026-10-19).** Since this PR opened, #1473 added `textHeight`, `arrowSize`, `dimScale` and `precision` to `properties.set` for dimensions. Behind it, `properties.set` ignored every dimension key but `textOverride`/`dimStyle` and most text and mtext keys, and answered `changed: n` even when it took nothing.

Separately, editing a dimension style or a text style didn't redraw dimensions read from a DWG or DXF: they kept drawing the `*D` block they were read with, and since #782 saving kept it too.

## Changes

- **`properties.describe {handles?, type?}`** (new, read-only) returns the palette's rows for the objects, in groups:
  - General for every object.

title: Read VIEWPORT view centre relative to the view target
author: craigsignature
body:
## Problem

Layout viewports in many DWG files open pointing at the model-space origin. On a sheet with several viewports, every viewport shows the same clipped corner of the drawing instead of its own plan, section or isometric.

The DXF Reference gives a VIEWPORT's view centre (groups 12/22) in display coordinates, whose origin is the view target (17/27/37). DWG files commonly keep the view in the target and leave the centre at 0,0. The reader only took 12/22, so the target offset was lost.

## Fix

`crates/io/src/dxf_read.rs`: the viewport's model-space view centre is now `target + centre`. If the sum isn't finite (hostile input), it falls back to the centre alone. This is exact for plan views without twist. Twisted and non-plan views get the same approximation, because the 2D display applies neither.

The writer already writes only 12/22 (no target), so a read and write round trip keeps the view.

## Tests

`crates/io/tests/viewport_view_target.rs`:
- view stored in the target (centre 0,0) is read as the model centre
- centre is added to the target
- round trip keeps the view
- a non-finite target or an overflowing sum falls back to the centre

Three of these fail without the fix.

`cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

Checked against real-world A1 DWG sheets with 8 to 10 viewports each, both plan/section sheets and isometric sheets. Before the fix every viewport showed the origin; after it, each sheet matches its issued PDF. The drawings are client files, so they're not included.

`docs/file-format-parity.md` updated (VIEWPORT row and revision history).

title: Validate KEEP option in BLOCK to prevent accidental object deletion
author: rangoDJ
body:
Fixes #935.

When creating a block with `BLOCK` or `-BLOCK`, passing an unrecognized or misspelled `keep` parameter (like `keep: "retian"`) silently deleted the original objects without inserting a block reference.

This adds upfront validation for `keep`:
