title: Fix SVG ellipse axis and elliptical arc conversion (#945)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #945.

SVG import (`crates/io/src/svg_read.rs`) got four geometric conversions wrong. Each point from the issue:

1. **Ellipse major axis.** `<ellipse>` (and a circle under a non-uniform transform) stored `center + axis * radius` in `Ellipse.major`, but `Ellipse.major` is a vector from the centre (see how `entity.rs` transforms it with `apply_vec`). Any ellipse away from the origin came in with the wrong size and direction. It now stores `axis * radius`.
2. **Elliptical arcs under a uniform transform.** The bulge path was taken whenever the transform was uniform, using `rx` only, so an `A4 2 ...` arc became a circular arc. A bulge is now used only when `rx == ry`; elliptical arcs are flattened, as they already were under non-uniform transforms.
3. **Radii too small for the chord.** `elliptical_params` scales the radii up (SVG F.6.6), but `flatten_arc` then sampled with the original radii, so the flattened arc missed its endpoint. `elliptical_params` now also returns the corrected radii and `flatten_arc` uses them.
4. **Degenerate arcs.** An arc with a zero radius was dropped (and the pen position was not moved). It now draws a straight line to the endpoint (F.6.6). An arc whose endpoints coincide is skipped (F.6.2).

The existing `svg_shapes_become_entities_in_millimetres` test subtracted the centre from `major`, which matched the bug; it now reads `major` as the vector it is.

## Tests

New `svg_ellipse_major_is_relative_and_arcs_follow_the_spec` (`crates/io/src/tests.rs`). Each part fails without the fix:
- an off-origin ellipse has `major == (4, 0)`;
- `A4 2` under the page's uniform transform is flattened (no bulges) and rises by `ry`;
- `A1 0.5` across an 8-unit chord ends exactly at its endpoint after the radius scale-up;
- `A0 3` gives a two-vertex line to the endpoint.

No Rust toolchain was available locally, so the tests were not run here. CI will run them.

title: Keep associative-array parameters when an xref is loaded (#943)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #943.

When an xref is attached or reloaded, `import` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/blocks/xref/load.rs` rebuilds each block of the referenced drawing as `key|name` with a fresh `Block::new`, copying the base point, description, flags and units, but not `array`. Array blocks therefore arrived without their `ArrayParams`, so an associative array inside an xref lost its kind, counts, spacing and replaced items.

The fix copies `array` along with the other block fields:

- `source` and each `replaced[].block` go through the same `dep(Sym::Block, …)` renaming as the blocks themselves and the items' block references, so they name the adopted `key|…` blocks.
- `editing` (the ARRAYEDIT Source state, which is never saved) is cleared, so the import never carries a source edit over.

XREF Bind already keeps this metadata: it clones each bound block whole, and `Drawing::array_params` re-syncs the source and replaced names from the items, which bind renames.

Test: `imported_array_blocks_keep_their_parameters` imports a drawing with a rectangular array block. It checks that the loaded `SITE|*U2` still has its rectangular parameters, with `source` remapped to `SITE|*U1`, the replaced item remapped to `SITE|ALT`, and `editing` cleared. Without the fix, `array` is `None` and the test fails.

title: Read dynamic block element tags from the entity's own xdata (#942)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #942.

Since #890 the DXF reader moves entity xdata out of the kept foreign data and onto the entity (`Common::xdata`). `etag()` in `dynblock/apply.rs` still looked only in `d.foreign.entities[h].xdata`, so for an imported drawing it found no `AcDbBlockRepETag` and `by_tag` paired the dynamic block's objects with the reference's copies by position. When the anonymous block has its objects in a different order, or leaves some out (visibility-dependent geometry), a stretch, move or visibility change hit the wrong copy or none.

Changes (`crates/doc/src/dynblock/apply.rs`):
- `etag` reads the tag from the entity's own xdata first. If there is none there, it uses the kept foreign data, as before. The parsing moved into `etag_in`, so both lookups use one parser.
- When a change copies objects into the new anonymous block, a 1005 handle in a copy's own xdata that pointed to its original now points to the copy. This is the same rewrite the function already does for the kept foreign data, which is empty for imported entities since #890.

Test: `element_tags_are_read_from_the_entitys_own_xdata` builds a definition and an anonymous block with the tags in entity xdata, with the order changed and one object left out. It checks that `by_tag` pairs them by tag. Without the fix it gets positional keys.

Not run locally (no Rust toolchain here); relying on CI.

title: Keep an application's own 102 groups on unknown entities when saving DXF (#940)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #940.

`unknown_entity` in `crates/io/src/dxf_raw.rs` dropped every `102 {NAME … 102 }` group of an entity type CADCraft doesn't model. That was meant for `{ACAD_REACTORS` and `{ACAD_XDICTIONARY`, which `finish` regenerates from the kept foreign data. But it also removed any other application's own group (for example `102 {ACME_DATA 300 payload 102 }`), so saving lost that data.

Now only `ACAD_REACTORS` and `ACAD_XDICTIONARY` groups (case-insensitive) are dropped, so `finish` still writes each of them once. Other groups are written as read, in place. Any handles in them are remapped by the existing unknown-entity path in `finish`. A stray `102 }` outside a group is still dropped. This matches how unknown objects already keep application 102 groups (`Remap::object`).

Test: `unknown_entity_keeps_an_applications_own_102_group` in `crates/io/tests/roundtrip_audit.rs` adds a custom `{ACME_DATA` group and an `{ACAD_REACTORS` group to an unknown `ACME_WIDGET`. After both saves it checks that the custom payload survives exactly once and that the reactor group is not duplicated. Without the fix, the `ACME_DATA` assertion fails.

title: Close idle control-server connections so abandoned clients free their slot (#937)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #937.

The control server serves at most 16 connections, and a connection that never sends a full line held its slot forever: the 60-second request timeout only starts after a complete request has arrived. After 16 idle or stalled clients, every new client got "too many control connections" until one of them closed.

**Server** (`apps/cadcraft/src/control_server.rs`)
- Each accepted socket gets a read and a write timeout of 10 minutes (`IDLE_TIMEOUT`). A client that sends nothing for that long, or stops partway through a request, is closed and its slot is freed. A reply write that blocks for that long ends the connection too. The read clone shares the socket, so the one setting covers both directions.
- Before it closes an idle client, the server sends `{"ok": false, "error": "connection idle too long; closing it"}` instead of the raw OS error text (which is `WouldBlock` on Unix and `TimedOut` on Windows).
- The timeout is a parameter of `accept_loop`/`serve`, so the test can use 200 ms.

**Persistent clients** (`crates/mcp/src/backend.rs`)
The issue asks for an idle policy that works with persistent clients. Our own one is `cadcraft-cli mcp --connect`: it keeps one connection open between tool calls. Without a change there, the first call after 10 quiet minutes would go into the closed socket. A mutating call would then fail with "may or may not have been applied", or read the idle notice as its reply. Before each call, `Remote` now does a non-blocking peek on its connection. If the app closed the connection or sent something unasked, the client opens a new connection and does not use the old one. A live idle connection is reused as before.

**Docs**: `docs/control-protocol.md` gives the 16-connection limit, the 10-minute idle close and the notice line, and says that the MCP bridge reconnects by itself.

**Tests**
- `idle_connections_release_their_slot`: 16 clients connect and send nothing. After the 200 ms deadline, a new client is served, and an idle client…

title: Table commands reject a malformed handle instead of using the selected table (#934)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #934.

The table editing commands (`table.set`, `table.insertrow`/`deleterow`/`insertcol`/`deletecol`, `table.merge`/`unmerge`, `table.cellstyle`, `table.break`, `datalink`, ...) resolve their table through `edit()` in `cmd/table.rs`. It turned a `handle` it could not read (`"zzz"`, `-1`, `true`, ...) into "no handle" and edited the selected table. `tableexport` had its own copy of the same lookup (`table_handle` in `cmd/table/cells.rs`), so it exported the selected table instead.

- The lookup is now one helper, `table_handle` in `cmd/table.rs`, used by both `edit()` and `tableexport`. It does what the shared `targets()` resolver in `cmd/mod.rs` has done since #330: a present `handle` that is not a hex string or an unsigned number is an error (``invalid parameters for `table.set`: `handle`: "zzz" is not an object handle (a hex string such as "1A2")``). The selected table is used only when `handle` is missing or `null`.
- Valid hex and numeric handles, and the selection fallback when no handle is given, work as before.

Test: `tests/table_malformed_handle.rs` selects a table, then sends `table.set` and `tableexport` with six malformed handles (bad strings, a negative number, a bool, an array). Each must fail with the "is not an object handle" error and leave the cell unchanged. Then it checks that an explicit valid handle and an omitted handle (the selection) still edit and export the table. Without the fix, the first `table.set` succeeds and edits the selected table.

title: ARRAYEDIT: a rejected request no longer keeps its earlier changes (#933)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #933.

`run_arrayedit` applies a compound request step by step: reset, then replace, then rebase, then the counts and spacings. A later step could fail after an earlier one had already changed the drawing. For example, `reset: true` with `levels: 0` cleared the replacements and then failed on the count. Another example: `replace` with bad `items` left the new replacement block behind. `Session::execute` restores the drawing only after a panic, not after an ordinary `Err`.

The fix: `run_arrayedit` takes a snapshot of the drawing (a cheap `Arc` clone) and runs the old body, now `arrayedit_steps`. On any error it puts the snapshot back. `boundary` in `hatch.rs` already restores a refused call the same way. The restored drawing is the same `Arc` that `execute` saved, so a rejected request also records no undo step and does not bump the revision. Requests that succeed behave as before.

Test: `rejected_arrayedit_request_leaves_the_drawing_unchanged` in `crates/engine/tests/assoc_array.rs` covers both cases from the issue. It checks the replacement count, the block table and the entity count after each rejected request. Without the fix, the reset-plus-`levels: 0` case loses the replacement and the bad-`items` case leaves an extra `*U` block.

title: Release a closed drawing's Lisp state on CLOSE and CLOSEALL (#932)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #932.

CLOSE and CLOSEALL removed the drawing from `Session::docs` but left its Lisp environment (globals, open `LispFile` buffers, `entdel` references, caches) and its startup bookkeeping in `LispState`, keyed by the closed drawing's UID, for the rest of the session.

- `run_close` now reads the drawing's UID before removing it and calls the new `Session::lisp_forget(uid)`, which drops that drawing's environment and its `autoloaded` entry. This runs after `s.cancel()`, so a routine waiting for input in that drawing has already been aborted and its environment put back before it is forgotten.
- `run_closeall` calls `Session::lisp_forget_all()`, which clears every environment and the `autoloaded` set.
- Session-wide state stays: APPLOAD'd files (`LispState::files`) and `acad_loaded` are not touched, as the issue asks.

Test: `lisp::tests::closing_drawings_releases_their_lisp_state` sets a variable in three drawings, closes an inactive one, then the active one, and checks that only the closed drawings' environments and startup entries are gone and the remaining drawing still sees its variable; then CLOSEALL clears all environments and startup entries while an APPLOAD'd file stays. Without the fix the environment count stays at 3 after the first close.

title: Lisp: CLOSE reports a failed file write and keeps the buffered output (#931)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #931.

`CLOSE` on an output stream removed the stream, then wrote its buffer with `write_text_file`, which ignored both the open and the `write_all` error. A routine got `nil` as if the file was saved, and the buffered output was gone.

## Changes
- `write_text_file` now returns `std::io::Result<()>` (the wasm stub returns `Ok(())`; on wasm `OPEN` never returns a write stream anyway, because `can_write` is false there).
- `CLOSE` turns a failed open or write into a Lisp error, `cannot write file <path>: <OS error>`, so `*error*` and `vl-catch-all-apply` see it.
- On failure the stream goes back into the open-files table with its buffer, so the output is not lost and `CLOSE` can be retried (for example after the routine frees the path). A successful `CLOSE` still returns `nil`, as before.

Not changed: staged replacement (write to a temp file, then rename) for `"w"` streams, which the issue lists as something to consider. That is a separate design choice and is left to the maintainers.

## Test
`close_reports_a_failed_write_and_keeps_the_stream` opens a directory as a `"w"` stream (a directory cannot be opened for writing on any desktop OS), writes a line and checks that `CLOSE` returns the error, and that a second `CLOSE` reports the same error rather than "bad argument" (the stream is still open). Without the fix the first `CLOSE` returns `nil` and the test fails.

title: Blocking LISP runs count steps across input waits toward the cap (#930)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #930.

A blocking LISP run (a programmatic call) is meant to stop after `BLOCKING_CAP` steps. Before this change, `lisp_drive` charged steps only when a slice ran out (`Need::Yield`), and charged a flat `SLICE` for it. A routine that reached `getint`/`getpoint`/… (`Need::Get`) or a resumable `Need::Pause` before its slice ran out was answered and resumed without any steps being counted, because `Machine::run` starts a new counter every time. So `(while t (getint))` in a blocking run never stopped.

Changes:
- `Machine::run` records how many steps it actually ran (`last_steps`, without the one past the budget that never ran).
- `lisp_drive` adds those steps to `run.steps` after every outcome, and checks the cap on every `Wait` outcome (Get, Pause and Yield), so resumptions after input count too. A run that finishes or errors is not stopped at the end; the error message is the same as before.
- The cap moves into `Limits` (`blocking_steps`, default `BLOCKING_CAP`), like the existing `cells` and `string_bytes` limits, so a test can use a small one.
- Non-blocking (interactive) runs are unchanged: they wait for the user, which is not a runaway.

Test: `blocking_input_waits_count_toward_the_step_cap` sets the cap to 10 000 and checks that `(while t (getint))` stops with "routine stopped after 10000 steps", and that a finite run with 10 `getint` calls still finishes.

title: Region: test very long segments against every segment so no crossing is missed (#929)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #929.

`build()` in `crates/geom/src/region.rs` finds segment crossings with a uniform grid. A segment whose bounding box covers more than 4096 cells was registered only in a sampled subset of its cells, with a stride of `(span / 64)`. A short segment that crossed it in an unsampled cell never shared a cell with it. The pair was never tested, the long segment was not split there, and region/hatch boundary discovery could miss that boundary.

Change: very long segments are no longer put in the grid. They go into a separate list, and each one is tested against every other segment. The pair test moved into a small `split_pair` helper that both loops use. Pairs are still deduplicated through `tested`, and the existing 20M-pair cap still applies, so hostile input returns `None` as before instead of silently skipping pairs. Long-long pairs are covered by the same loop.

Short segments go through the grid exactly as before.

Test: `long_segment_crossing_in_unsampled_cell_is_split` builds a diagonal across the drawing plus 17,000 short filler segments, so the grid has 131x131 cells and the old stride is 2. A short segment then crosses the diagonal in cell (1, 1), which the old sampling skipped. The test asserts the crossing becomes a graph vertex with 4 edges. Without the fix, no vertex exists at the crossing and the test fails.

title: Geometry: circle intersection judges tangency against the smaller circle, so a small circle crossing a huge one gives two points (#926)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #926.

`circle_circle` measured the chord from `c1` and treated every normalized `h2 <= 1e-12` as a tangency. When a small circle crosses a much larger one (radii 1e7 and 1, centres 1e7 apart), the half-chord seen from the large circle is a difference of nearly equal numbers and its square falls below that fixed threshold. The function returned one chord-foot point instead of the two intersections.

Changes in `crates/geom/src/intersect.rs`:
- The chord is measured from the smaller circle, so `h2` stays well conditioned. When the arguments are swapped internally the direction is reversed and the result order is restored, so the output order still depends only on the argument order, as before.
- The tangency threshold scales with the smaller circle (`1e-12 * rs²`), with a floor for the rounding error in the chord-foot distance (`8 * EPSILON * rs / ds`). Without that floor, true tangencies between very different circles would round to zero or two points.

Tests (`crates/geom/src/tests.rs`):
- `small_circle_crossing_a_huge_circle_gives_two_hits`: radii 1e7 and 1 with centres 1e7 apart give two hits in both argument orders, each lying on both circles within 1e-6. On `main` this returns a single point, so the test fails there.
- In the same test, external and internal tangency of the same pair (centres 1e7 ± 1 apart) still gives exactly one point at the touch point, in both orders.

The existing tests are unchanged: `circle_circle_hits`, the tiny (1e-9) and huge (1e160) secant tests, and the randomized property tests (points on both circles, symmetry, closed-form agreement). Equal-radius pairs take the same path as before.

title: Share the block bounds cache with DIMENSION blocks so nested dimensions do not expand exponentially (#924)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #924.

`bounds_in` in `crates/doc/src/extents.rs` already measures the contents of an INSERT's block once per block name and depth (#255, #706). The DIMENSION branch walked its block's entities directly and never used that cache, so dimension blocks that reference other dimension blocks were expanded once per reference: work grew exponentially with the nesting depth, bounded only by `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH`.

The INSERT cache lookup is now a small helper, `block_content_bounds`, and the DIMENSION branch calls it too. Both branches already measured block contents the same way (visible entities, at `depth + 1`, in block coordinates), so they can share cache entries. The coordinate handling stays as it was: INSERT still applies its transform and array offsets, and DIMENSION still adds its block contents untransformed. The `depth < MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH` check for DIMENSION is unchanged. With the cache, the work is at most one pass over each definition per depth, so I did not add the separate work budget the issue suggests.

Test: `nested_dimension_blocks_do_not_expand_exponentially` builds 15 levels of dimension blocks with six dimensions each pointing at the next level, and a line at the bottom. Without the fix, extents would need about 6^15 visits and the test hangs. With the fix, it finishes at once and the extents still reach the line at the bottom.

title: Cap HATCH spline edge degree at 10 like the SPLINE reader (#923)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #923.

The DXF reader took a HATCH spline edge's degree (group 94) as-is, up to 100000, and then tessellated it. The cost of each basis evaluation grows with the square of the degree, so one crafted edge could keep the import busy for a long time. The ordinary SPLINE entity reader already clamps its degree (group 71) to `1..=10`.

**Change** (`crates/io/src/dxf_read.rs`): the HATCH spline edge now clamps group 94 to `1..=10`, the same as the SPLINE reader. The rest works as it does for SPLINE:
- If the knot vector was written for the original degree, it no longer matches, so `is_valid()` fails and the edge is rebuilt with `Spline::from_control(control, 10)`, the same fallback SPLINE uses.
- If the edge has no usable knots, it goes through the same `from_control` fallback with the capped degree. Before this change, that fallback only limited the degree to the control point count.

The other places that set a spline degree (the `spline` command's `degree` parameter, `draw2`, and the interactive Degree prompt) already limit it to 1..10. This was the only uncapped one.

**Test** (`hatch_spline_edge_caps_degree_like_spline`): a degree-12 HATCH spline edge with 13 control points, read twice. The first copy has a 26-knot vector that is valid for degree 12. The second has no knots, so it uses the fallback. In both cases the hatch extents must equal those of the degree-10 curve over the same control points. Without the fix, both copies come out as the degree-12 Bezier curve, which has a different peak, and the test fails.

title: Fix grid index span overflow with a very large view (#920)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #920.

`draw_grid` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`) cast the view bounds divided by the grid spacing to `i64` and then checked `(x1 - x0) < 2000`. With a very large finite view, `adaptive` stops after 40 steps, so the casts saturate at `i64::MIN` / `i64::MAX`. The subtraction then overflows: a panic in a debug build, and in a release build a wrapped negative span that passes the guard and starts an enormous loop.

The index math is now in a small `grid_index_ranges` helper. It computes each span with `checked_sub` and returns `None` (no grid lines, as before for over 2000 lines) when the span overflows or reaches 2000. The drawing loops are unchanged.

Only the orthogonal grid had this bug. The isometric grid (`snap::iso::grid_lines`) already checks the span as a float before the cast, and it is not changed.

## Tests

New `grid_index_ranges_survive_extreme_views` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`):
- a `±1e300` view gives `None`; the old inline arithmetic overflows (panics in a test build) on this view;
- a normal `-5..5 × 0..10` view with spacing 1 still gives `((-5, 5), (0, 10))`.

No Rust toolchain was available locally, so the tests were not run here. CI will run them.

title: Autosave no longer writes the old host as recovery when the Block Editor's changes can't be composed (#918)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #918.

`DocState::recovery_drawing` swallowed the error from `BlockEdit::compose` (for example when the edited block now refers to itself) and returned the old host drawing. Autosave then wrote that host as the recovery file and marked the editor and host as covered, so the unsaved Block Editor changes were never retried and a crash lost them.

- `recovery_drawing` now returns `Result<Arc<Drawing>>` and passes the compose error through, the same error BSAVE already reports for this case.
- `Autosaver::plan` skips the write when composition fails and leaves its markers (`written`, `host`, `since`) unchanged, so the drawing stays due and the next pass tries again. Once the changes can be composed, they are written.
- Outside the Block Editor, and in the editor without unsaved changes, nothing changes.

Tests:
- `autosave::a_block_editor_that_cannot_be_composed_is_not_autosaved_as_the_old_host`: an unsaved self-reference in the editor writes nothing on later passes, the drawing is still due (`next_due`), and after the reference is removed the next pass writes the recovery file. Without the fix, the first due pass writes the old host.
- `block_editor::a_file_save_writes_the_drawing_outside_the_editor` updated for the new return type (valid edit still composes into the block).

title: Keep replacement blocks of an array that shrinks, so growing it back restores them (#916)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #916.

An associative array keeps its replaced items in `ArrayParams::replaced` even when they fall outside the item grid, so growing the array back brings them back. Two places decided whether such a replacement block was still in use without looking at that list, and deleted it:

- **ARRAYEDIT** (`drop_unused` in `cmd/array/edit.rs`): after a rebuild it already kept a block named as some array's `source`; it now also keeps a block that some array's `replaced` list names. Before, replace item 3 of a 3-item array, set 2 columns, set 3 columns again: the new array block referred to a block that no longer existed and the replaced item was lost.
- **PURGE** (`used_blocks` in `cmd/blocks/purge.rs`): the reachability walk only followed block references, so after shrinking the array, PURGE Blocks removed the same replacement block. It now also follows the source and replacement blocks an array block's parameters name, like `drop_unused` does.

RESet is unchanged: it clears the replacement list on purpose and still removes the blocks it no longer needs.

Tests (`crates/engine/tests/assoc_array.rs`):
- `shrinking_an_array_keeps_replacements_outside_the_grid`: replace, shrink, grow back; the replaced item's geometry and the other items are back.
- `purge_keeps_replacements_outside_a_shrunk_array`: replace, shrink, PURGE Blocks, grow back; the replaced item's geometry is back.

Both fail without the fix: the grown array refers to a deleted block.

title: CLI --save, convert and sample write through a staged file so a failed write keeps the previous drawing (#912)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #912.

`export_framed` (used by `run --save` and `convert`) and `sample` in `apps/cadcraft-cli/src/main.rs` wrote the output with `std::fs::write(out, ...)`, which truncates the destination first. If the write failed or the process was interrupted, the previous drawing was already gone or half-written.

Both now go through a new `write_atomic` helper:

- the bytes go to a uniquely named file in the same folder (`.<name>.<pid>.<n>.tmp`, opened with `create_new`, so it never reuses or clobbers an existing file; a name clash just tries the next number);
- the file is flushed with `sync_all` and then renamed over the destination;
- on any failure before the rename the staging file is removed and the destination is left as it was.

These are the only two places in the CLI that write a file. Serialization still happens before anything touches the disk, as before. The engine's own save helper (`cmd/file.rs` `store`, fixed `.cadcraft-tmp` name) is the separate issue #540 and is not changed here.

## Tests

Two unit tests in `apps/cadcraft-cli/src/main.rs`:
- `write_atomic_replaces_file_and_leaves_no_staging_files`: creates a file, overwrites it, checks the new content and that only the target is left in the folder;
- `write_atomic_failure_keeps_destination_and_cleans_up`: makes the final rename fail (the destination is a directory) and checks the destination is untouched and no staging file is left behind.

A mid-write I/O failure can't be injected portably without a mock, so the failure test fails the last step (the rename) instead, which covers the same "keep the original, clean up" path.

No Rust toolchain was available locally, so the tests were not run here. CI will run them.

title: SpaceMouse: calibrate devices that are silent at rest, fix the pan Y direction, zoom on push/pull only
author: alexanderalber
body:
Follow-up to #650, tested on real hardware (#623): classic SpaceNavigator 046d:c626, Windows 11, no 3DxWare.

**Calibration never finished on a device that is silent at rest.** The SpaceNavigator sends no reports while the cap rests. Measured over 40 s: `[0 ×17, 38, 125 ×8, 16, 0 ×14]` reports per second, all axes exactly 0 when it starts again. The rest calibration waits for 16 resting samples in 400 ms, so it finished only by chance, from a light touch, and used that touch as the bias. Now 300 ms without an axis report counts as rest at zero (`Filter::quiet`). Devices that stream at rest still calibrate through the existing window. My original measurement in #623 claimed the device streams at rest, which was wrong. Sorry.

**Other fixes from the device test:**
- Pan Y was inverted: HID +Y points towards the user, the drawing's +Y away from them.
- Twist no longer zooms: next to push/pull it felt odd on the device (I had suggested it in #623).
- Zoom direction reversed: lifting the cap zooms in, pressing it zooms out. Having tried both on the device, this one is clearly more natural to me. "Reverse zoom direction" still flips it.
- The 3D Mouse dialog no longer blocks navigation. Other dialogs still do.
- Default pan sensitivity 0.8 → 1.2 (felt slow on the device; taste, drop if you disagree).

title: Input: PointInput layer; LINE resolves deferred TAN first point from …
author: william-wwh
body:
Fixes the root cause behind #788.

## Problem

`Input::Point` carried a bare `Vec2`, so the form the user typed
(absolute, `@dx,dy`, `@d<a`, direct distance, pick, snap) was lost by the
time a command saw it. `#788` worked around this with `Session.last_polar`,
a stopgap that held only the one piece of semantics `LINE` needed and sat
outside the type system.

## Fix

`Input::Point` now carries a `PointInput`:

```rust
pub enum PointInput {
    Absolute(Vec2),
    RelativeCartesian { at: Vec2, delta: Vec2 },
    RelativePolar { at: Vec2, dist: f64, angle: f64 },
    DirectDistance { base: Vec2, dist: f64, dir: Vec2 },
    Picked(Vec2),
    Snapped { at: Vec2, mode: u32 },
}
```

Commands that don't care about the form call `.point()`, which is exactly
the old `Vec2`. Commands that can use the form match on the variant.

`prompt::parse_point_input` returns the right variant from the typed text;
`parse_point_with` becomes a thin wrapper
(`parse_point_input(...).map(|pi| pi.point())`).

When the first point of `LINE` is a deferred TAN and the next is `@d<a`,
`LineM::input` matches `PointInput::RelativePolar` and computes the exact
tangent point from the direction. `Session.last_polar` and
`prompt::parse_polar_text` are deleted — #788's stopgap is gone.

## Update (2026-10-18): Command layer compatibility fix

During testing, several commands (e.g. in `draw2.rs`, `array.rs`, `plotters.rs`, `annotate.rs`) were only matching `Input::Point(PointInput::Picked(p))`. Typed keyboard coordinates (`Absolute`, `RelativePolar`, etc.) and LISP-generated points were being ignored, breaking backward compatibility for scripts and MCP.

This is now fixed:
- Commands destructure `Input::Point(pi)` and call `pi.point()` regardless of how the coordinate was entered.
- The test suite imports and constructs `PointInput` variants correctly.
- `cargo test --workspace` passes (0 failures).

## Update (2026-10-18): Every PointInput variant is now used

`DirectDistance` and `Snapped` were defined…

title: Index entity storage and batch selected deletions
author: PedroGuille
body:
Large selections repeatedly search entity chunks and copy the same chunk while deleting its objects. This splits the storage/index changes from #839 onto upstream main at `e707ab4`.

- Index chunk positions and entity slots for direct handle lookup, retaining copy-on-write undo snapshots.
- Delete selected objects once per affected chunk in ERASE, CUT and keyboard Delete. Preserve surviving draw order and locked-layer handling.
- Index associated dimensions per chunk so the post-command update pass skips unrelated entities. Keep the index current through replacement, mutation, deletion and reordering.

Review follow-up: the original process-global hit-test cache is omitted. Main's incremental spatial index and #701 intersection pruning remain in place. DRAWORDER keeps its existing algorithm for every selection size; the 256-object branch is omitted.

Validation: all six local CI gates completed successfully. New tests cover multi-chunk deletion, duplicate/missing handles, surviving order, empty middle chunks, independent snapshots, and association-index updates across editing and reordering.

Independent of the other two replacement branches. Split from #839.

title: Reuse unchanged model geometry and GPU buffers
author: PedroGuille
body:
A small edit currently rebuilds and uploads the model's complete geometry. This splits the render/GPU work from #839 onto upstream main at `e707ab4` and adapts it to the background view rebuilding added by #903.

- Cache model display lists by copy-on-write entity chunk identity. Rebuild changed chunks and reuse unchanged ones while preserving complete primitive order.
- Reuse per-chunk CPU mesh data and GPU buffers, keyed by geometry, origin, background and lineweight display.
- Use a map lookup for uploaded parts, avoiding the original per-part linear search.
- Keep wipeout barriers in the complete scene's order, rather than treating each chunk as an independent drawing.
- Retain every entity and the full display-list bounds. The original off-screen entity culling is omitted.
- Use the same stable vertex origin in the worker and drawing callback so a completed background build is not immediately uploaded again on the UI thread.
- Invalidate dependent geometry when fonts are replaced or preferences change. Use bounded second-chance eviction for glyph outlines and meshes.

The geometry cache is limited to 32 MiB and 4,096 parts; the CPU mesh cache to 32 MiB and uploaded buffer retention to 64 MiB. Layouts, plotting and oversized scenes use the full builder. The existing cancellation and background GPU upload paths remain in use. The original recent-tab scene cache and selection snapshot changes are omitted to keep this review focused.

Validation: all six local CI gates passed. New checks cover one-chunk edits, undo, cancellation, symbol and transparency changes, full bounds, GPU byte equivalence across wipeout boundaries, and reuse of unaffected meshes when extents grow. The cached display list is compared with the full builder.

Independent of the storage and DXF branches. Split from #839.

title: Avoid cloning DXF tag payloads during file loading
author: PedroGuille
body:
The DXF reader copies parsed tags into section vectors and then copies them again into entity records. Borrow section and record tag ranges instead, retaining owned data only where it must survive parsing.

This splits the remaining file-loading work from #839 onto upstream main at `e707ab4`. Main already implements background opening through #797, so its worker, opening indicator and startup behavior are retained. The earlier replacement background opener and startup changes are omitted.

- Add borrowed section/record views and a read-only section interface.
- Preserve the public owned section/record APIs as wrappers.
- Use borrowed views in the drawing, image, multiline and foreign-data readers.
- Keep foreign payloads owned for roundtrip preservation, including ACDSDATA.
- Preserve current main's multiple ENTITIES sections and skipped-record accounting.

Validation: formatting, strict native Clippy, the complete workspace tests, attribution and layering checks passed. The WebAssembly gate was checked separately after clearing stale cross-checkout build artifacts. New tests verify borrowed payload ranges and handling of empty records and unterminated sections. Existing roundtrip, binary DXF, damaged-file, multiple-section and ACIS data-store tests passed.

Independent of the other two branches. Split from #839.

title: Select: dimensions and block references are not picked along their bounding box edges
author: codyvogt
body:
## What
Hovering (or clicking) in empty space could highlight a dimension or block reference far from it. Reported on a survey drawing: the cursor lined up with an aligned dimension's two definition points, well away from its text and lines, highlighted the whole dimension. Other spots did too.

**Cause:** `hit_polylines` gave dimensions, block references and multileaders their drawn geometry **plus the outline of their bounding box**. That code dates from the first skeleton commit. The box reaches out to a dimension's definition points (or a block's farthest object), so its four edges were invisible pick lines through empty space.

## Change
- These objects are now picked on what they draw, and on their text inside its box (`in_text`, as #807 does for dimensions and multileaders). The box outline is only kept for something that draws nothing but text.
- **Block references:** attributes (multiline ones by their text layout) and the text of their block are now picked inside their boxes. Before, block text was only reachable through those same box edges.

## Checked on the reported drawing
A pick map around the dimension, with a 2-unit aperture as at the reported zoom:
- **Before:** full-width rows along the top and bottom box edges and a column down the right edge picked it, including the line level with the two definition points.
- **After:** only the text box, the leader and the arrows pick it.

## Tests
`engine/tests/pick_text.rs::bounding_box_edges_pick_nothing`:
- the middle of a dimension's bottom box edge (between its definition points) picks nothing, while its dimension line still does;
- an empty spot on a block reference's box edge picks nothing;
- its line, its block's text and its attribute still pick it.

The test fails without the fix. The whole engine suite passes; clippy `--no-deps` shows nothing in `select.rs`.

author: Silvertree2010

`draw_crosshair` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`) made every arm `height × CURSORSIZE / 100` long. At 100 that is the height of the drawing area. New `crosshair_reach(rect, percent)` gives the arm lengths. Below 100 they are what they were (`height × percent / 100`, at least 12 points). title: Block reference grips: none on locked or invisible attributes; a moved multiline attribute moves its text
author: codyvogt
body:
## What
Reported while testing a dynamic block: in one visibility state, dragging what looked like the block's position grip moved the grip, but the label stayed put. That grip was the reference's ordinary **attribute grip**, and two things were wrong with it:

1. **Every attribute had a grip**, including ones locked in position (Lock position, kept since #876) and invisible ones. AutoCAD gives neither a grip.
2. **Dragging a multiline attribute's grip** moved its position (`text.insert`) but not its multiline text, which is what draws and saves. So the grip moved and the text didn't.

## Change
- `Insert::grip_attribs()`: the attributes that have a grip of their own (shown, not locked), with their index. `EntityKind::grips` and the grip stretch both use it, so grip numbers stay consistent.
- The stretch also moves a multiline attribute's text (`transform_multiline`).

## Tests
`engine/tests/attrib_modes.rs::only_shown_unlocked_attributes_have_grips_and_a_multiline_one_moves_its_text`:
- a block with a free, a locked, an invisible and a multiline attribute gets grips for the free and multiline ones only;
- dragging the multiline one moves its text.

It fails without the fix (grips at 100, 110, 120, 130). The engine and doc suites and clippy `--no-deps` on doc pass.

title: Read the Arabic labels right to left (the visual-order pass for #798's catalog)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
Follow-up to #798: the merged Arabic catalog hands its labels to egui's run-by-run layout, and egui 0.36 lays those runs left to right with no bidi over them (its text code still carries `TODO(emilk): heed bidi characters`) — so every multi-word label read with its words in reverse order: each word shaped correctly, but drawn at the wrong end of the line. The other Crafting Apps' Arabic PRs grew the same pass this week after their reviewers confirmed the behaviour (lightcraft #1360, vectorcraft #1532, effectcraft #1150, filmcraft #1469, craft-launcher #258, wordcraft #1042, deckcraft #256, gridcraft #721, soundcraft #337, photocraft #4569, artcraft #2229).

`i18n/bidi.rs` reorders a translation into visual order when it is looked up (UAX #9 with an RTL base via unicode-bidi, cached per label so each string is reordered exactly once): the runs left to right as a right-to-left reader meets them, the characters inside each run in logical order because harfrust reverses the run itself, and brackets mirrored — the `BidiMirroring.txt` pairs, guillemets included. Curly brackets are deliberately left alone, and each `{placeholder}` rides through the pass as one character, so it can be neither split, reversed nor mirrored and the fill always finds it. What a user types keeps its logical order — only catalog lookups go through the pass; `tr`, `tr_menu` and the named-placeholder `format` all keep their signatures.

Honest limits, same as everywhere the pass landed: the shell's chrome keeps its left-to-right layout, and a label long enough to wrap still wraps from its visual end.

title: Faster CJK-heavy drawings: per-thread font caches, offscreen glyphs left out (#666, #662)
author: aldozar
body:
Addresses #666 and #662.

The reporter's drawings are around 5 MB and full of Chinese text and annotations, and can't be shared. So I measured a synthetic stand-in: 3.8 MB of DXF with 24,000 TEXT and 2,500 MTEXT in Chinese (SHX with a big font, and a TrueType style), plus 30,000 lines. Measured on macOS, Apple silicon, release build.

**1. Text builds were waiting on global locks.** Display lists are built on all cores. But every text looked up its font, and every character its font lacks (every character of a CJK text) looked up its fallback face, glyph outline and glyph mesh. All of these went through shared tables behind a `Mutex`/`RwLock`. A profile of building the MTEXT spent most of its samples in `__psynch_mutexwait` and the lock in `ttf::outline`, not in shaping. Font lookups, fallback faces, FONTALT, glyph outlines and glyph meshes now have per-thread caches in front of the shared ones. A generation counter empties them when a font is registered or FONTALT/FONTFALLBACK changes.

| display list build (fit) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 24,000 TEXT | 106 ms | 40 ms |
| 2,500 MTEXT | 226 ms | 72 ms |
| whole drawing | 335 ms | 103 ms |

**2. Zoomed in, every glyph of every text was drawn each frame (#666's laggy crosshair).** The list doesn't depend on the view, so at higher zooms every glyph in the drawing was filled at that zoom's detail, on screen or not. The GPU then drew all of it on every repaint, which means every mouse move. On screen, glyphs outside the area being looked at are now left out, as hatch patterns already are. The canvas already builds again (on its worker) when the view leaves that area, with half a view of margin on each side. Plots and exports keep every glyph.

| triangles in the screen list | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 4× | 9.2 M | 5.8 M |
| 16× | 11.2 M | 0.44 M |
| 64× | 19.0 M | 45 k |

Not the cause, measured: hover picking and object snaps cost microseconds per mouse move on this drawing. On 6,000 dimensions with Chine…

title: DWG: classes keep the C++ names the file gives them (a rotate action made dynamic blocks static)
author: codyvogt
body:
## What
A dynamic block with a **rotate action** stopped being dynamic in a DWG that CADCraft saved, even with nothing changed. AutoCAD then reports `IsDynamicBlock = false` and no dynamic properties.

**Cause:** the DWG bridge (acadrust) keeps its own built-in C++ class names over the file's CLASS entries. Its name for the rotate action's class is `AcDbBlockRotationAction`, while AutoCAD's own files call it `AcDbBlockRotateAction`. AutoCAD drops objects of a class it doesn't know, so the rotate action disappeared from the evaluation graph and the block was no longer dynamic. CADCraft's DXF output was fine, because it keeps the CLASS entries as read.

I compared every class in a set of AutoCAD drawings against acadrust's table. The only other difference was letter case: `AcDbBlkRefObjectContextData` vs `AcDbBlkrefObjectContextData`.

## Change
`crates/dwg`: before writing the DWG, each class takes the C++ name the DXF's CLASSES section gives it (`file_class_names`, `use_file_class_names`). The class order is kept, since a custom object's type code is its class's position. A drawing whose classes already agree is untouched.

## Checked with AutoCAD
Driven through its COM API on copies; the company drawings stay private.
- **A block with rotate, flip and move actions**, saved as DWG by CADCraft:
  - before: `IsDynamicBlock = false`, no properties, because the rotate action had been dropped;
  - after: dynamic, with Angle1, Flip state1 and Position1 as in the original.
- **A block with visibility, lookup and stretch actions:** still dynamic, with the same values.

## Tests
`cadcraft-dwg`: `native::class_names::the_files_class_names_win` checks that:
- the file's names replace acadrust's built-in ones;
- only the CLASSES section is read;
- the class order stays the same.

The io suite (DWG round trips) passes; clippy `--no-deps` on dwg is clean.

title: Save: keep the previous drawing as .bak (ISAVEBAK), replace files durably (part of #540)
author: aldozar
body:
Fixes #911. Part of #540: the `.bak` and durable-save items of its Phase 0. See [the breakdown in the issue](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/issues/540#issuecomment-6150746546) for what already existed.

**`.bak` on save (ISAVEBAK)**
- Saving over a DWG/DXF/DWT first copies the file to `<name>.bak` beside it, as AutoCAD does (`Plan.dwg` → `Plan.bak`). It is on by default.
- The copy is streamed, not read into memory, and written atomically.
- A file that doesn't start like a drawing is not copied, and the `.bak` already there is kept. That covers an empty or truncated file, or a file another program overwrote. This is the backup invariant from craft-libs#22.
- `ISAVEBAK` (0/1) is a profile setting like SAVETIME. It is kept with the autosave settings, available in `options`/`setvar`, and shown in the Options dialog as "Create backup copy with each save" (with uk and es translations).
- If the backup can't be written, nothing is saved and the error says so. Exports (PDF/PNG/SVG) never make a backup.

**Durable replace**
- The engine's `store` wrote `<path>.cadcraft-tmp` and renamed it, with no fsync. It now uses `craft_atomic::atomic_write` (craft-libs#16, already merged): a unique staging file beside the target, `F_FULLFSYNC` on macOS (plain fsync where a share refuses it), rename retries on Windows, and a directory sync on Unix.
- A crash or power loss right after a save now leaves the old file or the new one, never a truncated one.
- `craft-atomic` comes from craft-libs at a pinned rev, like `craft-ui`.
- #982 does the same for the CLI's own writes (#912). It doesn't touch the engine's `store`, so the two don't overlap.

**Tests** (`crates/engine/tests/save_backup.rs`)
- Three saves rotate the backup correctly: the `.bak` is always the previous save, and only the drawing and its `.bak` are left in the folder (no staging files).
- A drawing truncated by another program doesn't replace the good `.bak`. `ISAVEBAK 0` leaves the backup alone.
- `looks_like_drawing…

title: feat(engine): durable saves and .bak backup of the previous version (part of #540)
author: filforce95
body:
Part of #540 (phase 0: atomic writes). Does not close it.

## What changes
- New `engine::durable` module (native builds only):
  - `write_atomic`: stage in a temp file beside the target, `fsync`, rename over the target, flush the folder on Unix. A failed write removes the staging file and leaves the old content.
  - `backup_previous`: before a drawing is overwritten, keep the current version as `<name>.bak`, but only if it still reads as a drawing. A damaged or empty file never replaces a good backup.
- Saving (`store` in `cmd/file.rs`) makes the `.bak` for drawing files (DXF/DWG/DWT, not SVG/PNG/PDF exports) and then writes durably. A backup that cannot be made is logged and never stops the save.
- Autosave (`.sv$` files) uses the same durable write.

## Not included (rest of #540 phase 0)
- An `ISAVEBAK`-style switch to turn the `.bak` off (it is always on for now).
- The command journal between snapshots and a lossless snapshot format; both need design agreement first.

## Tests
- Unit tests in `durable.rs` (atomic replace, failed write, backup validity rules).
- `tests/save_backup.rs`: save keeps the previous version as `.bak`, a damaged file keeps the good `.bak`, no staging files are left.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: fix(svg): read the T/t smooth-quadratic endpoint as an (x, y) pair (#944)
author: saadkhantareen
body:
Fixes one defect from #944: SVG path parsing of the smooth quadratic command.

## Summary

`parse_path` in `crates/io/src/svg_read.rs` gave `T` an arity of 1, grouping it with `H`/`V`. Per SVG 1.1 §8.3.8, `T`/`t` takes an (x, y) endpoint pair — and its handler already read `args[1]` as the endpoint's y. So for every `T` segment the y was read as 0, and the real y was re-parsed as another implicit `T` segment, adding a phantom curve and shifting the geometry that followed.

Example: `M0 5 Q5 0 10 5 T20 5` imported with the T endpoint at (20, 0) plus an extra segment to (5, 0), instead of ending at (20, 5).

## Changes

- `crates/io/src/svg_read.rs` — arity table only: `T` now reads 2 values, grouped with `M`/`L`; `H`/`V` unchanged. No other path command is affected; the remaining #944 items (cubic flushing, composite-Bezier knots, closure of mixed subpaths) are untouched and left for follow-ups.
- `crates/io/src/tests.rs` — new regression test `svg_path_smooth_quadratic_t_takes_an_xy_pair`, covering absolute `T` and relative `t`: it asserts the resulting spline's control points (start, endpoint, and count — no phantom segment). It fails on the old code (10 control points, endpoint (20, 10) in drawing coordinates) and passes with the fix.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p cadcraft-io` — all suites pass (83 lib tests + integration suites).
- `cargo fmt -p cadcraft-io -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-io --lib` — no warnings.
- The full workspace `cargo xtask ci` was not run; the change is confined to `cadcraft-io`.

title: SETVAR: check and list the hatch, array and multiline-style variables (U10)
author: flyboy-byte
body:
Seven header variables that commands already read (`HPASSOC`, `HPGAPTOL`, `HPISLANDDETECTION`, `HPORIGINMODE`, `HPSEPARATE`, `ARRAYASSOCIATIVITY`, `CMLSTYLE`) were missing from the SETVAR table in `crates/engine/src/sysvars/table.rs`. `GETVAR HPGAPTOL` said "unknown variable" until a first SETVAR, SETVAR stored anything without checking (`HPGAPTOL -5`, `HPORIGINMODE 99`, `HPASSOC banana`, even `CMLSTYLE X`, the current multiline style that MLSTYLE manages), and `SETVAR ?` did not list them. They now have the defaults the commands already use and range checks; `HPGAPTOL` is limited to 0–5000 (new `Kind::RealRange`), the same clamp `gap_tolerance` applies, and `CMLSTYLE` is read-only like `CPLOTSTYLE`. No command code changed. Follow-up to #799, same U10 row.

**Checked:** `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) passes locally on the final commit. Also tried in an app built from this branch over the control channel: the accepted and refused values above behave as described.

**Tests** (`crates/engine/tests/setvar_coverage.rs`): defaults, listing in `SETVAR ?`, refused values including hostile ones, the whole accepted range (also typed as a bare name), and that `HPASSOC` and `ARRAYASSOCIATIVITY` still reach HATCH and ARRAYRECT. With `table.rs` reverted to `main`, three of the six tests in that file fail; the "reach the commands" test passes either way and only guards that the commands keep honouring the values.

**Not covered:** the other ~800 AutoCAD variables (U10 stays open). `HPISLANDDETECTION` defaults to what HATCH uses today (0); not compared with real AutoCAD. Nothing tested on Windows or macOS. This and #847 both edit the `gaps.md` status line, so whichever merges second needs a one-line rebase.

title: Hatch: keep a pattern line's dash shift in step with a negative line offset
author: Tangpixel2296
body:
## Problem

Patterns read from DWG drawings whose pattern lines have a negative offset (delta y < 0), such as AR-CONC and AR-SAND, came apart: AR-CONC's small triangles were drawn as scattered, unrelated strokes instead of closed shapes.

The sweep in `crates/render/src/hatch.rs` draws pattern lines at y = k·|Δy| but gave line k a dash shift of k·Δx. With a negative Δy, the line at y = k·|Δy| is line −k of the pattern, so its dashes moved the wrong way along the line. Patterns with several families that have to meet (AR-CONC's triangles) no longer lined up.

## Change

The shift per swept line follows the sign of Δy: with Δy < 0, it is −Δx. Patterns with a positive offset are unchanged.

## Test

`a_negative_line_offset_draws_the_same_lines`: a family with (Δx, Δy) and the same family written with (−Δx, −Δy) describe the same lines, and they now draw the same dashes.

Checked against a real architectural DWG: AR-CONC renders as closed triangles, as it does in the program that wrote the file.

title: Large drawings: build only what the view shows, cull block contents, one primitive per hatch's dots
author: Tangpixel2296
body:
## Problem

On large drawings, every zoom band or pan out of the built area rebuilds the whole model space, whatever the view shows. #903 moved that rebuild off the UI thread, but the work itself still grows with the drawing, not with the view:

- a 170k-object survey plan takes 75–80 ms per build at every zoom level;
- a 40 MB architectural DWG takes about 450 ms per build, including when zoomed in 64× on a small area. Its site plan is a single block reference, drawn in full on one core, and its AR-SAND hatches make about 258k point primitives.

## Change

Four commits, each one usable on its own, all limited to screen builds. Plots, PDF/SVG exports and hit-testing build exactly what they built before.

1. **Build only what is near the view** (`015f3d8`)
   - `render::Options` gains `only: Option<Arc<Vec<u32>>>`.
   - The canvas fills it from the engine's cached spatial index (`spatial::near_view`) when the view touches less than 60 % of the space.
   - Background rebuilds query the index on the worker. Edits use it once a list exists.
2. **Block contents** (`7c6bfa9`)
   - The view window is brought into block coordinates and tested against bounds measured once per block definition and layer state (`blockcull.rs`, bounded cache). Entities outside the view are skipped.
   - Entities smaller than a pixel are drawn as a dot in their colour.
   - A top-level reference to a block with 512 or more entities to draw builds them on all cores (rayon), joined in drawing order.
3. **Hatch dots as one primitive** (`8e7825d`)
   - `Kind::Point` holds `verts[start..start+len]`, and every consumer draws all of the points: GPU and CPU canvas, highlight, raster, PDF, SVG and the viewport clip.
   - A hatch's pattern dots now go into one primitive instead of one per dot.
4. **Layer index per build** (`9a052d4`)
   - Layers are indexed once per build by lower-case name, instead of a linear, case-insensitive scan for each object (270 layers in the DWG above).
   - When two names diffe…

title: fix(engine): protect locked layers in property, table, block and array edits
author: PedroGuille
body:
Editing an object on a locked layer through Properties, a table command, BLOCK/-BLOCK or ARRAYEDIT currently changes or removes it. Mixed property/block selections can also modify unlocked objects before the protected source is checked.

Validate source locks before changing the drawing:
- Reject the whole `properties.set` selection before creating a destination layer or editing any object.
- Guard the shared table editor, covering cells, formulas, rows/columns, merges, cell styles, breaks and data-link edits.
- Validate every BLOCK/-BLOCK source before conversion or deletion. Keep `keep: "retain"` available because it copies the sources without changing them.
- Guard ARRAYEDIT's JSON, interactive and shared mutation paths before creating replacement blocks or temporary source objects.
- On ARRAYCLOSE, recheck the array before saving and every temporary source object that saving/discarding would remove. Refusal leaves the edit open so the user can unlock the layer and retry.

Uses the existing lock helper, including its REFEDIT working-set protection. Refused programmatic edits preserve the drawing, handle allocation, selection and undo/redo history. Interactive refusals leave the drawing and history unchanged. Valid unlocked edits and copying locked replacement sources remain supported.

Regression coverage: 13 tests across explicit handles, selection fallback, interactive commands, both mixed-selection orders, source-layer changes during array editing, existing redo steps, and successful undo/redo. On unmodified upstream main, 10 tests fail; all 13 pass with the fix.

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` passed all six gates (formatting, strict native Clippy, 2,023 workspace tests, asset attribution, dependency layering, and all 11 WebAssembly packages). Testing used synthetic drawings; the regression suite checks the complete drawing snapshot and history on refusal.

Fixes #936.

title: SVG import: name what was left out instead of dropping it silently (#627)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #627

#636 added SVG/SVGZ import, which covers what #627 asked for: shapes, paths, transforms, viewBox and units, Inkscape layers, SVGZ, and the Open dialog filter. One point from the issue was still missing: *"Unsupported elements are skipped with a warning, never a crash."* Text, raster images, `<use>` copies, `<style>` sheets and rounded rectangle corners were all dropped without a word, so a drawing could open with parts missing and no sign of it.

What this changes:
- The SVG reader counts what it leaves out and adds one note to `Drawing::read_notes`. That is the same channel DWG reading uses for records it skipped. OPEN echoes the note on the command line and returns it under `warnings`. For example: `SVG: CADCraft doesn't read these yet, so they were left out: 2 texts, 1 raster image, 2 `<use>` copies, 1 `<style>` sheet (its class rules aren't applied), 1 rectangle with rounded corners (drawn square)`.
- Content that isn't drawn isn't counted (anything inside `<defs>`, or hidden with `display:none`). A `<style>` sheet counts wherever it is, because its rules apply to the whole document.
- A file with nothing left out gets no note.
- FF14 in `docs/gaps.md` and the SVG row in `docs/file-format-parity.md` now mention the note.

The geometry fixes in #944, #945 and #946 (and their open PRs) are separate. This PR doesn't touch them.

Tests: `svg_left_out_content_is_noted` in `crates/io/src/tests.rs`. `cargo test -p cadcraft-io` passes, `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, and `cargo fmt` changes nothing. I didn't run the wasm build locally (no wasm32 std on this machine).

title: fix(canvas): a pick made while the mouse moves selects the object (fixes #1001)
author: filforce95
body:
Fixes #1001.

## Cause
egui reports a press that travels more than a few pixels before the button comes up as a drag, not a click. At an object-selection prompt (TRIM, STRETCH, MOVE, COPY, ERASE…) and with no command running, the canvas then opened a selection window at the press point and closed it at the release point. A quick click therefore selected nothing (window selection) or whatever a window the size of a smudge crossed (crossing selection).

Point prompts (LINE, RECTANGLE, CIRCLE, base points) were already fixed by #835; that fix is not in a release yet (v0.6.2 does not contain it), and it does not cover object-selection prompts, which is what was left.

## Change
- `canvas.rs`: a button released within `CLICK_SLOP_PX` (10 points, about PICKBOX) of where it went down is a click at the press point. A longer drag still selects with a window.

## Tests (`tests/rapid_clicks.rs`)
- A pick made while the mouse moves selects the object (no command running).
- The same at an object-selection prompt (ERASE, then Enter erases the picked line).
- A real drag still selects with a window.
- The first two fail without the change.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Drawing locks and WHOHAS: say when a drawing is open elsewhere (part of #540)
author: aldozar
body:
Part of #540: the "who has this drawing open" item of its Phase 0. It is independent of #1003 (`.bak` and durable save); the two merge cleanly in either order.

**What it does**
- While a drawing opened from a DWG/DXF/DWT file is open, the app keeps a lock file beside it, `.<file name>.cadcraft-lock`.
  - It is a small JSON file: user, computer, app instance and when the drawing was opened.
  - The file's modification time is the heartbeat, touched every minute. A lock not touched for five minutes is stale, the same rule autosave's instance locks use.
- **Opening a drawing someone else has open** shows a message on the command line and in the status bar, for example: `Plan.dwg is also open by maria on studio-pc, since 2026-10-13 17:13 UTC. Saving it here can overwrite their changes (or theirs yours).` The drawing opens anyway: **the lock only informs**, and their lock stays theirs.
- **Releasing.** A lock is released when its drawing closes, when it is saved under another name (the lock moves to the new file), and when the app exits. Only the instance holding a lock ever deletes it.
- **Taking over.** A stale lock (left by a crash) is taken over silently. If an app finds on its heartbeat that another instance took over its lock, for example after the machine slept past the stale time, it reports the new holder instead of touching the lock.
- **`WHOHAS`** (`{path?}`) reports the holder of the current drawing or of any file.
- **Wiring.** The locks run on the autosave tick (`Autosaver::tick`/`shutdown`), which already has an instance id and a per-frame call. Nothing runs on the web build.
- **Format.** CADCraft's own JSON, not AutoCAD's `.dwl`: we don't copy or read that format (clean-room), and it doesn't get in AutoCAD's way. An "also open in AutoCAD" hint could come later.
- **Privacy.** The lock holds the OS user name and computer name, written into the drawing's folder. That is the point of WHOHAS on a shared folder, but worth knowing.

title: RENAME keeps a layer's, block's or style's xdata, extension dictionary and reactors
author: mattlafy
body:
## The problem

What CADCraft keeps of a table record or block without modelling it (#528) — other applications'
xdata, its extension dictionary, its reactors — lives in `Drawing.foreign.records`, keyed by kind
and upper-case name (`("LAYER", "WALLS")`, `("BLOCK_RECORD", "DOOR")`), and the roles of the
file's handles in `foreign.targets` are keyed the same way. RENAME changes the name and leaves
both maps under the old one, so:

- RENAME a **dynamic block** and it stops being dynamic: `dynamic_block` (and BEDIT, the grips,
  Properties ▸ Custom) find its evaluation graph through the BLOCK_RECORD's extension dictionary
  by name, and on save the dictionary is no longer attached to anything;
- RENAME a layer (or rename it in the Layer manager), a text style, a dimension style, a linetype,
  a view, a UCS, a multileader style or a table style, and its other applications' xdata,
  extension dictionary and reactors are dropped on the next save.

AutoCAD keeps all of these across RENAME; a renamed dynamic block stays dynamic.

## The change

- `cadcraft-doc` `foreign.rs`: `Foreign::rename(kinds, from, to)` moves the `records` entries and
  rewrites the `targets` values of those kinds from the old name to the new one (names trimmed and
  upper-cased as the reader keys them, so a case-only rename changes nothing).
  `Foreign::rename_shared` calls it on the drawing's `Arc<Foreign>`, cloning it only when it holds
  something for that name.
- `cadcraft-engine`: every rename site calls it with the keys the reader gives that kind —
  `layer.set {newName}` (used by RENAME and the Layer manager) `LAYER`; blocks `BLOCK_RECORD`,
  `BLOCK`, `ENDBLK`; text styles `STYLE`; dimension styles `DIMSTYLE`; linetypes `LTYPE`; views
  `VIEW`; UCSs `UCS`; multileader and table styles their named-object-dictionary entries.
- Undo needs nothing: `foreign` is part of the drawing snapshot.

  dynamic DOOR …

title: HATCH pick points find boundaries in large drawings (fixes #1014)
author: NakaSato
body:
Fixes #1014.

## Problem
A HATCH, GRADIENT or BOUNDARY pick point fed every visible curve in the space to the boundary search (`geom/src/region.rs`), which gives up above its 60,000-segment cap. In a large drawing every pick reported `Valid hatch boundary not found.`, even inside a rectangle just drawn with RECTANG.

Reproduced with a synthetic DXF: 50,000 lines hatch fine, 70,000 lines fail.

## Fix
`boundary_near` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/hatch.rs` searches only the curves whose bounds reach a window around the pick point, and doubles the window until the boundary found lies inside it. Anything that could change that boundary reaches into its bounds, so into the window, and was already a candidate. The last step searches the whole space, as before.

The segment cap stays as the hostile-input guard. When the neighbourhood of the pick is itself over the cap, the error now says so ("Too many objects around the point to find a hatch boundary. Select the boundary objects instead.") instead of "not found".

## Testing
- New regression test `pick_point_in_a_crowded_drawing_finds_the_boundary` (`crates/engine/tests/hatch_options.rs`): 70,000 lines elsewhere, a rectangle with an island, a large boundary of separate lines that needs the window to grow, a pick with no boundary, and a pick inside the crowd.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).
- In the running app: opened the 70,000-line drawing, RECTANG, HATCH with SOLID, clicked inside; the rectangle fills. This went through the command-line prompts (HPDLGMODE 0); the dialog's pick command `hatchpick` was run through the control channel, not by clicking the dialog.

## Not covered
Not tested against the reporter's DWG, only synthetic drawings.

title: fix(select): select wrapped text and glyph overhangs using rendered layout
author: leonardopbatista
body:
Crossing selection can miss visible letters in wrapped MTEXT and in TEXT glyphs that extend beyond the estimated box. For example, `AAAA AAAA AAAA` at height 1 and width 5 wraps into three lines without any explicit `\P`; a small crossing window on its last line previously selected nothing.

The engine now measures TEXT, MTEXT and ATTDEF selection boxes with the renderer's layout, including glyph outlines, wrapping, inline height, decorations, obliquing and fit alignment. Picking, window/crossing selection and the spatial index use the same bounds. Text-style changes invalidate cached spatial bounds.

Validation:
- Five synthetic regression tests use CADCraft Stroke and cover direct scans and indexed drawings, positive picks, partial/full containment, misses, rotation, inline height, overlines, oblique/fit text, style changes and blank text. Four fail on the unchanged upstream baseline; all five pass with the fix.
- A local architectural DXF was checked at 35,284 sampled points on top-level TEXT/MTEXT geometry: 20,666 crossing-selection misses before, zero after. A CLI crossing selection also finds a previously missed text object. The drawing remains local and is not included in this PR.
- Full workspace validation: `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, Clippy with warnings denied, tests, assets, layers and WASM).

Scope: document extents and block-reference bounds remain approximate; this change measures selection bounds for the text entities above.

title: Ribbon: a Windows-style tabbed command bar and panel layout

An optional Windows-style layout with a Ribbon. **Nothing changes until it is chosen**: CADCraft opens exactly as today.

title: fix(select): reject empty space in block crossing windows
author: leonardopbatista
body:
Right-to-left crossing windows select block references even when the window covers only empty space between their contents. A block containing a radius-10 circle is selected by a window from (-1,-1) to (1,1), although no part of the circle touches the window. Touching an empty corner of the insert's bounding rectangle also selects it.

The narrow-phase INSERT crossing-window test now uses the renderer's visible primitives and bounded block expansion. It checks real polylines and individual filled triangles instead of the enclosing rectangle. Nested transforms, mirrored/nonuniform scales, array copies, text, visible attributes and child-layer visibility follow the rendering path. Testing triangles separately preserves filled interiors without inventing connecting edges between separate fills or across holes.

Validation:
- Six synthetic regression tests cover hollow interiors and bounding-box corners, actual boundary hits, strict whole-object window containment, nested/transformed/arrayed references, disconnected triangular fills, text, ATTMODE, hidden child layers and cyclic block input. All six fail on upstream main and pass with the fix; the main geometric cases exercise both direct scans and the spatial index.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, Clippy with warnings denied, workspace tests, assets, dependency layers and WASM.

Related work:
- #401 fixed crossing selection inside SOLID/TRACE fills and explicitly left block selection unchanged.
- #716 / #775 fixed stale block bounds after a child layer is hidden; this is a separate narrow-phase false-positive issue.
- This PR is independent of #1022, which measures standalone text selection bounds.

Scope: INSERT crossing-window selection. Point picking, fence/crossing-polygon selection and the document's approximate block bounds are unchanged.

title: fix(dxf): hostile-input hardening in the DXF reader and writer (fixes #1025)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1025

Hardens `crates/dxf` against hostile or merely unusual input. One regression test per finding in `crates/dxf/tests/hardening.rs`.

## Cause and fix per finding

- **Binary reals** were kept as NaN/inf (`Value::Real(c.f64()?)`) while the ASCII reader filters them. The binary reader now maps non-finite reals to 0.0.
- **ASCII BOM / CR-only lines**: a leading UTF-8 BOM is stripped, and lines end at LF, CRLF or a lone CR (new `ascii_lines`). The up-front `TooLarge` precheck counted only `\n`, so CR-only files skipped it; it now counts the same line ends. The `$DWGCODEPAGE` header scan splits on CR too.
- **Mixed encodings**: the ASCII reader decoded the whole file with the code page as soon as one byte was not UTF-8, and the binary reader always used the code page. Both now use one policy. Single-byte code pages (and files without a known one, read as Windows-1252): per line (ASCII) / per string (binary), valid UTF-8 first, otherwise the code page (`decode_text`). Multi-byte East Asian pages (Shift-JIS, GBK, Big5, EUC-KR/Wansung; Johab is not mapped): the declared code page is used, and UTF-8 only wins when the whole file is valid UTF-8 (ASCII: the whole text; binary: all non-ASCII strings; a file that mixes valid-UTF-8 and other strings is re-parsed from the code page). `decode_code_page` (public, strict) is unchanged.
- **Trailing whitespace** on code-0 values and the section name no longer hides `SECTION` / `ENDSEC` / `EOF` (compared with `trim_end()`, ASCII and binary EOF, and `sections()`).
- **Integer groups** accepted `inf` / `1e30` through the f64 fallback and became `i64::MAX`. Only finite floats are accepted now; the float fallback clamps to the group's width (16-bit, 32-bit, 64-bit); NaN/inf/text become 0. `Value::as_i64` on text got the same finite filter. Plain integer text is unchanged (e.g. unsigned 32-bit values in 90-series groups are kept as read).

title: Dynamic blocks: rotation and flip parameters with their rotate and flip actions and grips
author: codyvogt
body:
Dynamic block references now evaluate **rotation** and **flip** parameters with their **rotate** and **flip** actions, edit them in Properties and with grips, and save them the way AutoCAD records them.

> Stacked on #967 (its first commit, `84dd94a`, is that PR). Without #967, references saved by recent AutoCAD fall back to positional tags. For DWG, a drawing with a rotate action also needs #1000; without it the block is written as static.

## What changes
- **Reading** (`doc::dynblock`): `ParameterKind::Rotation` (base, radius end, value set) and `ParameterKind::Flip` (reflection line, the two state names). `ActionKind::Rotate` (with the base-point options: dependent, offset, independent point) and `ActionKind::Flip`.
- **Evaluating** (`apply`):
  - A changed angle turns the rotate action's selection about the parameter's base by the change.
  - A changed flip state mirrors the flip action's selection across the current reflection line.
  - Text and attributes keep reading left to right (MIRRTEXT 0 behaviour).
  - Parameters in an action's selection are carried (transformed) along.
  - The reference's attributes follow their definitions, including multiline ones.
- **Recording** (`write_history`, `write_value`):
  - The history entry holds the angle in radians (`40`) or the flip state (`70`).
  - The flip value record keeps its state after its points.
  - The flip grip record keeps its state too.
- **Properties**: Angle1 (degrees, AUPREC) and Flip state1 (its state names), both editable. `blocks.reference.set` takes degrees, and a state name or 0/1.
- **Grips** (`blocks.reference.grips` / `.grip`, canvas):
  - A circle at the radius' end: drag it to turn, or type an angle at `** ROTATE **`.
  - An arrow across the reflection line: click it to flip. It is placed from the block's grip object and turns with the line.

title: fonts: read user SHX text fonts and keep Latin accents single-stroke
author: leonardopbatista
body:
DXF text styles naming SHX fonts currently use a generic stroke substitute. Latin accents such as Ç, Ã, Á and Ó then come from filled TrueType glyphs, so one word mixes different shapes, weights and advances. A local architectural DXF and the reporter's screenshots reproduce this in a Romans style.

This change reads user-supplied SHX text fonts and uses their native strokes, cap height and pen-end advances. It also adds original precomposed Latin accents to CADCraft Stroke, so an unavailable SHX no longer produces that mixed appearance for Portuguese text.

Part of #801 (FF8); this does not close its separate MTEXT layout work. Searches found that issue and related CJK fallback PRs, but no open PR implementing the SHX reader.

- Shares bounded lazy glyph caches and limits file sizes, recursion, stacks, work, points, coordinates and loaded memory. Invalid or excessive programs return errors and fall back.

title: feat(options): add a saved two-click selection preference
author: leonardopbatista
body:
Options > Selection now offers **Select using two clicks only**. Checking it requires a separate click for each corner of a selection window; dragging no longer creates or completes that window. Unchecking it preserves the current clicks-or-drag behavior.

The preference is exposed as `PICKDRAG` through `OPTIONS`, `SETVAR` and `GETVAR`: 0 selects the two-click behavior, 2 allows clicks or drag (the default). title: fix(fonts): paragraph direction skips bidi isolates; harakat no longer block the Lam-Alef ligature
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1033

Two fixes in `crates/fonts/src/bidi.rs` only.

## Causes and fixes

- **Paragraph direction looked inside isolates.** `base_rtl` took the first L/R/AL character anywhere, so `"\u{2067}שלום\u{2069} abc"` gave `Some(true)`. UBA P2 skips everything between an isolate initiator (LRI/RLI/FSI) and its matching PDI, or to the end of the paragraph when unmatched. It now tracks isolate depth (saturating, so a stray PDI is harmless) and only considers strong characters at depth 0. The example gives `Some(false)`.
- **Harakat blocked the Lam-Alef ligature.** `presentation_forms` required the Alef to be the next code point. Marks are transparent for joining (`joining_forms` already skips them), so Lam + fatha + Alef kept two separate glyphs. After a Lam it now looks past combining marks for the Alef, emits the ligature, then the skipped marks (logical order, each with its own source index), then continues after the Alef. A non-mark between Lam and Alef still blocks the ligature. The scan only runs for a Lam.

## Tests (in `bidi.rs`)

- `paragraph_direction_skips_isolate_contents`: the example, LRI/FSI variants, nested isolates, unmatched initiator, stray PDIs, no strong character outside the isolates, unchanged plain case.
- `harakat_between_lam_and_alef_keep_the_ligature`: Lam+fatha+Alef, medial with fatha+shadda, plain Lam+Alef unchanged, mark after the Alef, Lam+mark+non-Alef, Lam+mark at the end, non-mark between Lam and Alef.
- Both tests fail without their fix: I temporarily disabled each fix, ran `cargo test -p cadcraft-fonts --lib bidi`, saw both tests fail, then restored the fixes.

## Commands that ran

All with a separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`:

- `cargo fmt -p cadcraft-fonts` (a `--check` first reported one wrapping diff in my code, now formatted)
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-fonts --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-fonts`: 55 unit + 9 integration tests pass

- `cargo xtask layers`: OK
