title: fix(fonts): MTEXT keeps the text after an unterminated code; bound oblique, line spacing and relative heights
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1035

## Causes and fixes

**1. An unterminated code drops the rest of the text** (`mtext.rs` `plain_mtext` and `parse`, `mtext/para.rs` `Paragraphs::scan`). All three parsers sent `\U+hhhh`, `\M+nhhhh` and every other unknown code to the arm for codes with a `;`-terminated argument. Without a `;` the rest of the text went (`A\U+00B0 B C;D` gave `AD`).
- New `unescape_codes` decodes `\U+hhhh` (a surrogate pair gives one character, a lone surrogate U+FFFD) and `\M+nhhhh` (through `cadcraft_dxf::mif_escape_at`, the DXF reader's own decoder) before tokenizing. `plain_mtext`, `layout_mtext_with` and `Paragraphs::scan` call it, so they agree. A decoded `\`, `{` or `}` is escaped, so it stays text; an escaped backslash (`\\U+0041`) is not an escape.
- An unknown code now drops only the backslash and the code character (`takes_arg` lists the codes that do take an argument: `f F H W Q T A C c p`; `\S` keeps its own scan). Those keep their behaviour, so `plain_mtext("unterminated \\H2") == "unterminated "` still holds. No existing test was changed.

**2. NaN oblique and line spacing** (`layout_mtext_with`, `para::layout`). Only height, width factor, width and rotation were checked. A non-finite oblique is now 0. Line spacing goes through `sane_line_spacing`: 1.0 when not finite or not positive, otherwise clamped to 0.25..=4 (AutoCAD's range, decided by the owner). The paragraph layout uses the same function.

**3. Runaway relative heights** (`parse`, the `\H` arm). `\H…x` multiplied the current height without a bound (60 times `\H999999x;` gave 1e360 = inf). After each multiplication the height is held within 1e-3..1e3 times the MTEXT's own height (never inf). An absolute `\H` keeps its existing cap.

`cadcraft-fonts` now depends on `cadcraft-dxf` (both in the workspace; L0 under L2, `cargo xtask layers` passes). The only change in the dxf crate is that `mif_escape_at` is `pub` instead of private. `Cargo.lock` gains that one edge.

title: DXF: write the DIMSTYLE jog angle (DIMJOGANG) in degrees, as AutoCAD reads it
author: Slopapalooza
body:
**Merged main (`0b32c2e`, 2026-10-19)** to clear merge conflicts. Upstream's `$ANGBASE` reading (#1234) now sits beside this PR's `$DIMJOGANG` reading.

## Problem

CADCraft writes the jog angle (DIMJOGANG) to DIMSTYLE group 50 in radians, so 45° is saved as `50 0.7853981633974483`. AutoCAD reads that group in degrees, like other DXF angle groups.

I checked this black-box in AutoCAD LT 2026 with a synthetic drawing. CADCraft 0.6.2 saved a 2018 DXF and AutoCAD opened it. Re-saved as R2000, AutoCAD stored the jog angle as 0.0137077838904019 rad, which is 0.7853981633974483° in radians. So every 2004-or-later DXF from CADCraft gives AutoCAD a jog angle of 0.785° instead of 45°. That is also outside the 5–90° range the setting allows.

The DWG bridge agrees with AutoCAD: acadrust 0.6.4 reads and writes DIMSTYLE group 50 in degrees. CADCraft's reader converted that group from radians, so opening a DWG also lost its styles' jog angles. A 30° style came in as 1719°, was rejected, and fell back to 45°.

## Changes

- **Writing** (`dxf_ext.rs`, `dxf_write.rs`): the jog angle is encoded as a new `DimVal::Angle` in degrees. `W::dimval` writes degrees to a DIMSTYLE group and radians to xdata.
- **Reading** (`dxf_ext::jog_degrees`) accepts either unit and decides from the value. A style takes 5–90°. In radians those angles are 0.087–1.571, and as degrees those numbers would all be below the 5° minimum. So 5 to 90 reads as degrees and 0.087 to 1.571 as radians. Both are rounded to 1e-9° so whole degrees come back whole. Anything else is dropped and the style keeps its default, as before. This means:
  - files from CADCraft 0.7.0 and earlier, with radians in group 50, still read. (0.7.0 shipped without this change.)
  - DWG open now gets the jog angle, which the bridge passes in degrees.
  - xdata from any CADCraft version reads.
- **Each path:**

  | Path | Written | Read |
  |---|---|---|
  | DIMSTYLE group 50 (2004 and later) | **degrees** (was radians) | either unit (was radi…

author: STE1200

Part of the agent-interface series (#1039).

An agent reading a drawing through MCP paid for whitespace and still had to guess at the coordinate contract. `inspect_drawing {}` on `examples/apartment.dxf` (58 entities) returned 72 KB of pretty-printed JSON, most of it the entity list that `query_entities` already serves with filters and paging. title: JSON handles: an unknown or erased handle is an error that names it, and nothing changes
author: STE1200
body:
Part of #1039 (agent interface).

## What

Commands that take `handles` (or `handle`) as a JSON parameter dropped handles that name no object without a word. `move {handles: ["FFFFF"], delta: [5, 0]}` answered `{"moved": 0}`; `move {handles: [a, "FFFFF"]}` moved `a` and said nothing about the other one; `select {handles: ["FFFFF"]}` even put the handle into the selection.

Now a handle in an explicit `handle`/`handles` that is not in the drawing (never made, or erased) is an error that lists the unknown handles, each once, and the command changes nothing:

```
unknown handles: FFFFF, 1A2BC (no such object in the drawing, or it was erased)
```

This completes #330 / #331, which made a *malformed* handle an error; a well-formed handle that names nothing was still accepted.

## Why

Agents (MCP `execute`, control channel `engine.execute`) work from handles they read earlier: from `query_entities`, an earlier result, or their own memory of the drawing. When one of those objects has since been erased, joined or exploded, the command quietly acted on fewer objects (or none), and the reply gave the agent no reason to notice. It then carried on as if the edit had happened. A clear error lets it look again, and acting on all of the named objects or none of them keeps a half-done edit out of the drawing.

## Change

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs`: the shared resolver is split into `explicit_handles` (parse `handles`/`handle`, then check every handle against the drawing) and `targets` (that, or else the selection). About 120 command call sites go through `targets`, so they all get the check. The check runs before the command touches anything.
- `datalinkupdate` (`cmd/table/breaks.rs`) had its own copy of the lookup that skipped unreadable and unknown handles. It now uses `explicit_handles`, so it gets the same errors. Without handles it still updates every linked table.
- The check is independent of the space on screen: a handle is known when its object is in model space or …

title: Prevent REGION data loss when saving DWG files
author: PedroGuille
body:
QSAVE previously wrote the DWG and marked the drawing saved before reporting omitted objects. Refuse incomplete DWG/DWT saves before writing, keep the original file and unsaved state intact, and direct the user to SAVEAS to DXF.

Recognize supported inline SAT REGION geometry instead of falsely reporting it as lost. Preserve modern binary modeler data, reject unconvertible or missing geometry and unsafe binary downgrades, and let the unmodified DWG writer reject unsupported custom entities and objects rather than deleting them. DWT saves now honor the requested version.

Synthetic regressions cover real QSAVE with 72 REGIONs, repeated geometry round trips at all six DWG versions, blocks and layouts, rejected conversions and downgrades, file/dirty/history preservation, and DXF backup.

Fixes #1019.

title: fix(polyline): preserve segment widths and generate grips in linear time
author: LabDennis

Bounded microbenchmark, same machine/profile, five grip-list generations of a synthetic open polyline:

| Vertices | Before | After |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,000 | 50.87 ms | 0.234 ms |
| 2,000 | 130.57 ms | 0.483 ms |

The performance improvement follows from one segment pass instead of rebuilding it for every vertex, with no cloned input vertices or intermediate segment vector in the consumers.

title: fix(render): stabilize dashed highlights of filled objects
author: leonardopbatista
body:
Dashed highlights of filled primitives can appear to flicker when the pointer moves over a stationary object. `fill_outlines` extracted boundary segments from fresh `HashMap`s, and their randomized iteration order chose a different contour start/direction on each call. Both CPU dashing and GPU highlight meshes measure dash distance from that start, so the visible dash phase changed without a geometry change.

The boundary chaining step now normalizes segment endpoints and sorts segments in coordinate order before traversal. This fixes contour starts, directions and loop ordering while retaining the existing odd-coverage handling for slab edges, holes, expansion limits and large-input fallback. Hash lookups remain in place; their iteration no longer controls traversal.

Affected paths:
- Filled glyphs (TrueType text, including text within blocks), SOLID/TRACE, filled hatches, wide polylines and arrowheads when highlighted with dashed outlines.
- Hover preview with PREVIEWEFFECT 0 or 2 (including default 2): the CPU overlay is redrawn every frame even with the GPU canvas enabled.
- Selected fills with SELECTIONEFFECT 0: CPU repaints, and GPU highlight mesh rebuilds. Cached GPU meshes stay stable until rebuilt.
- Wipeout masks are always outlined; deterministic traversal also stabilizes their dashed preview.

Ordinary polylines and solid-color fill highlights do not use this randomized boundary traversal. Changing the hovered object or zooming to different tessellation detail can legitimately change the highlight; this fix addresses an unchanged fill outline on repaint/rebuild.

title: MCP and control channel: engine errors carry a stable code, the command and the parameter
author: STE1200
body:
Part of #1039. Stacked on #1040 (only the last commit is new).

The engine already knows what kind of error it has (`EngineError`: unknown command, not available, bad parameters, no document, failed, internal), but at the MCP and control boundary it became one string. An agent that wanted to tell "I sent a wrong parameter" from "this command can't run right now" had to parse English text such as ``invalid parameters for `circle`: `radius` or `diameter` is required``.

## Changes

**Codes from the engine's variants** (`crates/engine/src/error_data.rs`). `EngineError::code()` maps each variant to a snake_case code; `EngineError::info(command)` returns `ErrorInfo {code, command, param?, message}`. `ERROR_CODES` lists them with a one-line meaning:

| Variant | Code |
|---|---|
| `UnknownCommand` | `unknown_command` |
| `Disabled` | `not_available` |
| `BadParams` | `bad_params` |
| `NoDocument` | `no_document` |
| `Other` | `failed` |
| `Internal` | `internal` |

No new categories: the codes are exactly what the engine distinguishes today. `command` is the command the error names (the variants that carry one), else the command that was called. `param` is best effort, filled only for `bad_params` when the message names a parameter that looks like a JSON key (lower-case first letter, so values such as `` `Door` `` or `` `ISO-25` `` are not taken for one), either as a leading quoted key (`` `radius` must be positive``, the form most `bad_params` messages already use) or serde's ``missing field `x` `` / ``unknown field `x` ``; otherwise it is left out. `message` is `to_string()`, unchanged. `EngineError` itself is not changed.

**MCP** (`crates/mcp/src/backend.rs`, `tools.rs`). `Backend` gains `call_detailed`, returning `CallError {message, data}`; `call` stays and is now a provided method on top of it, so existing callers and tests are untouched. OPEN echoes them and MCP `open` returns them as `warnings`, but `cadcraft-cli info` and `cadcraft-cli convert` did not show them; `convert` only warned about the DXF reader's `skipped_records` (#872). title: Canvas: a click made while the mouse moves selects too (#1001)
author: aldozar
body:
Fixes #1001. It follows up #835, which made a click made while moving place a point at point prompts and left selection prompts as they were.

**Problem.** egui counts a click only if the button comes up within a few points of where it went down; otherwise it is a drag. When drafting fast, the hand is already moving as you click. At prompts that select objects, that click was lost:
- **At "Select objects"** (MOVE, COPY, ERASE, TRIM's cutting edges…) and **with no command running**, the press-and-drag selection window (PICKDRAG = 2) took it. Letting go then closed a tiny window that selected nothing.
- **At point prompts that pick an object**, nothing handled it: STRETCH's own "Select objects", "Select object to trim/extend", "Select first object"… (`Prompt::picks_objects`, which #835 deliberately excludes).

**Change** (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`)
- The canvas remembers where and when the button went down for each primary drag, since egui forgets both once the button is up.
- A drag let go within **0.3 s** counts as a click **where the button went down**, which is the object being aimed at:
  - at "Select objects" and with no command, the window the drag opened is dropped, and the click picks the object there or starts a click-click window on empty space;
  - at object-pick point prompts, the press point is given to the command.
- A slower drag is still a press-and-drag window.
- Drawing prompts are unchanged: #835 places their point where the button comes up.

**Tests** (`crates/ui-egui/tests/rapid_clicks.rs`, 60 fps harness). The four new tests fail on main and pass here:
- **STRETCH:** a moving click on a line picks it, and one on empty space starts STRETCH's window there.
- **MOVE:** a moving click picks the line, and a half-second drag still selects by window.
- **No command:** a moving click picks the line.
- **TRIM (Quick):** a moving click trims the part the button went down on.

title: DXF: no CLASS instance counts in R2000 files (AutoCAD LT 2026 hung opening them)
author: Slopapalooza
body:
## Problem
AutoCAD LT 2026 stops responding when it opens a DXF that CADCraft saved as R2000 (`AC1015`); it has to be ended from Task Manager. Every R2000 file from v0.6.2 does this, even a one-rectangle drawing. A drawing opened from an R2000 file is saved as R2000 again (Default Save Version applies only to new drawings), so files that started in v0.5.0, which wrote only R2000, keep hitting it.

Since #635, every CLASS record carries group 91, the instance count, at every version. Group 91 came with the 2004 format. R2000 CLASS records are `1, 2, 3, 90, 280, 281` (DXF Reference, CLASSES example).

Isolated black-box in AutoCAD LT 2026 with synthetic drawings, one change per file:

| File | AutoCAD LT 2026 |
|---|---|
| R2000 DXF from v0.6.2 | hangs |
| The same content with `$ACADVER AC1032` | opens |
| The same R2000 file without the CLASS 91 groups | opens |
| The same, also without MLEADERSTYLE 179/271–273 | opens (these groups are not the cause) |

A second cause, already fixed on main: a DXF without the `ACAD_PLOTSTYLENAME` dictionary and the layers' 390 groups also makes AutoCAD LT 2026 hang, at any version. Removing them from a working 2018 file reproduces the hang. v0.5.0 files lack them. The writer has added them since #418, so a v0.5.0 file opened and saved with this change opens in AutoCAD.

## Changes
- `dxf_write::add_class_instance_counts` writes group 91 only when the file is 2004 or later. For the DWG bridge, that is the target DWG version, so 2004+ DWG output is unchanged.

title: Split canvas.rs into modules by concern, and show() into frame phases
author: mattlafy
body:
## Why

`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` is the UI's largest file and the one most open PRs
touch (those that would conflict with this one are listed below). Its `show()` is a single function of
some 640 lines that reads input,
navigates, handles every kind of click, and paints the drawing, the overlays and the cursor. Two
PRs on unrelated features (say Dynamic Input and VPORTS tiles) both land in the same file, often
in the same function.

## The change

No behaviour change. Two parts:

1. **A mechanical move**, generated by a script: every top-level item except `show()` and the
   canvas state moves unchanged into `canvas/<module>.rs`, doc comments and attributes with it.
   The only edited lines are `pub(super)` on moved private items (and on the private fields and
   methods of moved types, which sibling modules reach), and the `mod`/`use` lines in canvas.rs.
   `git diff --color-moved` shows the rest as moved.
2. **`show()` split into frame phases**, statement order unchanged: one private `Frame` struct
   carries what crosses phases (the rects, painter, response, transforms, this frame's input), and
   `show()` is now a short sequence: `Frame::setup` → `navigate` → `reread_view` → `clicks` →
   `paint::drawing` → `paint::overlays` → `paint::cursor`. The two early `return`s of the old body
   are `ControlFlow::Break` from `navigate` and `clicks`; the re-bound `view`/`scale`/`xf` became
   `Frame` field updates. Every other statement reads exactly as it did in `show()` (each phase
   binds its own `painter`, `resp` and so on), so a PR's hunk inside `show()` applies to the phase
   that now holds it.

| Module | Holds |
|---|---|
| `canvas.rs` | `Xf`, `CanvasState`, `SnapCycle`, `show()`, the module list |
| `canvas/frame.rs` | `Frame`, setup and view re-read, `navigate`, `clicks` |
| `canvas/paint.rs` | `drawing`, `overlays`, `cursor` |
| `canvas/list.rs` | building the display list for the view; `PrimIndex` |
| `canvas/viewport.rs` | the active MSPACE viewport's …

title: AutoCAD interop: justified text, DIMPOST, current dimension style, *D block colours
author: aldozar
body:
Fixes #1050, #1051, #1052 and #1053. It also covers #1054 with a test (already fixed on main by #855).

Thanks to @Rickpixell for the reports. Each one came with a script and what AutoCAD 2026 reads from the file, which made these quick to pin down. All the changes concern values AutoCAD reads from CADCraft's files **as they are**, without recomputing them.

**#1050: justified TEXT drawn from the wrong end.** A justified TEXT, ATTRIB or ATTDEF is placed by its alignment point (group 11). Its insertion point (group 10) is the start of its baseline, which AutoCAD recomputes from DXF but takes from DWG as it is. CADCraft wrote the alignment point in both. Group 10 is now computed from the alignment point and the text's width (`cadcraft_fonts::baseline_start`, sharing `place`'s frame).
- **Kept when close:** a stored point near CADCraft's own is left alone: along the baseline within 10 % of the width plus half the height, across it within a fifth of the height. That is AutoCAD's value and exact for its fonts, so drawings that come from AutoCAD keep it. On 12 drawings made in AutoCAD (1,055 justified texts) the points written are the same as with a distance-only check. Multiline attribute values, placed by their embedded MTEXT, keep the distance-only check.
- **Replaced when stale:** the point is replaced when it is the alignment point (text made in CADCraft) or when the text has changed length since. Left Middle and Left Bottom text made here used to pass as "close", since the alignment point is only h/2 or h/3 from the baseline start, and AutoCAD drew it half a height high (found by @lee-cyrille-maskell).
- **Remaining offset:** CADCraft measures with its own fonts, so for text made here AutoCAD may start it a little off from where its own font would. In the report's case it is 71.8 vs AutoCAD's 69.2, instead of 100.

title: DIMASSOC: reference polyline vertices by segment, as AutoCAD does (#1049)
author: aldozar
body:
Fixes #1049. Thanks to @Rickpixell for the AutoCAD-side evidence, both in the issue and in the black-box observation of what AutoCAD 2026 writes ([review comment](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/pull/1064#issuecomment-6158773784)).

**Problem.** A dimension on a polyline vertex was saved with a DIMASSOC `AcDbOsnapPointRef` that names the polyline but not the part of it: subentity type (73) and GS marker (91) were both 0. When AutoCAD regenerated the dimension, it resolved the reference to the polyline's first segment and changed the value silently (210 became 5, 190 became 20).

**Change: write.** A polyline vertex is referenced the way AutoCAD 2026 does, as observed in the review.
- **Segment.** It is an end of one of its segments: subentity type 73 = 2, and the 1-based segment in 91. Segment *k* runs from vertex *k−1* to vertex *k*, and a closed polyline's closing segment is the last.
- **Osnap.** It is 1 with parameter 1.0 for a segment's end, and 13 with 0.0 for its start.
- **Which segment.** Vertex 0 is written as the start of segment 1, and vertex *k* as the end of segment *k*. When that segment is an arc, the other neighbour is used instead.
- **Still left out:**
  - a vertex between two arcs, because there AutoCAD writes an angle in 40 and that hasn't been tested;
  - references to 3D polylines and MLINEs.
  - Both are left out of the DIMASSOC object as before, so their dimensions keep their values. CADCraft keeps every link in its own xdata anyway.

**Change: read.** AutoCAD leaves the reference point (10/20) at 0,0. CADCraft's nearest-vertex fallback therefore attached AutoCAD's associative dimensions on polylines to the vertex nearest the origin. The reader now uses the segment (91 with 73 = 2) and the osnap (1 or 13) to find the vertex, and keeps the nearest-point fallback for files without them.

- `polyline_vertex_references_name_the_segment`: the observed open, closed and arc cases. A vertex between two arcs gets no reference.

title: DWG: entities of a second layout stay on it in AutoCAD (#1057)
author: aldozar
body:
Fixes #1057 and #1463. Thanks @Rickpixell. The black-box observation in AutoCAD pointed straight at it. #1463 is the same with `cadcraft-cli convert` and ZWCAD 2025: its `repro.dxf` writes S1A's and S2's entities as mode 1 on main and owned by their blocks here.

**Cause.** In DWG, each entity carries an *entity mode*: 2 for model space, 1 for paper space, 0 for "owned by the block whose handle follows" (ODA's public DWG specification). acadrust writes mode 1 for every paper-space entity, including those of `*Paper_Space0`, `*Paper_Space1`…, and relies on each block's entity list to place them. AutoCAD reads mode 1 as the `*Paper_Space` block's, the first layout. Everything drawn on another layout landed there, and that layout's tab stayed empty.

**It also affects drawings that come from AutoCAD.** On a real construction drawing set with two layouts, a CADCraft DWG save wrote Layout2's two viewports with mode 1, so AutoCAD showed them on Layout1.

**Change** (`crates/dwg`, before writing). Entities owned by a `*Paper_SpaceN` block get `entity_mode = Some(0)`, acadrust's per-entity override, so the writer emits mode 0 with the owner handle. Model space and the first layout keep modes 2 and 1. acadrust's own reader already resolves mode 0 through the owner handle, so CADCraft reopens these files the same way.

**Tests**
- New `crates/io/tests/dwg_layout_owner.rs`: fails on main (mode 1), passes here.
  - It writes a drawing with entities in model space, on the first layout and on a second one, then reads the DWG **as written** with acadrust.
  - The second layout's entities are mode 0 and owned by its block, and the first layout's stay mode 1.
  - Read back, each layout keeps its own entities.
- **New dev-dependency.** The test reads the DWG with acadrust, added as a dev-dependency of cadcraft-io at the same version as cadcraft-dwg's, so the lock file gains no new package.

title: Implement OSOPTIONS snap filters and drafting controls
author: ecke101
body:
Adds AutoCAD-compatible `OSOPTIONS` to control object snap filtering, defaulting to `7`.

- Bit `1` ignores hatch objects and stays synchronized with the legacy `OSNAPHATCH` setting.

title: Dimension text below the line (\X) and leader text at DIMSCALE (#1055, #1056)
author: aldozar
body:
Fixes #1055 and #1056. Thanks @Rickpixell.

**#1055: `\X` in dimension text.** `\X` starts the text that goes below the dimension line (DXF Reference). CADCraft drew only the part before it, on screen, in plots and in the `*D` block.
- **Placement.** The part after `\X` is now drawn below the dimension line, on the other side of it and at the same distance as the part above. Text centred on the line (DIMTAD 0) moves above it. "The line" is the line through the longest dimension-line piece, since arrowheads are short and the line may be broken around centred text.
- **`*D` block.** It holds the lower part as a second MTEXT, as AutoCAD writes it after a regen.
- **Fit.** When deciding whether the text fits, its width is the wider part's and its height the upper part's.
- **API.** `DimGeometry` gains `below: Option<(String, Vec2)>`.
- **Not covered here:** the reporter's side note that the DWG has flag 70 = 128 (user-positioned text) where the DXF has 32 comes from the DWG writer and deserves its own issue.

**#1056: LEADER annotation height.** The annotation `leader {"text": …}` makes was DIMTXT high whatever DIMSCALE said, 0.25 next to dimensions at 6.25. It is now DIMTXT × DIMSCALE (the style's, else the drawing's; 1 for annotative styles), in the style's text style, as AutoCAD's LEADER makes it.

**Tests.** The io and engine tests fail on main and pass here.
- **render:** `text_after_backslash_x_goes_below_the_line`, for horizontal and vertical dimensions, with DIMTAD 0 and 1. The parts land on opposite sides of the line at the same distance, and text without `\X` has nothing below.
- **io:** `dim_text_below.rs`, the `*D` block has both MTEXTs, above and below the line.
- **engine:** `leader_text_scale.rs`, the annotation is 6.25 at DIMSCALE 25 / DIMTXT 0.25.

`cargo xtask ci` passes. This PR and #1062 both touch the MTEXT part of `dim_block_entities` (that one sets its colour), so whichever lands second needs a one-hunk merge.

title: Layouts in millimetres plot in millimetres whatever MEASUREMENT says (#1058)
author: aldozar
body:
Fixes #1058. Thanks @Rickpixell for the ezdxf cases.

**Problem.** Paper-space units followed the drawing's `$MEASUREMENT` only. A layout whose page setup is in millimetres (LAYOUT/PLOTSETTINGS group 72 = 1), common in drawings from AutoCAD that keep `$MEASUREMENT = 0`, was taken as inches. Its PDF drew everything 25.4 times too large: the 10 mm frame started at 720 pt instead of 28.35, and the page came out blank.

**Change**
- **`PageSetup.paper_mm`:** read from group 72 = 1. Group 72 = 0 still leaves the units to `$MEASUREMENT`, because earlier CADCraft versions wrote 0 for every layout and metric drawings saved by them must not turn into inches.
- **`paper::page_unit_mm(d, page)` and `paper::unit_mm_of(d, handle)`:** they give the layout's units. They are used by:
  - the layout sheet;
  - PDF and raster plots;
  - PREVIEW;
  - the pens of what a layout's viewports show, so lineweights aren't 25.4 times too thin there.
- **Unchanged:** model-space plot defaults (A4 versus ANSI A) still follow `$MEASUREMENT`.
- **Writer:** it stores 72 = 1 for layouts in millimetres; before, it wrote 0 always.

**Tests** (`crates/io/tests/layout_paper_units.rs`)
- An imperial drawing (`$MEASUREMENT 0`) with an A4 landscape layout in mm: the sheet is 297 × 210 paper units, and in the uncompressed PDF the frame spans 28.35 to 813.54 pt.
- Round trip through DXF: 72 = 1 is written and read back.
- A metric drawing whose layouts say 72 = 0, as older CADCraft files do, still has its layouts in millimetres.

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

The VIEWTARGET part the report mentions is left to #959, as the report says.

title: Fix native DWG layouts and saves; speed up dense contour selection
author: danielmigueltejedor
body:
DWGs could open correctly through CADCraft's dialog but fail from Finder, show blank or displaced layouts, misalign title-block attributes, and freeze during dense contour selection. Saving a modern drawing could also make AutoCAD reject render-setting objects: retained records were decoded as R2000 instead of their source version.

This PR fixes those paths and reduces large-drawing import memory without committing user drawings, proprietary fonts, screenshots, or generated PDFs.

- Finder Open Documents events use the existing OPEN path, during launch and while running; an already-open drawing is selected without losing edits. macOS registers both the fallback DWG type and AutoCAD's installed type.
- Native unsized, unvisited empty layouts initialize on first activation. Configured layouts and erased viewports remain intact. Paper framing follows the actual sheet and canvas; inactive DWG viewport IDs and native frozen-layer handles are restored.
- Layout sheets use the printable origin, with correctly rotated landscape margins and per-layout plot offsets preserved through DXF/DWG (PLOTSETTINGS 46/47). Screen framing, the generated overall viewport, PDF/PNG/SVG plots and preview share the origin without moving entities. Synthetic two-layout round trips and PDF/PNG coordinate tests cover distinct margins and positive/negative offsets.
- Untwisted top views apply their WCS target, including long direction vectors with rounding noise. Attributes use group 74 for vertical alignment, and MTEXT distinguishes absolute paragraph lengths from height-relative lengths.
- DWG conversion decodes retained foreign records at the source version before writing the requested version. Native sheet units are millimetres, and LAYOUT 331 references the overall paper viewport, including generated implicit viewports.
- Dense polyline grips are generated in linear time. Their mesh is reused across unchanged frames, with hover/active recolouring and a 128 MiB cache budget. Cached and uncach…

title: New text follows its style: fixed and paper heights, width factor, oblique, TEXT's Style option (stacked on #1083)
author: Slopapalooza
body:
Stacked on #1083 (which is stacked on #1042, #1008, #994 and #954); this PR's change is the last commit.

**Rebased onto main at `0b32c2e` (2026-10-19)** to clear merge conflicts; what this PR does is unchanged.

## Problem

New text ignores most of its text style:

- **Fixed height:** a fixed-height style (height > 0) is still asked for a height, and new text gets TEXTSIZE instead. AutoCAD uses the style's height and doesn't ask.
- **Annotative styles:** the height prompt doesn't say that the height is the paper height.
- **Effects:** new TEXT gets width factor 1 and obliquing angle 0, whatever the style says.
- **Style option:** TEXT's Style option is offered at "Specify start point of text or [Justify/Style]", but choosing it does nothing.
- **Enter at the start point:** it does nothing. In AutoCAD it continues directly below the last text.

## Changes

- **Fixed-height styles:**
  - TEXT goes straight from the start point to the rotation.
  - MTEXT starts at the style's height, and MTEXT's Style option takes a fixed style's height.
  - The JSON `text` and `mtext` forms default to it; an explicit `height` is kept.
  - TEXTSIZE is left alone.
- **Annotative styles:** TEXT asks "Specify paper text height", the size annotative text is stored at.
- **Width factor and obliquing angle:** new TEXT takes them from its style. Later style changes don't change existing text, as in AutoCAD.
- **Style option:**
  - TEXT takes a style name, which becomes current (as AutoCAD's does), and the status line is shown again.

title: Dynamic blocks: show a distance's grip only at an end an action follows, and the grips of parameters a visibility state lists
author: codyvogt
body:
Dynamic block references show the grips AutoCAD shows, and no others: a distance's arrow only at an end an action follows, and every grip of a parameter the current visibility state lists.

## What changes (`doc::dynblock::grips`)
- **A distance's unused end has no grip.** A linear parameter's base or end grip shows only when an action is attached to that end:

- **A visibility state that lists a parameter shows its grips.** A grip used to show only when the state listed the grip object. title: TRIM/EXTEND: shift-select does the other one, as the prompt says
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1091.

TRIM and EXTEND (from #403) already offer "shift-select to extend / to trim" at the pick prompt, but the canvas sends the running command a plain point and Shift never reaches it, so the pick always does the command's own operation. In Quick mode that's the worst case: a Shift+click meant to extend an object erases it instead. This adds `Session::with_shift`, which holds the Shift state for the inputs given inside it (the same scoped pattern `input_snapped` uses for its viewport), has the canvas click and the control channel's `ui.pointer` (which already took `shift` for idle clicks) pass it, and swaps trim/extend for that one pick in `trimextend.rs`. Fence and Crossing are unchanged.

Left for you, since they're UI choices rather than this bug: the issue also says the tooltip shouldn't show X/Y at this prompt and that object snaps shouldn't appear while picking objects. `Prompt::picks_objects` would be the natural hook for both, happy to do it here or in a follow-up if you want that behaviour. FILLET/CHAMFER's "shift-select to apply corner" has the same gap (the Shift state now reaches commands, so it'd be a small change there too).

Validation:
- `canvas::trim_shift_tests::shift_click_switches_between_trim_and_extend` drives a real Shift+click through the canvas: fails on main (the TRIM pick erases the line instead of extending it), passes here; also run alone with `--test-threads=1`, and it fails again if the canvas passes `false` instead of the Shift state

title: DWG dimensions: text at its default position unless it was moved, and bit 32 kept
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1094.

Thanks @Rickpixell for the measurements, and @aldozar for spotting it in #1084. The DWG bridge hands dimensions to acadrust, which stores `text_user_positioned` as is in bit 0 of the DWG dimension flags byte. In DWG that bit means the opposite of DXF group 70's bit 128 (set: the text is at its default position), and bit 1 carries group 70's bit 32, which acadrust doesn't keep from DXF. So every dimension in a CADCraft DWG came out as 128 without 32, exactly the table in the issue. The bridge now maps both bits before the DWG writer runs (bit 32 always, as the DXF writer does; 128 only when the text was really moved), and maps bit 0 back after a DWG is read. The read side has to change too: without it CADCraft's own DWGs would come back with every text "moved", and AutoCAD DWGs were already being read that way. One side effect: DWGs saved by earlier CADCraft versions now open with their dimension texts as user-positioned, which is what AutoCAD sees in them as well.

The fix lives in `crates/dwg` next to the other acadrust workarounds (`table_merges`, `table_style_rows`). It could also go upstream in acadrust; happy to switch if you'd rather report it there and pin a fixed release.

Validation:
- `dimension_text_position_flags_reach_the_dwg_as_autocad_reads_them` (crates/dwg): a linear, an aligned, a radius and an angular dimension, each with the text at home and moved, saved to DWG; the test reads the raw flags byte back. It fails on main (`0 Linear: bit 32 of group 70 is lost (flags byte 0x00)`) and passes here. It also checks that the DWG reads back with 128 only on the moved texts.
- Undoing only the bit 0 inversion makes it fail again (`HOME Linear: flags byte 0x02`), so the check doesn't depend on the reader agreeing with the writer.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-io --lib dwg`, `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-dwg --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Dynamic blocks: a visibility or lookup grip carried by an action goes with it
author: codyvogt
body:
A visibility or lookup parameter that an action carries along now keeps its new position: its grip moves with the block's objects, and the position is read from and saved to the reference's value record the way AutoCAD records it.

> Stacked on #1030 (and through it on #967). The first commits on this branch are those PRs; the change here is the last commit.

## The problem
A stretch, move, rotate or flip action can have a visibility or lookup parameter in its selection. AutoCAD then moves the parameter, and records where it went in the reference's value record next to the state (`10/20/30` before the group `1` text). CADCraft read only the state, never carried the parameter, and drew its grip where the dynamic block has it. On a well-label block, moving the label with its Position1 grip left the visibility arrow behind.

## What changes (`doc::dynblock`)
- `Value::Text` has an optional `at`: the record's position, when it has one.
- Evaluating (`apply`): a carried visibility or lookup parameter moves with the action (stretch frame, move, rotate, flip), and its state or value is kept. A change that sets the state itself leaves the position where it is.
- Recording (`write_value`): the record gets the new position and keeps its state.
- Grips: the visibility or lookup grip is drawn at the record's position.

## Checked against AutoCAD (black-box, owner-provided drawing, nothing committed)
- The label was moved with its Position1 grip in CADCraft and saved as DXF and as DWG (DWG with #1000). Opened in AutoCAD, the visibility grip sits where CADCraft draws it, on the label's moved top edge.

## Tests
`crates/io/tests/dynblock_visibility_position.rs`, on the synthetic DOOR fixture with Visibility1 put in the Width stretch's selection:
- changing Width carries the visibility grip by the stretch;
- the record holds the new position and the state;
- the position survives a save and read;
- changing the state leaves the grip where the stretch put it.

title: Dynamic blocks: tick marks at the stops of a grip on a value list or increments
author: codyvogt
body:

title: Dynamic blocks: an attribute hidden by a visibility state has no grip, snap or preview
author: codyvogt
body:
An attribute that a dynamic block's visibility state hides now has no grip, insertion snap, grip-preview text or listing, and stays hidden through a save, as in AutoCAD. (Once #990 lands, its attribute-text picking in `select.rs` should use `Attrib::shown()` too; that is a one-line follow-up.)

> Stacked on #993 (its commit is the first on this branch); the change here is the last commit.

## The problem
A visibility state that leaves an attribute definition out hides the reference's attribute too. AutoCAD saves that attribute with its own visibility off (group 60 on the ATTRIB). CADCraft didn't draw it, because the definition was hidden. But the attribute still had a grip and an insertion snap, still showed in the grip preview, and the flag wasn't kept through a read.

## What changes
- `AttribModes::hidden`: hidden with its definition. It is read from the ATTRIB's group 60, and set when a visibility state changes (from whether the new block's definition of that tag is shown). It is saved as group 60, as before.
- `Attrib::shown()` (not Invisible and not hidden) is used for:
  - the reference's attribute grips;
  - insertion snaps;
  - the grip preview;
  - text listings.
- The renderer skips a hidden attribute whatever ATTDISP says, as its definition is hidden.

## Tests
`crates/io/tests/dynblock_hidden_attribs.rs`, on the synthetic DOOR fixture with an attribute definition in its Open state:
- in Closed, the attribute is hidden and has no grip;
- it is saved with group 60 and read back hidden;
- back in Open, it is shown with its grip, and saved without group 60.

title: Collapsed Tool Sets leave a strip on the left edge that expands them again
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1095.

The chevron on the Tool Sets tab row sets `show_toolsets = false`, and the panel then leaves the dock entirely, so nothing on screen brings it back: the only route was Window > Tool Sets (Cmd/Ctrl+3), which is easy to miss when the menu bar isn't where you'd look. This keeps a narrow strip on the left edge while the Tool Sets are collapsed, a bit like a collapsed palette title bar; clicking anywhere on it (chevron at the top, "Tool Sets" tooltip) runs `ui.toggle.toolsets {"on": true}`, the same docking `open` the menu already uses, so the panel comes back where it was. The strip only shows with a drawing open, same as the dock. Thanks @grandixximo for the report and the screenshot.

The strip appears whenever the Tool Sets are hidden, including after closing the panel from its tab menu; if you'd rather keep that case strip-free, or prefer a toolbar toggle like the Properties one for the right palettes, happy to switch.

About the `>` on the right palettes from the comment: in v0.5.0 that chevron was only painted, with no click handler, so it really did nothing. Since #456 (in v0.6.2) Layers and Properties are docked panels with their own headers, and that row isn't drawn any more, so there was nothing left to change on that side.

title: MEASUREGEOM typed at the command line asks for the option, then the points
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1103.

MEASUREGEOM had only its JSON form, so typing it at the command line ran it with no params and forwarded that straight to DIST, which is where the "`p1` ([x,y]) is required" came from. It now has a prompt sequence like the other inquiry commands: "Enter an option [Distance/Radius/ARea] <Distance>", then it hands over to DIST's or AREA's own prompts (so Multiple points, Object, Add/Subtract all keep working), and Radius asks for an arc or circle and reports radius and diameter through the existing `radius.measure`. The JSON form for agents/scripts is unchanged.

I left Angle out of the option list for now: there's `angle.measure` in the JSON form but no pick-two-lines prompt yet. Happy to add it (and Volume/Quick later) in this PR or a follow-up, and happy to switch the keyword spelling if you'd rather have `Area` than AutoCAD's `ARea`.

title: Cache extents per drawing revision: drawing.inspect answers at once (fixes #1079)
author: Lion-1209
body:
Fixes #1079.

**What changed**

`DocState` keeps the extents of each space in a small cache keyed by `(space, revision, doc identity)`. A cached answer is reused only while the revision **and** the `doc` `Arc` pointer are unchanged, so every edit, undo, reopen or Block Editor swap recomputes — one notch stricter than the revision signal the canvas already repaints on. Opening a drawing warms the cache with the extents the view fit computes anyway, so the first inspect after OPEN is already fast.

Readers switched to the cache: `drawing.inspect` (the loop-facing one from the issue), STATUS, and ZOOM Extents / All / Dynamic. One-shot paths (io plots, PDF/DXF writers) intentionally keep the direct walk — they run once, not in loops.

**Evidence**

Tests (`crates/engine/src/tests.rs`):
- inspect extents follow an edit and an undo, with repeated reads identical
- the cache is per space (model vs Layout1 keep separate extents)
- invalidation keys pinned directly: a bare revision bump recomputes; a different drawing swapped in at the same revision recomputes

Timing through the real MCP server on a 200k-line DXF (lines are cheap bounds; the 985k mixed-entity drawing in the issue scales these up):

| call | before-style (walk) | after |
|---|---|---|
| inspect after open | ~one full walk | **2–3 ms** (cache warmed at open) |
| inspect after an edit | — | 24 ms (correct invalidation) |
| inspect again | — | 2–3 ms |

Checks: `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine` 298/298, fmt clean, clippy clean for the touched files, ui-egui/mcp/cli compile. I couldn't find a gaps.md row for #1079, so no row updated; #1040 touches inspect's serialization layer, not this, so they should merge independently.

title: ARC continuation starts from the last picked end of a clockwise arc
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1107.

Arcs are stored counter-clockwise, so when a 3-point arc is picked clockwise the last picked point ends up as the arc's start. `curves::last_curve_end` always continued from the stored end with the CCW tangent, which is why the new arc hung off the first point instead of the last one. It now continues from whichever end is the last picked point (LASTPOINT, as AutoCAD does), leaving it in the drawing direction; otherwise nothing changes. JSON `arc.continue` now also sets the last point to its `end`, so chained continuations keep following the drawing order. Lines and polylines are untouched (`arc_continue_from_last_line` still passes).

Using LASTPOINT means an arc added through JSON (which doesn't move the last point) keeps continuing from its stored end, same as before. Happy to switch to a different source for the drawing direction if you prefer.

Validation:
- `cmd::draw2::tests::arc_continue_from_last_picked_end_of_three_point_arc` (clockwise and counter-clockwise 3-point arcs, Enter, end point): fails on main (clockwise case continues from (0,0): center (1.667, 0) instead of (3, 0)), passes here
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib draw2`, `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Status bar toggles don't cancel the running command, as F7-F12 don't
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1108.

The status bar buttons started their command with `app.start`, which cancels whatever is running, while F3 and F7-F12 already run the same toggles transparently through `session.execute` in `menus::shortcuts`. This moves that F-key path into a small `menus::run_transparent` and has the status bar toggles (Grid, Snap, Ortho, Polar, Isodraft, OTrack, Osnap, Lineweight, Transparency, Dynamic Input, Quick Properties, Annotation Visibility) go through it, so clicking one mid-LINE flips the setting and LINE keeps going, as in AutoCAD. The `ui.*` buttons (Drafting Settings, Workspace) still start their dialog as before.

One visible change: the Isometric Drafting button used to start the interactive ISODRAFT prompt ("Drafting mode?"); it now toggles isometric drafting on click, which is what `run_isodraft`'s doc says the status bar button does. Happy to switch it back to the prompt if you prefer that.

title: Center snap: hovering a circle, arc or ellipse offers its center, however far
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1112.

The Center snap only looked for a center within the aperture of the cursor, so on an open arc or a large circle it was practically unreachable: you had to aim at a point you can't see. Now, with CEN on, hovering the curve of a circle, an arc (polyline arcs included) or an ellipse offers its center: the center marker appears there and a click picks it, which is how AutoCAD finds centers from the circumference. It is the last resort in `finish()`: any snap under the cursor (Endpoint, Midpoint, Quadrant, Intersection, a deferred Tangent on the first point of a line, Nearest) still wins, so existing priorities don't change. One consequence is that with Nearest on, Nearest keeps winning on the curve; I kept that conservative, but happy to switch to the issue's "marker only, not a snap" variant, or to rank the center above Nearest, if you prefer.

Validation:
- `snap::tests::center_snaps_from_the_curve_far_from_it` (arc with its center 80 units from the cursor; CEN off, off the curve and past the arc's end give nothing; Midpoint under the cursor still wins): fails on main (`osnap` returns `None` on the arc), passes here, also alone

- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: drawing.inspect: cache a space's extents by revision (#1079)
author: william-wwh
body:
Fixes the polling cost behind #1079.

## Problem

`drawing.inspect` and `status` compute the active space's extents on every call by walking every visible entity (`Drawing::extents`, `crates/doc/src/lib.rs`). On the 985k-entity test drawing from #1079 that is about 2.5 s per call, on the UI thread. Agents poll these calls, so the cost lands over and over.

## Fix

Cache the extents on `DocState`, keyed by `(space, revision)`. `revision` is bumped on every edit, undo, redo and `touch()`, so a stale entry is never served. The first call after a change pays the walk; later calls in the same revision are a lookup.

- `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`: `DocState.extents_cache: RefCell<HashMap<Space, (u64, Bounds2)>>`, `DocState::extents_cached`.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/inquiry.rs`: `run_inspect` and `run_status` use it.

`touch()` bumps the revision for view-only changes, so the cache rebuilds a little more than it strictly must — safe, and cheap next to the walk on a large drawing.

## Scope

This is a partial fix: it removes the repeated cost of the polling calls, but the first call after a load still walks the drawing once, and the extents are not computed off the UI thread. #1079's acceptance criteria ask for `drawing.inspect` <= 100 ms after the first call, the same values as the uncached result, the same behaviour for `status`, and documentation of the cost of each diagnostic field — those are not all met here, and this PR does not claim to close the issue.

## Tests

- New `drawing_inspect_reuses_extents_until_the_drawing_changes` in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`: the cached answer equals a fresh walk, is served again without an edit, and follows an edit.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --workspace`, `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine` pass.

title: RECTANG: the other corner ignores ortho, so the rectangle keeps its area
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1113.

RECTANG's "Specify other corner point" prompt carried the first corner as a plain `base`, so with ORTHOMODE on `snap_cursor` pulled the other corner onto the horizontal or vertical through the first one: the preview disappeared, and the click was then refused with "The rectangle has no area." Like AutoCAD, ortho now leaves the other corner alone, using the same `Prompt::corner` flag that #790 added for ZOOM Window, so the preview and the picked point are both the real cursor position. Base, Dynamic Input and object snaps behave as before.

I looked at the other "corner" prompts too. ARRAYRECT's unit cell ("Specify other corner") had the same problem (refused with "The unit cell must have a width and a height."), so it gets the flag as well. The "Specify opposite corner" prompts (W/C/Box selection, REVCLOUD Rectangular, MTEXT, VPORTS/MVIEW, VIEW window, STRETCH, PLOT window, INSERT corner scale) are left as they are to keep this small; happy to switch them over here or in a follow-up if you want them to behave the same way.

Validation:
- `rectang_ortho`: both tests fail on main (the command stays at "Specify other corner point" / "Specify other corner" after the click), pass here; each checks the result is identical with ortho off
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test rectang_ortho --test zoom_window_ortho --test array_commands`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: TEXT Align and Fit by the baseline's two ends, and the typed line drawn in place (stacked on #1089)
author: Slopapalooza
body:
Stacked on #1089 (which is stacked on #1083, #1042, #1008, #994 and #954); this PR's change is the last commit. It closes gaps.md F25, which #1089 opened.

**Rebased onto main at `0b32c2e` (2026-10-19)** to clear merge conflicts; what this PR does is unchanged.

## Problem

- **Align and Fit:** TEXT treats them like the other justifications: one point, a height and a rotation. AutoCAD asks for the two ends of the baseline. Align then works out the height so the text spans the baseline, and Fit keeps the height and stretches the width factor. CADCraft's aligned and fit text got the same point as both ends, so it wasn't stretched at all.
- **Typing:** the line being typed only appears on the command line. AutoCAD types it in place on the drawing.

## Changes

- **Align and Fit** ask "Specify first endpoint of text baseline", then "Specify second endpoint of text baseline". The second point gives the rotation.
  - **Align** asks nothing more. Each line gets the height that makes it span the baseline at the style's width factor.
  - **Fit** keeps the height (asked, or a fixed-height style's) and gets the width factor that makes it span the baseline.
  - **Measuring:** lines are measured as the renderer measures them, so they span the baseline as drawn. The height or width factor is stored as AutoCAD stores it, so the Properties palette shows the real values.
  - **Further lines** go one line spacing below, along a baseline of the same length.
  - **Same point twice:** it's refused and the second end is asked again.
  - **Enter at the start point** continues aligned and fit text the same way.
- **`text {justify: "A" | "F", end?}`:** the JSON form takes the baseline's other end. Without `end`, the baseline runs along `rotation` as long as the text is at `height`, so existing calls keep working. An `end` equal to `at` is refused.
- **Typing in place:** at TEXT's "Enter text", the line typed on the command line is drawn on the canvas where it will go.

title: LEADER: annotation text height is DIMTXT x DIMSCALE, like the arrows (#1056)
author: ChristopheAwad
body:
Fixes #1056.

## Cause

`run_leader` sized the annotation MTEXT with DIMTXT alone (`crates/engine/src/cmd/annotate.rs`). AutoCAD sizes a LEADER's text as DIMTXT × DIMSCALE (the style's, else the drawing's). The leader arrows already honoured that scale; the text did not.

## Fix

- `crates/render/src/lib.rs`: `leader_scale` is now public, so arrows and text use one source of truth.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/annotate.rs`: `th = style.text_height × leader_scale(drawing, style)`.

With the issue's repro (`DIMSCALE` 25, `DIMTXT` 0.25) the MTEXT height is now 6.25 instead of 0.25.

## Tests

New `crates/engine/tests/leader_text_height.rs`, six cases:

- the issue's repro: 0.25 × 25 = 6.25, and the text offset scales with it
- default scale keeps DIMTXT (0.18)
- style DIMSCALE 0 falls back to the drawing's DIMSCALE (0.25 × 2.5 = 0.625)
- a hostile negative style scale falls back to 1
- the saved DXF carries the scaled 6.25 height
- a leader without text adds no MTEXT

All six fail on `main`.

## Verification

Local runs: engine + render full suites (1088 tests), io full suite, doc/mcp/fonts/constraints/dxf full, cli (488 + 22 tests) — all pass; `cargo xtask` fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm all pass. The `cadcraft-ui-egui` test binaries were not run locally (disk limit on the test machine); the diff does not touch the UI crate.

The issue also mentions a DWG flag 70 = 128 "user-defined text position" quirk and marks it as probably its own issue; it is out of scope here.

title: OVERKILL deletes lines and arcs lying on a polyline segment
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1120.

OVERKILL compared lines with lines and arcs with arcs, and optimized polylines on their own, but never compared a polyline's segments with other objects (it was the last item left in the F19 row after #452). So a line drawn on the side of a rectangle survived. With "Optimize segments within polylines" on (`plines`, the default), the straight segments of each polyline now join the collinear groups `lines()` already builds and its arc segments join the circle buckets of `arcs()`, both only as covers: a line or arc lying entirely on a segment (or on consecutive segments) with the same compared properties is deleted, and the polyline is kept untouched. Building on @vangel76's bucketing in #452, the work stays O(n log n).

A line that sticks out past the segment stays as it is: AutoCAD would trim or break things there depending on "Do not break polylines", which CADCraft doesn't have yet, so I left it out and narrowed the F19 row in `docs/gaps.md` to say so. Happy to switch if you'd rather have the overlapping part trimmed off the line.

Validation:
- `lines_on_polyline_segments_go` (the reporter's steps: LINE, OFFSET, RECTANG on the ends, OVERKILL; plus a line running past a corner, a line of another colour and a line over two collinear segments): fails on main (0 deleted, both lines left), passes here
- `arcs_on_polyline_segments_go` (an arc on a bulge segment goes, one sticking out of it stays): fails on main (0 deleted), passes here
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test overkill`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Dynamic blocks: a grip drag previews the reference in its own colours
author: codyvogt
body:
While a dynamic block grip is dragged, the preview now shows the reference as it will look, in its own colours, instead of everything in the preview colour.

## The problem
The preview of a dynamic grip drag is the reference re-evaluated at the cursor. It was drawn entirely in the current layer's colour, with solid fills left out. On a filled label block (red outline, white fill, red text) the preview's text was white on the drawing's white fill, and the block read as a jumble of white lines.

## What changes
- **`Interactive::preview_objects`** (engine, default empty, under the crash guard like the other steps): a command can give preview objects that keep their own properties, as entities. `Session::preview` draws them first, then the command's rubber band. The UI already builds previews with the full renderer, so nothing changes there.
- **The dynamic grip drag** (`cmd/blocks/dyngrip.rs`) gives the block's objects with the properties they draw with in the reference, as the renderer resolves a block's contents:
  - layer 0 is the reference's layer;
  - ByBlock colour, linetype, lineweight and transparency are the reference's;
  - attributes take their definition's properties, except those set on them;
  - fills are included, in the block's order, so outlines and text draw over them.
- **Over such objects the rubber band is grip blue** (#2F6BFF), so it shows over their fills whatever their colour. Otherwise, in the current layer's colour, it could vanish on a white fill.

This goes beyond AutoCAD, which drags a plainer preview. The owner asked for it because it keeps the block readable while it changes.

## Tests
`crates/engine/tests/dynamic_grips.rs`: `a_grip_drag_previews_the_reference_in_its_own_colours`. With the DOOR reference on its own layer, the preview's block objects (on layer 0 in the block) come first, on the reference's layer; the rubber band follows, on the current layer, in grip blue.

title: TRIM highlights only the piece a click removes, EXTEND the extended object
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1118.

Stacked on #1092 (Shift+click does the other one in TRIM/EXTEND): until that one is merged, this diff also shows its commit. The commit for this issue is the last one.

At "Select object to trim", the canvas used the generic rollover highlight, which always lights up the whole object under the cursor, so you couldn't see which piece a click would remove. The trim geometry in `modify.rs` now has a pure step, `trimmed`, that returns what a pick keeps and what it removes without touching the drawing. `trim` uses it to replace the object, and TRIM's new `Interactive::highlight` uses it to tell the canvas which part to highlight. With no cutting edge in Quick mode (the click erases the object), the whole object is highlighted, as before. EXTEND works the same way: `extend` got a pure `extended` step, and the highlight shows the object as the click leaves it, extension included. With Shift held, the highlight follows the command the click will run (#1092). Lines, arcs, circles, polylines, ellipses and splines (open and closed) all go through the code the click itself uses.

On the canvas side, when the command returns a part, the hover look is drawn on that part instead of on the whole object. Working the part out means running the trim against every cutting edge (every object in Quick mode), so it is cached with the rest of the hover state: it is computed again only when the object, the cursor, Shift, the zoom, the drawing or the prompt changes, never on frames where the cursor is at rest. I kept the change to the hover code since #1061 is reorganising `canvas.rs`; happy to rebase onto it if it lands first.

In Standard mode, picking an object that no edge crosses still highlights the whole object, as it did before: nothing would change there, so I left it alone. Happy to switch if you'd rather show nothing in that case.

title: Quick Properties shows AutoCAD's text, mtext and dimension rows (stacked on #1121)
author: Slopapalooza
body:
Stacked on #1121 (which is stacked on #1089, #1083, #1042, #1008, #994 and #954); this PR's change is the last commit.

**Rebased onto main at `0b32c2e` (2026-10-19)** to clear merge conflicts; what this PR does is unchanged. Quick Properties keeps #1275's block rotation, and text rotation comes from the `direction` rows (#994).

## Problem

Quick Properties (QPMODE) has its own few rows for text: Contents, Height and Rotation for TEXT, and Contents and Text height for MTEXT. A dimension gets only Text override. They're edited one object at a time, so several selected texts get no text rows at all. AutoCAD's defaults are:

- **TEXT and MTEXT:** Layer, Contents, Style, Annotative, Justify, Height and Rotation.
- **Dimensions:** Dim style, Annotative, Measurement and Text override.

## Changes

- **Text, mtext and dimensions:** Quick Properties shows the rows `properties.describe` flags `quick` (#954), which are AutoCAD's defaults:
  - **TEXT:** Layer, Contents, Style, Annotative, Justification, Height and Rotation (Text height for MTEXT).
  - **Dimensions:** Layer, Dim style, Annotative, Measurement (read-only) and Text override.
  - **Shared code:** the rows are drawn and edited by the Properties palette's row code (#994). Units, `*VARIES*` for several objects of one type, fixed-height notes and refused values behave the same in both.
  - **Other objects** (lines, circles, arcs, polylines, blocks) keep Quick Properties' own rows.
- **Palette rows:**
  - The described rows give their labels to screen readers; the labels are painted text, so AccessKit didn't see them.
  - The Layer row gets a drop-down of the drawing's layers.
  - Applying a described edit is now one function, shared by the palette and Quick Properties.
- **Docs:** gaps.md U14 is narrowed to the rows CADCraft doesn't model yet; ui-parity.md.

## Limits

- The rows aren't customisable: AutoCAD sets them in the CUI, and CADCraft uses the defaults.

author: Blade-Punisher
body:

title: Middle-button pan follows the frame's pointer events, so a drag isn't lost on slow frames
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1131.

The middle-button pan only looked at the button state and the pointer position at the end of each frame. On a heavy drawing frames are slow, and eframe hands over a whole drag in one go: when the release lands in the same frame as the moves, the button already reads as up when the frame ends and all the movement is dropped. The wheel sums its raw events (`wheel_zoom_points`, #660), so it always zooms, which is the "pan doesn't work, only scroll-zoom does" asymmetry in the report, and why it depends on the file and on the zoom level (zooming out on a big drawing makes frames slower). The pan now walks the frame's pointer events in order, like the wheel: a middle press over the drawing starts it (same `inside` check as before, so a press over a floating panel still doesn't pan), each move while it is on adds its delta, and the release ends it. At normal frame rates the result is the same as before, since the moves add up to the end-of-frame position.

This makes the pan correct on heavy drawings, not smooth: each slow frame still lands as one jump. The frame time itself is #1071, with #997 and #1012 working on it.

I also dropped the `i.focused` check from the pan (added with docking in e09fb50, without a test of its own): the wheel zooms in an unfocused window, and a middle click doesn't focus the window on macOS, so the pan silently didn't start there. A pan in progress still ends when the window loses focus. Happy to switch back if the check was there for a reason I missed.

The change stays inside the pan block of `canvas.rs`, since #1061 (splitting `canvas.rs` into modules), #1059 and #1012 touch the same file; happy to rebase onto any of them if they land first.

- `middle_pan_slow_frames::a_middle_drag_that_ends_within_one_slow_frame_still_pans`: fails on main (`View { center: (100, 70), height: 220 }` unchanged after a 100 px drag), passes here

title: TEXT's own Backwards and Upside down (DXF 71 generation flags) (stacked on #1128)
author: Slopapalooza
body:
Stacked on #1128 (which is stacked on #1121, #1089, #1083, #1042, #1008, #994 and #954); this PR's change is the last commit.

**Rebased onto main at `0b32c2e` (2026-10-19)** to clear merge conflicts; what this PR does is unchanged. The one `Text` built since this PR opened (in `crates/io/tests/acad_interop.rs`) gets the new fields' defaults.

## Problem

In AutoCAD, TEXT, ATTDEF and ATTRIB each have their own Backwards and Upside down (DXF group 71, "text generation flags"). New text takes them from its text style; changing the style later doesn't change existing text. CADCraft only had the style's flags:

- **Reading files:** a file's per-object flags were ignored. A backwards text in a normal style was drawn normally, and normal text in a backwards style was drawn backwards.
- **Saving:** the flags weren't written.
- **Properties palette:** no rows for them (gaps.md U14).

## Changes

- **Model:** `Text::backwards` and `Text::upside_down`, both defaulting to false in serde. ATTDEF and ATTRIB share `Text`.
- **DXF:**
  - Read from group 71: 2 backwards, 4 upside down. Only the object's own groups are read, before any embedded MTEXT, whose 71 is the attachment point.
  - Written after the style (group 7) when set; flags of 0 aren't written, as AutoCAD omits them.
- **New text:** TEXT (typed and JSON) and ATTDEF take the flags from their style. ATTDEF now builds its text the way TEXT does, so it also takes the style's width factor and obliquing angle.
- **Rendering:**
  - Text is drawn from its own flags.
  - The approximate extents box mirrors with them, so Zoom Extents frames mirrored text.
  - Text in complex linetypes keeps the style's flags.
- **Properties palette:** TEXT has a Misc group with Upside down and Backwards, from `properties.describe`, which shows `*VARIES*` across several texts. `properties.set` takes `backwards` and `upsideDown`.
- **Docs:** gaps.md U14 is narrowed to MTEXT's mask, direction and defined height; file-format-parity.md has the TEXT r…

title: Dynamic Input: the CIRCLE radius prompt shows one distance field, not X/Y
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1135.

At "Specify radius of circle" Dynamic Input showed the pointer boxes, because nothing told it the prompt wants a distance: X/Y with DYNPIFORMAT=1 (as in the screenshot), distance and angle otherwise. A value Tab-locked in X then became a point, not a radius. Prompts now say so with `Prompt::distance()`, and Dynamic Input shows one length field from the base point instead, the dimensional input @vangel76 built for grips in #527, with the prompt and its down-arrow options (Diameter) kept beside the cursor. Enter sends the typed value (or the one Tab locked) to the command as a number, so the commands keep their own checks: a radius of zero is still refused, a negative PLINE arc radius still gives the major arc.

Marked as distance prompts: CIRCLE radius and diameter, CIRCLE Ttr radius, POLYGON radius, and PLINE arc radius, chord length and line length. I left the isometric circle radius out (it's measured on the isoplane, not straight from the centre) and the ELLIPSE other-axis distance too; happy to add them, or others, if you'd like.

I didn't touch `docs/ui-parity.md`, since #819 is re-auditing it.

Validation:

It checks the centre prompt still shows X/Y, the radius prompt shows one field with the live radius, and `25` Enter draws a circle of radius 25, with DYNPIFORMAT 1 and 0

title: A fixed point stays put when its grip is dragged: Fix locks the position it had before the edit
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1134.

@grandixximo found that a Fix on a line's end didn't hold it: the grip still dragged the end around. A Fix keeps no position of its own. The solver locks the parameters at whatever values they have, so after a grip edit it locked the point where the drag had left it. The post-command pass in `after_command` also saw nothing to do, since every residual was zero. Now, before checking whether the constraints hold, `cs::restore_fixed` puts each fixed reference back where the drawing had it before the command, and then the usual re-solve runs. Dragging the grip of a fixed end leaves it in place, and the free end still moves. It only touches Fixes that already existed before the command, on objects whose shape didn't change. A Fix on a derived point (a midpoint, which the solver anchors instead of locking) is left as it was. Happy to change that, or to reject the edit with a message instead of quietly holding the point, if that's closer to what you want.

The other point raised in the issue (typing a user parameter name) isn't in this PR.

Validation:
- `fix_holds_grips` (new): fails on main (`the fixed start moved to (3, 4)`), passes here
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test post_command_passes --test constraint_geometry --test constraint_infer --test grip_options --test dynamic_grips`, `--lib constraints`; `cargo test -p cadcraft-constraints --lib tests`

title: Angular constraint between two lines holds the angle it draws, whichever way the lines run
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1134: the angular constraint quadrant from @grandixximo's last screenshot (100° drawn as roughly 80°). The other points in the issue are handled separately.

A two-line angular constraint measured the angle between the lines' start-to-end directions, but the dimension is drawn between the rays from the vertex to each line's far end. When a line is drawn towards the vertex its direction points the other way, so the solver held the supplement: you type 100 and the drawn angle settles at 80. The constraint now measures those same rays (the far end of each line is read from the geometry when the constraint is interpreted, just like the existing sign), so the value offered at the prompt, the value held by the solver and the arc on screen always agree. Nothing changes in the stored data or in files.

AutoCAD lets you choose the quadrant from where you place the dimension. Here the drawn quadrant is always the far-ends one, so I matched the solver to that rather than adding a new placement step. Happy to switch to a stored quadrant if you'd prefer that.

Validation:
- `dcangular_constrains_the_drawn_angle_whichever_way_the_lines_run` (engine): fails on main (offers 101.31 at the prompt; with that check removed, the drawn angle settles at 80°), passes here with the second line drawn either towards the vertex or away from it
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-constraints --lib` angle/dimensional tests, `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-constraints -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Parameters Manager: double-click a name to rename the parameter and every expression that uses it
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1134.

In @grandixximo's screenshot the Parameters Manager is open with `user1` selected, and what he typed ("testte") ended up on the command line. The name column was a plain label, and there was no way to rename a parameter at all: `PARAMETERS` could only set an expression or delete. This adds both halves, as in AutoCAD:

- **Engine.** `parameters {name, rename: newName}` renames a user parameter or a dimensional constraint's name, and rewrites every expression that uses it (user parameters and dimensional constraints). It replaces whole names only, so renaming `d1` leaves `d10` and `1e1` alone. Taken names, invalid names (`1x`, `pi`) and unknown parameters are refused and change nothing. It's one undo step, like the other parameter edits. The `{name, rename}` form follows what MLSTYLE already uses.
- **UI.** Double-clicking a name in the dialog turns it into a text field that has focus and the old name selected. Enter renames and Esc cancels. While the field has focus, keys stay out of the command line, through the same `egui_wants_keyboard_input` check the other dialog fields rely on.

Clicking away from the field cancels the rename instead of committing it. Happy to switch that if you'd rather it commit, like the expression column does.

title: Constraints: the settings checkboxes show or hide all, dropping per-object exceptions
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1134.

Ticking "Show dynamic constraints" in Constraint Settings could hide the very constraints you had just shown. `constraintsettings` only flipped `dims_visible` and left `dim_exceptions` alone, and the overlay draws a constraint when `dims_visible != (it's in the exceptions)`. So after Hide All and then showing one constraint with DCDISPLAY, ticking the box showed every constraint except that one. "Show constraint bars" had the same problem with `bars_visible` and `bar_exceptions`.

Now, when `dimsVisible` or `barsVisible` actually changes, the matching exception list is cleared, which is what Show All / Hide All already do in `set_bars`. Sending the current value again leaves the exceptions alone.

title: Drawing history: a version on every save, a palette to browse them, gzip and restore
author: kostyk348
body:
Ports a small AutoLISP revision-history toolkit I use in AutoCAD (`OMNI.lsp`: snapshots of the drawing, a listing of them, an overlay diff of an older revision, a toggle, a clear, and spatial note markers) into CADCraft as native commands — and takes it further, because here it is not tied to DWG or to a Windows file system.

**Since the review:** a version is written by every save without being asked, the history is browsable in a palette, versions are gzipped, and a version can be put back. A history write can never fail or delay a save.

![CADCraft with the Drawing History palette open beside the drawing: the saves and the named milestone of the plan, with Open, Compare and Restore for the selected version](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kostyk348/cadcraft/omni-drawing-history/docs/images/ui-drawing-history.png)

*The screenshot is the running app, not a mock-up: a plan saved three times and named once (`OMNI-SNAP` → `approved`), then the palette opened with `VERSIONS` typed at the command line. Every row is a version the app wrote by itself.*

## Two kinds of version

- **Every save leaves one behind**, without being asked. `SAVE`, `QSAVE` and `SAVEAS` write one when the drawing differs from what its file held — the unsaved-changes flag is the test — so the history is a timeline of the saves you already make. Those are filed under the description `save`. A save of an unchanged drawing adds nothing, and neither does a save after an edit and its undo: the drawing comes back to what the newest version already holds (the comparison is byte-exact against the stored copy, so it costs one `memcmp`).
- **`OMNI-SNAP` takes a named milestone** of the drawing as it is right now — unsaved changes included, the file on disk untouched — for a state you want to name and come back to.

The kind is the description: `save` is a save's version, anything else is a milestone. Timed autosave (versions on a clock) is a separate PR — the timed autosave that exists (`SAVETIME`, `SAVE…

title: Windows: single instance file handoff, window state persistence, and Full Screen (F11) support
author: fromhd
body:
## Summary
This PR brings quality-of-life desktop windowing improvements to CADCraft:

1. **Windows Single Instance & File Handoff (\pps/cadcraft/src/single_instance.rs\)**:
   - Implements local named-socket IPC single-instance claim on Windows (similar to \pdfcraft\).
   - When opening DWG/DXF files from Windows File Explorer while CADCraft is already running, file paths are forwarded to the existing process and opened in new tabs rather than spawning endless separate application windows.

2. **Window State Persistence & Full Screen Support**:

title: Selection cycling: a click over overlapping objects lists them, Shift+Space steps through them
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1143, fixes #1145.

SELECTIONCYCLING was only an on/off flag that nothing read, so a click on overlapping objects always took the nearest one. This adds `select::pick_all` (every object under the pick box, nearest first, so the first is what `pick` already chooses) and uses it on the canvas the way AutoCAD's variable describes it: with SELECTIONCYCLING 2 a click over more than one object opens a small list beside the cursor, one row per object with its type and layer; hovering a row highlights its object and clicking it selects it (or hands it to the command at "Select objects"), anywhere else or Escape closes the list. With 1 only the badge shows over overlapping objects, with 0 (or turned off) clicks pick as before. SELECTIONCYCLING is now a real system variable: negative while off, as in AutoCAD, so the existing SELECTIONCYCLING toggle keeps the display mode it turns back on; the initial value stays off (-2), as in AutoCAD.

For #1145: Autodesk documents Shift+Space as selection cycling's temporary override, which works even with the toggle off and shows no badge or list. Here it steps the hover highlight to the next object under the still cursor, and a click selects the highlighted one; moving off the pick box ends it. That Space doesn't reach the command line, so it doesn't repeat the last command.

The list and the Shift+Space highlight only live as long as what they were made for: a command starting or ending, a new prompt, an edit (undo, erase) or a pan/zoom drops them, so the next click is a normal click (a command's first point is never swallowed), and a cycled pick of an object that is no longer in the drawing selects nothing.

Not included: Ctrl+W as the toggle shortcut (Cmd+W is Close here), and the "Selection" title bar of AutoCAD's list. Happy to change the row layout or the ordering (nearest first, topmost among equals) if you prefer something else.

title: MTEXT background mask and drawing direction (stacked on #1136)
author: Slopapalooza
body:
Stacked on #1136 (which is stacked on #1128, #1121, #1089, #1083, #1042, #1008, #994 and #954); this PR's change is the last commit.

**Rebased onto main at `0b32c2e` (2026-10-19)** to clear merge conflicts; what this PR does is unchanged. TXT2MTXT, added since this PR opened, makes its MTEXT left to right without a mask.

## Problem

AutoCAD's MTEXT can have a background mask: a box behind the text, filled with the drawing's background or a color, which hides lines under the text. CADCraft didn't model it:

- **Reading:** masks in other programs' files were dropped.
- **Drawing:** text over geometry wasn't masked.
- **Properties palette:** no row (gaps.md U14).

The drawing direction (DXF 72) was always written as left to right, whatever the file said.

## Changes

- **Model:** `MText::background: Option<MTextMask>` and `MText::direction: MTextDirection` (left to right, top to bottom, by style).

  - **45** fill box scale, the border offset factor, limited to 1–5 as in AutoCAD's dialog.
  - **72** drawing direction.
  - **Reading:** from the MTEXT's own groups, not those of an embedded object.
  - **Writing:** after the line spacing.
  - **Bad values:** they fall back to the defaults.
- **Rendering:** a box behind the text.
