title: A copied group stays a group: COPY, MIRROR, ARRAY and paste make an unnamed group of the copies
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1151.

COPY, MIRROR, ARRAY (and ROTATE/SCALE/grip edits with Copy) copy the selected objects one by one in `transform_entities`, and PASTECLIP does the same from the clipboard, so the group the objects belonged to was never copied and the copies came out as loose objects. AutoCAD gives a copied group a new unnamed group (`*A1`, `*A2`...) holding the copies, so this does the same: when every member of a group is among the copied objects, the copies become an unnamed group with the original's description and selectable flag. A group copied only in part makes no group, and each copy of a multiple COPY or each array item is its own group. Which groups are held whole is worked out once per command (`GroupCopies`), before the copies, so a large ARRAY doesn't walk the drawing's groups again for every item. For paste, the clipboard now carries the groups held whole, and pasting maps them onto the new handles. The xdata part of the issue is already covered by #890 (thanks @mattlafy); its tests still pass here.

Keeping the description on the copy is my choice; happy to switch to an empty one if you prefer.

Not covered yet, to keep this small: the system clipboard (DXF text between windows) does not carry groups, and copying with grip stretch (Stretch mode with Copy) makes loose objects as before.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test group_copies`: fails on main (no new group after COPY, MIRROR, ARRAY or paste), passes here; includes an ARRAY of a group with 2000 items (2000 groups)
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test groups --test group_selection --test xdata_follows_entity --test clipboard --test assoc_array`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- docs/gaps.md F16 narrowed

title: Plots draw sub-resolution dash patterns as continuous lines (part of #1068)
author: graficaeusebio-cloud
body:
Part of #1068. Thanks @cyfung1031 for the measurements and the synthetic control.

**Problem.** Plot builds (PDF, PNG/plotter, PREVIEW) set `min_dash = 0`, so every dash of every dashed line becomes a primitive, however small it is on paper. In the #1068 control (lines whose 0.75-unit pattern repeats 40,000 times, fitted to the sheet) a period is about 0.007 mm on paper, and each line still turns into 40,000 primitives.

**Change.** The plot builds pass their chord tolerance as `min_dash`. `linetype::apply` (and the hatch and multiline paths that use `min_dash`) already draw a run whose pattern repeats in less than `min_dash` as one continuous line. Plotting text detail does not change, because the builder ignores `min_dash` for glyphs while plotting.
- PDF: tolerance 0.05 mm on paper (`crates/io/src/pdf.rs`).
- Raster plots (PNG/plotter): a fifth of a pixel, the same value they already use to flatten curves (`crates/io/src/plotter.rs`).
- PREVIEW: half a pixel (`crates/engine/src/cmd/exchange.rs`).

Dashes that are visible on paper still plot one by one. The threshold is the same one already accepted for flattening arcs, so the output does not lose anything at that tolerance.

**Not covered.** This does not change the display list's memory per primitive or stream the sheet. A drawing whose dashes are visible on paper still builds every dash. The rest of #1068 is left open.

**Tests** (`crates/io/tests/plot_subresolution_dashes.rs`)
- 10 lines with 40,000 periods each, fitted to the sheet: the uncompressed PDF has at most 20 path segments (400,000 on `main` e707ab4).
- 10 lines with 20 visible periods each: every dash is still a separate path segment.

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Layouts plot their page setup's window or extents
author: halu0915
body:
## Problem

A layout's page setup can plot a **window** of paper space (PLOTSETTINGS plot type 4, corners in groups 48/49 and 140/141) or its **extents** instead of the whole sheet. CADCraft ignored the window (it wasn't read) and always plotted a layout's whole sheet at 1:1, and PAGESETUP refused `window`/`extents` for layouts as "not available yet" (#491/#597).

That breaks a very common office setup: several title blocks side by side in one layout tab, each plotted through its own window with "Fit to paper". On such files every layout plot came out as the same 1:1 corner of paper space (typically an empty corner or a fragment of the first frame) instead of the sheet the page setup points at.

## Approach

- **doc**: `PageSetup::window: Option<[f64; 4]>` (lower-left, upper-right in the plotted space's units; omitted from JSON when absent).
- **io / DXF+DWG**: read 48/49/140/141 into `window` (finite, within ±1e12, with an area, corners ordered; otherwise `None`) and write it back instead of zeros. DWG goes through the existing acadrust bridge; a DXF→DWG→DXF round trip keeps the window.
- **io / plotting** (`pdf.rs`, `plotter.rs`): `layout_frame` resolves a layout's plot area (the plot's `plotArea`, else the page setup's): `window` uses the plot's `window` or the page setup's, `extents` the layout's extents, anything else the whole sheet as before. A framed layout is placed exactly like a model-space plot (shared `placement`), using the page setup's *Fit to paper*, scale and *Center the plot* unless the plot overrides them, and **clipped to the window** so neighbouring title blocks don't print:
  - PDF: the content clip rectangle is the window as placed on the sheet, intersected with the printable area.
  - PNG: `raster::blank_outside` paints the background outside the window after rendering.
  - SVG: the layout export shows the window (or extents) instead of the sheet.
- **engine**: `pagesetup {window, plotArea: layout|extents|window}` for layouts (`window` needs …

title: Block references with a tilted extrusion are placed at their WCS point (#1158)
author: graficaeusebio-cloud
body:
Fixes #1158.

**Problem.** A block reference with a tilted extrusion (block plane not parallel to XY) was left as read: its OCS insertion point counted as WCS. In a drawing far from the origin (UTM coordinates) the OCS point is millions of units away, so `extents` took it in and `convert`/fitted plots shrank the drawing to a dot (0.02 % non-white pixels on a real 10,086-entity drawing).

**Change** (`crates/io/src/dxf_read.rs`, INSERT). For a tilted extrusion, map the insertion point to the WCS and take the rotation from the OCS x axis turned by group 50, projected on XY. The block is still drawn flat: `Insert` cannot hold the 3D transform, and that is unchanged. Mirrored references (extrusion ≈ (0,0,−1)) and the default extrusion take the same paths as before. DWG goes through the same reader.

On the real drawing above, extents go from (−9.2e6, −9.0e6)–(9.6e6, 9.6e6) to the drawing's own (562377, 9567237)–(563868, 9569767), and the fitted PDF shows it (10.45 % non-white).

**Test** (`crates/io/src/tests.rs`, `tilted_insert_extrusion_maps_point_and_direction_to_wcs`): extrusion (0.6, 0, 0.8), OCS (2000, −800, 600) → WCS (1000, 2000, 0), rotation 90°, extents of a 2-unit line in the block = (1000, 2000)–(1000, 2002).

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: BLOCK: a `keep` value other than convert, retain or delete is an error, not a delete
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #935.

## What was wrong

`make_block` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/blocks.rs` erased the selected objects for every `keep` value except `"retain"`, and converted them to a reference only for `"convert"`. A misspelt value such as `keep: "retian"` therefore succeeded and removed the objects from model space without inserting the new block.

## What changed

- `keep` is parsed into a `Keep` enum (`Convert`, `Retain`, `Delete`) before any mutation. A value that is not documented returns an error that names the three accepted values; the drawing, the selection and the undo history stay as they were.
- The documented values are accepted in any case (`"Retain"`, `"DELETE"`, `" convert "`).
- BLOCK and -BLOCK share the check; the interactive BLOCK / -BLOCK forms pass the enum directly.

## Tests

`crates/engine/tests/block_keep.rs`:
- five undocumented values, through BLOCK and -BLOCK, each an error that leaves objects, blocks, selection and undo depth unchanged and defines no block;
- the three documented values in mixed case, with their expected results (reference or not, objects kept or erased).

`cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the existing `dash_block` tests pass.

title: EXPLODE keeps array levels, row elevations and a reference's Z (fixes #917)
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #917.

Exploding an associative array placed the source objects through the planar block transform only, so items on different levels or row elevations ended up at the source's own Z. A plain block reference inserted at a height lost it too.

`EntityKind::transform_z(scale, offset)` in `crates/doc/src/entity.rs` moves every point's elevation; EXPLODE applies it after the planar transform, for array items (`explode_array`) and ordinary references (`explode_kind`). A nested reference's Z scale is not multiplied again, since the planar transform already carries its uniform factor there.

Tests: `explode_keeps_level_and_row_elevations` (two rows, two levels, row elevation, then a SCALEd array) and `explode_insert_keeps_elevations` (insert at z = 4 with Z scale 3).

title: AREA, Object: an open polyline's perimeter is its length, without the closing side
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1168.

`object_area` measured every LWPOLYLINE as closed, so on an open polyline the closing side ended up in the perimeter as well as in the area. When the perimeter is calculated that line length is ignored." So the area keeps the closed geometry, and the perimeter is now the length of the polyline as drawn. Typing points (`AREA` without Object) is unchanged: there the help says the closing line *is* added to the perimeter. Thanks @EP995LAB for the clear repro.

title: DIMRADIUS/DIMDIAMETER: a location outside the circle puts the text at that point
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1170.

title: AutoLISP entity lists hold angles in radians, as entget does in AutoCAD
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1165.

Thanks @EP995LAB for the precise report. The LISP bridge passes the DXF groups through as the file writer produces them, so the angle groups 50–58 kept the file's degrees. AutoCAD's group code table says those groups are degrees in DXF files and radians through AutoLISP, so `entget` now converts them to radians and `entmake`/`entmod` convert back, which also covers the writing direction the report left open. `ssget` filters go through the same list, so they compare in radians too. The one exception is MTEXT, whose 50 after the column type (75) is a column height, not an angle; those stay as they are. `docs/autolisp.md` says so now.

Validation:
- `lisp::tests::entity_lists_hold_angles_in_radians` (ARC from the command line, TEXT and MTEXT through entmake, an ANSI31 hatch, entmod of an arc's end angle, an ssget filter on 51): fails on main (`(assoc 51 …)` is 90.0, not pi/2), passes here

title: BREAK opens a closed polyline instead of refusing it
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1173.

`break_entity` only had an arm for open LWPOLYLINEs, so a closed one fell through to "Cannot break that object." It now handles the closed case the same way the circle arm already does: the stretch from the first point to the second, following the vertex order, is removed, and what remains becomes one open polyline that starts at the second point and ends at the first. With the drawing from the issue, `BREAK 50,0 100,30` leaves 100,30 → 100,60 → 0,60 → 0,0 → 50,0, which matches what @EP995LAB saw in the reference app. It walks a doubled segment list, the way TRIM already handles closed polylines (#726). Breaking a closed polyline at a single point is still refused, just like a circle. I followed the vertex order rather than the geometric counterclockwise direction. Autodesk's BREAK reference only gives the counterclockwise rule for circles, and the issue's rectangle is drawn counterclockwise, so the two readings agree there. Happy to switch if you know of a case where they differ. I also updated the BREAK row in `docs/geometry-parity.md`.

Validation:
- `break_closed_polyline` (new): both tests fail on main ("Cannot break that object." / BREAK stays at the second-point prompt) and pass here, also run alone with `--test-threads=1`
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test pedit_splinedit --test break_join_locked_layers --test prompt_keywords`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: FILLET and CHAMFER keep each line's start and end
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1178.

`fillet_lines` rebuilt both lines as (kept end, corner point), so any line whose start was the end near the corner came out reversed, with FILLET and CHAMFER alike, at any radius or distance. Now only the corner end moves and each line keeps its start and end, as @EP995LAB observed in AutoCAD. The line-and-arc path (`trim_for_fillet`) already did this, so the two paths now behave the same way.

Validation:
- `fillet_and_chamfer_keep_each_line_direction` (FILLET R 0 / R 10, CHAMFER D 0 0 / D 10 10, both lines drawn either way, checks start and end of each by handle): fails on main (`FILLET R 0`: second line comes out as (120,100)-(120,0)), passes here

- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: Select objects accepts keywords with a leading underscore (_L, _ALL, _W…)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1172.

Since #855 the command line drops a leading underscore when it matches a prompt's own keywords, but the "Select objects" modes are read further down (`preprocess_selection`, `SelectMode::from_keyword`, `SelectPhase::feed`) and never saw it stripped, so `_L`, `_ALL`, `_P`, `_F`, `_WP`, `_CP`, `_R`, `_A`, `_U`, `_SI` were "*Invalid selection*" and `_W`/`_C` only worked by luck as an implicit window. Now the underscore is dropped from typed text at "Select objects" (not inside a mode, so a group name starting with `_` is left alone), the Previous/Last/ALL check that beats a command keyword (HATCH's "picK") looks past it too, and STRETCH, which reads its own "Select objects", does the same. Thanks @EP995LAB for the clear report.

Validation:
- `select_underscore_keywords` (new): every keyword above, plus STRETCH `_C`/`_L`, gives the same drawing as the plain keyword; on main 13 of the ERASE/MOVE cases differ (`_L` ends MOVE and `0,0` becomes an unknown command, `_ALL` erases nothing), and at HATCH `_P` turns into "picK internal point". Passes here.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine` on `selection_modes`, `select_keywords`, `stretch_select`, `stretch`, `group_selection`, `prompt_keywords`, `--lib machines`, `--lib lisp`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: New metric drawings get metric Standard multileader and table styles
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1171.

`Drawing::new_metric` already swaps in the metric header (TEXTSIZE 2.5) and the ISO-25 dimension style, but it kept `MLeaderStyle::default()` and `TableStyle::default()`, which are the inch values, so a new multileader or table in a millimetre drawing came out with 0.18 text. This adds `MLeaderStyle::metric()` and `TableStyle::metric()` next to `DimStyle::iso25()` and uses them for the Standard styles of a new metric drawing. The imperial drawing and the DXF reader's fallbacks are unchanged. Thanks @EP995LAB for the clear report.

The values: text and arrowheads 2.5 like ISO-25; landing gap 0.625 (ISO-25's DIMGAP, like the inch style reuses 0.09); landing length 5.0 (twice the text height, the same ratio as the inch 0.36); table cell margin 1.0 (what the metric table fixtures in `io/tests` already use). Happy to switch any of these if you'd rather follow different metric defaults.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-doc --lib new_metric_drawing_has_metric_multileader_and_table_styles`: fails on main (`left: (0.18, 0.18)`, `right: (2.5, 2.5)`), passes here; it also checks that a new imperial drawing keeps the 0.18 styles
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-doc --lib tests::`, plus the io multileader/table/annotative round-trip tests and `-p cadcraft-engine --test annotative`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-doc --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Pick a wide polyline on the edges of its band, not only its centre line
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1176.

`hit_polylines` measured a lightweight polyline only along its centre line, so the band a width draws was never hit: a click on its edge picked nothing, and a crossing box touching only the band didn't select it either. A wide polyline is now also hit on the edges of the triangles it is drawn with (taken from the same display list the renderer builds, as the pattern-hatch case already does), which gives the sides, ends, joints and diagonals you observed in the reference app, for constant and tapered widths. Window and fence selection use the same polylines, so they follow too; window "entirely inside" already used the band extents from #127.

I kept the centre line pickable, so a click inside the band on it still selects the polyline, where the reference app would not. Dropping it for exact parity is a one-line change, happy to switch if you prefer.

One thing I haven't covered with a test: the issue says AutoCAD picks a wide polyline inside a block the same way. Block references go through the `Insert` branch, which reads the band's triangles as a polyline in sequence, so the start side of the band may still not pick there. Happy to add that here if you'd like.

Validation:
- `select::wide_polyline_pick_tests` (constant width from the issue's PLINE, and a 0→10 taper): fails on main (`edge of the band at 25,5`), passes here; also run alone with `--test-threads=1`
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib select::`, `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: JOIN with a single arc or elliptical arc offers cLose: the arc becomes its circle, the elliptical arc its full ellipse
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1175.

When the selection held a single arc, JOIN went straight to the two-object join and refused it, so the Close option AutoCAD offers there was missing. Per the [JOIN reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-Core/files/GUID-4D2A28C3-3E7F-4830-BE6A-7C9907C95488.htm) ("The Close option converts the source arc into a circle" / "...the source elliptical arc into an ellipse"), a lone arc or open elliptical arc now gets "Select arcs to join to source or [cLose]:" (or "Select elliptical arcs ..."). `L` makes it its circle or full ellipse, keeping its handle. Arcs picked at that prompt still join on Enter as before, and Enter alone gives the old refusal. The JSON form takes `close: true` with the same rule, and refuses anything other than one arc or elliptical arc. The elliptical-arc merge from #469 is untouched. The echo after Close is my own wording, happy to switch.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test join_close`: all 4 fail on main (no cLose prompt after `JOIN 80,50` + Enter; `close: true` ignored), pass here, also alone with `--test-threads=1`

title: Holding Shift overrides ortho while it is held, as in AutoCAD
author: mxx-kor
body:
## Why

I've used AutoCAD in real work, and this is a feature I needed when drawing plans. F8 toggles ortho mode, but while drafting I constantly need to switch it on or off for just a moment, and this is super necessary for working quickly. I used Shift because that's the key AutoCAD itself uses for this: holding Shift temporarily overrides ortho, and releasing it restores the previous state.

## What changed

- `Session::snap_cursor` (`crates/engine/src/snap/tracking.rs`): while Shift is held, ortho is flipped for that cursor update (`orthomode ^= shift`, on a local copy of the settings).
  - Ortho off + Shift held → ortho on
  - Ortho on + Shift held → ortho off
- The saved ORTHOMODE setting never changes, so the status bar keeps showing the real state.
- The UI already passed the Shift state to the engine (`CursorQuery.shift`, used by POLARMODE 8 "Shift to acquire"), so no UI code changed.
- Docs: Ortho row and revision history in `docs/ui-parity.md`.

## What to check

1. Run `LINE` and pick a first point.
2. Ortho off (default): move the cursor and the rubber band is free. Hold Shift and it locks horizontal/vertical. Release Shift and it is free again.
3. Press F8 to turn ortho on: move the cursor and it is horizontal/vertical. Hold Shift and it is free. The status-bar Ortho button stays on.
4. Polar on (F10): holding Shift applies ortho instead of the polar tracking path.
5. Not affected: prompts with no base point, and the second corner of ZOOM Window (#787).

## Tests

Added to `crates/engine/tests/snap_tracking.rs`:
- `shift_overrides_ortho_while_held`
- `shift_ortho_override_wins_over_polar`

Both tests fail without the change and pass with it. `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: LTSCALE typed at the command line asks for the scale factor
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1194.

`ltscale` only had its JSON form (`{scale}`), so typing LTSCALE (or LTS) at the command line ran it with no parameters and stopped on "`scale` (number) is required". #799 made bare variable names start SETVAR, but left LTSCALE alone because it is also a command, and it called that out as a separate decision. This gives the command a typed prompt, the same way PICKSTYLE has one: "Enter new linetype scale factor <current>:", a positive number sets LTSCALE and echoes "Regenerating model.", Enter keeps the current value, and zero, negatives or text are refused and asked again. The JSON form and the `lts` alias are unchanged.

The refusal message ("Requires a positive number.") is my wording; happy to switch to whatever reads better.

Validation:
- `typed_ltscale_asks_for_the_scale` (crates/engine/src/tests.rs): fails on main (`BadParams { cmd: "ltscale", msg: "`scale` (number) is required" }`), passes here

title: Select: pick text on its letters, and blocks, dimensions and multileaders on what they draw, not their empty boxes
author: EP995LAB
body:
A click picked a block reference, a dimension or a multileader anywhere along the outline of its bounding rectangle, a TEXT anywhere inside its box and an MTEXT anywhere inside its defined column, however short its words; a crossing window anywhere inside those boxes selected them. The text inside a block could not be picked at all. In AutoCAD a click on empty space picks nothing: only the line, the object's drawing or the letters under the cursor. On a real floor plan (a DWG I can't share) door labels typed with a column wider than their words took clicks meant for the door leaves.

**AutoCAD** (black-box, AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, synthetic drawings made by script, PICKBOX 3; clicks on a grid and crossing/window boxes, described here in words):
1. TEXT and MTEXT, on their own, turned, inside a block, and the text of a dimension, are picked only on the strokes of their letters: not in the gap between two letters, not inside the hole of an "0", not in the rest of an MTEXT's column. A crossing window in the gap between letters, or in the empty column, selects nothing.
2. A window around the letters of an MTEXT selects it even when it doesn't hold the whole column.
3. Inside a block, a SOLID and a solid hatch are picked on their edges only (the SOLID also on its diagonal from its second to its third corner, the one it is filled across); a crossing window inside them selects nothing unless it touches that diagonal. The same solid hatch on its own is picked anywhere inside it.
4. The empty parts of a block's or a dimension's bounding rectangle never pick it, by click or by crossing.
5. A dashed line is picked along its whole length, across the gaps between its dashes, on its own or in a block. A wide polyline, on its own or in a block, is picked on the edges of its band, at its ends, where its segments meet and on the diagonal of each straight segment, from the right corner of its start to the left corner of its end (a tapered segment and the closing segment of a closed pol…

title: MIRROR: a text takes its mirrored extent and an MTEXT stays readable (#1169, points 1 and 2)
author: EP995LAB
body:
MIRROR with MIRRTEXT 0 moved a TEXT's insertion point to its mirror image and kept the text reading left to right from there, so the copy ran back towards the mirror line instead of occupying the box its mirror image would: `TEXT 10,10 5 0 ABC` mirrored about x = 0 started at −10 and ran to the right. A justified TEXT did the same with its alignment point. An MTEXT mirrored about a vertical line came out with rotation 180, upside down, with MIRRTEXT 0 and 1 alike: its branch of `EntityKind::transform` added the matrix's rotation even when the matrix mirrors, while a TEXT in the same command stayed at rotation 0. The drag preview of MIRROR, which transforms texts one by one, showed the same.

**AutoCAD** (observed black-box, AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, synthetic drawing typed at the command line, described in words): with MIRRTEXT 0, `TEXT 10,10 5 0 ABC` then `MIRROR` about the axis x = 0 keeping the source gives a readable copy, still left-justified, whose insertion point is at −(10 + width): the text occupies the box its mirror image would, so it ends at −10, where the source starts. The width measured there is that of AutoCAD's font; CADCraft measures its own, so the tests check the position against the width of CADCraft's rendering, not AutoCAD's number. Only a vertical mirror line was observed; the rule below is applied to any line.

**Change**

- `crates/doc/src/entity.rs`: `EntityKind::transform` now goes through `transform_measured(m, text_box)`, which takes a measure of the box a TEXT, ATTDEF or MTEXT draws in; `transform` itself measures with the extents' estimate (`extents::text_kind_box`, new, the same boxes `entity_bounds` uses). title: JOIN: collinear lines and arcs of one circle join across a gap (fixes #1174)
author: EP995LAB
body:
**Before.** JOIN chained objects only where their ends met (within 1e-6). `LINE 0,0 50,0`, `LINE 120,0 150,0`, `JOIN 25,0 130,0` answered "Objects are not connected." and left both lines; two arcs of one circle with a gap between them (`ARC C 50,50 80,50 50,80` and `ARC C 50,50 20,50 50,20`) got the same answer. Two touching collinear lines became a polyline. Elliptical arcs on one ellipse already joined across their gaps.

**AutoCAD** (observed black-box, AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, the same synthetic objects): the two lines become one LINE from 0,0 to 150,0; the two arcs one ARC from 0 to 4.71239 rad (270°), counter-clockwise from the first arc's start, so the gap after the first arc closes and the one before it stays open.

**Change** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs`):

- `join` tries `join_on_one_line_or_circle` before the polyline chain (after `join_curves` and the locked-layer check). When every selected object is a line and all lie on the source's (the first one's) line, within 1e-6 of it, `merge_collinear` makes one line from the first to the last of their ends along that line, whatever the gaps and overlaps between them. When every object is an arc of the source's circle (centre and radius within 1e-6), `merge_arcs_of_circle` makes one arc that holds every piece, closing the gaps between them but the one just before the source's piece (so the result starts at the source's start, or earlier when other arcs run back across it or touch it; see the follow-up below); arcs that go all the way round make the circle, as elliptical arcs make the full ellipse. The source keeps its handle (and its centre's elevation); the others are removed. Any other selection (lines meeting at a corner, arcs of different circles, mixed kinds) goes to the polyline chain as before, so what joined before still joins. Hostile numbers (NaN, infinite, a zero-length source line) fall through to the chain, which answers as before.

title: DXF: a drawing with a table keeps its handles and $HANDSEED from one save to the next (fixes #1177)
author: EP995LAB
body:
#495/#508 made a CADCraft file keep its handles from one save to the next. With an ACAD_TABLE in the drawing, every open and save still renumbered the table records, the objects and the block contents:

```
cadcraft-cli run --cmd 'table {"at":[0,0],"rows":2,"cols":2}' --save t0.dxf
cadcraft-cli convert t0.dxf t1.dxf
cadcraft-cli convert t1.dxf t2.dxf
cadcraft-cli convert t2.dxf t3.dxf
```

`$HANDSEED`: 115B → 21B2 → 3209 → 4260; the handle of layer "0": 113D → 2194 → 31EB → 4242; `CADCRAFT_HANDSEED` (the drawing's own next handle): 101 → 1158 → 21AF → 3206. The entities and their data don't change. With a single line instead of the table, `$HANDSEED` stays 1152 every round. The same happens through DWG, and with a dimension style that names a standard arrowhead block (`_DOT`): the block is written for other readers and nothing inserts it.

**Cause** (`crates/io/src/dxf_read.rs`): the writer numbers the structural handles and the entities of the blocks it generates (a table's `*T` block, standard arrowhead blocks) above the drawing's own seed (`CADCRAFT_HANDSEED` + 0x1000). The reader drops those blocks (they are rebuilt on save), but it had already read their entities, and every entity read raises the seed past its handle. So the seed read back was not the one saved but the last `*T` entity's handle + 1, and the next save started every structural handle 0x1000 + (the records between) higher: 0x1057 per round for this table.

**Change** (`crates/io/src/dxf_read.rs`, end of `read`): for a file CADCraft wrote (one with a `CADCRAFT_HANDSEED` record), the seed read back is that record, raised only by the handles the drawing keeps (entities of model space, the layouts and the blocks kept), never by those of the blocks dropped on read. A dimension's `*D` block read on its first reopen still raises it, as before (its entities are kept and reused, #508). Files other programs wrote are read as before (`$HANDSEED`, and every handle in the file, #783). The seed never drops belo…

title: Add editable vector PDF import with automatic page previews
author: Tomsak8
body:
IMPORTPDF converts a selected PDF page into editable CAD geometry that can be
saved as DXF or DWG. Invoking the command immediately opens a PDF file picker,
then automatically analyzes every page and displays the total count and clickable
thumbnails. Switching pages reuses the cached analysis. Open, Import and dropped
PDFs use the same dialog; cancelling the file picker leaves the drawing unchanged.

The converter supports paths, Bezier curves, nested Form XObjects, page
rotation/CropBox, polygon clipping, Unicode text and embedded CID TrueType glyph
outlines. Units, paper scale, insertion point and rotation are selectable; the
selected page imports as one Undo step. PDFIMPORT remains a typed alias. JSON
and CLI calls use the same engine command without opening dialogs.

The implementation uses unmodified MIT-licensed lopdf and existing font/render
code. Decoding, recursion, operations and geometry are bounded. All-page previews
load the PDF once and run on a single desktop background worker. Unsupported
pages keep their numbers and errors so other pages remain selectable. The
overview is limited to 512 pages, 5 million operations and 10 million vertices.

Known limits are documented and shown in the preview: raster images and gradients
are skipped, fills become boundary outlines, dashed paths become continuous,
printed dimensions remain separate geometry/text, and editable TEXT can use a
substitute font. No OCR, PDF underlay or solid hatch reconstruction is provided.

Validation covers path/text/Form/clipping conversion, CMap decoding, hostile
inputs, atomic import/undo, DXF/DWG round trips, immediate picker/cancellation,
all-page previews and selecting page 2 without another Analyze action. Private
local PDF samples and offscreen UI views were checked; only original synthetic
fixtures are included. This PR contains the PDF feature and its integration,
tests and documentation. Contributor credit: @Tomsak8.

title: Tables: blocks in cells, per-edge borders, cell formats, row growth, mouse editing and cell clipboard
author: asimfali
body:
Layer 1 ("table core") of the proposal in #1205. It stands on its own: everything here is useful without the reports and templates the proposal describes.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `TINSERT` | A block in a cell, fitted into it or at a fixed scale. Attribute values and dynamic block visibility states are shown in the cell. |

title: DXF files that declare no units stay unitless when saved again
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1209.

The DXF reader builds every file on top of `Drawing::new_imperial()`, so a header without `$INSUNITS` kept the template's `1` (inches) and the writer then declared it. Before reading the header, the reader now sets `INSUNITS` to 0. A file that states its units still overrides that, and new drawings keep their template's units (metric 4 mm, imperial 1 in). One side effect: an xref of such a file is now treated as unitless rather than as inches, and that matches what the file declares. This doesn't touch the "ask for units on the first New" idea in #1182. Thanks @MauroSalvadori for the clear report and the LibreDWG samples.

Validation:
- `io::tests::drawing_without_insunits_stays_unitless` builds a minimal R12 DXF in the test (no external files), with `$INSUNITS` absent, 0 or 6, reads it, writes it and checks the group. It also checks that new metric/imperial drawings still write 4/1. Fails on main (`left: Some("1") right: Some("0")`, "absent"), passes here, including on its own with `--test-threads=1`

title: Linux: build an Arch package (.pkg.tar.zst)
author: ujo4eva
body:
Adds an Arch Linux package to the Linux release, next to the `.deb` and `.rpm`. Arch users (Manjaro, EndeavourOS, Omarchy, ...) can then `sudo pacman -U` it, and ArtCraft Launcher can install and update it through pacman (storytold/craft-launcher#389).

## What changes

- `packaging/linux/package.sh`:
  - adds an `arch` format, on by default;
  - builds `cadcraft-<ver>-linux-<arch>.pkg.tar.zst` with nfpm's `archlinux` packager from the same `nfpm.yaml`.

  nfpm can't rename a package per format and doesn't env-expand `archlinux.packager`, so the script writes a copy of the config with both set.
- `packaging/linux/nfpm.yaml`:
  - an `overrides.archlinux` block with Arch dependencies: `glibc gcc-libs hicolor-icon-theme libxkbcommon vulkan-icd-loader`;
  - `provides: cadcraft`;
  - `conflicts: cadcraft, cadcraft-bin, cadcraft-git`.
- **Named `ai.storyteller.cadcraft`, not `cadcraft`.** The AUR already has `cadcraft`, `cadcraft-bin` and `cadcraft-git`. An AUR helper treats an installed package with an AUR name as its own and would rebuild it on the next update. The bundle id is also how the launcher tells this package (which it updates) from an AUR build (which it leaves to the AUR helper).
- The README's Linux download table gains an Arch row.

**No workflow change is needed.** `craft-common-actions` uploads and checksums everything `package.sh` writes to `dist/release`, and the riscv64 job passes `--formats "deb rpm tar"`.

## Notes

- nfpm has no `optdepends` for Arch, so the Debian `recommends` have no Arch equivalent.
- Pre-releases sort correctly: `0.7.0-rc.1` becomes pkgver `0.7.0rc.1`, which pacman places before `0.7.0`. Arm64 maps to `aarch64`.

## Testing

title: CLI: convert to an image warns about the entities it can't draw
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1208.

Entities the reader keeps as unknown objects (what `info` counts as `Proxy`: foreign `REGION`s, `PDFUNDERLAY`, polyface/polygon meshes…) have no geometry for the renderer, so `convert` to svg/png/pdf left them out without saying so. It now prints one line on stderr before writing, next to the skipped-records warning from #872 and in the same shape:

```
in.dxf: 3 entities not drawn (PDFUNDERLAY: 1, REGION: 2)
```

It counts model space only (what the image shows), and only for image outputs: a DXF copy keeps those entities, and a DWG copy already reports what it can't write. The exit code stays 0, as for skipped records. Drawing these types is a separate job (#1019 for regions). If a non-zero exit is useful for server-side previews, I'm happy to add an opt-in flag (say `--strict`) in a follow-up. There isn't one in the CLI yet, so I didn't want to pick the name.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-cli --test undrawn_entities` (new): a DXF with a line, two REGIONs and a PDFUNDERLAY gives `info` `Proxy: 3`, and the warning appears once each for svg, png and pdf, as the whole line above. No warning for a `.dxf` copy or for the floorplan sample. On main: no warning (`left: 0, right: 1`). Here it passes; it fails again when the image-only check is dropped, and with the previous count format (`1 PDFUNDERLAY, 2 REGION`).
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-cli --test skipped_records`, `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: HATCH by internal point keeps the arcs of its outer boundary (fixes #1167)
author: EP995LAB
body:
**Before.** A hatch made from an internal point stored the traced outline as it came out of the boundary search: the tessellated chords. `CIRCLE 50,50 40` then `-HATCH P SOLID` at `50,50` gave a boundary of 158 straight edges (group 93 = 158) and `AREA O` on the hatch answered 5025.2235 instead of 5026.5482 (π·40²). A 100×50 rectangle with a semicircular side (`PLINE 0,0 100,0 A 100,50 L 0,50 C`, internal point 50,25) gave 63 edges and 5981.2992 while the polyline measures 5981.7477. The same circle as an island, or a hatch made by selecting the object, was exact (two vertices with bulge 1). Because the stored loop was not the shape of its objects, the associative check that runs after the command also unlinked such hatches: the hatch in the circle came out non-associative, with no sources.

**AutoCAD** (observed black-box, AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, the same circle): the boundary stays exact, two vertices with bulge 1.

**Change** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/hatch.rs`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/hatch/assoc.rs`):

- `with_arcs` (new, `hatch.rs`): given a traced loop and the handles of the objects it came from, it collects the circular pieces of those objects (`rounds_of`: a CIRCLE, an ARC, the bulged segments of an LWPOLYLINE) and classifies each edge of the loop by the piece both its ends and its middle lie on, within the tessellation tolerance (the middle, so a chord between two points of a circle does not pass for its arc). Each run of edges on one piece becomes one vertex with the bulge of the angle it turns through, or two vertices above a half-turn; a loop made of one whole circle becomes the two vertices with bulge 1 that `closed_loop` makes for islands and selected objects. The corners between pieces move from the traced chords to where the pieces meet (line–circle or circle–circle intersection nearest the traced corner, else the radial projection), so the result is exact: AREA on the hatch equals AREA on the object. Straight edges, ellipses and splines stay as traced. …

title: TRIM keeps the trimmed object, so its associated dimensions follow (fixes #1164)
author: EP995LAB
body:
**Before.** TRIM removed the object and added the piece (or pieces) that stay as new objects. `LINE 0,0 100,0`, `LINE 60,-10 60,10`, a linear dimension of the first line (`dimlinear {"object":"100","at":[50,-20]}`), then `trim {"handle":"100","pick":[90,0],"edges":["101"]}`: the line ran from 0,0 to 60,0 but was a new object (handle 103), and the dimension still measured 100 (`p14` at 100,0, no `assoc` left). Xdata and hyperlinks were copied to the new piece, but anything that named the object by handle (associative dimensions and hatches, reactors) lost it. LENGTHEN and EXTEND already kept the object (`modify_entity`), so a dimension followed them.

**AutoCAD** (observed black-box, AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, a synthetic drawing made by script, DIMASSOC 2, described in words): the same line and crossing line, with an associative linear dimension of the line; TRIM with the crossing line as cutting edge, picking the line at x = 90. After the trim the line is the same object (same handle, still carrying the dimension's reactor), running from 0,0 to 60,0, and the dimension measures 60 with its second point moved to 60,0. Trimming the middle out of a dimensioned line (two cutting edges at x = 40 and x = 60, pick at x = 50): the piece from 0 to 40 keeps the handle, and the dimension follows it, measuring 40.

**Change** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs`, `trim`):

- The first piece (the one at the object's start) is written into the object with `modify_entity`, so it keeps its handle, its common properties, xdata and hyperlinks, and the associative-dimension and associative-hatch passes that run after every command (`assoc::update`, `hatch::assoc::update`) see a changed object instead of an erased one and follow it. title: PLOT: a layout plots at the scale saved in its page setup when the command gives none (fixes #1163)
author: EP995LAB
body:
**Before.** A layout plotted without a `scale` in the command plotted at 1:1 whatever its page setup said. With `pagesetup {"layout":"Tavola","device":"CADCraft PDF","paper":"A3","landscape":true,"scale":0.1,"margins":[0,0,0,0]}` and `rectang {"p1":[100,100],"p2":[4100,2870]}`, `plot {"path":"a.pdf","layout":"Tavola"}` drew the rectangle from 100 to 4100 mm on the 420 × 297 mm sheet; only `"scale":0.1` written in the `plot` itself gave 10 to 410 mm. **Change**

- `crates/io/src/pdf.rs`: `sheet_scale(space, page, options)` resolves the scale of a plot that isn't fitted: the options' `scale`, else, for a layout, the `scale` saved in its page setup unless the page setup fits to paper (then the saved scale is greyed out and the plot stays 1:1, as before), else 1:1; zero, negative, NaN and infinite values count as none. `sheet` passes it to `plot_scale` (both the chord tolerance estimate and the mapping) instead of the options' scale alone. It is resolved per sheet, so a multi-sheet plot (`layouts: [...]`) gives every layout its own page setup scale while a `scale` in the command still applies to all of them. Model-space plots are unchanged (`sheet_scale` returns the options' scale there).
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/exchange.rs` (`run_preview`): the same rule for PLOT PREVIEW of a layout.

Not changed: a layout's "Fit to paper" saved in its page setup is still not applied to a whole-sheet plot without `fit` in the command, as before.

title: DXF 2007 and later: ACAD_TABLE cells carry the cell value block, so AutoCAD shows their text (fixes #1162)
author: EP995LAB
body:
**Before.** A table saved as DXF 2007, 2013 or 2018 (the default) had the same ACAD_TABLE as a 2004 file: each cell's text only in the plain group 1 (250-character group 2 chunks before it), as the DXF Reference lists for every version. The DXF Reference adds, from AutoCAD 2007, group 92 "extended cell flags", group 301 "cell value block begin" and the cell text in group 302 (250-character chunks in 303). CADCraft never wrote those, so `saveas {"path":"t2018.dxf","version":2018}` and `saveas {"path":"t2004.dxf","version":2004}` gave the same cells.

**AutoCAD** (observed black-box, AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, the table of the issue: `table {"at":[0,0],"rows":2,"cols":2,"cells":[["a","b"],["c","d"]],"title":"T","header":["H1","H2"]}`): with the DXF 2007, 2013 and 2018 files the table is there but its 8 cells have empty text, and AutoCAD rebuilds the table's block with lines only; with DXF 2004 and with DWG 2018 the cells have their text (T, H1, H2, a, b, c, d). AUDIT reports 0 errors. The DXF 2018 written by this change, loaded into AutoCAD 2027 for Mac (DXFIN, a synthetic drawing made by script): the ACAD_TABLE carries the 8 texts, and AutoCAD rebuilds the table's block with its 8 lines and 7 MTEXT entities reading T, H1, H2, a, b, c, d.

**Change** (`crates/io/src/dxf_write.rs`, `crates/io/src/dxf_read.rs`):

- In the ACAD_TABLE entity, from 2007 each cell writes `92 0` (extended cell flags) after its `91`, keeps its plain text in groups 2/1 as before, and then the cell value block: `301 CELL_VALUE`, `93 0`, `90 4` (a string value), `1 <text>`, `94 0`, `300 ""`, the text in 302 with 250-character 303 chunks before it, `304 ACVALUE_END`. Groups 92, 301, 302 and 303 and their meaning are the DXF Reference's (TABLE entity, "from AutoCAD 2007"). The Reference does not give the string of 30…

title: DWG: a fit-point spline is rebuilt as the SPLINE command builds it, which is now the net AutoCAD builds (fixes #1179)
author: EP995LAB
body:
**Before.** A DWG keeps a fit-point spline's fit points only (ODA scenario 2), so the control net has to be rebuilt on read. The DWG bridge renders such a spline into DXF with its fit points and no control net, and the DXF reader rebuilds it with `Spline::fit_with` — the function the SPLINE command uses. Both, with free ends, built one control point per fit point with knots averaged from the chord parameters: for the four points of the issue (0,100 / 30,130 / 60,90 / 100,120) a single cubic Bézier, 4 control points, knots 0,0,0,0,1,1,1,1. The curve passed through the four points with a different shape between them, and `fit_opts.knots` said Chord. (The issue reports the SPLINE command building the six-point net; on main it builds the same four-point one. The DXF path was not affected: AutoCAD's DXF carries the control net and the reader keeps it.)

**AutoCAD** (observed black-box, AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, the same four points, chord knots, DXF 2018): 6 control points, knots 0,0,0,0, 42.43, 92.43, 142.43 ×4 — two control points more than fit points, the fit points' chord lengths as the knots.

**Change** (`crates/geom/src/spline_fit.rs`):

- `interp_knots`: with free ends (no end tangent, three or more points) the knots are the fit parameters themselves, with the ends of multiplicity four, for two control points more than fit points; CADCraft's parameter runs from 0 to 1, so they are AutoCAD's knots divided by the total chord length. With an end tangent the knots average the parameters as before.
- `interpolate`: with free ends the two extra equations are natural end conditions, zero curvature at both ends (at a clamped end the curvature vanishes when the first two legs of the control polygon, each divided by its knot span, are equal). With end tangents the derivative rows are unchanged.
- `open_fit`: an end tangent's derivative length is the speed at that end (the chord to the neighbouring fit point over its parameter step) instead of the whole chord length everywhere:…

author: EP995LAB
body:

title: FILLET/CHAMFER with polylines: picked side, two polylines, middle segments, closed polylines, arc segments
author: aldozar
body:
Five problems with FILLET and CHAMFER on polylines, found while drawing a floor plan. AutoCAD's results on the same geometry are the reference: the same corners were filleted in AutoCAD, the result was saved, and the vertices were compared.

### 1. The wrong side was cut when a line crosses a polyline's end segment
Take an L-shaped open polyline whose last segment a line crosses. Pick the segment on the far side of the crossing, towards the polyline's end. CADCraft still kept the part towards the polyline's other end, so it cut away the part that was picked.

AutoCAD keeps the picked part and drops everything past the crossing on the other side. That includes the L's short leg. The line's picked part then joins the polyline.

### 2. Two polylines were refused
FILLET with a line works, but two open polylines picked at their end segments were refused with *"A polyline fillets or chamfers with a line…"*. It is easy to miss that message, so the command seemed to do nothing. In a plan this is common, because wall segments are often 2-vertex polylines rather than lines.

AutoCAD joins them into one polyline through the corner.

### 3. Middle segments were refused
Only an end segment of an open polyline could take a line. AutoCAD also accepts a middle segment. An open polyline whose first segment crosses another polyline's middle segment joins it. Each keeps its picked side of the crossing and drops what lies past it, which here is the middle segment's far part and the leg after it.

### Change
`polyline_and_line` in `modify2/fillet_pline.rs` becomes `polyline_and_other`:
- **Picked side:** each object keeps the side of the corner it was picked on. A line keeps its picked end. A polyline keeps the vertices on its picked side of the picked segment.
- **Segments:** any straight segment of an open polyline can be picked, not only an end segment.
- **Other object:** it can be a line or another open polyline's straight segment.
- **Result:** the first polyline picked keeps its …

title: DXF R2000: read and write AutoCAD's jog angle xdata on dimension styles (stacked on #1038)
author: Slopapalooza
body:
Stacked on #1038. Until that merges, this diff includes its two commits; the change here is the last commit.

**Merged main (`0b32c2e`, 2026-10-19)**, through #1038, to clear merge conflicts.

## Problem

R2000 DIMSTYLE records have no group for the jog angle (DIMJOGANG), so AutoCAD keeps it in its own xdata. I checked this black-box with a synthetic drawing: when AutoCAD LT 2026 saves R2000, the style record carries `1001 ACAD_DSTYLE_DIMJOGGED_JOGANGLE_SYMBOL`, `1070 384`, then `1040` with the angle in radians.

CADCraft ignored that xdata, so a style's jog angle in an R2000 file from AutoCAD came in as the default 45°. In the other direction, CADCraft's own R2000 files carry the angle only in `CADCRAFT` `DIMVARS` xdata, which AutoCAD doesn't read, so AutoCAD gets 45° from them too.

## Changes

- **Reading** (`dxf_ext::read_jog_xdata`): takes the angle after `1070 384`, through the same unit check as group 50 (`jog_degrees`). Xdata with another marker, or with an angle no style takes, is ignored.
- **Writing** (`dxf_write.rs`): in R2000 files, a style whose jog angle isn't the default gets the same xdata, plus an APPID record for it. The APPID is added only when some style needs it, so most R2000 files are unchanged. Files from 2004 on have group 50 and don't get the xdata.
- **Which copy wins** (`dxf_read.rs`): the DIMSTYLE groups first, then AutoCAD's xdata, then CADCraft's `DIMVARS`. Each fills only what's still missing. Before, `DIMVARS` overwrote the groups.
  - AutoCAD keeps its own xdata current but leaves CADCraft's as it was. So after a style is edited in AutoCAD and saved again (R2000 or later), CADCraft's copy is stale.
- **Pass-through** (`dxf_raw.rs`): on DIMSTYLE records this app now counts as CADCraft's own, like `ACAD` DSTYLE. The copy read from a file is no longer written back next to the current value, and can't go stale after an edit in CADCraft. On other records it's still kept as read.

## Limits

- **Not yet checked that AutoCAD reads this xd…

title: Plot: a scale given without fit plots model space at that scale
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1226.

`PdfOptions::from_json` left `fit` unset when the command gave only a `scale`, and model space then defaults to fit, so `plot_scale` threw the scale away: `exportpdf {"paper":"A3","scale":"1:10"}` drew the 1000 mm square 284 mm wide instead of 100 mm. Now a `scale` without `fit` means "not fitted", the way choosing a scale in the Plot dialog turns Fit to paper off; an explicit `fit: true` still fits, and nothing changes when no scale is given. The change sits where the options are parsed, so PDF and PNG plots (and PLOT as well as EXPORTPDF) get it alike. Layouts were already unfitted by default, so they're unaffected, and it doesn't touch the page-setup scale work in #1219. I went with "the scale wins" over refusing the combination, since that's what the dialog does; happy to switch to an error if you'd rather keep `fit` the default whenever it's absent.

PLOT PREVIEW (`run_preview` in `exchange.rs`) still resolves fit on its own and fits model space with a scale; I left it alone to stay clear of #1219, which edits the same lines, but can follow up.

- `crates/engine/tests/plot_model_scale.rs` (new, the issue's command through `exportpdf` and the real PDF plotter): fails on main (`{"scale":"1:100"}: 284.3 mm, want 10`), passes here; also covers 1:10 with and without `fit: false`, `fit: true` with a scale, and the default fit
- `crates/io/tests/plot_model_png_scale.rs`: new `{"scale": 0.5}` row, 287 mm on main, 50 mm here

title: DXF: $ANGBASE is in degrees
author: codyvogt
body:
`$ANGBASE` in DXF is in degrees. CADCraft read and wrote it as radians, so a drawing whose angles run from north came in with an angle base of 90 *radians* (about 116.6°).

## The problem
A drawing measured clockwise from north (ANGBASE 90°, ANGDIR 1) has `$ANGBASE 90.0` in its HEADER. AutoCAD shows that drawing's angles from north: a block reference rotated 2.23° shows Rotation 87.77 (90 − 2.23), which only fits an angle base of 90°. CADCraft took the 90.0 as radians, `GETVAR ANGBASE` reported 5156.6°, and everything measured from the angle base went wrong: typed angles, polar tracking and angles shown to the user.

## What changes
- **DXF read** (`dxf_read::header`): `$ANGBASE` is converted from degrees to radians, the unit the variable is held in (as `$DIMJOGANG` is converted the other way).
- **DXF write** (`header_vars`): written back in degrees.
- **DWG read**: the DWG reader hands the header to the DXF reader in DXF form for the variables acadrust's writer leaves out. DWG stores ANGBASE in radians, so that hand-off now gives degrees.
- Two comments in `engine` that said `$ANGBASE` is in radians are corrected.

Both the owner's DXF sample and its DWG save now read ANGBASE as 90°.

## Tests
`crates/io/tests/angle_header.rs`:
- the round trip now also checks that the file says `90` for π/2;
- `angbase_in_degrees_is_read_as_radians` reads AutoCAD's `$ANGBASE 90.0` as π/2.

`dwg_header_vars` (ANGBASE through DWG) still passes. `cargo fmt --check` and clippy `-D warnings` on doc, engine, io, render, dwg and ui-egui pass. The doc, io and render test suites, the engine's unit tests and its block, attribute, grip and snap test programs pass. (The local toolchain is Rust 1.95, whose new `collapsible_match` and `nonminimal_bool` lints fire on untouched code; they were allowed for the clippy run.)

author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1237.

POLARANG is held in radians, and Drafting Settings formatted it straight from `to_degrees()`, so 15 and 30 came back as 14.999999999999998 and 29.999999999999996 (and the list didn't highlight them as selected either). The combo now rounds the shown value to 1e-6 degrees, the same rule the Additional angles field next to it already uses (`format_angle_list`), and writes POLARANG back only when a different angle is picked, so opening the dialog never rounds an angle set through SETVAR.

Validation:
- `crates/ui-egui/tests/drafting_polar_increment.rs`: fails on main (`left: "14.999999999999998"`, `right: "15"`), passes here; it checks 15, 30, 22.5 and 45, plus a finer angle (12.3456789) that is shown rounded and kept untouched in the settings

title: Only the pick box shows while a command asks for objects
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1241.

`draw_crosshair` always drew the arms and only added the pick box when the cursor picks objects, so ERASE's "Select objects" or FILLET's "Select first object" looked the same as the idle cursor. Now the cursor follows AutoCAD's three states: crosshair with the pick box when no command is running (PICKFIRST on), the pick box alone at a prompt that asks for objects (`Prompt::picks_objects`, from #206), and the crosshair alone at a point prompt. Since the box is now the whole cursor at object prompts, it follows `Session::picking_objects` rather than SELECTIONPREVIEW (which still drives the rollover highlight), so turning the highlight off no longer leaves you without a pointer. With PICKBOX 0 there is no box to draw, so the arms stay; happy to switch if you'd rather follow AutoCAD differently there.

This touches the same function as #992 and the same call site as #1028; the overlap is a few lines, and I am glad to rebase on whichever lands first.

Validation:
- new `crates/ui-egui/tests/pickbox_cursor.rs` reads the painted cursor in each state (idle, ERASE, FILLET, LINE, plus ERASE with SELECTIONPREVIEW 0): the ERASE and FILLET cases fail on main (`left: (true, true) right: (false, true)`, crosshair still drawn), all four pass here
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: TRIM, FILLET and CHAMFER on rays and xlines: a finite piece becomes a line, an unbounded one a ray
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1235, fixes #1236.

Thanks @CryingDeadman for both reports. TRIM fell through to `trim_other`, which had no case for rays and xlines, and FILLET/CHAMFER only took lines (`as_line`). AutoCAD accepts both ([FILLET](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/AutoCAD-LT/files/GUID-64F8B700-23B3-4BD6-8C03-66121AA13E8F.htm): "lines, rays, splines, and xlines"; [CHAMFER](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/AutoCAD-LT/files/GUID-B1DCF991-90A7-4DB0-96FC-BDA3FB76337C.htm): "lines, polylines, rays, and xlines"), and the rule is the one in the issue: a piece left with two ends becomes a LINE, one that stays unbounded a RAY.

- TRIM: a ray trimmed on its far side becomes a line from its base, trimmed on the base side it stays a ray from the edge; an xline becomes a ray (or two, between two edges).
- FILLET/CHAMFER: a ray or xline goes through `fillet_lines` as a very long line, so the corner maths is unchanged, and afterwards the side that is still unbounded becomes a ray again (`unbounded_after_fillet`). A ray that keeps its base becomes a line.
- Xlines are handled as two half-lines from the base (TRIM cuts both, FILLET/CHAMFER take the one towards the picked side), so cut points keep full precision: a segment starting 1e8 away was ~1e-8 off, enough for a second TRIM to leave a tiny line behind.
- EXTEND (second commit): a ray's only end is its base, so it moves back to the nearest edge behind it.

Not covered: a ray/xline filleted with an arc, a polyline or a spline, and the parallel-lines fillet. `docs/geometry-parity.md` rows updated.

Heads up: #1192 also touches `fillet_lines`. Here the only change in its body is the line that builds `l1`/`l2`; `unbounded_after_fillet` doesn't depend on the end order #1192 keeps.

Validation:
- `crates/engine/tests/rays_xlines_trim_fillet.rs` (8 tests, type and points of every resulting object, plus the precision of a cut point): all fail on main (rays and xlines come back unchanged), pass here; each one also passes run …

title: DXF: annotative blocks keep their flag, uniform scaling, and their references' and attributes' annotation scale contexts on save
author: codyvogt
body:
Saving a drawing with **annotative blocks** changed how AutoCAD scales them. A metre block shown at Scale 5 came back as Scale 0.005 with Unit factor 1000 and Annotative = No. With only the flag restored, it came back at Scale 25, five times too big. This keeps what AutoCAD needs for the block and its attributes, and keeps it right when the block is edited.

## What was lost on save
Found by re-saving an owner-provided drawing (no edits) and comparing it in AutoCAD:
1. **The block record's `AcadAnnotative` xdata.** `AcadAnnotative` is among the applications CADCraft writes itself, so the reader dropped it from every record. It is written for styles but never for block records, so annotative blocks came back plain. AutoCAD then scaled their references by units: Unit factor 1000, Scale 0.005.
2. **The block record's group 281** (scale uniformly).
3. **A reference's annotation scale contexts** (`AcDbContextDataManager` ▸ `ACDB_ANNOTATIONSCALES` ▸ `ACDB_BLKREFOBJECTCONTEXTDATA_CLASS`). Each holds the reference's insertion point, rotation and scale at one annotation scale. They were dropped along with the other contexts CADCraft means to write from its model, but CADCraft models none for references. With the flag restored and no contexts, AutoCAD scales the reference once more by the current annotation scale (5 → 25).

## What changes
- **Block records** (`dxf_read`, `dxf_write`): the annotative flag is read into `Block::annotative` (which already existed) and written back as `AcadAnnotative` xdata. Group 281 is read into a new `Block::scale_uniformly` and written back.
- **A reference's annotation scale contexts** (`dxf_raw`): kept with the reference's extension dictionary, and refreshed when written (`block_contexts`). The default context (290 = 1) was the reference itself when the file was read, so each context moves, turns and scales by what the reference did since. A reference left alone keeps its contexts exactly as read, while a moved, turned or scaled one stays r…

title: packaging: RPM requires library sonames, so openSUSE can install it
author: tydude001
body:
## What and why

CadCraft's RPM requires Fedora package names: `libxkbcommon`, `(vulkan-loader or libglvnd-egl)`.
openSUSE has no `libxkbcommon`, `vulkan-loader` or `libglvnd-egl` package, so zypper refuses it with
`nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` (exit 4, which the ArtCraft Launcher shows as "error 4";
storytold/craft-launcher#341).

This requires the libraries' sonames instead, as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft already do, so the same RPM
resolves on Fedora/RHEL and openSUSE. It also declares the binaries' glibc floor, matching the deb's
`libc6 (>= 2.35)`. The floor names libm, not libc: the
binaries' only GLIBC_2.35 symbols are `hypot` and `hypotf` from libm, and RHEL 9's current glibc
(`2.34-283.el9_8`) provides `libc.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)` through backports but not libm's.

## How it was tested

CadCraft 0.6.2's released x86_64 binaries, repackaged with nfpm 2.47.0 and this branch's `nfpm.yaml`, then
installed with the distro's own package manager in a fresh x86_64 container and run with `cadcraft-cli --version`.
The released RPM is the same test on the release's own package.

| | released 0.6.2 RPM | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Fedora 44 | installs, runs | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Tumbleweed | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Leap 15.6 | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| Rocky Linux 9 (glibc 2.34) | installs; `cadcraft-cli`: ``libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.35' not found`` | refused: `nothing provides libm.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)(64bit)` |

The aarch64 RPMs get the same requires. I checked that side on FilmCraft only: its 0.7.2 arm64 binaries need
GLIBC_2.35 for the same two libm symbols, and its branch RPM installs and runs on arm64 Fedora 44,
Tumbleweed and Leap 15.6 (qemu-user).

`cargo xtask ci` passes. This tests installation and the CLI, not the GUI. The same results for every
Crafting App: https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/issues/341#issuecomment-6171570045

title: Refuse unknown parameter names in rectang
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1225

## Cause
`run_rectang2` reads its options by name with defaults and never checks the keys it was given. A misspelt or invented key such as `widht` or `bogus` was silently dropped, and the command succeeded.

## Fix
Added a `reject_unknown_params` helper in `cmd/mod.rs`. `run_rectang2` now calls it with the 12 keys it reads (`p1`, `p2`, `dimensions`, `area`, `length`, `breadth`, `rotation`, `fillet`, `chamfer`, `width`, `elevation`, `thickness`). Any other key returns a `BadParams` error that names it and lists the accepted ones, so `run --cmd` exits non-zero.

## Verified
- Regression test `rectang_unknown_parameter_is_refused`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib rectang_unknown_parameter_is_refused`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Other commands still ignore unknown parameter names. Each needs its own verified list of accepted keys, so a generic check in `Session::execute` was not added. Interactive and command-line entry are unchanged.

title: Carry engineering distance rounding into the next foot
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/units.rs:14-20` (no existing issue): Engineering-unit distances round up to 12 inches without carrying to the next foot (e.g. 0'-12.00").

## Cause
Engineering-unit distances (LUNITS=3) rounded up to 12 inches without carrying to the next foot. The LUNITS=3 branch of `format_distance` split the value into feet and inches first, then let the `{:.*}` formatter round the inch part. A value just under a whole foot, such as 11.999 at LUPREC 2, therefore printed as `0'-12.00"` instead of carrying to `1'-0.00"`.

## Fix
The engineering branch now rounds the absolute value to LUPREC decimals before the feet/inches split, so a rounded 12 inches carries into the next foot. This matches the architectural and fractional branches. If the scaled value overflows to infinity, it falls back to the unrounded value.

## Verified
- Regression test `engineering_rounding_carries_to_feet`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib engineering_rounding_carries_to_feet`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The architectural, fractional, scientific and decimal linear branches and all angle formatting are unchanged. A tiny negative value that rounds to zero still prints with a leading minus, as it did before.

title: Wrap format_angle to zero when rounding reaches a full turn
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/units.rs:63-66,87-88,102` (no existing issue): format_angle prints 360.00 (or 6.28r) instead of wrapping to 0 when a decimal-degree or radian angle rounds up to a full turn.

## Cause
format_angle normalizes the angle to [0, 2π) and then formats it. The decimal-degree, grad and radian modes round at AUPREC without carrying through a full turn. An angle like 359.9999° printed `360.00`, `400.00g` or `6.28r` instead of wrapping to zero. The DMS mode already carried correctly.

## Fix
A new helper, `wrap_full_turn`, returns 0 when the value rounds at the displayed precision to the same value as a full turn (360, 400 or 2π). Decimal degrees, grads and radians now go through it, so they match the DMS mode.

## Verified
- Regression test `rounding_to_a_full_turn_wraps_to_zero`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib rounding_to_a_full_turn_wraps_to_zero`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
DMS mode (AUNITS 1), which already carries correctly. Surveyor's mode (AUNITS 4) is also unchanged.

title: doc: a mirrored dimension reflects its direction about the mirror line
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
MIRROR turns a linear dimension's direction the wrong way whenever the mirror line is not axis-aligned: the transform adds the transform rotation to `DimKind::Linear.rotation` and double-reflects `DimMarks.oblique`, while a reflection must take a direction `a` to `rot - a`. A 45° linear dimension mirrored across the X axis keeps `rotation = 45°` while its second point flips sign, so it re-renders reading 0; a 60° oblique mirrored across the 45° line becomes 120° instead of 30°.

The fix reflects both the dimension line's direction and the oblique angle about the mirror line, exactly as the Arc and Insert arms already do. Regression test `mirroring_a_rotated_dimension_reflects_its_direction` fails on the old code (first assertion) and passes with the fix; the full `cadcraft-doc` suite stays green.

Partially addresses #1232 (finding 2, MIRROR dimension rotation). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: engine: renaming a layer repoints every viewport's frozen list and colour overrides
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Renaming a layer (`rename {table:"layer"}` or `layer.set {newName}`) repoints entities, `CLAYER` and block definitions but leaves the layout viewports' name-keyed state stale: a renamed frozen layer stops being frozen under its new name and colour overrides point at a name that no longer exists (a DXF save even writes the dangling `VPFROZEN` name). `layer.delete`, LAYMRG and LAYDEL already use `forget_in_viewports` for exactly this viewport state; rename had no equivalent.

The fix adds `rename_in_viewports` beside it — rewriting matching names in every viewport's frozen list and colour overrides case-insensitively — and calls it from `layer.set`'s rename block right after the block repoint loop. Regression test `renaming_a_layer_repoints_viewport_lists` exercises both command forms and undo; it fails on the old code and passes with the fix, and the neighbouring `layer_merge_delete` and `rename_cmdline` suites stay green.

Partially addresses #1232 (finding 3, layer-rename viewport staleness). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: doc: a rotated hatch turns its gradient's angle too
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
ROTATE (and grip-rotate) leaves a gradient hatch's fill direction untouched: `EntityKind::Hatch::transform` turns `h.angle` but not `h.gradient.angle`, and the renderer draws the gradient from `gradient.angle` alone, so after the edit the pattern and the fill disagree even though the engine set both fields from the same value when the fill was made.

The fix turns the gradient's angle with the same normalized rotation as the hatch angle, keeping the two in step. Regression test `rotating_a_gradient_hatch_turns_its_gradient` fails on the old code and passes with the fix; the full `cadcraft-doc` suite stays green.

Partially addresses #1232 (finding 4, gradient hatch angle). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: engine: check a paper's margins against its own axis
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
PLOTTERMANAGER validates a custom paper's margins against the wrong axes: the horizontal pair is checked against `min(width, height)` and the vertical pair against `max(width, height)`, so a landscape paper accepts margins that leave a negative printable height and refuses a perfectly valid set. The contract — and the line's own error text — is `l + r < width` and `b + t < height`; the built-in papers are generated portrait, which masked the swap.

The fix compares each sum with its own axis. Regression test `paper_margins_are_checked_against_their_own_axis` (a 400×200 paper: `[0,250,0,0]` must be refused, `[150,0,150,0]` accepted) fails on the old code and passes with the fix; the whole `plotters` test file stays green.

Partially addresses #1232 (finding 5, PLOTTERMANAGER margin axis). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: cli: convert --layout plots paper-space layouts to PDF at their page setup
author: graficaeusebio-cloud
body:
**Problem.** `cadcraft-cli convert` writes only the model space, and never PDF. A drawing whose sheet lives in a layout (paper size, viewport scale, title block) cannot be converted to a PDF of that sheet; only `run --cmd exportpdf` can.

**Change** (`apps/cadcraft-cli/src/main.rs`). `convert IN OUT.pdf --layout NAME` plots layouts at their page setup through the engine's existing commands:
- one layout → `exportpdf {"path": OUT, "layout": NAME}`, writes `OUT.pdf`;
- several `--layout`, or `--layout all` → `publish`, one `OUT-<layout>.pdf` per sheet, as `publish` already names them;
- `all` mixed with names is an error;
- without `--layout`, `convert` behaves as before (model space).

**Test** (`convert_plots_named_layouts_to_pdf`): a sample drawing with layouts `SHEET A` and `SHEET B`; one layout writes `one.pdf`, `all` writes one PDF per sheet.

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Keep Z and elevation of the pieces left by BREAK
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs:1457 (break_entity; helpers `line()`/`arc()`/`lwpoly()` in crates/engine/src/cmd/helpers.rs:10-23)` (no existing issue): BREAK discards the Z / elevation of the pieces it leaves (lines, polylines, arcs).

## Cause
`break_entity` flattened lines and arc centres to 2D and rebuilt the pieces with helpers that hardcode z = 0 (`lwpoly()` hardcodes elevation 0). Every surviving piece therefore dropped to z = 0, whatever the source Z or elevation was.

## Fix
Line pieces now take their Z by interpolating between the source endpoints at the cut parameter. Arc and circle pieces keep the source centre Z, and polyline pieces keep the source elevation, through a small `with_z` helper. The 2D cut-point math is unchanged.

## Verified

The shared `line()`/`arc()`/`lwpoly()` helpers in helpers.rs are unchanged, so their other callers behave as before.

title: dxf: audit follow-ups - code 255, more DOS/ISO code pages, cheaper unescape and hex (fixes #1269)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1269

Follow-up to #1025 / #1026: the crates/dxf audit findings that PR deliberately left out.

## Problem and changes
- **B10** The binary reader treated group code 255 as an R12 escape and read the next two bytes as the real code, so `write_binary(&[Tag::s(255, "x"), ..])` could not be read back. The branch is gone; 255 is an ordinary code. (R12 binary DXF is not supported anyway.)
- **B14** `$DWGCODEPAGE` DOS720, 737, 775, 855, 857, 860, 861, 863, 864, 865, 869 and ISO8859_15 had no decoder and fell back to Windows-1252 (wrong characters). They now decode: ISO8859_15 through `encoding_rs`, the DOS pages through tables in the new `crates/dxf/src/dos_tables.rs` (upper halves of the IBM PC code pages, generated from the public code page definitions; unassigned bytes are U+FFFD). ANSI_1361 (Johab) stays unsupported: `encoding_rs` has no Johab decoder.
- **S1** `format_real`: removed the dead `e`/`inf`/`NaN` tests (`{v}` of a finite f64 never uses an exponent).
- **S2** `is_utf8_version` removed; `BinaryText` uses `Version::for_acadver(..).utf8()`. Only difference: a lower-case `ac1021` now counts as R2007 too, and a `+` sign in the number no longer does.
- **O2** (partly) The ASCII reader hands its owned string to `unescape_owned`, which returns it unchanged without an escape instead of copying it.
- **O3** `unescape_unicode` no longer collects the whole string into a `Vec<char>` (4 bytes per character: a 100 MB string with one escape took ~400 MB extra). It copies plain text between backslashes and looks at a 14-character window per backslash. Same results (tests below); linear.
- **O5** Binary hex is read through a digit table instead of `write!` per byte.
- `Cur::cstr` uses `position` (same behaviour, simpler; counted as a simplification, not an optimization).

Measured (release, 400k LINE-like groups plus a 120-digit hex group each, best of 7, this machine): binary parse 640 ms -> 100 ms (O5), ASCII parse 166 ms -> 145 ms (O2). O3 is memory (reasoning abov…

title: fix(fonts): MTEXT \W…x multiplies the width factor; document the atom cap
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1272

## Problem
In MTEXT, a trailing `x` on the width code (`\W2x;`) makes the value relative: it multiplies the current width factor (public DXF reference). `parse` stripped the `x` and used the number as an absolute factor, so `\W2x;` set 2 instead of doubling. `\H...x` was already correct. Separately, the 200 000-atom cap in `parse` dropped the rest of an MTEXT without saying so anywhere.

## Changes
- `crates/fonts/src/mtext.rs`: `\W<n>x;` multiplies the current `wf`; `\W<n>;` is unchanged (absolute). The compounded result is clamped to 0.01..100, the range an absolute `\W` already accepts, so a long relative chain stays finite (same idea as the relative `\H` bound).
- Doc comment on `MAX_ATOMS` states that parsing stops after the cap and the rest is silently dropped. Behaviour is unchanged.
- Regression test `width_factor_x_is_relative`: absolute, relative, relative after absolute, capital `X`, 50-step chains up and down (clamped to 100 and 0.01), and `1e999`, `NaN`, empty values (ignored).

## Limits
- Only `\W...x`. `\K`, `\T`, `\A` are untouched.
- No warning channel for the atom cap; docs-only, as decided. I found no suitable page in `docs/` for it, so the doc comment is the only place.
- A relative value below 0.01 (for example `\W0.005x;`) is still ignored, like an absolute one.

## Test plan
- New test fails without the fix (`left: 2.0, right: 3.0` on the relative case) and passes with it.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-fonts --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p cadcraft-fonts -p cadcraft-render`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p cadcraft-fonts`: all pass.
- `git merge-tree` against upstream/main, #1036's branch and #950's head: no conflicts.

## Did not run
- Full `cargo xtask ci` (whole-workspace clippy/tests, assets, wasm build) and the rest of the workspace tests.
- No visual check in the running app.

title: Properties: a rotation shows and is typed as the drawing measures directions (ANGBASE, ANGDIR)
author: codyvogt
body:
The Properties palette and Quick Properties now show a block reference's or text's **Rotation** as AutoCAD does: measured from ANGBASE, clockwise when ANGDIR is 1.

## The problem
In a drawing measured clockwise from north (ANGBASE 90°, ANGDIR 1), AutoCAD's Properties shows a block turned 2.23° as **Rotation 87.77**, as it shows any direction in that drawing. CADCraft showed the raw angle from +X, **2.2273**. A value typed there was read from +X too.

## What changes
- `units::AngleSettings::shown` and `unshown` (engine): turn a direction (radians from +X, counterclockwise) into the value the drawing shows (from ANGBASE, in the ANGDIR sense, 0 to a full turn), and back.
- Properties and Quick Properties show the Rotation of block references and text that way, and convert a typed rotation back before calling `properties.set`. `properties.set` still takes the angle from +X counterclockwise, so scripts and other callers are unchanged.
- Hatch Angle is left alone: a hatch pattern's angle is measured from the X axis (as `cmd/hatch.rs` notes).
- Line and arc angles are not changed here either; whether AutoCAD shows them the same way hasn't been checked.

In a drawing whose DXF has `$ANGBASE 90.0`, the angle base is only read right with #1234 (`$ANGBASE` in DXF is in degrees). With both, the owner's drawing shows Rotation 87.7727, as AutoCAD shows 87.77.

## Tests
`units::tests::directions_show_from_angbase_in_the_angdir_sense`:
- 2.22729505553431° shows as 87.7727… with ANGBASE 90° clockwise, and back;
- the defaults leave a direction as it is;
- 45° shows as 15 counterclockwise from a 30° base.

`cargo fmt --check` and clippy `-D warnings` on doc, engine, io, render, dwg and ui-egui pass. The doc, io and render test suites, the engine's unit tests and its block, attribute, grip and snap test programs pass. (The local toolchain is Rust 1.95, whose new `collapsible_match` and `nonminimal_bool` lints fire on untouched code; they were allowed for the clippy run.)
