title: io: a handle at the top of the range leaves new objects their own
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A hostile or damaged DXF can name a handle at the top of the u64 range — an object's own handle or its `$HANDSEED`. `bump_handseed` saturated there, so every fresh handle repeated the top one, and the store replaces an entity with the same handle: the next object drawn silently replaced the file's own entity, and the duplicate identity survived into saves. Handles at or above `HANDLE_LIMIT` are now not followed or handed out: an object read with such a handle gets a fresh one, and the seed is never bumped from one, so a later allocation is always above everything the file brought. The regression test reads a DXF whose line sits at handle `FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` (and one whose `$HANDSEED` alone is there), draws more objects, and asserts nothing was replaced and handles stay unique; an ordinary high handle keeps its identity. `cargo test -p cadcraft-io --test handle_exhaustion`, the doc suite and the io suite pass.

Fixes #913

title: render: a plot keeps the dashes of a line longer than 50,000 pattern periods
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A dashed line of more than 50,000 pattern periods came back as one solid run in plots, exports and PNG/PDF output: the guard against huge dash counts is meant for a display zoomed out a lot, but it fired with the level of detail off too, where there is no zoom (`min_dash` is 0). The guard now applies only where a level of detail exists (`min_pattern` above 0); plots and exports keep the pattern along the whole line, bounded per polyline by the existing two-million-dash work limit. A unit test checks 50,001 periods produce 50,001 dashes in a full-detail build (and still one run in a display build), and an integration test reads a DXF and asserts the plot list holds 50,001 primitives. `cadcraft-cli perf` now shows 50001 in the `full` row (was 1) and a converted PNG shows the dashes. Render and io suites pass.

Fixes #1069

title: render: a display list past the block-expansion budget says what it left out
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Every display-list build may expand at most 2,000,000 block-expansion units, and past that it silently stopped drawing block contents: on a 3,000-reference drawing of a 1,000-line block, plots, exports and PNGs were missing about a third of the drawing with no message. The list now records that the budget was spent (`DisplayList::truncated`, merged across parallel parts and viewport clips), and the surfaces that can report it do: `cadcraft-cli perf` prints a note, `cadcraft-cli convert`/`--export` warns for image outputs, and `ui.render` (control channel and MCP) and the control `perf` reply carry `truncated`. The budget itself is unchanged, so hostile nested or arrayed block references stay bounded and the existing block-expansion test keeps passing. A new test builds a 10,000 × 10,000 MINSERT and asserts the list says it truncated while an in-budget drawing says nothing.

Fixes #1070

title: ui: the options reset brings a hidden menu bar and tool bar back
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Hiding the interface (Window ▸ Tool Bar, In-window Menu Bar, Hide Palettes…) can leave no way back: on Windows the in-window menu bar is the only menu there is, and Options ▸ Reset — the documented restore — only reset theme, animations, save format and a few more, never the visibility flags, so the tool bar and menu bar stayed hidden even after a reinstall kept the preference. Reset now returns the whole interface state to its defaults (visibility, panel layout, tool sets, menu bar), keeping only the interface language, the open dialog, the start tab and the recent files. A test hides the tool bar, palettes and menu bar, resets through the OPTIONS command and asserts they all come back; the ui-egui suite passes.

Fixes #1240

title: io: a handle repeated across ENTITIES sections keeps both entities
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A damaged DXF can split its entities over several ENTITIES sections; when a handle repeats across sections, the second entity replaced the first in the store — the earlier geometry was silently lost, and a save kept only the later one (within one section duplicates were already renumbered). The reader now renumbers repeats across every ENTITIES section once all are parsed, so both geometries are kept under unique identities and the file's own handle stays with one of them. This addresses the cross-section entity loss from the report; the other two parts (foreign records from later sections, unmarked truncation acceptance) were not reproduced in this round and are left as reported. A regression test in `split_entities_section` pins the two-section case; the io suite passes.

Fixes #939

title: Improve Italian localization and add localized CAD commands
author: mitikoge
body:
## Summary

This PR improves the Italian localization and adds localized command names to CADCraft.

The Italian catalog has been reviewed to improve terminology and remove several unnatural or partially translated strings.

It also adds Italian names for all 295 user-facing CAD commands available in CADCraft 0.7.0.

Examples:
- LINE -> LINEA
- CIRCLE -> CERCHIO
- MOVE -> SPOSTA
- COPY -> COPIA
- ROTATE -> RUOTA
- BEDIT -> MODIFICABLOCCO
- MLEADERALIGN -> ALLINEAMULTIDIRETTRICI

Technical identifiers such as LISP and SCRIPT remain unchanged.

## Command localization architecture

Localized command names are implemented only at the UI boundary.

For example:

LINEA -> line -> CAD engine

The CAD engine continues to use canonical command IDs internally.

This means the change does not modify:
- JSON
- CLI
- MCP
- APIs
- scripts
- control protocols

When Italian is active:
- the command line accepts Italian command names;
- autocomplete searches and displays Italian command names;
- visible command history uses the localized name;
- internal logging and execution continue to use canonical IDs;
- canonical English commands remain accepted for compatibility but are not shown as alternatives in Italian autocomplete.

Switching the UI back to English restores the normal English command names and autocomplete.

The implementation is catalog-based and designed so the same mechanism can be reused by other localizations in the future.

## CADCraft 0.7.0 compatibility

The implementation preserves the current 0.7.0 behavior, including:
- all existing 13 languages and plural rules;
- English autocomplete alias priorities;
- LISP raw prompts;
- Session::prompting() behavior;
- existing automation and drawing behavior.

The `@command` localization context has been added to the supported localization contexts.

All 295 registered user commands have a complete and unique Italian mapping.

title: Keep the polyline's elevation when EXPLODE splits it
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs:~1330-1345 (explode_kind, LwPolyline branch using helpers::line/arc)` (no existing issue): EXPLODE of an elevated polyline produces lines at z=0 (elevation lost).

## Cause
The LwPolyline branch of `explode_kind` builds its pieces with the `line()` and `arc()` helpers. These take 2D vectors and set z = 0, so the polyline's `elevation` was never applied to the resulting lines and arcs.

## Fix
After each segment is built, `explode_kind` sets the polyline's elevation as the z of the line endpoints and of the arc center.

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The shared `line()`/`arc()` helpers and every other caller of them are unchanged. Other explode branches (Insert, Polyline3d, Helix and the rest) are unchanged.

title: Add cadcraft-hub: the CraftHub client path (the v3 adapter, spec §3.6 phase C / §18.4 row 10)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

`cadcraft-hub` — the app-side binding that speaks the generalized collaboration core ([`craft-collab`](https://github.com/hasan-sdaif/crafthub), extracted from figcraft's proven `figcraft-collab` and proposed as `storytold/craft-libs#128`). This is CADCraft's row of the adoption table — **units and precision** (§18.4 row 10): CAD quantities are unit-bearing (drawing units per `INSUNITS`, degrees for angles) and the file stores full `f64`s, so this row's whole contribution is the precision discipline that keeps two collaborators from turning float noise into a write war.

Nothing here changes user-visible behavior. The session wiring (a v3 `NetLink` behind the app's `crafthub` feature flag, default off) lands as the pilot follow-up once this contract is reviewed.

## The honest map

CADCraft's model is a drawing database, not a scene tree — and it maps honestly:

- **Model space is the node tree.** Entities are the root's children, ordered by their draw order (fractional sibling keys; an insertion in the middle costs exactly one key, tested). A CAD entity owns no sub-entities — a block reference displays a definition's entities without containing them — so `CONTAINERS` is honestly empty and the schema says so explicitly instead of by omission.
- **Entities** sync the per-kind payload (`kind`, one value: the DXF entity record) plus every common field (`layer`, `color`, `linetype`, `lineweight`, `ltscale`, `transparency`, `visible`, `thickness`, `extrusion`, `plotStyle`, `annoScales`, `xdata`), with the compile-time guard on `Common` that a new saved field must decide how it syncs.
- **Symbol tables, blocks, layouts, constraints and parameters** sync as document-level keyed lists — per-entry `Put`/`Remove` plus one order property per list (the v2 discipline). Blocks and layouts carry their entity content inside the entry value as one last-writer-wins blob: paper-space content and block definitions are usually owned by one author at a time, and per-enti…

title: Security hardening: authenticated control channel, xref confinement, parser limits
author: jnbdz
body:
## Security hardening from a code audit

This PR fixes the issues found in a security review of the control channel, the MCP bridge, the file loaders and the packaging scripts. Each change is a separate commit; the regression tests follow the repo's `hostile_*` convention.

### Control channel: token and fail-closed framing (high)

`cadcraft --control PORT` listened on loopback with no authentication, and the line loop kept reading after a line that wasn't JSON. Any local process could run `engine.execute`, `app.save`, `script`, `lisp` and so on as the user, and a web page could too: `fetch("http://127.0.0.1:PORT/", {method: "POST", body})` arrives as HTTP header lines (each answered "bad JSON") followed by the body, which was executed.

- The app now generates a random 128-bit token at start (or takes `CADCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN`) and writes it to `<settings>/control.token`, mode 0600. Every request must carry `"token"`; a wrong or missing one is refused and the connection closed.
- The first line that isn't JSON closes the connection.
- `cadcraft-cli mcp --connect` reads the token from that file (or the variable) itself; `--token` and `--token-file` override. The lazy/launch bridge re-reads it on each connection, so a restarted app still works.
- New module `cadcraft_engine::control_token` holds the token helpers and the settings-directory lookup (moved from `apps/cadcraft/src/main.rs`, with its tests).
- Docs: `docs/control-protocol.md` (new "Token" section), `docs/mcp.md`, `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` examples.

### Xrefs: OPEN loads only files in the drawing's folder (medium)

A received DXF named its own xref paths, and OPEN read them wherever they pointed (`../../private/plan.dwg`, absolute paths, UNC shares) and showed the content to anyone driving the app. Automatic loading on OPEN is now confined to the host drawing's folder and subfolders; other xrefs stay `Unresolved` with a message, and the user's own XREF Reload/Attach/Path still load from anywhere. title: PAN pans in realtime by dragging; -PAN asks for two points
author: mattlafy
body:
## What

PAN (typed, alias `P`, View ▸ Pan ▸ Realtime) is realtime: a left-button drag moves the drawing
with the cursor until Esc or Enter. It is built like ZOOM Realtime: `PanM::begin` pushes one
Zoom Previous entry for the whole session, the prompt is "Drag to pan; press Esc or Enter to
exit", and `Session::realtime_pan_active` / `Session::realtime_pan(dx, dy)` sit beside
`realtime_zoom_active` / `realtime_zoom` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/view.rs`. The canvas routes a
primary-button drag to `realtime_pan` while the mode is active and keeps it from placing points.

`-PAN` is the two-point form: a base point and a second point, or a point then Enter, which takes
the point as the displacement. The JSON form of `pan` (`delta`, `from`/`to`, `center`) is
unchanged, and `-pan` accepts the same parameters.

## Why

#1245: PAN asked for a base point and a second point, which is the command-line form; PAN itself
pans by dragging.

## Tests

`crates/engine/tests/named_views.rs` — `pan_realtime_drags_and_enter_ends` (PAN and `P` start the
mode; an 80, −40 px drag over an 800 px view of height 100 moves the centre to −10, −5; NaN is
ignored; Enter ends; a later drag does nothing; Zoom Previous restores the view) and
`dash_pan_takes_two_points_or_a_displacement`. `crates/engine/tests/transparent.rs`'s script
pans with `'-PAN 0,0 1,1`. `cargo xtask ci` green.

Fixes #1245.

can_show only asked the installed-font lookups for those two languages, and both lookups hard-code None on wasm32, where there are no system fonts. The Korean gate already falls back to a craft-fonts face (korean_font), but the web build embeds a Jpan CJK face and an Arabic face precisely as the web's only fonts, so a Chinese or Arabic interface could never be selected on it, however complete the catalog; the embedded Arabic face was also never added to the UI font families (the embedded filter only kept Jpan/Han faces).

title: Add Craft AI: the family's built-in local assistant (Gemma 4, optional, shared, private)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

**Craft AI** — one assistant across the ArtCraft family, as a palette in CadCraft. It talks to a
local model runtime on this machine and never to a cloud service:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Local and private** | Every request is `http://127.0.0.1` — Ollama (11434), LM Studio (1234) or llama.cpp's server (8080), whichever answers. No account, no key, no telemetry, and no address a cloud service could be reached at exists in the code. |
| **Light by design** | No inference engine, no weights, no GPU code enters the app. The runtime the user already has (or installs) does the running — Craft AI is a loopback conversation. |
| **Optional** | Without a runtime or a model the palette says so and touches nothing beyond loopback. Downloading is a button, never a default. |
| **Specialised** | The system prompt tells the model it is inside CadCraft and names this app's world — the drawing entities (lines, polylines, circles, arcs, splines, hatches), layers with their colours, linetypes and lineweights, blocks, attributes and external references, the dimension family with its styles and leaders, snap and grid, object snaps, model and paper space, the command line and its aliases, DXF/DWG/SVG/PDF — so answers are about this app, not generic advice. The ready-made tasks (explain a command or entity, dimensioning advice, layer organisation, DXF and DWG questions) are framed for it. |

title: render: the even-odd fill cuts a slab at the crossings inside it (#927)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #927.

`triangulate_evenodd` cuts the region into slabs at every vertex y, sorts the active edges by their x at the slab's middle, pairs them, and emits one trapezoid per pair from the pair's x at the slab's top and bottom. When two edges cross strictly inside a slab, their order at the top differs from their order at the bottom, so the pair straddles the crossing and the trapezoid is a bowtie quad: its two triangles cover the wrong side. For the bowtie `(0,0) (2,2) (2,0) (0,2)` the filler covered the two upper half-squares instead of the two lobes.

## Change

A slab is now cut again at every y where two edges adjacent in the middle ordering swap sides inside it (the gap between them is linear in y, so the y is exact), and each part is paired on its own. A crossing between non-adjacent edges shows up as an adjacent one in the part it lands in, since each part re-sorts at its own middle. The cuts are capped (`MAX_CROSSING_CUTS`, 100,000 over a region) so hostile input stays bounded; past the cap the remaining slabs are emitted as before. The 6,000,000-vertex output cap stays. Plain loops produce exactly the output they did.

## Tests

`crates/render/src/fill.rs`: a parity oracle (ray crossings against the loops) checked against triangle coverage on a 23×23 sample grid, for a centred bowtie, an off-centre bowtie (crossing not at the slab's middle), two crossing parallelograms (overlap left empty), and the existing square-with-hole, reversed winding and triangle cases; plus the bowtie's area (2). With the cuts disabled (`MAX_CROSSING_CUTS = 0`, i.e. the old behaviour) the three crossing tests fail; with them all 87 render tests pass.

Run: `cargo test -p cadcraft-render`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Keep line and arc elevation when lengthening with LENGTHEN
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/modify2.rs:764` (no existing issue): LENGTHEN drops the Z of a line (and an arc's centre) to 0.

## Cause
`lengthen_kind` rebuilt the changed line with `helpers::line` and the changed arc with `helpers::arc`. Both helpers set every Z coordinate to 0, so an elevated line lost the Z on both ends, including the end that should stay put, and an elevated arc's centre dropped to z=0.

## Fix
The line branch now clones the original line and replaces only the XY of the moved end, keeping that end's Z. The arc branch now clones the original arc and changes only its radius and start/end angles, so the centre keeps its Z.

## Verified
- Regression test `lengthen_keeps_elevation`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib lengthen_keeps_elevation`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The shared `helpers::line` and `helpers::arc` helpers are unchanged because many other commands use them. LENGTHEN still measures and extends lines in the XY plane, as before. Polylines, ellipses and splines already kept their elevation and are not changed.

title: Fix table formula range shifting for one-cell and reversed ranges
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/table/formula.rs:660` (no existing issue): Table formulas: deleting a row or column makes a one-cell or reversed range point at the wrong cells.

## Cause
`shift_refs` treated the first corner written in a range as its start and the second as its end. The parser takes the min and max of the corners, so for `A5:A2` or `A3:A3` a deleted row moved the wrong corner. Deleting row 2 turned `=Sum(A5:A2)` into `=Sum(A4:A1)`, which pulled the title row into the sum. Deleting row 3 turned `=Sum(A3:A3)` into `=Sum(A3:A2)`, which added two unrelated cells.

## Fix
`shift_refs` now handles each `A:B` range as one unit. It normalises the corners to min and max, then moves them with the existing rule: the start stays and the next row moves up into it, and the end moves up. A range whose only row or column is deleted becomes `#REF`. A range that changes is written back normalised, so `=Sum(A5:A2)` becomes `=Sum(A2:A4)` when row 2 is deleted. A range that does not change keeps its original text.

## Verified
- Regression test `shifting_references`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib shifting_references`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Single-cell reference handling and insertion semantics are unchanged.

title: Don't print a minus sign for distances that round to zero
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/units.rs:7-55` (no existing issue): format_distance prints a negative zero ("-0.00", "-0'-0\"", "-0") for small negative or -0.0 values.

## Cause
`format_distance` took the sign from `v < 0.0`, or from Rust's own formatting for the decimal and scientific units. It did this before rounding to the displayed precision. Tiny negative values and `-0.0` therefore printed as `-0.0000`, `-0'-0"` or `-0`.

## Fix
The sign is now kept only if the rounded result is non-zero. LUNITS 4 and 5 check the rounded integer total. LUNITS 3 checks the feet and the formatted inches. LUNITS 1 and 2 strip the minus from a formatted mantissa that is all zeros, the same way `decimal()` does in the LISP `rtos` path.

## Verified
- Regression test `negative_zero`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib negative_zero`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`format_angle` and the LISP `rtos` path are unchanged. Values that round to a non-zero result keep their sign.

author: marcoarnulfo

title: Fix AutoLISP real printing of subnormals and mantissa round-up
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/lisp/value.rs:401-410 (real_text)` (no existing issue): AutoLISP real printing: subnormal reals print as "inf.0e-310" and rounding up to a power of ten prints "10.0e+010".

## Cause
`real_text` computed the mantissa as `r / 10f64.powi(exp)`. For subnormal reals the power of ten underflows to 0, so the mantissa is infinite and the output is `inf.0e-310`. The exponent was also taken before rounding to six digits, so a mantissa that rounded up to 10 printed as `10.0e+010`. The same stale exponent made values such as 999999.5 print in fixed form.

## Fix
`real_text` now formats with `{:.5e}`, which rounds to six significant digits and carries into the exponent. It takes the mantissa and exponent from that result and uses the carried exponent to choose between fixed and exponent form. `1e-310` now prints `1.0e-310`, `9.9999996e10` prints `1.0e+011`, and `9.9999996e-7` prints `1.0e-006`.

## Verified
- Regression test `real_print_subnormal_and_rounding`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib real_print_subnormal_and_rounding`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Fixed-notation output and the non-finite value texts are unchanged.

title: io: the four symbol tables honour the same record cap as their peers
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
In the DXF reader's TABLES loop, LAYER / LTYPE / STYLE / DIMSTYLE records were appended with **no cap** (`crates/io/src/dxf_read.rs:1423-1571`), while the VIEW / UCS / VPORT arms of the same loop guard at `MAX_OBJECTS = 1_000_000` (`:1517`, `:1541`, `:1603`) — the file's own established pattern for exactly this class of input. A hostile DXF could therefore grow the layer table (each record found by a linear case-insensitive name scan over a `Vec`, `crates/doc/src/lib.rs:202`) without bound: ~20 MB of layer records is ~700 000 records, ~125 MB of `Layer` structs, and the opening never completes.

**Fix:** the same `MAX_OBJECTS` guard on all four arms, matching their peers. Behaviour is unchanged for every legal drawing — none approaches a million table records, which is also why no unit test can reach the cap (the same reason the peer guards shipped without one).

**The larger half of this finding is deliberately left to the maintainers:** the quadratic cost is the *name lookups*, not the memory. A minimal `if name.is_empty() || d.layers.len() >= MAX_OBJECTS` bounds memory but 1 000 000 records is still ~5×10¹¹ comparisons. The real fix is resolving table names through a local `HashMap` while the table records are read (the same shape as the `Rx` maps already in this function), or capping table records far below `MAX_OBJECTS` as AutoCAD's own limits effectively do.

title: Remember the main window size and position between sessions (#1295)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1295.

The native app built its `NativeOptions` with `persist_window: false`, so eframe threw away the window geometry and every launch opened at the default 1600x1000 size and position. The `persistence` feature is already enabled for eframe in `apps/cadcraft/Cargo.toml` (the theme and other preferences are stored through it), so turning `persist_window` on is enough: eframe saves the window size and position in the same app storage and restores them at the next launch. No Cargo or lockfile change.

The issue was reported on Windows, but the setting is the same on every desktop platform, so the fix applies to all of them (on Wayland the compositor decides the position; the size is still restored).

title: BREAKLINE: a polyline with a break symbol between two points, with Block, Size and Extension
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
BREAKLINE (Tools > Express Tools > Break-line Symbol): draw a line with a break symbol between two points.

In AutoCAD the Express Tool asks for the first point (with Block/Size/Extension options), the second point and the location of the symbol (Enter for the midpoint), and draws a single polyline with the symbol in it. Size scales the symbol and DIMSCALE scales it further, Extension runs the line past both points, and Block takes a symbol drawing whose two points on the Defpoints layer mark where the line meets it. This PR does the same: one polyline, one undo step, the location projected onto the line and kept between the two points, a line shorter than the symbol refused, and the options remembered for the session. The built-in symbol is our own zigzag (one unit wide and tall at size 1), not BRKLINE.DWG. Two choices, happy to switch: Block takes a block already in the drawing rather than a `.dwg` file (`.` goes back to the built-in symbol), and the symbol is centred on the picked location. The defaults (Size 1, Extension 0) are what I could find in public material but couldn't confirm against AutoCAD's own help. TXT2MTXT, BURST, SUPERHATCH and Move/Copy/Rotate stay in E3.

title: Stop fence and crossing window selecting a ray behind its base
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/select.rs:49-52 (hit_polylines, Prim::Infinite) together with crates/geom/src/intersect.rs:17-21 (line_line)` (no existing issue): Fence and crossing-window selection pick a RAY from up to 1 drawing unit behind its base point.

## Cause
hit_polylines turns a ray into a 1e9-long segment from its base. line_line accepts a fixed 1e-9 slack on the segment parameter, which on a 1e9-long segment is about 1 drawing unit before the base. A fence or crossing window touching the ray's backward extension within that distance therefore selected the ray. The same happened for entities with a crossing window.

## Fix
Added geom::line_line_capped. Its end slack is 1e-9 drawing units (the parameter tolerance divided by the segment length, with the length floored at 1), so it no longer grows with segment length. seg_hits_box, select_fence_with and select_polygon now use it.

## Verified
- Regression test `fence_and_crossing_window_ignore_ray_behind_its_base`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib fence_and_crossing_window_ignore_ray_behind_its_base`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
line_line keeps its existing behaviour for all other callers. The 1e9 ray length in hit_polylines is unchanged.

title: TXT2MTXT: selected TEXT combined into one MTEXT top-down, or one MTEXT per TEXT, with SEttings
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
TXT2MTXT (Tools > Express Tools > Convert Text to Mtext): turn selected single-line text into one MTEXT, or one MTEXT per text.

In AutoCAD, TXT2MTXT asks "Select objects or [SEttings]" and by default combines the selected TEXT (and MTEXT) into a single MTEXT, lines ordered top-down; SEttings switches to one MTEXT per TEXT, to selection order, or to word wrap. This follows it: combined, the lines go top-down (or in selection order) into one MTEXT at the top left of the texts, with the first text's height, style, rotation, layer and other properties, and each line that is taller or shorter keeps its own height through an inline `\H` code, so nothing changes size (it replaces that object, so one undo step brings everything back); with word wrap the lines become one paragraph wrapped at the widest text. Per text, each TEXT becomes an MTEXT attached where it was justified, width factor and oblique kept as inline codes. Texts on locked layers are skipped. AutoCAD shows the settings in a dialog; here they are three Yes/No prompts after SEttings, remembered for the session like BREAKLINE's options. Happy to switch to a dialog. The uniform line spacing setting is left out: lines get MTEXT's normal spacing, so their distance apart can differ from the original TEXT positions.

title: BURST: explode block references with their attribute values as text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
BURST (Tools ▸ Express Tools ▸ Explode Attributes to Text) explodes block references and keeps what their attributes show.

In AutoCAD's Express Tools, BURST asks to "Select objects", explodes each block reference one level like EXPLODE, but turns every visible attribute into a TEXT with its value (not the definition's tag), keeping the attribute's text style, height, position, rotation, layer and colour; invisible attributes are dropped. This PR does the same and reuses EXPLODE for the geometry (EXPLODE's loop now takes the pieces function, so locked layers, undo and xdata behave the same), so non-uniformly scaled references give exactly what EXPLODE gives and nested references stay block references. An attribute defined on layer 0 lands on the reference's layer and a ByBlock colour takes the reference's, as EXPLODE does for the block's objects; a multiline attribute becomes MTEXT. Other objects in the selection are left alone. Constant attributes are dropped, since CADCraft doesn't draw them on references today; happy to switch if you'd rather have them as text too.

title: DXF/DWG: annotative text, MText and dimensions keep their annotation scales on save (stacked on #1244)
author: codyvogt
body:
Annotative **text, MText and dimensions** now keep their annotation scales when saved, the way AutoCAD stores them. AutoCAD opens the output with every scale intact.

> Stacked on #1244 (its five commits come first; this PR's change is the last commit, `2b1da25`). It reuses #1244's DWG bridge fix for block reference contexts, generalised here to text and dimension contexts.

## What was lost
AutoCAD keeps an annotative object's size at each scale it supports in *scale contexts*: `AcDbContextDataManager` ▸ `ACDB_ANNOTATIONSCALES` ▸ one `*OBJECTCONTEXTDATA_CLASS` object per scale. The object's own groups are at its **default** scale (290 = 1).
1. **AutoCAD's contexts were dropped on read.** An annotative text at 1:2 opened in CADCraft as plain text at the 1:2 size (2.5 instead of 1.25 on paper). On save, it lost its scales.
2. **CADCraft's own annotative objects went out with only CADCraft's private record** (`CADCRAFT_ANNOTATION`). AutoCAD saw plain objects at one size at every scale.

## What changes
- **New `crates/io/src/dxf_anno.rs`** handles text, MText and dimensions in model space and layouts:
  - **Writing.** Each object is written at its default scale (the current scale when the object supports it, else its first). It gets `AcadAnnotative` xdata and one context per scale:
    - text: insertion and alignment points (a justified text's start point moves with its size) and rotation in degrees;
    - MText: insertion point, direction, width and columns;
    - dimension: text position, text rotation (radians), the kind's points, and a `*D` block with its geometry at that scale.
  - **Reading.** The scales come from the contexts, found by SCALE name. Sizes are taken back to paper size from the default context.
- **`dxf_write`**:
  - An annotative dimension gets a `*D` block per scale; the entity names the default one.
  - The context manager shares the dimension's extension dictionary with its DIMASSOC.

title: CI runs the quality gates on every pull request
author: NakaSato
body:
Pull requests have no check that runs the Rust tests: `.github/workflows/` has only packaging lint and release builds, so every open PR shows no checks and regressions land unseen. This closes [gaps S1](docs/gaps.md#stability) (top-10 row 6).

### `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
Runs on every pull request, every push to `main`, and by hand. The same gates as `cargo xtask ci`, one step each so a failure names its gate:

- **test (ubuntu):** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo xtask assets`, `cargo xtask layers`
- **wasm32 check:** `cargo xtask wasm`

Modelled on photocraft's `ci.yml`: a newer push to a PR cancels its older run (main's runs always finish), only `main` saves the Rust cache and PRs restore it, and dev builds keep line tables only. Linux only for now; Windows, macOS or the web build can be added once this is green.

### Flaky test
`connect_to_closed_port_fails` (`apps/cadcraft-cli/tests/mcp_connect.rs`) bound an ephemeral port, dropped the listener and expected nothing there. Under a full parallel `cargo test --workspace` another test can take that port first: it failed once that way here and passed 5/5 alone. It now tries five fresh ports and, if all fail, says what the CLI printed.

### Docs
`docs/gaps.md` (S1 closed, top-10 row 6 removed) and the stability evidence in `docs/target-app-parity.md`, with status lines and revision history.

`cargo xtask ci` passes locally. This PR's own run is the first test of the workflow.

title: DXF/DWG: annotative multileaders keep their scales, and drawings open at their current annotation scale (stacked on #1362)
author: codyvogt
body:
Annotative **multileaders** now keep their annotation scales on save, like text, MText and dimensions in #1362. A drawing also now opens at its own **current annotation scale**, the one AutoCAD saved it at.

> Stacked on #1362 (and so on #1244). This PR's changes are the last two commits: `023ff81` (multileaders) and `c55dfe4` (current annotation scale).

## What was lost
- **Annotative multileaders.** AutoCAD keeps a multileader's size at each scale it supports in `ACDB_MLEADEROBJECTCONTEXTDATA_CLASS` contexts. Each holds the multileader's whole `CONTEXT_DATA` body at that scale: overall scale (40), text height, arrowhead size, landing gap, content position and leaders. CADCraft dropped them on read and wrote none. So annotative multileaders came back plain at the default scale's size, and AutoCAD showed CADCraft's at one size at every scale.
- **The current annotation scale.** AutoCAD keeps it in the named object dictionary's `AcDbVariableDictionary`, as a DICTIONARYVAR `CANNOSCALE` naming the scale. CADCraft read only its own record, so AutoCAD's drawings opened at 1:1 whatever their scale. The variable was also written back as read, so after CADCraft changed the scale, AutoCAD reopened the drawing at the old one.

## What changes
- **Multileaders (`dxf_anno`, `dxf_write`).** Each is written at its default scale with `AcadAnnotative` xdata and one context per scale. A context is the entity writer's `CONTEXT_DATA` at that scale, with its overall scale (40) and landing gap (145) set; CADCraft wrote those as 1 and at paper size. Reading takes the multileader back to paper size from its default context.
- **DWG (`crates/dwg`).** acadrust 0.6.4 reads a multileader context only after a `300 CONTEXT_DATA{` group, which AutoCAD doesn't write. The bridge adds it for acadrust and takes acadrust's braces and marker out again.
- **Current scale (`dxf_anno`, `dxf_raw`).** The variable is read when the scale is in the drawing's list. It is read after CADCraft's own record and …

title: Annotative objects keep a position per scale; ANNORESET synchronizes them (stacked on #1370)
author: codyvogt
body:
An annotative object that supports several scales can now sit in a different place at each one, as in AutoCAD. People with several viewports use this to nudge a note at 1:50 without moving it at 1:100. **ANNORESET** used to do nothing; it now puts every scale back where the current scale has it.

> Stacked on #1370 (and so on #1362 and #1244). This PR's changes are the last two commits: `b1e41d1` and `befda38`.

## Behaviour
- **Grips move an object at the current annotation scale only**, when the object supports more than one scale. With one scale it moves everywhere, as before.
- **MOVE, COPY, ROTATE, SCALE, MIRROR, paste and CHSPACE** move every scale together. The per-scale offsets turn, scale and mirror with the object.
- **ANNORESET** moves every scale to the current scale's position.
- **OBJECTSCALE**: deleting a scale (or Remove Current) also drops that scale's position.
- **Grips are shown where the object is drawn** at the current scale. Before, they came from the stored paper-size object, so an MText's or a multileader's grips were in the wrong place at any scale except 1:1. A shape grip's edit is taken back to paper size.

What moves at one scale, per kind (what AutoCAD's contexts store):
- text, MText and block references: the whole object;
- multileaders: the landing and the content (arrowheads stay);
- dimensions: the text.

## How
- `Common::anno_moves`: a list of offsets by scale name (`AnnoMove`). It's empty for almost every object and isn't serialized when empty.
- Objects get their offset in the one place they are drawn at a scale. `AnnoDraw::Scaled` now carries `{ factor, by }`, and `anno_placed` = `anno_scaled` + `shift_position`. Render, extents, explode and grips all go through it, so each caller changed by one line.
- `grips::shown_grips` / `stretch_shown` are used by `grip.*`, the hot-grip machine, grip dimensions and the canvas.

title: MLEDIT Merged Tee: the first multiline's inner elements run on to the second's
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
MLEDIT Merged Tee (MT) works now instead of reporting "not available yet".

AutoCAD's help only says the merged tee trims or extends the first multiline to its intersection with the second, like CT and OT; the merging part follows the F21 note and how MC already treats inner elements here (outer ones break, inner ones run through): the first multiline is trimmed where its path meets the second's nearest inner element, its outer elements get a break from the second's near side to the end, and the second's near outer element opens between them as in Open Tee. With two-element styles there is nothing inner to merge, so it behaves like Open Tee. When the second multiline has several inner elements the stem stops at the nearest one; happy to switch if you'd rather it reach the centre one. title: Selected annotative objects show their other scales faded (SELECTIONANNODISPLAY)
author: codyvogt
body:
A selected **annotative object now also shows at its other scales, faded**, the way AutoCAD does. Example: a multileader supporting 1:1 and 1:2 that was moved at 1:2 shows its 1:2 text, landing and leader faded while it's selected at 1:1. Grips stay on the current scale's representation only. ## Changes

title: Print signed two-digit exponent for scientific units (LUNITS 1)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/units.rs:13` (no existing issue): Scientific units (LUNITS 1 / RTOS mode 1) print the exponent as `E1` / `E-5` instead of `E+01` / `E-05`.

## Cause
`format_distance` formatted scientific units with Rust's `{:.*E}`. Rust writes the exponent with no sign and no zero padding, so 17.5 became `1.7500E1` and 0.00001 became `1.00E-5`. LISP `rtos` mode 1 uses the same function and showed the same output.

## Fix
A new `scientific` helper in `crates/engine/src/units.rs` splits the formatted string at `E`. It rewrites the exponent with an explicit `+` or `-` and at least two digits, so the output is `1.7500E+01` and `1.00E-05`. Exponents with three digits, such as `E+100`, are kept whole. `format_distance` calls the helper for LUNITS 1.

## Verified
- Regression test `scientific_exponent_is_signed_and_padded`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib scientific_exponent_is_signed_and_padded`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I left the render crate's `format_linear` alone, because its tests already expect the `5.0E-02` form. I also left the mantissa rounding as it was: `1234.5` at precision 3 still gives `1.234E+03`.

title: MOCORO: move, copy, rotate and scale a selection from one base point until eXit
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
MOCORO: move, copy, rotate and scale a selection from one base point, at one prompt, until eXit

Express Tools' MOCORO asks for objects and a base point once, then keeps offering `[Move/Copy/Rotate/Scale/Base/Undo] <eXit>` after each operation. This follows it: Move carries the base point along (so a later Rotate turns about the same spot on the objects), Copy leaves the originals in place and the next options act on them from the same base point, Base picks a new base point, Undo steps back one option, Base included (the last 1000 are kept), and Enter (or X) ends the command. Each option shows its drag preview from the base point; Enter inside an option goes back to the option prompt. The whole command is one undo step, and Esc keeps what was done so far as that one step. Objects on locked layers stay put (copies of them are still made, as COPY does), and if every object is locked nothing is recorded. Rotate reads ANGDIR like ROTATE; Rotate and Scale don't offer Reference here, I left that out to keep the PR small. The menu entry is Tools ▸ Express Tools ▸ Move/Copy/Rotate, next to BREAKLINE's. The JSON form is `{handles?, base, ops: [{move}|{copy}|{rotate}|{scale}|{base}]}`, checked as a whole before the drawing changes. Whether the base point should follow a Move is the one choice I couldn't confirm from the docs, happy to switch.

author: marcoarnulfo

Double-click a layout tab to rename it in place (gaps.md U7)

In AutoCAD a double-click on a layout tab turns its name into an edit field: Enter or a click elsewhere keeps the new name, Escape keeps the old one, and the Model tab can't be renamed. This PR does the same in the status bar: the field opens on the tab with the name selected and renames through `layout.rename`, so it's one undo step and the name goes through the command's own checks. While the field is open, typing doesn't reach the command line, and the Enter or Escape that closes it doesn't repeat or cancel a command either. Add Vertex from the grip menu on a polyline arc segment now leaves two arcs instead of two straight segments.

In AutoCAD, Add Vertex on an arc segment of a polyline splits it into two arc segments that meet at the new vertex; it doesn't flatten them. title: A clipped viewport and its clip boundary move, rotate, scale, copy and erase together (gaps F15)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
A clipped viewport and its clip boundary now move, rotate, scale, copy and erase together (gaps F15)

In AutoCAD a polygonal or object viewport is tied to the outline that clips it: picking either one for MOVE, ROTATE or SCALE carries the other, a copy gets its own outline, and erasing one erases both. Here they came apart: moving the viewport left its outline behind, erasing the outline left a rectangular viewport. Now MOVE, ROTATE, SCALE, MIRROR, grip edits and ERASE add the partner of any clipped viewport or clip boundary in the selection (once, when both are picked), all in one Undo step; COPY, MIRROR without erase and ARRAY copy the outline too and point the new viewport at its copy. If either half is on a locked layer the pair stays put as a whole, so the two never split. In STRETCH, an outline whose vertices the window moves isn't also moved whole with its picked viewport.

After a rotation the viewport's rectangle is refitted to the outline's new extents, as VPCLIP already does: model space stays still on the sheet and the view doesn't turn with the viewport, which is AutoCAD with VPROTATEASSOC set to 0 (its default is 1; view twist is #1230's). Happy to switch.

title: Drop minus sign from dimension text that rounds to zero
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/render/src/units.rs:139-160 (format_linear, unit 3 and 4 arms) and feet_inches at :101` (no existing issue): Dimension text prints "-0\"" / "-0.0000\"" for tiny negative values in architectural and engineering units.

## Cause
In engineering (DIMLUNIT 3) and architectural (DIMLUNIT 4) units, `format_linear` decided the sign with `v < 0.0` before rounding. The shared `feet_inches` helper then printed it, so a tiny negative value that rounds to zero came out as `-0"` or `-0.0000"`. The decimal and fractional arms already suppress the sign in that case.

## Fix
`feet_inches` now prints the minus sign only when the result is not all zero, meaning the feet are non-zero or the inches are non-zero. Both the engineering and architectural arms go through it, so both are fixed in one place. Genuinely negative values keep their sign.

## Verified
- Regression test `negative_values_rounding_to_zero_have_no_sign`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-render --lib negative_values_rounding_to_zero_have_no_sign`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Scientific units (DIMLUNIT 1) are unchanged. Rounding to the displayed precision cannot make the mantissa zero, so `-1e-9` correctly prints `-1.00E-09`, and a DIMRND result of zero already prints without a sign. The regression test covers both cases. The decimal and fractional arms are also unchanged.

title: Tables: report tables from the drawing's objects (REPORT) and table templates (TABLETEMPLATE)
author: asimfali
body:
**Stacked on #1206 (table core).** Review the commits after it; I'll rebase when it merges.

These are layers 3 and 4 of the proposal in #1205: **report tables** made from the drawing's objects, and **table templates** that say how a kind of table looks. Together they turn tables from hand-typed text into views of the drawing.

## Why this matters

In practice a drawing's tables are lists of what is in the drawing: parts lists, bills of materials, cable and wire lists, door and window schedules. People build them by counting by hand or with DATAEXTRACTION, and they go stale the moment the drawing changes. Every company also has its own standard form for them (ISO 7200, ASME Y14.34, GOST 2.106...). Tools either hard-code a few of those forms or leave all the formatting to the user.

This PR splits the problem in two, and **both halves are plain JSON files**: a company can keep them in a folder and version them like code, and an agent can write them.

- **A report definition** says *what* goes in the rows: which objects to read, which fields to take, and how to filter, group, sort, count, sum and look up.
- **A template** says *how the table looks*: columns, a header of one or more rows, text, line weights, how rows grow, and how a long table breaks across sheets.

The engine knows no standard. A parts list, an ERP export or a wire list is just a different definition file.

## Example: a parts list in one command

```json
{
  "title": "Parts list",
  "template": "iso-parts-list.json",
  "sections": [{
    "from": "insert",
    "fields": {"part": "{att.PART}", "desc": "{att.DESC}"},
    "where": {"part": "?*"},
    "group": ["part"],
    "row": ["{#}", "{part}", "{desc}", "{count}"]
  }]
}
```

```
Command: REPORT
  report file?       parts.json      (a window lists the definitions in the usual folders; Tab completes)
  objects?           Enter           (the whole drawing; or pick some)
  insertion point?   300,200
```

Every block reference with a `PART` attribute be…

title: Wires and connectors: wire data on polylines, and wire ends that stay attached to block connectors
author: asimfali
body:
**Stacked on #1405 (report tables, itself stacked on #1206) and includes #1404 (grip drag).** Review the last three commits; I'll rebase as those merge.

Third step of the proposal in #1205: the drawing knows its **wires**, and wires know **what they are connected to**.

## Why this matters

Panel and harness drawings in AutoCAD are mostly polylines that *mean* wires. But AutoCAD doesn't know that, so:

- The wire list (length, terminal at each end, wire type, colour) lives in a spreadsheet and drifts away from the drawing.
- Moving a contactor leaves its wires behind. Every wire end has to be dragged back by hand, and one end that is missed is a wrong drawing.

Electrical add-ins solve this, but they are closed, expensive, and the data they store is theirs.

This PR does it in the core, with open data:

1. **Wire data** on any polyline or line: length, end terminals, number, type and colour. You enter it in the Properties palette, at the command line or through JSON. Reports (#1405) read it into wire lists and bills of materials.
2. **Connectors**: named points of a block (`A1`, `A2`, `13`, `14` on a contactor; `W`, `E`, `S` on a pipe tee). A wire end placed on a connector **is attached** to it. Move, rotate, scale or mirror the block, or redefine it in the Block Editor, and the wire ends follow in the same undo step, keeping their right angles.

Everything is a command. The same thing works from the mouse, the command line, scripts, the control channel and MCP, so an agent can draw a schematic and get a correct wire list out of it.

## Example: a contactor and its wires

```
Command: CONN                       (in the Block Editor of block "KM")
Specify connector point: 6,30
Enter connector name <1>: A1
Specify connector point: 6,0
Enter connector name <2>: A2
Specify connector point: 0,20
Enter connector name <3>: 1
...                                 (Enter ends; BSAVE, BCLOSE)

Command: INSERT KM at 100,0  →  KM1
Command: PLINE 40,24  80,24  80,20  100,20      …

title: Tab cycles through every object snap under the cursor, not one per mode (gaps U4)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Tab now cycles through every object snap under the cursor, not just the closest one of each mode.

In AutoCAD, pressing Tab at a point prompt steps through all the snap points in the aperture: with two line ends a hair apart, Tab reaches both, and after the last one it comes back to the first. Until now `snap_candidates` offered the closest snap of each running mode, so the second endpoint (or a second intersection, a second midpoint) was out of reach. This adds `snap::points_near`, which returns every gathered snap point within the aperture (it reuses the same gather/intersection/PER-TAN pass `osnap` runs, by letting `finish` add to the candidate list instead of consuming it), and `snap_candidates` merges those with the per-mode hits, nearest first, without repeats. The UI side is unchanged: the cycle still starts from the snap the marker shows, wraps around, and starts over once the cursor leaves the aperture. Nearest and deferred TAN/PER stay one candidate each (they have no fixed points), and model geometry seen through a layout viewport still offers one snap per mode; happy to extend that to every point too if you want it in this PR.

Two things I noticed and left alone, both already there before this change: leaving the canvas over a palette and coming back doesn't reset the cycle (a one-line change in `canvas.rs`, which I kept out because of #1061), and the quick-click path from #815 recomputes the snap without `override_cursor`, so it ignores a candidate picked with Tab. Happy to follow up on either.

Validation:
- `tab_snap_cycling::tab_reaches_both_close_endpoints`, `tab_goes_from_the_nearest_out_and_back_to_the_first`, `a_click_places_the_candidate_tab_chose`: fail on main (Tab stays on 10,0, the only candidate), pass here
- `tab_snap_cycling::moving_the_cursor_away_starts_the_cycle_over`, `snap_overrides::tab_cycling_offers_every_endpoint_in_the_aperture_nearest_first` (main returns 1 candidate of 3)

author: william-wwh
body:
### Problem

The ARC prompt `Specify end point of arc (hold Ctrl to switch direction)` has been shown to the user for a long time, but Ctrl never reaches the engine. Every arc is counter-clockwise. PR #407's Limits section documented this:

> Ctrl to switch the arc direction is not supported (picks reach the command without modifier keys).

### Fix

A `Session.ctrl_down: bool` field, written unconditionally every frame by the UI, and read by the ARC state machines:

title: Double-clicking an MTEXT opens the in-place text editor
author: asimfali
body:
## What

Double-clicking an MTEXT runs `TEXTEDIT`, which asked for the new text **at the command line**:

```
TEXTEDIT Enter new text <hello>:
```

The in-place editor from #792 (toolbar, ruler, formatting) opened only while MTEXT was creating a new text. So an existing paragraph could only be retyped as plain text in one line, and its formatting was lost.

Now, as in AutoCAD, double-clicking an MTEXT (or picking one in TEXTEDIT) opens the **in-place editor on it**:

- it holds the text's current contents and formatting (bold, fonts, colours, stacked text…), with the caret at the end;
- the keyboard goes to the text box straight away, so typing edits the text;
- **OK** or **Ctrl+Enter** keep the text, and **Esc** cancels;
- an editor emptied to nothing keeps the old text, as Enter at the prompt does.

Single-line TEXT is still edited at the prompt.

## Changes

- **engine** `cmd/modify2.rs`: `TextEditM` keeps the picked MTEXT and reports it through `Interactive::editing_mtext`. This is the hook MTEXT already uses to open the editor.
- **ui-egui** `mtext_editor.rs`:
  - an opened MTEXT's contents are loaded with `Formatted::from_contents`;
  - the text box takes focus on the editor's first frame;
  - the caret position waits until the text box has a state to put it in;
  - an empty result in TEXTEDIT sends Enter (keep the old text).

## Tests

- `engine` `textedit_opens_the_text_editor_on_mtext`: the editor gets the MTEXT with its formatted contents; the editor's text replaces them in one undo step; a TEXT does not open the editor.
- `ui-egui/tests/mtext_double_click.rs` (kittest): double-click an MTEXT; the editor opens with its text; type, then Ctrl+Enter; the MTEXT has the new text.

`cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: Command line: a typed point keeps its Z, and 3DPOLY draws with it
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1409
Fixes #1410

## Cause

`prompt::parse_point_with` accepted `x,y,z` but only validated the third number, and `Session::typed` sent the `Vec2` it returned as the point. No typed Z reached a command. On top of that, the interactive 3DPOLY (`Poly3dM`) kept `Vec2` vertices and lifted each one with `v3`, so it was always flat at z = 0.

## Fix

- `prompt::parse_point3_with` is the same grammar keeping Z: `x,y,z` and `#x,y,z` give that Z, `x,y` and `d<a` lie at z = 0, and the relative forms add to the last point's Z (`@dx,dy,dz`; `@dx,dy` and `@d<a` keep it, as in AutoCAD). `parse_point_with` now calls it and keeps its `Vec2` signature, so its other callers don't change.
- The session gives a command the Z of the point being entered (`Session::point_z`: the typed third number, 0 for a pick) and remembers LASTPOINT's Z (`Session::last_point3`, which the `LASTPOINT` system variable now reports). `Input::Point` stays 2D, so no other prompt machine changes. The Z only holds while `last_point` is still that point, so the places that set `last_point` without a Z put it back on z = 0.
- `Poly3dM` stores `Vec3`: typed vertices keep their Z, picks stay at z = 0, and a vertex straight above the previous one is a new vertex (it used to be dropped as a repeat, since only X and Y were compared). The JSON form is unchanged.

MOVE/COPY with a Z displacement (#1407) is a separate change in the edit path. It can read `Session::point_z` the same way.

## Tests

- `prompt::tests::points_with_z`: `1,2`, `1,2,3`, `#10,20,30`, `*1,2,3`, `@0,0,5`, `@1,2`, `@`, `@5<90`, `5<0`, the hostile forms (`1,2,3,4`, `1,2,`, `1,2,z`, `1,2,inf`, `1,2,NaN`, `,,`, `@,,1`, and a relative Z that overflows) give `None` without a panic, and `parse_point` still drops the third number.
- `cmd::draw2::tests::poly3d_typed_points_keep_their_z`: typed absolute, relative-with-Z, relative-without-Z and `#` points plus a pick give the expected six vertices. `LASTPOINT` reports the typed Z.
- `cmd::draw2::tests:…

title: Reject lone '-' or '"' in parse_distance instead of reading 0
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/units.rs:107-132` (no existing issue): parse_distance accepts a lone "-" or '"' as a valid distance of 0, so typed junk becomes a coordinate.

## Cause
`parse_distance` strips a leading `-` and trailing `"`, and skips the number parse when nothing is left. It then returns `Some(total)` with `total` still 0.0. A lone `-` or `"` therefore parsed as a distance of 0, and `parse_point_with` accepted it as a coordinate.

## Fix
`parse_distance` now tracks whether a feet part or a number was actually parsed. It returns `None` when neither was. `1'` still parses as 12.

## Verified
- Regression test `parse_distance_needs_a_number`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib parse_distance_needs_a_number`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`parse_point_with` in prompt.rs is unchanged. It calls `parse_distance` for each coordinate, so it picks up the fix. I added no separate point-level test.

title: MOVE/COPY: carry an optional Z delta instead of silently dropping it
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A translation that carried a Z offset silently dropped it: `MOVE`/`COPY` with `{"delta":[1,2,3]}` moved 1,2,0. `delta_of()` returned a `Vec2` and `EntityKind::transform` takes a `Mat3`, which cannot express a translation along Z — so every Z-carrying kind (`Polyline3d`, `Face3d`, `Helix`, `Insert`, `Spline`, MLeader leaders) lost its Z through the edit path, corrupting data a 2D user already had. The DXF round trip kept Z; only the edit path dropped it.

The fix stays narrow — no `Mat4` migration:

- `delta3_of` reads an optional third element of `delta` (or `to[2] - from[2]`);
- `EntityKind::transform_dz(m, dz)` applies the Z offset in the same point helper, and `transform` delegates with 0 so every planar operation is untouched;
- `MOVE`/`COPY` call `transform_entities_dz` (COPY multiplies the offset per copy); ROTATE/SCALE/MIRROR, STRETCH and ARRAY are unchanged and still pass Z through exactly.

Typed `x,y,z` points and the interactive 3DPOLY prompt are deliberately left alone — they belong to the separate open PR.

Tests in `crates/engine/tests/move_copy_z.rs`: MOVE with a Z delta on a `Polyline3d` and a `Helix` (failed on main), COPY accumulating the Z per copy with the source untouched, from/to displacement with a Z, a malformed Z rejected, and ROTATE/SCALE/MIRROR preserving Z (green today, locked in). The doc and engine suites pass.

Fixes #1407

title: A hatch copied with its boundary stays associative to the copied boundary
author: mattlafy
body:
## What

COPY (including a count), MIRROR, and ROTATE and SCALE with Copy keep an associative hatch
associative when it is copied together with all of its boundary objects: the copy follows the
copied objects, and the original keeps following its own. A hatch copied without all of its
boundary objects stops being associative, as before.

## How

`transform_entities` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs`) records each original handle and its
copy during the call. For every copied hatch, `remap_sources`
(`crates/engine/src/cmd/hatch/assoc.rs`) rewrites the loops' source handles to the copies when
every source of every loop was copied; otherwise the sources are left as they are. The
associative pass then finds the copy's loops where its objects are and keeps the link. ARRAY and
paste can use the same helper.

The branch leaves `docs/gaps.md` unchanged. For whoever merges: in the F13 row, the clause
`a hatch copied with its boundary isn't linked to the copy; ` comes out, and this revision-history
row goes at the top of the table:

```
| 2026-10-16 | trivial | F13: a hatch copied together with all of its boundary objects (COPY, MIRROR, ROTATE and SCALE with copy) stays associative to the copied objects |
```

## Tests

title: MENUBAR and TOOLBAR at the command line bring hidden bars back (#1341)
author: aldozar
body:
Fixes #1341.

On Windows and Linux the in-window menu bar is the only menu. Once it is hidden, the item that shows it again (*Window → In-window Menu Bar*) is inside it. The reporter typed `MENUBAR` and `TOOLBAR`, as AutoCAD users do, and got "unknown command".

### Change
- **`MENUBAR`** asks `Enter new value for MENUBAR <1>:`, like AutoCAD's system variable. 1 shows the in-window menu bar and 0 hides it; anything else is refused and asked again.
- **`TOOLBAR`** (alias `-TOOLBAR`) asks `Enter tool bar option or [Show/Hide] <Show>:`. Enter shows the tool bar. CADCraft has one tool bar, so there is no toolbar-name step.
- **JSON forms:** `menubar {value: 0|1}` and `toolbar {show: bool}` set the bars, and without parameters they report them. MCP and scripts can use them too.

The UI owns the bars, so the engine only records the request (`Session::bars_request`). The UI applies it after each command line and at the start of each frame, and reports what it shows (`Session::bars_shown`) for the prompt's default.

### Related
This complements #1279 and #1283 (for #1240), which make *Options → Reset* bring the interface back. It doesn't touch the reset, so it doesn't conflict with either.

### Tests
`crates/ui-egui/tests/menubar_toolbar.rs`:
- Hide the menu bar, type `MENUBAR` then `1`, and it is back; `2` is refused.
- Hide the tool bar, type `TOOLBAR` then Enter, and it is back; `H` hides it.
- The JSON forms report and set both bars.

Translations: "Menu Bar" in Ukrainian (required) and Spanish. `cargo xtask ci` passes locally (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: A wide polyline thinner than a pixel keeps every side on screen
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1434.

Thanks @brains0l for narrowing it down to the global width. A polyline with a width is drawn only as a filled band of triangles, and the GPU canvas renders without MSAA, so a band thinner than a pixel lights only the pixels whose centres it happens to cover: depending on the zoom, whole sides disappear. Width 0 goes through the hairline path, which always draws. AutoCAD shows a sub-pixel wide polyline as a one-pixel line, so on screen builds (`min_dash > 0`, not plotting) the render now also draws the centre line of opaque wide polylines as a hairline in the polyline's colour, one per dash for linetyped polylines. Transparent ones are left as they were, since a hairline would add its alpha along the centre. It is added at every zoom rather than below a pixel threshold because one display list serves a whole band of zooms. Plots, PDF/SVG/PNG exports and picks build with `min_dash = 0` and are unchanged.

The hairline is drawn without lineweight, like the band itself (with plot styles shown it takes the style's colour but not its lineweight), so wider bands look the same. A side effect, as in AutoCAD: a polyline with per-vertex widths now shows its zero-width segments on screen as hairlines. One visible difference: a selected or hovered wide polyline now also shows its centre line inside the highlighted band. Happy to filter it out of the highlight if you'd rather not have it.

SOLID, TRACE and DONUT go through the same filled-triangle path and likely thin out the same way; I left them out to keep this focused.

Validation:
- `thin_wide_polyline_keeps_every_side_at_every_zoom`: rasterises a closed square at widths 0 / 0.01 / 0.05 across 40 zooms without anti-aliasing; fails on main (100 missing sides, all with width > 0), passes here
- `wide_polyline_centre_line_is_drawn_on_screen_only`: a screen build has the hairline (colour, lw 0, on the centre line), solid and DASHED; `build` with `min_dash = 0`, `build_plot` and a 50% transparent polyline have none

title: Strip the UTF-8 BOM when reading a data link CSV file
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/table/breaks.rs:167 (parse_csv), fed by read_link at :236 (String::from_utf8_lossy, no BOM removal)` (no existing issue): Data link (DATALINK) CSV import does not strip the UTF-8 byte-order mark, so a quoted first cell is mis-parsed and the table gets an extra column.

## Cause
`read_link` decoded the file with `String::from_utf8_lossy` and never removed a leading U+FEFF. The BOM ended up in the first CSV field, so `parse_csv` did not treat a quote that followed it as an opening quote. A quoted first cell kept its literal quotes, a comma inside it split the cell, and the table gained an extra column.

## Fix
`read_link` now strips a single leading U+FEFF from the decoded text before returning it. A CSV saved as "CSV UTF-8" now links the same way as one without a BOM. A regression test links a BOM-prefixed file whose first cell is quoted and contains a comma.

## Verified
- Regression test `link_strips_utf8_bom`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib link_strips_utf8_bom`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`parse_csv` and `separator` are unchanged, and so are the other file readers.

title: Fail to offset a polyline whose segments collapse or flip
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs:679 (offset_polyline; reached from offset_kind at :598-614)` (no existing issue): OFFSET of a closed polyline by more than its half-width returns an inverted, wrongly placed polygon instead of failing.

## Cause
offset_polyline offsets each segment and joins neighbours at their extended intersections, but never checks whether a line segment collapsed or reversed direction. Offsetting a closed 10x10 square inward by 6 therefore returned an inverted 2x2 square instead of failing.

## Fix
After joining, offset_polyline returns None when a line segment's joined start-to-end vector no longer points the same way as its offset segment (collapsed or flipped). The offset command then reports 'cannot offset that object', as it already does for circles. An offset inside the half-width still gives the inset polygon with its original winding.

## Verified
- Regression tests `offset_closed_polyline_past_half_width_fails`, `offset_closed_polyline_within_half_width_keeps_winding`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib offset_closed_polyline`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Arc segments of polylines get no collapse or flip check, because joins can legitimately extend an arc's sweep. Open polylines with a short segment that flips now also fail instead of returning a distorted result. I did not add trimming.

title: Window plots build only the objects that reach the page
author: mattlafy
body:
## Problem

A model-space plot of a window (`exportpdf` with a window, and each page of a multi-page export with `pages: [{window}]`) builds every object in the drawing and then clips to the page. Exporting many windows of one drawing therefore costs frames × drawing size, and a block reference that reaches the window (a whole plan inserted as one block) is built in full.

## Change

- The cull lives in a new `render::cull` module, because render is the one layer that both screen and plot builds go through. It holds the window a build culls against, the test of whether an object reaches it, and the selection of a block reference's entities that reach it once the window is brought into the block's coordinates. Each block definition's entity bounds are measured once per layer state and kept. A builder carries its cull window; `None` builds everything.
- `render::build_plot` of model space with `Options::view` set culls against the view widened by 2% of its larger side for lineweights and rounding: top-level objects and block contents wholly outside it are left out, nested references at each level. Objects without measurable bounds (construction lines, rays) are always built. Kept objects build exactly as before, in the same order. Screen builds and layout plots are unchanged.
- Viewport contents use the same reach test for the model objects they pick.
- A window PDF page passes the part of the drawing that lands on its paper as the view: the window, widened to the printable area when the window's shape differs from the paper's. The page shows the same as before.
- MTEXT bounds (`cadcraft_doc::entity_bounds`, used for culling, extents and selection) word-wrap each paragraph to the column width, follow `\H` height changes, space lines as the renderer does and leave room for the last line's descenders. Wrapped text is no longer measured as one line, so it is not left out while visible, and middle and bottom attachments place the whole wrapped block. This applies to MTEXT…

title: AREA: an ellipse's perimeter is its exact length, not a closed-form estimate
author: SBaksa
body:
AREA's Object option reported a full ellipse's perimeter with Ramanujan's closed-form estimate instead of measuring it. The estimate is close for round ellipses but falls short as they flatten, and the error shows up in the printed result even at the default four decimals:

| Ellipse | Exact perimeter | AREA reported |
|---|---|---|
| 10 × 4 | 46.0262 | 46.0256 |
| 10 × 0.1 | 40.0110 | 39.8741 (0.34% short) |

(Exact values from the arithmetic–geometric mean, Gauss–Kummer.)

## Why we want this
- **AREA is a measuring command.** People read its perimeter off to cut, order or quote material: trim around an oval window, an elliptical table edge, a track. A number that is wrong in the shown digits is a wrong measurement, not a rounding detail.
- **One ellipse, one length.** LENGTHEN, and the `vlax-curve-*` functions in #1335, already measure an ellipse by integrating along it. AREA was the odd one out, so the same ellipse could report two different lengths depending on the command. It now uses the same geometry-crate function, `Ellipse::arc_length_from`.
- **It costs nothing.** The exact length is a few hundred evaluations, once per AREA pick.

## Changes
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/inquiry.rs`: a full ellipse's perimeter is `arc_length_from(0, 2π)`.
- `crates/geom/src/nurbs.rs`: `Ellipse::arc_length_from` halves a panel where it needs to (the same adaptive Gauss–Legendre spline arc lengths already use). With fixed panels a 100:1 ellipse came out 4e-8 long, because it turns sharply at its ends. LENGTHEN on very flat ellipses benefits too.

## Tests
- `area_of_an_ellipse_reports_its_exact_perimeter`: four ellipses (round, 2:1, 2.5:1 and 100:1, off the origin and turned 90°) against the AGM values to 1e-9 relative, plus the printed `Perimeter = 46.0262` line from the command line.
- `ellipse_arc_length` in geom: the 100:1 ellipse to 1e-9.
- `cargo xtask ci` green (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: HATCH by internal point keeps the arcs of its boundary (#1167)
author: aldozar
body:
Fixes #1167.

**Before.** A hatch made by picking an internal point stored its boundary as the chords the boundary search traced. `CIRCLE 50,50 40`, then `-HATCH P SOLID` at `50,50`, gave 158 straight edges, and the area was 5025.22 instead of π·40² = 5026.55. AutoCAD keeps the circle exact, as reported in the issue.

### Approach: provenance, not proximity
#1217 tried this by matching traced edges to nearby circles and was withdrawn: a line or an ellipse close to a circle was taken for the circle, and a shallow line cut gave an arc outside it. Here nothing is matched by distance.

- **`geom/src/region.rs`:** the graph already knew the input polyline of each edge (`edge_src`). It is now reported per edge of the traced loop: `Boundary::outer_edges`, `Island::edges`, `outline_edges` and `enclosing_loop_edges_gap`. Edges that bridge a gap (HPGAPTOL) are `None`, and `prune` keeps the edge sources for island outlines.
- **`engine/src/cmd/hatch/arcs.rs` (new):** each input polyline is one primitive of one object, as `hit_polylines` makes them: a line, a circle, an arc or one segment of an LWPOLYLINE. `pieces_of` records the exact curve behind each. `with_arcs` then turns each run of consecutive edges on the same circular piece into one bulged vertex, with the bulge of the angle the run turns through. It moves the corners onto the exact curves: the line–circle or circle–circle crossing nearest the traced corner, or else onto the circle. A crossing is accepted within the distance a shallow crossing can be off by, √(2·r·tol), and only when no other crossing is as near. A loop that is one whole circle becomes two half circles, as a hatch made by selecting the circle has. Ellipses, splines and anything that doesn't check out stay as traced.
- **`loops_at`** (outer loop and open-curve islands) and **the associative refill** both use it, so a hatch keeps its arcs when its objects move.

title: Offset elliptical arcs towards the picked side
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs:584-597 (offset_kind, EntityKind::Ellipse branch)` (no existing issue): OFFSET of an elliptical arc ignores the picked side and always offsets outward when the side point is on the concave (centre) side.

## Cause
The Ellipse branch of `offset_kind` chose the side with `point_in_polygon` on the tessellated arc. An open arc is implicitly closed by its chord, so a side point at the centre fell outside that shape and the offset always went outward.

## Fix
The side is now decided by whether the picked point lies inside the full ellipse. The point is expressed in the ellipse's local frame and tested against (x/a)² + (y/b)² < 1, written without division. This works for open arcs as well as full ellipses.

## Verified
- Regression test `offset_elliptical_arc_follows_picked_side`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib offset_elliptical_arc_follows_picked_side`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The polyline-based approximation of the offset curve and the other entity kinds are unchanged.

title: Treat polyline bulges with a sub-EPS sweep as straight segments
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/geom/src/curve.rs:435 (bulge_to_arc) together with crates/geom/src/lib.rs:45-48 (ccw_sweep)` (no existing issue): Polyline segments with a tiny non-zero bulge (below about 2.5e-10) are treated as a full-circle arc of enormous radius.

## Cause
`bulge_to_arc` only treated `|bulge| < 1e-12` as straight. A bulge like 1e-10 produced an arc whose sweep (about 4e-10 rad) is below `EPS`, and `ccw_sweep` maps any sweep <= EPS to a full TAU. The segment then counted as a full circle of enormous radius, so length, area and bounds were wrong.

## Fix
`bulge_to_arc` now returns `None` (a straight segment) when the included angle `4*atan(bulge)` is at most `EPS`. This is the point where `ccw_sweep` would otherwise read it as a full circle. The regression test checks that a polyline with a 1e-10 bulge has length about 10 and bounds within the chord box.

## Verified
- Regression test `tiny_bulge_is_not_a_full_circle`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-geom tiny_bulge_is_not_a_full_circle`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`ccw_sweep` still returns TAU for sweeps <= EPS, because full circles rely on that. The existing `1e-12` bulge check and the zero-length skip in `Polyline::segments` are unchanged.

title: feat: reference clipping (XCLIP/IMAGECLIP/CLIP), viewport sync (F15), and model plot margins
author: aljormon84
body:
Adds reference clipping (`XCLIP`, `IMAGECLIP`, and unified `CLIP`), closes gap F15 by keeping non-rectangular clipping boundaries synchronized with paper space viewports across transformations, and adds margins support for model extents plotting in PDF export.

### What's included:

- **Reference Clipping (`XCLIP`, `IMAGECLIP`, `CLIP`)**:
  - Implements `xclip`, `imageclip`, and the unified `clip` command for block references, external references (XREF), underlays (PDF/DWF/DGN), and images.
  - Supports rectangular boundaries, polygonal boundaries, inverted clip modes, and deletion/removal of clipping boundaries (`Delete` / `Off`).
  - Correct boundary transformation, spatial query filtering, and extents handling for clipped references.
- **Viewport Clipping Boundary Synchronization (`F15`)**:

title: Add wheelZoom preference to always zoom with the mouse wheel
author: icelyfire
body:
## Summary

- Adds a `wheelZoom` user preference (Options › User Preferences) that forces the mouse wheel to always zoom, overriding the macOS auto-detection that makes trackpad/Magic Mouse scroll events pan the drawing.
- The setting is persisted across restarts via the user profile.
- No change in behaviour for users who leave the option off.

## Motivation

On macOS, egui distinguishes trackpad (point-unit) from notched mouse wheel (line-unit) events to decide whether scrolling pans or zooms. Some mice (Magic Mouse, smooth-scroll third-party drivers) send point-unit events and were unconditionally treated as trackpads, giving users no way to get zoom behaviour from their wheel.

## Files changed

- `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` — respect the new flag when setting `scroll_pans`
- `crates/ui-egui/src/options/mod.rs` — add `wheel_zoom` to `UiOptions`, `UiChanges`, parse/apply/report/persist
- `crates/ui-egui/src/options/dialog.rs` — add checkbox in the User Preferences tab

title: Viewports keep their own UCS and their other settings through save and copy (part of #1316)
author: SBaksa
body:
Part of #1316: a layout viewport's **own UCS** and **every other setting CADCraft doesn't model yet** now survive opening and saving a drawing (DXF and DWG) and copying the viewport. Before this, all of them were dropped on read, so a sheet set saved from CADCraft lost them for good.

## What's kept
- **Per-viewport UCS, modelled:** `Viewport::ucs` (origin, X/Y axes, elevation, orthographic type, named and base UCS) and `Viewport::ucs_per_viewport` (UCSVP), from and to VIEWPORT groups 110–112, 146, 79, 345/346 and 71. The named and base UCS are stored by name, like frozen layers, so they point at the right UCS record after a save, and at nothing when that UCS has been deleted.

On save, `dxf_raw::finish` writes them at the end of the viewport's own subclass (new `ForeignExtra::tail`) and repoints their references the same way it does for kept foreign data.

- **View twist (51), view direction (16) and target (17).** They say where the view centre is measured from. CADCraft writes the centre in drawing coordinates, so writing them back raw would shift the view on the next read. The twist is #1230 and the target is #1476; this PR leaves both alone.

title: feat(viewer): add a lightweight read-only desktop frontend
author: AGICOGROUP
body:
Superseded by #1606, submitted from the contributor's personal account with corrected authorship.

Opening a drawing just for review currently starts the full editing frontend. This adds a separate experimental native `cadcraft-viewer` app that reuses the existing reader, document and renderer without linking the editing engine, constraint solver or editor UI.

The frontend opens DWG/DXF/DWT, supports cursor-centered zoom, pan/fit, transient layer visibility, model/layout navigation, freely picked two-point distances and export to a **new** PDF.
