title: Scale SVG export precision and point size to the drawing's extents
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/io/src/svg.rs:50-60 (export_list: viewBox, stroke-width, circle r and coordinates all formatted with {:.6})` (no existing issue): SVG export writes a zero-size viewBox for a single-point drawing and a zero stroke-width for small-scale drawings.

## Cause
`svg::export_list` wrote the viewBox, stroke width, point radius and every coordinate with a fixed `{:.6}`. A drawing about 1e-4 across got a stroke width of about 7e-8, which printed as 0.000000. A single point has no extent, so its viewBox and radius collapsed to about 1e-9, which printed as 0.000000, and viewers rendered nothing.

## Fix
A drawing whose extents are both at most 1e-9 (for example a single point) now gets a unit viewBox centred on the point, with a 0.5 margin on each side. This also applies to a point-sized window. The number of decimals is now chosen from the stroke width: at least 6 and at most 15, with enough digits to keep the stroke's leading significant digits. The same count is used for the viewBox, stroke width, circle radius and all coordinates.

## Verified
- Regression tests `single_point_has_a_visible_view_box_and_radius`, `small_drawing_has_a_non_zero_stroke_and_keeps_precision`, `normal_drawing_keeps_six_decimals`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-io --test svg_tiny_extents`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Output for normal-sized drawings is unchanged, because the minimum is still 6 decimals. I did not change the 2% margin, the stroke-to-extent ratio, the opacity format or the SVG reader.

title: Read R12 and earlier binary DXF (1-byte group codes)
author: valentinevg812-eng
body:
Narrows FF13 in docs/gaps.md (R12 binary DXF read).

## Problem
Binary DXF written before R13 stores each group code in **one** byte, with 255 escaping a 2-byte code (DXF Reference, "Binary DXF Files"). `parse_binary` only knew the R13+ layout (2-byte codes), so such files failed to open with `invalid parameters for 'open': no sections found`, although the README lists R12 binary as supported and docs/file-format-parity.md marked it as a gap. Hit on a real GIS export (`AutoCAD Binary DXF`, POLYLINE/VERTEX, `$DWGCODEPAGE ansi_1252`, no `$ACADVER`).

## Change
- `legacy_binary_layout` tells the layout from the first tag: R13+ starts with a 2-byte code (`00 00` for `0 SECTION`, `E7 03` for a 999 comment); the old layout with a 1-byte `00` followed by the string's first character, or with the 255 escape.
- In the old layout codes are read as one byte, 255 followed by a 2-byte code. Value decoding (strings through `BinaryText`, reals, ints, hex) is shared.
- In R13+, 255 is now an ordinary code, as in #1271 (B10). The two PRs touch the same lines; whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase, and the result is the same.

## Tests
- `cadcraft-dxf`: `r12_binary_parse` (1-byte codes, a real, an int16, a 255-escaped 1001), `binary_layout_detection`, `truncated_r12_binary_never_panics` (every prefix), `r13_binary_code_255_is_ordinary`.
- `cadcraft-io` (`tests/r12_binary.rs`): a synthetic R12 binary drawing with an old-style POLYLINE (closed, 3 vertices) and a LINE on a Cyrillic ANSI_1251 layer opens with both entities; every truncation of it reads without panicking.
- Checked by hand on a third-party R12 binary file (not committed): 2 polylines, correct extents, renders through `cadcraft-cli convert`.
- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm pass.

Docs: file-format-parity.md R12 binary row (read: yes, write: no) and revision history; gaps.md FF13 narrowed to pre-R13 DWG and R12 binary output.

title: DWG: leave out orphaned DGN line style components, so DGN-bloated drawings open (fixes #1482)
author: gurparvez
body:
Fixes #1482.

A DWG that has been through MicroStation can carry hundreds of thousands of DGN line style components (`LS*COMPONENT`) that no line style definition uses. In the file from #1482 (82.8 MB, AC1032) they were 888,483 of 889,053 components and made acadrust's DXF rendition 1,245.9 MB. That's over the 1 GB limit, so the file didn't open. CADCraft doesn't draw DGN line styles. For this file, `dxf_raw::read` would have dropped every one of them after parsing anyway, because their owning `ACAD_DGNLINESTYLECOMP` dictionary is one of the records the failsafe read skips.

## Change

In `crates/dwg`, `drop_orphaned_dgn_components` runs after the failsafe read and before the DXF write:

- It starts from every `LSDEFINITION`'s `root_component` and follows compound entries and point components' stroke and symbol references. Each component is visited once, so cycles end.
- It removes the components it doesn't reach, and the dictionary entries that name them (`hard_owner_entries` is kept consistent).
- Definitions, `Registered` LS objects and every reachable component are kept.
- A read note says how many were left out:

  > DWG: 888483 DGN line style components that no line style definition uses were left out

`docs/file-format-parity.md` gets a line in the DWG paragraph and a revision history row.

## Result on the #1482 file

- **Before:** `converting this 82.8 MB file produced more than 1024 MB of drawing data (the limit)`.
- **After:** opens in the desktop app and in `cadcraft-cli info`/`convert`, with 11,648 model-space entities and 377 layers. The PNG export shows the plans as expected. The other 11,746 skipped records (the existing note) are all DGN line style data by their classes' instance counts, so nothing drawn is missing.
- Memory still peaks at about 6.9 GB. That's acadrust's read itself, the same as reading without CADCraft (#1076).

#1088 and #1155 show the same error with no file attached. They may have the same cause and could be retested with this.

title: Fade objects on locked layers on screen (LAYLOCKFADECTL)
author: mattlafy
body:
Objects on a locked layer draw faded on screen by LAYLOCKFADECTL percent.

- LAYLOCKFADECTL is a header variable, -90 to 90, default 50. 0 or a negative value turns the fade off. GETVAR and SETVAR read and set it.
- The fade applies on screen whether or not transparency display is on; it is not object transparency.
- An object whose own transparency is greater than the fade keeps its own.
- Layer 0 inside a block takes the reference's layer, so a block reference on a locked layer fades its layer-0 contents.
- The fade applies only to render builds with the `on_screen` option set, which only the interactive canvas sets. Plots and SVG, PNG and PDF exports never fade.

Tests: render tests cover the default, 0, negative and 70 values, transparency display on and off, an object more transparent than the fade, plots, unlocked layers, builds without `on_screen` and layer 0 inside a block; an io test checks that SVG and PNG exports of a locked layer's object are not faded; SETVAR/GETVAR coverage includes the range and default.

Part of #1372.

title: Offset: OFFSETGAPTYPE extends, fillets or chamfers polyline corner gaps
author: mattlafy
body:
## What

`OFFSETGAPTYPE` is a system variable (0, 1 or 2; default 0), kept in the drawing header beside
`OFFSETERASE`. When a polyline is offset, the gap at the outside of a corner between two line
segments is filled according to it:

- **0** — both offset segments are extended to meet (the existing join).
- **1** — an arc of radius equal to the offset distance, centred on the original vertex, joins the
  two offset segments.
- **2** — a chamfer line, at the offset distance from the original vertex and square to the
  corner's bisector, joins them.

Inside corners, and joints where either segment is an arc, keep the extended join. The ends of an
open polyline are not corners. OFFSET's "Current settings" line prints the variable's value.

`offset_kind` and `offset_polyline` take the gap type as a parameter; the three OFFSET call sites
read it from the header. The fill is computed in its own function, `gap_fill`.
`docs/geometry-parity.md`'s "Polyline with arcs" row describes the polyline offset as it now is.

## Tests

- A closed 10×10 square offset outward by 1: gap type 0 gives the 12×12 square; 1 gives eight
  vertices with four quarter-arc bulges centred on the corners, area 140 + π; 2 gives eight
  vertices with each chamfer at distance 1 from its corner.
- Inward offset, an open L's inside corner and a line-into-arc joint give the same result for all
  three gap types.
- The OFFSET settings line shows `OFFSETGAPTYPE=1` after `SETVAR OFFSETGAPTYPE 1`.
- `OFFSETGAPTYPE` defaults to 0 and 3 is refused.

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Inquiry: SHAPES reports closed-shape geometry facts
author: mattlafy
body:
## What

`shapes` is a read-only command (no undo, no menu) that reports geometry facts for every closed
shape in the current space: closed polylines (or ones whose last vertex equals the first), circles,
full ellipses and closed splines. Each shape gives:

- `perimeter` and `area` (≥ 0), exact with arcs and bulges (a spline's from its tessellation);
- `winding`: `ccw` or `cw`;
- `centroid`: the area centroid, or `null` at zero area;
- `selfIntersection`: the first crossing of two non-adjacent edges, in edge order, or `null`;
- `duplicateVertices`: `{index, distance}` for each pair of consecutive vertices (`index`,
  `index + 1`, wrapping) within the tolerance.

It filters and pages like `entities` (`type`, `layer`, `window`, `crossing`, `limit` default 200,
`offset`) and takes `tolerance` (positive; default 1e-9 × the extents diagonal). The result is
`{schema: 1, count, returned, offset, truncated, shapes, skipped}`; `skipped` counts every other
match by type with the reason (`open`, `not a closed shape`, …).

`Polyline::centroid` (chord triangles plus each bulge's circular segment, weighted by signed area)
and `polygon_centroid` are in `cadcraft-geom`. `docs/mcp.md` lists the command; the command title
is translated where `Query Texts` is.

## Tests

`crates/engine/tests/shapes.rs`, on drawings built in code with values derived by hand: a 10×10
square both ways round (area 100, perimeter 40, centroid (5, 5), ccw / cw); the square with one
side bulged into a semicircle (area 100 + 12.5π, perimeter 30 + 5π, exact centroid); a bow-tie
(crossing at (5, 5)); a repeated vertex; an open polyline whose ends meet; a circle; an open
polyline, a line and a text under `skipped`; paging (`limit: 1` of three is truncated); bad
`tolerance`, `limit` and `window` are refused. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

Fixes #1436.

title: Options: an interface scale preference
author: mattlafy
body:
## Problem

The interface's size follows the system's scale factor only. On some screens every menu, palette and dialog is too small to read (#1432); on others it is too large (#1369, #1376). There is no setting to change it.

## Change

This is a quality-of-life preference of CADCraft's own, not a parity feature: other CAD programs leave interface size to the operating system's display scaling.

- `interfaceScale` is a new interface preference in OPTIONS: a number from 0.5 to 3, default 1 (the system's own size). The JSON form reports and sets it (`options {"interfaceScale": 1.5}`), refuses values outside the range or that are not numbers ("interfaceScale must be from 0.5 to 3") with nothing changed, and `"reset": true` restores 1.
- The Options dialog's Display tab has an "Interface scale" row after "Animation effects", offering 75, 100, 125, 150, 175, 200, 250 and 300 %.
- The scale is applied as egui's zoom factor, so menus, palettes, dialogs and the command line all change together. It is applied only when the saved value changes, so egui's own keyboard zoom still works within a session and is not saved.
- The preference is kept in the profile and survives restarts; an out-of-range saved value is skipped.
- Ukrainian translation for the new label.

## Tests

`tests/options_followups.rs`: the default, setting 1.5 and the resulting zoom factor after a frame, refused values changing nothing, the profile round trip, a skipped out-of-range saved value, reset, and the Display tab showing the row. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

Fixes #1432.

title: ID, DIST and LIST report Z
author: aldozar
body:
ID, DIST and LIST said Z = 0 whatever the drawing held. `ID` printed a fixed `Z = 0`, `DIST` a fixed `Delta Z = 0` and `Angle from XY Plane = 0`, and `LIST` printed `Z=0` for lines, circles, arcs and polyline vertices, though the drawing kept every Z. In a topographic drawing (survey points, contours at their elevation, a TIN of 3D faces) the levels could not be read in CADCraft at all.

### Change (`crates/engine/src/cmd/inquiry.rs`)
- **ID / DIST:** points reach these commands in 2D, so the Z is that of what is drawn at the point, as AutoCAD reports a snapped point's. `z_at` takes the object a pick finds there and its Z at that point:
  - a POINT's Z;
  - a 3D LINE or 3D POLYLINE interpolated along the segment;
  - an LWPOLYLINE's elevation (down Z for a mirrored one, extrusion −Z);
  - a CIRCLE's or ARC's centre (already read in world coordinates);
  - a TEXT, MTEXT or block reference's insertion point;
  - the plane of a 3DFACE under the point.

  With nothing there it uses the current elevation (`ELEVATION`). A Z given with a JSON point (`[x, y, z]`) wins.
- **DIST** gives the 3D distance, `Delta Z` and the angle from the XY plane. The JSON result adds `dz` and `angleFromXY`. Flat points give the same answers as before.
- **LIST** gives the Z of lines, circles, arcs and text start points, a line's 3D length and its deltas, and a polyline's elevation, which is also the Z of its vertices.

Not changed here: snaps themselves still return 2D points (part of #1412). Drawing from a snapped 3D point still lands at Z = 0 until that is done. A full-turn angle that rounds to "360" in the output is #1256.

### Checked on a topographic drawing
On a real topographic DWG in UTM coordinates (survey points, contour polylines at their elevation, a TIN):
- `ID` at three survey points gives their stored elevations (1879.528, 1879.470, 1879.709).
- `ID` on a contour gives its elevation (1881.236).
- `DIST` between two points gives their 3D distance and `Delta Z = -0.058`.

title: Object snaps give points their Z; LINE and POINT keep it (OSNAPZ)
author: aldozar
body:
Part of #1412 (the snaps part: "snaps … are all 2D").

**Stacked on #1431 and #1509.** It uses #1431's `Session::point_z` (the Z of the point being entered) and #1509's `z_at` (the Z of what is drawn at a point). Until they land, the diff here includes theirs. The change of its own is the last commit.

### Problem
Points reach commands in 2D (`Input::Point(Vec2)`), so an object snap's Z was lost. A line drawn between a survey point at 1880 and a contour at elevation 1881 lay at z = 0, which quietly corrupts topographic and Civil 3D drawings.

### Change
- **Snapped picks:** `Session::input_snapped`, the path every snapped canvas click takes, sets `point_z` to the Z of what the snap found. That is the object a pick finds at the snap point, at that point, the same lookup ID uses (#1509): a point's Z, a 3D line interpolated, a polyline's elevation, a 3D face's plane, etc. This is AutoCAD's behaviour with `OSNAPZ` 0.
- **`OSNAPZ`** (new system variable, off by default): on, a snap gives the current elevation (`ELEVATION`) instead.
- **Picks with no Z:** a point picked through a layout viewport, or without an object snap, stays at z = 0.
- **LINE and POINT** build their points with `point_z`, so they keep a typed `x,y,z` (#1431) as well as a snapped Z. 3DPOLY already did. LASTPOINT's Z follows (#1431), so `@dx,dy` after a snapped point continues at its level.

Not changed: the rest of #1412 (display, extents and picking in 3D, extrusion direction), and other drawing commands (PLINE's elevation, CIRCLE, …).

### Tests
`crates/engine/tests/snap_z.rs`, 3 tests, all fail without this commit:
- **LINE:** snapped from a survey point (Node) to a contour's end (Endpoint) it runs from (0, 0, 1880) to (10, 0, 1881).
- **`OSNAPZ` 1:** the snapped end takes `ELEVATION`, an unsnapped pick stays at z = 0, and GETVAR reports it.
- **POINT:** snapped to a contour it takes its elevation, and LINE keeps typed Z values (`100,100,3`, `@10,0,2`).

title: Add MTEXT width and column-height grips
author: brunofon98
body:
# Add MTEXT width and column-height grips

Selecting MTEXT currently exposes only its insertion grip. This change adds a right-hand column-width grip and a bottom box-height grip, with click-click and press-drag-release editing. Width changes rewrap the text; box-height changes flow it through columns without changing character height.

The grips use the renderer's layout and follow rotated text. Resizing keeps the frame's top-left fixed, including non-top-left attachment points. Preview, cancel, undo/redo and JSON `grip.*` calls share the existing engine command path. The insertion grip continues to move the text.

## Validation

- Full `cargo xtask ci`: passed all six steps: fmt, Clippy, workspace tests, assets, layers and WASM.
- Engine regression tests cover width/wrapping, dynamic column flow, rotated attachment, preview/cancel, undo/redo and hostile grip sizes.
- An egui integration test presses, drags and releases each resize grip.
- Manual Windows check: all three grips are drawn; width and column height survive DXF save/reopen while character height stays unchanged.

## Scope

The height grip sets a uniform column height; shortening an uncolumned MTEXT creates dynamic columns. Independent per-column/gutter grips and single-line TEXT resizing are outside this change.

This branch is based directly on main. It does not include or depend on the selection-bounds and existing-MTEXT-editor changes proposed in #1022 and #1425, which were used in earlier local testing.

## Try it

1. Create MTEXT with height 1, width 5 and contents `AAAA AAAA AAAA`.
2. Select it once and drag the right triangle to widen or narrow the text box.
3. Drag the bottom triangle upward to shorten the box and flow text into columns.
4. Drag the square insertion grip to move the text; check undo/redo and cancel.

Implemented with assistance from OpenAI Codex on behalf of @brunofon98.

title: Bound control-port input, and follow stored paths only on this computer or the drawing's share
author: skylartaylor
body:
# Bound control-port input, and follow stored paths only on this computer or the drawing's share

- The control port closes the connection on the first line that isn't a request, with limits on
  idle time, writes and queued requests. Before this, it skipped bad lines, so anything that could
  reach the port could send commands to it while it was on.
- Xrefs and data links follow stored paths only on this computer or the drawing's share, with a
  per-open size cap.

## Dependency

`craft-libs` is merged (storytold/craft-libs#169) and this branch already pins `craft-docpath` to
the merged rev, `82a24b006eefa036b43c09a67fb9a3fbd17ffe63` — that is `main` after the merge, so it
includes `resolve_absolute` and the Windows colon refusal, not just the older `12281d07`. No
dependency change is needed before merging; `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` are already updated and
carry no reference to a fork.

## Credit

All commits on this branch are authored by **@aiongg**, who did the design and the implementation
across every app in this family. I have only opened the pull request, because they were unreachable
and the team was ready to build. Thank you for the work, and for the care taken over the test
coverage in particular.

## Testing

`cargo xtask ci` on the branch, plus the regression tests added in these commits, which fail
without the change. Please re-run the full gate on a current toolchain before merging.

---

Opened on @aiongg's behalf. Happy to hand this over, or close it in favour of their own PR, as soon
as they are back.

title: cadcraft-cli: --help / -h / help exit 0 and print the usage to stdout
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1525

## What

`--help`, `-h` and `help` now print the usage block to **stdout** and exit **0**, exactly like `--version` already did. Bare `cadcraft-cli` (no arguments at all) is unchanged: usage on stderr, exit 1, like git.

Verified on main (0.8.0, 714111d) before and after this change:

```console
$ cadcraft-cli --help >/dev/null; echo $?    # before
1
$ cadcraft-cli --help >/dev/null; echo $?    # after
0
$ cadcraft-cli --version >/dev/null; echo $? # already correct before
0
```

## How

One match arm in `cli()`, next to the existing `--version` arm, using `outln!` so a closed stdout is handled the same way as everywhere else in this binary (no broken-pipe panic, #537).

## Tests

New `apps/cadcraft-cli/tests/help.rs`:

- the three help flags exit 0 with the usage on stdout and an empty stderr
- bare invocation still reports on stderr and still exits 1

The whole `-p cadcraft-cli` suite passes (24 tests), `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` are clean.

Context: #1520 and #1521 were reports of mine that turned out to be wrong — I had filed them from an outdated install instead of the current development version, and closed them with corrections. This remaining point was re-verified on main before filing.

title: cadcraft-cli: a failed script line costs that line, not the drawing
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1522

## What

A failing line in a script no longer takes the whole run with it. Verified on main (0.8.0, 714111d) before this change: `run --sample --script-file bad.scr --save out.dxf` exited 1, printed only the error, wrote no DXF, and the good commands after the bad line never ran.

After this change:

```console
$ cadcraft-cli run --sample --script-file good.scr --save good.dxf
script line 2: unknown command `THIS_IS_NOT_A_COMMAND`
Command: CIRCLE
Command: LINE
wrote good.dxf (41458 bytes)
script: 1 line(s) failed; everything else ran
$ echo $?
1
```

Both good commands ran (sample counts: Circle 7→8, Line 16→17), the drawing is written, and the exit status still reports the failure, so scripts and agents can check it.

## How

- `Session::script_report` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`) runs the same lines as `Session::script` but collects every failure as `(1-based line, EngineError)` instead of propagating the first one. `Session::script` is unchanged, so the SCRIPT command and the UI keep their current behaviour.
- `cadcraft-cli run` uses it, prints `script line N: <error>` per failure as it goes, still performs `--save` / `--export`, and returns the failure only after the output is written.

## Tests

- `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`: `script_report_keeps_the_lines_that_are_fine` (the drawing survives the bad line, the position is the line in the script, the error is the unknown command) and `script_report_is_empty_when_everything_runs`.
- `apps/cadcraft-cli/tests/script_failures.rs`: the case above end to end (exit 1, the error names the line, the DXF is written with both good entities) and a fully good script still exiting 0.
- Whole suites pass: 298 engine tests, 24 CLI tests; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean.

title: UCS: the UCS command, and points, angles and coordinates in the current UCS (part of #1106)
author: SBaksa
body:
Part of #1106: a **current user coordinate system** and the **UCS command**, with points, angles and coordinates read and shown in it. This is the first of a few PRs: everything here works in UCSs whose XY plane is the world XY plane (any origin, any rotation about Z), which is what 2D drafting uses. UCSs tilted out of it come after the 3D views in #1005.

## What changes for the user
- **UCS**: pick an origin, then optionally a point on the new X axis and one in the XY plane (the default option); **World**, **Previous** (ten steps, per space), **NAmed** (Restore / Save / Delete / `?`, with wildcards), **OBject** (lines, arcs, circles, polylines, points, text, blocks, 2D solids, flat 3D faces, dimensions), **View** and **Z** (default UCSAXISANG). **X, Y, ZAxis and Face** tilt the UCS and say they are not available yet. Menus: Tools > New UCS > World / Origin / 3 Point / View / Z.
- **Typed input follows the UCS**: `x,y` from its origin along its axes, `@dx,dy` along its axes, polar angles from its X axis, `#` absolute in the UCS, `*` / `@*` world. Every direction prompt (TEXT, INSERT, ARRAY, HATCH, polar points…) and ANGBASE are measured from the UCS X axis; angle sizes (ROTATE by 90) are unchanged. **Dynamic Input** shows and sends its values in the UCS, so what's previewed is what's placed.
- **Coordinates are shown in the UCS**: the status bar, ID and DIST.
- **UCS icon**: turns with the UCS, sits at the UCS origin when it fits on screen (UCSICON ORigin, the default), and shows the corner square only in the World UCS. - **A UCS change is undone like an edit.**

title: macOS: file dialogs no longer run inside the window's event handler (fixes #1527)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Fixes storytold/CadCraft#1527

**Cause:** on macOS the Open and Save panels ran modally (rfd's synchronous `FileDialog`) inside winit's event handler. When you resize the panel, its window events go back into that handler, and winit aborts the app. This is the same crash VectorCraft fixed for storytold/vectorcraft#867 (#895, then sheets in #1099) and PhotoCraft fixed in #1071 (storytold/photocraft#1802). CADCraft uses crates.io `winit 0.30.13` and `rfd 0.17.2`, not craft-libs, so the fix has to be made in this repo.

**Fix:**
- `Services::start_pick` (new, optional): shows a file dialog without waiting and passes the answer to a callback. On macOS the desktop app starts the dialog from a thread. rfd 0.17 then runs the panel on the main thread through `dispatch2::run_on_main`, from the run loop and outside the event handler. Windows and Linux are unchanged.
- `CadApp::pick_then(Pick, then)` is now the one path for every place that opens a dialog: Open, New from template, Recover, Save As (and QSAVE on an untitled drawing), EXPORTPDF, Import, Export, Publish, XATTACH, Linetype Manager ▸ From File, and Plot OK. A synchronous picker (Windows, Linux, tests) gives the same results as before. With `start_pick`, `then` runs in a later frame once the answer arrives, and any error it returns shows in the status bar. A second dialog can't open while one is already up.
- Choosing Save in the close prompt waits for the Save dialog, then goes on closing. If you cancel the Save dialog, the prompt stays up.
- One small behaviour change: cancelling the XATTACH file dialog now does nothing. Before, it fell through to the command-line prompt. All the other dialogs already behaved this way.

**Tested (Windows host):**
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-ui-egui --lib -- exchange:: menus:: closing:: managers:: xrefs::` (21 passed), and `--test dialog_dispatch --test save_version` passed. This includes a new regression test, `exchange::tests::a_deferred_dialog_acts_when_its_answer_arrives`.

title: UCS: ortho, snap, grid, polar and object snap tracking, and DIMLINEAR follow the current UCS (part of #1106, depends on #1533)
author: SBaksa
body:
Part of #1106, **stacked on #1533** (the first commit of this branch is #1533's; review the second, "ortho, snap, grid, polar…"). Once #1533 lands this shrinks to that commit.

With #1533 the UCS changes how points are typed and shown, but the drafting aids still worked along the world axes, so a turned UCS felt half-done: ortho locked to world horizontal, the grid didn't turn. This makes them follow the current UCS.

## What changes
- **Ortho (F8)** along the UCS axes, also for direct distance entry with ortho on and TK tracking. In isometric drafting, the isoplane axes turn with the UCS.
- **Grid and grid snap** lie in the UCS: SNAPBASE is a UCS point and SNAPANG an angle from its X axis (`snap::grid_frame_in`). The red and green axes are the UCS's X and Y.
- **Polar tracking** is measured from ANGBASE off the UCS X axis; **object snap tracking**'s horizontal/vertical paths run along the UCS axes; the tooltip ("Polar: 20 < 0°") reads the angle in the UCS, matching Dynamic Input and the status bar.
- **DIMLINEAR**: automatic horizontal/vertical and the Horizontal/Vertical keywords measure along the UCS axes at the command line. JSON parameters stay in world coordinates, as everywhere.

## How
One new value, `Settings::ucs_angle`, filled in by `Session::drafting_settings()` (which ortho, polar and tracking already read), and one frame function for snap and grid. No per-command changes. In the World UCS everything takes the same path as before except the drawn rectangular grid, which now lies in the snap frame (below).

## A behaviour change worth knowing
The rectangular grid is now drawn in the snap frame, so it **honours SNAPANG and SNAPBASE**. Before, grid *snap* used them but the *drawn* grid ignored them, so the two disagreed whenever SNAPANG was not 0.

## Tests
One more LISP test for #1533's part: `entsel` and `getcorner` answer in the UCS.

title: Canvas: clicks count when the button goes down, even while the mouse moves (fixes #1001, #1546)
author: filforce95
body:
Fixes #1001. Fixes #1546.

Implements the press-first model @grandixximo proposed in [#1001](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/issues/1001#issuecomment-6184287156). Replaces #1017 and #1059, and covers the case #1299 fixes (several clicks in one slow frame).

## Problem
Clicks were decided when the button came up. egui treats a press that moves more than a few points as a drag, so a click made while the mouse was moving was lost (object picks, the second window corner, CP points) or taken where the hand had got to (points, #835), so MOVE/COPY base points landed off the clicked spot.

## Change
- **A press acts at once, where the button went down**: it places the point (snapped as the cursor would be there), picks the object, or sets a window corner. Every press in the frame's events counts (#815).
- **Drag detection** (`canvas/press.rs`): once the pointer leaves a 6-point tolerance, a 0.25 s timer starts. If the button is still down then, it is a drag and the release closes the window the press opened. Otherwise it was a click and the window waits for the next press. Holding still never makes a drag.
- Grips (no command running), ZOOM Realtime, the Dynamic Input options menu, model tiles and double-clicks keep their release-based clicks.

## Behaviour change to review
A drag that **starts on an object** used to open a window; now the press picks the object and the drag adds nothing. This follows the model, but differs from #63 ("even over an object"). It should be checked against AutoCAD.

title: Keep rectangle opposite corners free of ortho (STRETCH window and friends)

With ortho on (F8), STRETCH's crossing window was bent onto an axis: the opposite corner snapped to the horizontal or vertical from the first corner, the window collapsed to a line and selected nothing.

title: AutoComplete: Enter takes the suggestion, adaptive suggestions
author: silaghis
body:
## Problem
Typing part of a command name at the command line and pressing Enter (`str` for STRETCH) was refused as an unknown command, although AutoComplete was already highlighting STRETCH. Only Tab or a click took the suggestion. The list order was also fixed, so it never learned which command you meant. In AutoCAD, Enter takes the highlighted suggestion and adaptive suggestions keep the command you chose for a prefix on top.

## Change
**Enter takes the highlighted suggestion** (`ui-egui/src/cmdline.rs`, `submit`)
- Only when the word means nothing by itself. A command, alias, LISP `c:` command, system variable name (→ SETVAR), interface command or `(expression)` still runs as typed. New engine helper `Session::knows_command_word` follows the same resolution as `Session::start`.
- A line with spaces (a script) is read as before. Only keyboard Enter changes; `cmdline.input`, scripts and MCP are unchanged.

**Adaptive suggestions**
- The command line counts the commands started from it and remembers the command chosen for each typed prefix (by Enter, Tab or a click).
- Ranking: an exact command or alias stays first, then the command chosen for the prefix, then the most used; ties keep the current order.
- Kept with the preferences (`commandUsage`). It is bounded (512 entries) and validated on load, so hostile values are skipped.
- `adaptiveSuggestions: false` in `UiState` (`ui.set`) turns the ordering off. It is only written to prefs when off, so the default prefs JSON is unchanged.

**Docs**
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: AutoComplete row now "partial" with what is there and what is missing (sysvar, mid-string and synonym search); revision history entry.
- `docs/control-protocol.md`: `adaptiveSuggestions`.

## Tests
- 5 new tests in `cmdline.rs` (`autocomplete_tests`): Enter on a suggestion and again next time; words that must run as typed (sysvar, alias, LISP, unknown, script line); ranking by use and by pick, the exact match staying first, ordering off; Tab learning the…

title: Keep table cell line breaks through DXF save and reopen
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/io/src/dxf_write.rs:916-925 (ACAD_TABLE cell text written with w.s(1/2, …)) together with crates/dxf/src/lib.rs:416,450,514 (string tags turn '\r'/'\n' into ' '); read back in crates/io/src/dxf_read.rs:~580 (acad_table)` (no existing issue): Line breaks in table cell text are replaced by spaces when the drawing is saved to DXF and reopened.

## Cause
The ACAD_TABLE writer put raw cell text into group 1/2. The DXF tag writer replaces every carriage return or line feed in a string tag with a space, so a cell with a line break was read back on one line.

## Fix
The writer now encodes cell text with mtext_literal, the same encoding attributes use: a line feed becomes \P, and backslashes and braces are escaped. The reader decodes \P, \\, \{ and \} in acad_table. Other formatting codes in cell text are kept as written.

## Verified
- Regression test `table_cell_line_breaks_survive_a_dxf_roundtrip`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-io --lib table_cell_line_breaks_survive_a_dxf_roundtrip`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The DXF tag writer still flattens raw line breaks in other string tags. Other MTEXT formatting codes in cell text from foreign files are still kept as written. The anonymous *T block was not changed. Existing DXF files whose table cells already contain a literal \P, \\, \{ or \} now read those sequences as the decoded characters.

title: Menu bar switches to the hovered menu once one is open (fixes #1567)
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #1567.

The in-window menu bar built each title with `ui.menu_button` (`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`, `menu_bar`). In egui 0.36 that is a `MenuButton` whose popup only toggles on click. egui's `MenuBar` has no hover switching between top-level menus, only between submenus. Once a menu was open, pointing at another title only highlighted it.

`menu_bar` now draws the titles first. If one of the bar's menus is open, a new `switch_on_hover` helper opens the hovered title's menu with `Popup::open_id`, which also closes the old one, since egui keeps one popup open per viewport. Then the menus are shown with `Popup::menu`. The switch runs before any menu is drawn, so two menus never show in the same frame. A title clicked this frame is skipped, because the click already toggles it.

What stays the same:

- With no menu open, hovering does nothing.
- Clicking the open title, clicking elsewhere, Esc and choosing an item close the menu.
- Submenus, widget ids and styling are unchanged. The bar uses the default `MenuConfig`, so bare `Popup::menu` has the same close behaviour and style `MenuButton` gave it.

`docs/ui-parity.md` notes the behaviour in the Menu bar row and the revision history.

The change is about 20 lines. #961 uses the same `Popup::is_id_open` / `Popup::open_id` / `Popup::menu` pattern, so it should port either way.

title: AltGr types @, { and € at the command line instead of a key name or a shortcut (fixes #1551)
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #1551.

The input was lost in three places:

- **Key name typed as text.** Pressing AltGr in the browser typed `AltGraph` at the command line. eframe's web runner (0.36.2) passes on the browser's name for any key missing from its list as text (`text_from_keyboard_event` in `eframe/src/web/input.rs`), and `crates/ui-egui/src/cmdline.rs` appended it.
- **AltGr character dropped on Windows.** In a browser on Windows, the character AltGr types never arrived. The web runner drops the text of a key pressed with Ctrl held (`install_keydown` in `eframe/src/web/events.rs`), and browsers on Windows report AltGr as Ctrl and Alt held.
- **AltGr ran Ctrl shortcuts.** The shortcut table in `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs` used egui's `consume_shortcut`, which ignores an extra Alt. egui has no key for `€` or `£`, so the press carries the physical key. AltGr+E ran Ctrl+E (ISOPLANE) and AltGr+3 ran Ctrl+3 (Tool Sets).

The desktop app already types AltGr characters. On Windows, winit leaves Ctrl and Alt out of the modifiers while AltGr is held on an AltGr layout (`get_agnostic_mods` in winit's `keyboard_layout.rs`). On Linux, AltGr is its own modifier.

Changes:

- `crates/ui-egui/src/altgr.rs` (new):
  - `drop_key_names` removes key-name text such as `AltGraph`, `Dead` and `Unidentified` while no text field has the keyboard.
  - `restore_typed` puts characters typed with Ctrl+Alt back into the input right after their key press, and takes Ctrl and Alt off that press. It does nothing on macOS.
- `apps/cadcraft-web/src/altgr.rs` (new): a `keydown` listener on the canvas records characters typed with Ctrl and Alt both held (not letters or digits). The web shell's `raw_input_hook` passes them to `restore_typed`.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`: a Ctrl+Alt press no longer matches a Ctrl shortcut. No shortcut in the table uses Ctrl+Alt, and plain Ctrl shortcuts are unchanged.

title: FILLET with a circle keeps the circle whole and draws a short arc that runs on from the line (fixes #1559)
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Fixes #1559.

FILLET never edited the circle, but it chose the fillet arc badly. `fillet_curves` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/modify2.rs` took the tangent circle nearest the picks. It kept the side of the line on the pick's side of the tangent point, without checking that the two fit together. Users click the line between its two possible tangent points, and there this gave an arc that looped more than half way round or met the line at a cusp. A line tangent to the circle got a zero-length fillet, drawn as a full extra circle. Both look like a broken circle.

FILLET now looks at every tangent circle, nearest the picks first (`curves::ttr_all` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/curves.rs`; `ttr` returns its first, so CIRCLE TTR is unchanged). It takes the first whose short arc runs on smoothly from the picked part of each object. A full circle has no side and is never trimmed, so the line or arc decides. When no candidate fits the picks, FILLET takes the nearest and keeps the other side of the line or arc. That happens when the line is picked between the tangent points.

Also:

- Zero-length fillets are skipped.
- An arc trimmed to nothing is left alone instead of becoming a full circle.
- A negative or NaN radius is refused, as `fillet_curvy` already did.

Arc+line, arc+arc and arc+circle use the same choice, since they had the same loop and cusp problem. Circle+circle is unchanged. TRIMMODE and No trim work as before. Line/line FILLET still treats a negative radius as 0; that path is not touched. `docs/geometry-parity.md` is updated.

Tests, in `crates/engine/tests/fillet_circles.rs` (the command-line, crossing-lines and arcs tests fail on main):

- `fillet_keeps_the_circle_and_follows_the_picks`: JSON form, picks on either side and in either order. The circle keeps its handle, centre and radius. There is one radius-30 arc under 180°, tangent to both. The line ends at the tangent point and runs on into the arc. The fillet follows the picks.

title: Plot dialog: Apply to Layout saves model space's page setup too (part of #1563)
author: C00kieMonsta
body:
Part of #1563 (the Apply to Layout item). The other items in that issue (Save as PDF button, named page setups, scale presets, copies, plot style toggle) are not in this PR.

The Plot dialog showed Apply to Layout only for paper-space layouts. Model space had no page setup of its own. The dialog, PLOT and PREVIEW built the same default every time (extents fitted on A4 or ANSI A). DXF/DWG saves wrote a fixed default into the Model layout's plot settings.

The drawing now keeps a page setup for model space (`Drawing::model_page` in `crates/doc`). It is unset until saved, so drawings that never set it behave and save as before. `cadcraft_render::paper::model_page` gives the stored setup or the old default. It replaces the copies of that default in the ui, io and engine crates.

**PAGESETUP.** `pagesetup {layout: "Model", ...}` stores the setup as one undo step. "Model" matches in any case, and on the Model tab `layout` can be left out. Model takes extents, display or limits as its plot area. `layout` is refused (no sheet), and so is `window` (a page setup has no place for the corners). title: Bound CAL unary minus/plus and ^ chain recursion
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/utility/calc.rs:124-140 (Parser::unary recursion, MAX_DEPTH only counted in expr() and '[')` (no existing issue): CAL / QuickCalc: a long run of unary minus signs (or a long `^` chain) overflows the stack and aborts the process.

## Cause
`Parser::unary` calls itself once per leading `-`/`+` and once per `^` exponent without touching any depth counter. About 10,000 minus signs, which fits under `MAX_LEN`, recurse about 10,000 frames deep, overflow the stack and abort the process.

## Fix
Added `Parser::operand`. The `-`, `+` and `^` recursion in `unary` now goes through it. It uses its own `unary_depth` counter capped at `MAX_DEPTH` and returns "expression too deeply nested" beyond that. The counter is decremented before the result is propagated, so the error path leaves it consistent. The regression test covers 9,990 leading minus signs, a long `^` chain, and shorter `+`/`-`/`^` runs.

## Verified
- Regression tests `deep_unary_chain_does_not_overflow_the_stack`, `parenthesis_nesting_just_under_the_limit_still_parses`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib calc::tests::`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The existing `depth` counter and the paren/bracket nesting limit in `expr` and `[` are unchanged. A new test checks that 199 nested parentheses still parse and 200 are rejected.

Also adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

title: dxf: borrow sections and records from the tag list instead of copying them

Opening a DWG held its DXF rendition three times over: once as the parsed tag list, once more

58 MB heating plan (1.56 million entities, 33 million group codes) the read path peaked at
8.9 GB while the finished drawing is 183 MB (#1076).

- `cadcraft_dxf::Section` and the new `Record` alias are views into the parsed tag list

  the tests slice instead of cloning. `Tag::text()` borrows a string tag's value.

  the DXF-rendition limit (a fixed 1 GB today, which refuses a plain 238 MB architect's plan) is

title: io: read an attribute's vertical alignment from group 74, not the field length in 73
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

Attributes from DWG files sat too high: a middle-centred or middle-right one by half its text
height, a top-aligned one by a whole height; bottom-aligned ones sat a third too low.
Left-aligned attributes (the majority) looked right by luck.

Cause: an attribute's vertical alignment is DXF group 74; its group 73 is the *field length*.
`text_from` took `73.or(74)` for every text-like entity, and acadrust's DWG→DXF writer emits
`73 0` for every ATTRIB and ATTDEF before `74`, so the alignment was read as 0 = baseline and
the alignment point was taken for the baseline. (AutoCAD-written DXF can carry the field length
too; BricsCAD and libredwg omit it when 0, which is why DXF round trips didn't show it.)

- `text_from(t, attribute)`: TEXT reads group 73, ATTRIB and ATTDEF read group 74.
- `docs/file-format-parity.md` revision row; ROADMAP log entry.

## How you verified it

- New `attribute_vertical_alignment_is_group_74_not_the_field_length`: a placed ATTRIB with
  `73 0 / 72 1 / 74 3` reads as top-centre at its alignment point, an ATTDEF with `74 2` as
  middle-right, a TEXT with `73 2` still as middle. Fails before the fix (baseline).

  own PDF plot, both rasterised at 40 px/mm, glyph rows compared, calibrated on a middle-left

title: geom: a noise-level bulge is a straight segment (blown-up extents, frozen open)
author: grandixximo
body:
## Problem

Two real-world DWG block libraries (`FURNITURE.dwg`, 31 MB, 100k entities; a kitchen/bathroom blocks file) opened to a **blank canvas and froze the app**:

- The drawing's extents computed to ±10¹¹ units, so the opening view and Zoom Extents fit the window to nothing — the drawing is there, just sub-pixel.
- Tessellating the giant arcs behind those extents stalls the UI.

## Root cause

DWG reads leave floating-point dust **bulges of ~1e-10 to 1e-12** on long polyline segments (observed in closed LWPOLYLINEs inside dynamic blocks, e.g. bulge 3.4e-12 on a 99-unit chord). `bulge_to_arc` guarded only `bulge.abs() < 1e-12` **absolute**, so these slipped through and produced arcs of radius up to 7.4×10¹². Three inserts in `FURNITURE.dwg` carried the whole extents explosion; the other file rendered the noise-arcs directly as a \"spiral of circles\".

## Fix

The sagitta of a bulge segment is exactly `chord·|bulge|/2`. Guard on that instead of the absolute bulge: below `EPS` the arc is indistinguishable from the chord at any zoom, so it converts to a straight segment. Real shallow arcs (e.g. sagitta 0.005 on a 1000-unit chord) stay arcs.

After the fix both files open correctly with sane extents (`[348,-94] → [469,192]`) and render fully.

Regression test `bulge_noise_is_straight` covers a noise bulge on a long chord (→ straight), a noise bulge on a short chord (→ straight), and a real shallow arc (→ kept).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p cadcraft-geom` — 85/85 pass
- [x] Both affected DWGs open and render correctly via `cadcraft-cli run FILE --export out.png`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-geom --all-targets` clean

title: desktop: CADCRAFT_STENCIL=0 runs without a stencil buffer (black window on old Intel)
author: grandixximo
body:
## Problem

A user on an HP EliteBook 8470p (Intel HD 4000 / Ivy Bridge, Mesa on Devuan Linux, X11) gets a **black window at startup** on every release since 0.7.0; 0.6.x works. Their log shows a completely healthy startup — adapter and device created, `gpu canvas: target Rgba8Unorm, stencil Some(Stencil8)`, no errors — and a black window. `WGPU_BACKEND=gl` makes no difference.

The 0.6→0.7 delta includes `stencil_buffer: 8` on the window's render pass (clipped layout viewports, 7fcdc6e). A test build with the stencil request removed **draws correctly** on the user's machine, confirming the stencil pass as the trigger.

## Why not a capability query

The driver (Mesa/crocus on Ivy Bridge) *claims* stencil support — device creation and the stencil render pass succeed silently. wgpu's format-feature negotiation would report it supported. This is a driver bug, not a missing capability, so auto-detection at init can't catch it; the failure has to be worked around explicitly. (A targeted adapter-name heuristic for known-bad hardware is possible as a follow-up, but is unproven beyond this one sample and risks false positives.)

## Fix

`CADCRAFT_STENCIL=0` (also `no`/`false`) starts the window without a stencil buffer, with a startup warning. The no-stencil path already exists and degrades gracefully: clipped layout viewports simply draw unclipped. Documented in `docs/hardware-parity.md` next to `CADCRAFT_VSYNC`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p cadcraft` — 46/46 pass, incl. new `stencil_off_only_on_an_explicit_no`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p cadcraft --all-targets` clean
- [x] No-stencil binary verified on the affected hardware (user confirms graphics render)

title: render: a stale *D dimension block is regenerated from the defpoints
author: grandixximo
body:
## Problem

A real-world DWG (a Vietnamese as-built plan set, 1,899 dimensions) opens with **every dimension rendered ~400k units away from its geometry**: measurements and entities in different places.

Each dimension's cached `*D` block picture sits at a constant offset (+396,690, +259,489) from the dimension's defpoints — the geometry moved after dimensioning and the cache went stale. CADCraft draws the cached block as-is ([`EntityKind::Dimension`](crates/render/src/lib.rs) render arm), so the stale picture wins over the defpoints.

## Fix

Draw the cached block only when its picture still contains the defpoint (1e-3 relative tolerance). Otherwise regenerate from the defpoints — the same path already used when a dimension has no block.

## Test plan

- [x] Regression test both ways: stale block ignored and regenerated; fresh block drawn as cached
- [x] `cargo test -p cadcraft-render` — 84/84 pass
- [x] `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-render --all-targets` clean

title: Reject non-hex characters such as '+' in Rgb::parse_hex
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/lib.rs:23-29` (no existing issue): Rgb::parse_hex accepts a leading '+' as a valid hex colour.

## Cause
`Rgb::parse_hex` only checked that the text was 6 ASCII characters, then called `u32::from_str_radix`. That function accepts a leading `+`, so input like `+12345` was parsed as a colour.

## Fix

title: Write RevcloudProps xdata on revision clouds
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1570

## Cause
REVCLOUD created a closed arc LWPOLYLINE but never set the entity's `common.xdata`. The saved cloud therefore had no `RevcloudProps` xdata, which is what AutoCAD and readers like ezdxf use to tell a revision cloud from a plain polyline. In object mode, the code also copied the source object's `common` over the new cloud.

## Fix
A new `add_cloud` helper in `draw2.rs` is now the only way the JSON command and both interactive paths create a cloud. It attaches `1001 RevcloudProps / 1070 0 / 1040 <arc length>` xdata. In object mode it keeps the source object's properties and other apps' xdata, drops any old `RevcloudProps` block, then adds the new one. The existing DXF writer saves this xdata and registers the `RevcloudProps` APPID.

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::draw2::tests::revcloud_saves_revcloudprops_xdata`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib revcloud_saves_revcloudprops_xdata`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The DXF writer and the cloud geometry (vertices, bulges, calligraphy widths) are unchanged. The 1070 value is always 0, matching ezdxf's layout; it does not encode the Normal/Calligraphy style.

title: Add an experimental lightweight read-only CAD viewer
author: Dennis-pan-x
body:
Opening a drawing just for review currently starts the full editing frontend. This adds a separate experimental native `cadcraft-viewer` app that reuses the existing reader, document and renderer without linking the editing engine, constraint solver or editor UI.

The frontend opens DWG/DXF/DWT, supports cursor-centered zoom, pan/fit, transient layer visibility, model/layout navigation, freely picked two-point distances and export to a **new** PDF. Input files are opened read-only; there is no drawing save or autosave. Every diagnostic/export output uses `create_new`, so an existing output or source hard link cannot be truncated.

The shell follows CADCraft's slate palette, type scale, compact controls and bottom model/layout tabs. It uses the same `craft-ui` icon-button component and a small subset of CADCraft's original line-icon geometry. User-selected MIT/Apache-licensed origami-bird/drafting-tools artwork identifies the viewer in its toolbar, native window, Windows executable and desktop shortcut. Its cyan/charcoal/amber palette follows the family style while the origami bird distinguishes it from the editor. An RGBA PNG master and PNG/ICO exports are attributed in `ATTRIBUTION.md`. Restricted ArtCraft marks are not bundled. Windows version metadata identifies this as a community viewer preview.

The self-contained GPU backend is extracted from `ui-egui::gpu` into an engine-free L5 `cadcraft-render-wgpu` crate; the editor re-exports its existing API and keeps its original draw mode. The viewer defaults to hardware GPU geometry with four-sample antialiasing. Mesh preparation/upload runs on the worker; ordinary pan/zoom only updates view uniforms, retaining vertex origins until their precision budget is exceeded. Viewer-specific ordered groups preserve fills, transparency, masks and XLINE/RAY ordering. Infinite spans extend in the shader; remote bases are projected in f64 before upload to retain their line equation. Initial curve tolerance follows extents instead…

title: Keep block records' extension dictionaries on import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1614

## Cause
`import_drawing` copied the source blocks but never read the source drawing's foreign data. The block record's extension dictionary (where dynamic blocks keep their parameters), its xdata, and the objects it references were dropped.

## Fix
After copying each block, `import_drawing` now copies the block record's extension data into the destination. It copies the objects reachable through the dictionary's entry references (groups 350–369) with fresh handles and renumbers their references. Owner references (group 330) that point outside the copied set, such as the source block record, are dropped instead of left dangling. The traversal never follows owner pointers, so it can't pull in unrelated source dictionaries.

## Verified

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not change the `insert_file` block copy or the clipboard paste. They have the same gap, but this issue is only about `import`. The new owner handling also leaves the copied root dictionary without an owner pointer rather than pointing it at the destination block record.

title: Let = and /= compare symbols, as in AutoLISP (#1597)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1597.

`=` and `/=` sent every argument pair through `compare`, which only takes two numbers or two strings, so `(= (type x) 'INT)` failed with `bad argument type: numberp: INT`. AutoLISP accepts it, and routines use it to test a value's type.

Now, when neither argument of a pair is a number, `=` / `/=` compare them the way `eq` does (symbols by name, strings by text, lists only when they are the same cell). Two numbers compare by value as before (`(= 1 1.0)` is still T), and a number against a non-number is still an error. `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` are unchanged.

Test: `arithmetic_follows_autolisp` gains `(= (type 1) 'INT)` -> T, `(= (type 1.5) 'INT)` -> nil, `(/= (type '(1)) 'LIST)` -> nil and `(/= 'a 'b)` -> T; they error without the fix.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Equality operators now compare adjacent non-numeric values, including symbols, using equality semantics. Strings are compared by their text.
  * Numeric comparisons continue to use numeric conversion, and mixed numeric/non-numeric comparisons retain their existing error behavior.

title: Show the pick box for AutoLISP entsel/nentsel prompts with a message (#1598)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1598.

**Cause:** the pick box is shown when `Prompt::picks_objects()` is true. For a point prompt (which is what `entsel`/`nentsel` use) that was decided by `message.starts_with("Select")`. Without a message, `entsel`/`nentsel` show the default `Select object: `, so the pick box appears. With the routine's own message, like `"\nSelect second line or polyline: "`, the leading newline made the check fail, and a message that doesn't start with "Select" at all could never show it.

**Fix:**
- `picks_objects()` ignores leading whitespace before checking for "Select" (AutoLISP prompts almost always start with `\n`).
- A new `Prompt::pick` flag (serialized only when set, like `raw`/`distance`) says a click answers by picking one object whatever the message is. `GetRequest::prompt()` sets it for `GetKind::EntSel`, so `entsel`/`nentsel` show the pick box with any message.

**Tests:**
- `lisp::tests::entsel_and_nentsel_show_the_pick_box_with_their_own_message`: runs `(entsel)`, `(nentsel)`, the issue's `(nentsel "\nSelect second line or polyline: ")` and `(entsel "\nPick a line: ")`, and checks `Session::picking_objects()` at each prompt; `(getpoint "\nSpecify point: ")` still shows the crosshair.
- `prompt::tests::pick_box_shows_for_prompts_that_start_with_a_newline_or_are_entsel` covers `picks_objects()` directly.

Both fail without the fix.

  * Selection prompts with leading whitespace now activate object picking.

title: Open a drawing on the view it was saved at
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes the read half of #1602, and with it the write half: once the editor opens on the view the file stores, writing that view back makes open → save lossless. That is the single change @KongNan described in the triage thread.

### The drawing's own view was dropped on read

`dxf_read` parses the `*ACTIVE` VPORT record into a `VportTile` with its centre and height, then throws the record away because one tile is not a tiling:

```rust
// One *Active viewport is no tiling: the view is the editor's (it zooms to the extents).
d.vports.retain(|c| c.tiles.len() > usize::from(c.is_active()));
```

`$VIEWCTR` / `$VIEWSIZE` were read into the header and never used. `open_drawing` then fitted the geometry extents plus 10%, which on a drawing whose extents are dominated by far-away objects is a view the content is sub-pixel in — and `ZOOM Extents` fits the same box.

Measured on the 591-byte `saved-view-repro.dxf` from the report (a detail at (50, 50) height 20, plus a line near 5 000 000):

```
$ cadcraft-cli info saved-view-repro.dxf
before   "view": {"center": [2500050.0, 2500030.0], "height": 5500066.0}
after    "view": {"center": [50.0, 50.0], "height": 20.0}

$ cadcraft-cli run saved-view-repro.dxf --cmd 'view.get'
before   {"center":[2500050.0,2500030.0],"height":5500066.0,"viewportPx":[1200.0,800.0]}
after    {"center":[50.0,50.0],"height":20.0,"viewportPx":[1200.0,800.0]}
```

### And replaced on write

`vport_table` writes the `*ACTIVE` record from a fresh extents fit whenever there is no tiled configuration, and `$VIEWCTR` / `$VIEWSIZE` were not written at all. `cadcraft-cli convert` of the same file:

| | source | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `*ACTIVE` 12/22 | (50, 50) | (2500050, 2500030) | (50, 50) |
| `*ACTIVE` 40 | 20 | 5500066 | 20 |
| `$VIEWCTR` / `$VIEWSIZE` | (50, 50) / 20 | not written | (50, 50) / 20 |

### What changed

- `Header::saved_view()` / `set_saved_view()` — the `$VIEWCTR` + `$VIEWSIZE` pair, which is where DXF keeps the model v…

title: web: tell the embedding page when a drawing could not be opened
author: Hamza0101
body:
The first of the two requests in #1603: a drawing the embedding page sent that CADCraft could not open now comes back as `cadcraft:failed { error }`, instead of leaving the page to infer failure from the console.

The bridge already posts `cadcraft:failed`, but only when the app itself could not start. Everything after that — a file too large for the browser build, bytes that are not a drawing, a `cadcraft:open` whose `bytes` are neither an `ArrayBuffer` nor a `Uint8Array` — reached `CadApp::open_failed` or `opened(Err(..))`, which write to the command line and the status bar. Neither is any use to the page that sent the drawing, and in host mode the app is sitting on the Start tab with the message behind it.

### What changed

`CadApp` keeps why the last open failed until it is read (`take_open_error`), and the web shell posts it to the parent right after the inbox is drained. Nothing else changes: the command line and status bar still get the message, and the native build never reads it.

This covers every failed open, not only the ones the parent sent — a file picked in the iframe that fails to read is just as invisible to the embedding page.

### What it does not cover

The panic in #1603 is still a panic. On `wasm32-unknown-unknown` there is no unwinding, so `capacity overflow` aborts the module (that is the `RuntimeError: unreachable` after it) and no Rust code runs afterwards to report anything. This change reports the failures that *are* errors; the panic itself has to stop happening. I've left a note on the issue about where I think that total is computed, but without one of the files I can only guess, and I would rather not guess in code.

### Tests

`a_failed_open_is_reported_once` (ui-egui) — a reader that rejects the bytes: the error is readable once and then gone, so a failure is reported once per open; a successful open leaves nothing to report.

`cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm all pass.

title: AutoLISP: `=` compares the symbols `type` returns
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #1597.

`(= (type x) 'LIST)` is how an AutoLISP routine tests a type, because `type` returns a symbol. `=` coerced both sides to numbers, so the symbol failed the coercion and the whole routine stopped:

```
_$ (= (type 1) 'INT)
bad argument type: numberp: INT
```

The routine from the report now runs, and `equal` is no longer the workaround.

### What changed

`=` and `/=` compare numbers and strings exactly as before; any other atom — a symbol, `nil`, an entity name, a selection set, a file handle — compares by what it is, the way `eq` does. Two consequences worth stating, both closer to AutoLISP than what was there:

- a mismatch of kinds answers `nil` instead of raising: `(= 1 "1")` → `nil`, `(= '(1) '(1))` → `nil` (that is `equal`'s job, and AutoLISP answers `nil` here too);
- `(= nil nil)` → `T`.

The ordering comparisons (`<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`) still take numbers and strings only, as AutoLISP has them: `(< 'a 'b)` is still `bad argument type: numberp: A`.

### Tests

`equality_compares_symbols_as_autolisp_does` — the type-test idiom for `INT`, `REAL`, `LIST` and `STR`, `/=`, chained symbols, the reporter's `isint` routine on an int, a real and a string, the kind-mismatch and `nil` cases, the numeric and string behaviour unchanged, and the ordering comparison still refusing a symbol. On `main` the first line fails with the message above.

`cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm all pass.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * AutoLISP equality (`=`) and inequality (`/=`) now compare strings by text, numbers by numeric value, and other values using equality rules. This improves comparisons involving symbols, `nil`, and values of different kinds, including chained comparisons.
  * Ordering comparisons remain unchanged and still support numbers and strings.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: Draw the diameter sign with a mark the text style's own font has
author: Hamza0101
body:
Addresses #1608 along the lines its own diagnosis suggests, and the measurement below says what it does and does not fix. No sample file was needed in the end.

### What happens

`%%c` becomes U+2300 `⌀` (`crates/fonts/src/lib.rs`), which lives in Miscellaneous Technical. Arial, Times and most text faces do not have it, so `glyph_or_fallback` fell through to searching *other* installed fonts for U+2300:

```
a face with Ø but no U+2300:
  before   the glyph comes from another font entirely (gid 3781 of a different face)
  after    the drawing's own face, its Ø (gid 181)
```

That has two consequences, and the second is the reported one:

- the diameter sign was drawn in a different typeface from the text around it, which is wrong even where it is legible;
- on a machine where **no** installed font has U+2300 the search finds nothing and the text falls to the missing-glyph box — the "unreadable character" the tester saw. (On this macOS machine something does have U+2300, which is why it renders here at all.)

### What changed

`glyph_or_fallback` now tries the marks that mean the same thing in the style's own face — `∅`, then `Ø` — before searching other fonts for the exact character. The drawing still holds `⌀`: only the outline comes from a sibling mark, so text extraction, DXF round trips and PDF export still see U+2300.

The stroke font is unaffected; it already draws `'Ø' | 'ø' | '⌀'` from one glyph (`stroke.rs`), which is why this only ever showed with TrueType text styles.

### Tests

`a_diameter_sign_is_drawn_by_a_mark_the_face_has` — for an installed face that has `Ø` but not `⌀`, the glyph drawn is that face's own `Ø`, by gid and by face identity. On `main` it is a glyph from another face. The test skips where no installed font has `Ø` at all, since there would be nothing to draw with either.

### Still open from the issue

Files from other software may store the symbol as U+2205 or `\U+2205` rather than `%%c`; U+2205 now has the same fallback chain, but wh…

title: AutoLISP: an entsel prompt shows the pick box whatever its message says
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #1598.

The pick box shows at a prompt that `Prompt::picks_objects()` is true for, and that read the prompt's **wording**:

```rust
self.accept.select || (self.accept.point && self.message.starts_with("Select"))
```

An `entsel`/`nentsel` prompt takes a point and is not a selection set, so it fell to the wording. With no `[msg]` the message is the default `"Select object: "` and the pick box appeared; with a message of the routine's own it did not, because an AutoLISP prompt conventionally begins with a newline:

```lisp
(nentsel)                                        ; "Select object: "            → pick box
(nentsel "\nSelect second line or polyline: ")   ; starts with "\n"             → none
(entsel  "\nPick a line: ")                      ; never says "select" at all   → none
```

### What changed

A prompt can now say that it picks one object instead of being read for it, and `GetRequest::prompt()` sets that for `GetKind::EntSel`. So all three calls above show the pick box, whatever they say.

The wording test is also read past leading whitespace now, so a command machine's prompt that starts with a newline is not caught by the same thing.

One knock-on worth naming: `pointmod.rs` offers point modifiers (`.x`, `.y`…) at a point prompt that is not a pick, so they no longer appear at an `entsel` prompt with a message. That matches `entsel` with no message, which never offered them, and a point filter is not an answer to "pick an object" anyway.

### Tests

`an_entsel_prompt_picks_objects_whatever_its_message_says` — the three calls above plus a plain `getpoint` prompt that must *not* pick. On `main` the second call fails, printing the prompt it rejected (`Select second line or polyline:`).

title: INSERT from a file brings the file's multiline styles
author: viniau
body:
## What

`INSERT` of a DWG/DXF file merged the file's layers, linetypes and text, dimension, multileader and table styles into the drawing, but not its **multiline styles**. `merge_tables` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/blocks/insert_file.rs`) now merges `mline_styles` the same way: a style name the drawing already has keeps the drawing's definition.

## Why

AutoLISP add-ons commonly load wall styles by inserting a library file and erasing the reference, then drawing with `MLINE` in one of its styles:

```lisp
(command "-INSERT" "C:/lib/PAREDES.DWG" "0,0" "1" "1" "0")
(command "ERASE" (ssget "X" '((0 . "INSERT") (2 . "PAREDES"))) "")
(command "MLINE" "ST" "D-P-015" ...)
```

AutoCAD brings the multiline styles in with the block. CADCraft read them when the file was opened directly, but not when it was inserted, so the routine stopped at `Cannot find multiline style "D-P-015"`.

## Tests

- New unit test `inserted_file_brings_its_mline_styles` (a style is added, and merging again doesn't duplicate it).
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.
- `cargo test --release -p cadcraft-engine`: 1054 passed, 0 failed.
- End to end: inserting a real library DWG with 77 multiline styles makes them available, and `MLINE` draws with them.

title: HATCH treats rooms enclosed by multilines as islands
author: viniau
body:
## What

`loops_at` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/hatch.rs`) keeps an island found by the region search only when every curve it is made of passes `island_curve`. That list had lines, arcs, ellipses, polylines and splines, but not **multilines**, so a room enclosed by multiline walls was never kept as an island. `EntityKind::MLine` is now accepted like the other open curves.

## Why

Architectural drawings fill walls by picking inside the wall band (between the multiline's lines). The band was found correctly as the outer boundary, but the rooms inside were dropped as islands, so one pick filled the walls **and every room** they enclose.

## Tests

- New test `multiline_wall_hatch_keeps_the_room_as_an_island` (a closed multiline wall: picking inside the wall gives the outer face plus the room as an island). It fails without the change and passes with it.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.
- `cargo test --release -p cadcraft-engine`: 1053 passed, 0 failed.
- End to end on a real floor plan with `HPISLANDDETECTION` 1: wall fills stay inside the walls; rooms are left empty.

Independent of #1639 (multiline styles brought in by INSERT); both came out of running an AutoLISP drafting add-on on CADCraft.

Tab cycling through every candidate snap, split out of #1582 as asked in review

title: Show surveyor's angles as degrees/minutes/seconds (#1643)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1643.

With AUNITS=4 (Surveyor's Units), `format_angle` printed the bearing as decimal degrees (`S 73.6975d E`). Surveyor's units are degrees/minutes/seconds, so DIST and every other place that formats an angle through `format_angle` (for example `angtos` mode 4 and the Units dialog preview) now print `S 73d41'51" E`.

- The degrees/minutes/seconds code that the AUNITS=1 arm already had (rounding at the displayed precision, carrying into the next minute/degree) moves into a small `format_dms` helper. The AUNITS=1 arm calls it unchanged, and the surveyor arm now calls it for the angle between the N/S and E/W letters.
- AUPREC works the same way as for AUNITS=1: 0 gives `S 74d E`, 1-2 give `S 73d42' E`, 3-4 give `S 73d41'51" E`, and higher values add decimal places to the seconds.

Note: the issue gives `73d47'4"` as the expected value, but 0.6975 deg is 41.85' = 41'51", so the correct reading is `S 73d41'51" E`.

Test: `surveyor_display_is_degrees_minutes_seconds` in `crates/engine/src/units.rs` checks AUPREC 0, 2, 4 and 6. It fails on main (which prints `S 73.6975d E`) and passes with this change.

title: Write the ACAD_TABLE *T block relative to its insertion point (#1644)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1644.

The `*T` block of an ACAD_TABLE was filled with geometry laid out at the table's insertion point (`table_geometry` starts from `t.insert`), while the ACAD_TABLE itself also carries that point in group 10. AutoCAD adds the two, so a table placed at 200,100 showed up at 400,200. Tables at the origin were not affected.

`table_block_entities` now lays out a copy of the table with its insert at the origin, so the block is relative to its own base point (0,0) and the reference adds the insertion point once. DWG output goes through the same DXF writer, so both formats are fixed. Broken tables (TABLEBREAK) are covered too: their part origins are derived from the insert plus relative offsets, so they also move with it.

Test: `table_block_is_relative_to_the_insertion_point` builds the `*T` block for a table inserted at (5, 20) with columns totalling 8 and checks that its lines span x 0..8. Before the fix they span 5..13.

All the ways to draw a multileader go through `mleader_kind`: the JSON `mleader` command, the command-line prompts and the drag preview. So the fix covers all of them. Annotative styles were never scaled here, and they still aren't.

title: Write a landscape page setup as the long side first with plot rotation 0, like AutoCAD (#1649)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1649.

CADCraft keeps device papers short side first plus a `landscape` flag (the convention in `docs/plotters.md`), and the DXF writer copied that to the LAYOUT object as it was. A landscape A3 came out as 44 = 297, 45 = 420, 73 = 1. AutoCAD reads that as a Portrait plot of a rotated paper. AutoCAD itself saves the same layout as 420 / 297 / 0.

The LAYOUT writer (`crates/io/src/dxf_write.rs`) now writes the paper in the orientation shown on screen and always writes rotation 0:
- landscape: 44 = long side, 45 = short side, 73 = 0
- portrait: 44 = short side, 45 = long side, 73 = 0 (this was already the output before)

The in-memory model is unchanged. The reader (`page_setup` in `dxf_read.rs`) already treats media that is wider than tall with rotation 0 as landscape, so files round-trip to the same page setup. Files saved by older versions (portrait sizes with 73 = 1) still read as landscape. DWG export goes through the same writer, so it is covered too.

Test: `dxf_writes_landscape_page_like_autocad` checks the 44/45/73 groups of a landscape A3 layout (420 / 297 / 0) and that reading the file back gives 297 x 420 with landscape set. Before this change it fails because 297 / 420 / 1 is written.

Not changed: the issue says AutoCAD might use rotation 90 for papers whose own size is portrait. I didn't change that. The model doesn't store a paper's own orientation, so the writer always uses the orientation shown on screen.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed how landscape page dimensions and plot rotation are written to DXF files, so landscape pages display with the expected orientation.
  * DXF files now preserve landscape page settings when read back, including the original page dimensions.

title: DWG: write the current text style's own handle, so AutoCAD opens with it current (#1650)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1650.

acadrust's DXF reader stores only the name from `$TEXTSTYLE` (`current_text_style_name`). It leaves `current_text_style_handle` at Standard's handle, which is still a valid handle, so the DWG writer keeps it, and AutoCAD opens the DWG with Standard current.

The fix adds `current_text_style`, the text style counterpart of `current_dimstyle` (#1062). It looks up `$TEXTSTYLE` by name (case-insensitive) and sets the header handle to that style's handle. `convert` calls it right after `current_dimstyle`. If no style has that name, the handle stays as it was. Reading a DWG already handles both styles in `current_style_names`, so only the write path changes.

Test: `current_text_style_reaches_the_dwg` converts a small DXF with a ROMANS style and `$TEXTSTYLE` = ROMANS to DWG, reads the DWG back with acadrust, and checks that the header's current text style handle is ROMANS's. Without the fix it is Standard's.

* **Bug Fixes**

The resulting DWG points to the same current style, including when the DXF specifies a style such as ROMANS. This keeps the current text-style setting consistent between the source and converted drawings.

title: Save a dimangular made from two lines as a 2-line angular dimension (#1652)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1652.

`dimangular {lines: [h1, h2]}` and the interactive two-line pick (both go through `angular_from_lines`) built a `DimKind::Angular3P`, so the saved DXF/DWG had type 5 / `AcDb3PointAngularDimension` where AutoCAD writes type 2 / `AcDb2LineAngularDimension` for the same input.

`angular_from_lines` now builds `DimKind::Angular`, which the writer already maps to type 2, with the fields in the layout the renderer, snap, extents and `assoc.rs` already use for that kind:

- line 1: `p13` -> `p14` (the first line, with the picked leg end at `p14`)
- line 2: `defpt` -> `p15` (the second line, with the picked leg end at `p15`)
- `p16`: the arc location

The leg-end choice (which side of the vertex the user meant) is unchanged, so the measured angle and the text stay the same. The associativity now ties all four line points to the line ends (start/end snaps) instead of two ends plus an intersection snap, so the dimension still follows the lines when they move.

The vertex-and-two-points, arc and circle paths still build a 3-point angular dimension, as AutoCAD does for those.

title: Export to a browser download on the web instead of failing on a path (#1655)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1655.

On the web, the save "picker" (`apps/cadcraft-web/src/main.rs`) returns the suggested file name. So File > Export and a typed `EXPORT` ran `export {"path": "Drawing1.svg"}`, and the engine's wasm `write_file` rejected every path with "paths are not available on the web".

The engine now treats a path on the web the way SAVE (`file::store`) and TABLEEXPORT already do. It hands the bytes to the host's delivery hook (`file::deliver()`, a browser download), named after the path's file name and given a MIME type from its extension (SVG, PNG or PDF; anything else, such as DXF or DWG, goes as `application/octet-stream`). The new `deliver_file` helper is only built for wasm and tests, so native builds don't change.

The same error also blocked PDF output from the web menus. PUBLISH, EXPORTPDF and the Plot dialog all pass the picker's name to PLOT as `path`. `run_plot`'s wasm branch now uses the same helper and returns the same result shape as the native path branch. Calls without `path` (scripts, MCP) still get base64 `data` as before.

Test: `web_export_delivers_a_download_instead_of_writing_a_path` checks that `deliver_file` passes the bare file name and the right MIME type to the hook (`Drawing1.svg`, and `dir/Plan.pdf` delivered as `Plan.pdf`). It also checks that a build with no hook still gets a clear error that suggests the base64 `data` route.

title: Keep a layout's plot window corners when saving DXF (#1667)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1667.

A layout whose page setup plots a window (DXF `LAYOUT` group 74 = 4) kept the plot type on save, but the window corners (groups 48/49 and 140/141) were always written as 0. `PageSetup` had no field for them, so they were lost on open.

**Fix**

- `PageSetup` gets `plot_window: [f64; 4]` (`[x1, y1, x2, y2]`, default all zero). The struct is `#[serde(default)]`, so older saved data still loads.
- The DXF reader fills it from groups 48, 49, 140, 141 (a non-finite value becomes 0).
- The DXF writer writes those four values back instead of hard-coded zeros.

Nothing else changes: layouts still plot the whole sheet, and `layout.pagesetup` still only stores non-`layout` plot areas for DXF round trips. The new field shows up as `plotWindow` in the `page` JSON of `layout.list`.

**Test**

`crates/io/tests/layout_plot_window.rs` saves a layout with plot area `window` and corners (0, -297)-(420, 0) to DXF, reads it back and checks that the plot area and all four corners are unchanged (the same values as in the issue's repro).
