title: Measure an MTEXT's extents by the text it shows, not its raw formatting codes (#1668)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1668.

`mtext_box` sized an MTEXT without a wrap width by the character count of its raw `contents`, so inline codes like `{\fArial|b0|i0|c0|p34;\H0.8x;\W0.9;AB}` were counted as text and a two-letter label pushed ZOOM Extents / plot extents far out (0..76 instead of 0..10 in the issue's repro). The `blank()` check had the same gap: an MTEXT holding only formatting codes still got a box.

Both now work on the plain text:

- `mtext_box` counts lines and the longest line from `plain_mtext(&t.contents)` (paragraph breaks become `\n`).
- The MTEXT blank check runs on the plain text, so `{\fArial|b0|i0|c0|p34;}` takes no room.

`plain_mtext` lived in `cadcraft-fonts`, which `cadcraft-doc` does not depend on. It moved unchanged to `cadcraft-geom` (both crates already depend on it), and `cadcraft-fonts` re-exports it, so every existing `cadcraft_fonts::plain_mtext` caller and the `strips_formatting` test keep working.

I used `plain_mtext`, not `layout_mtext(...).bounds`: extents stay an approximation without font loading in `cadcraft-doc`, the same as `text_box` for TEXT.

Tests (`crates/doc/src/extents.rs`):
- `mtext_without_width_is_measured_by_its_shown_text`: the coded "AB" from the issue gets the same box as plain "AB", and a two-paragraph coded MTEXT is as wide as `A\PB`.
- `mtext_of_only_formatting_codes_takes_no_room`: an MTEXT with only a font switch has empty bounds.

Both fail on `main` and pass with this change.

title: DWG read: the DXF rendition limit follows the machine's free memory
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

The DXF-rendition limit of the DWG bridge follows the machine's free memory, as discussed in
#1588 (`crates/dwg/src/lib.rs`, `Limits`).

- `Limits::for_memory(free)`: the rendition may take a sixteenth of the free memory
  (`MEMORY_PER_DXF_BYTE` = 16: opening takes the rendition, its tag list, the entities staged
  while blocks are built and the finished drawing; measured on two 238 MB architects' plans: 8.6
  bytes per byte of rendition on one (1.65 GB rendition, 14.2 GB resident, #1076) and 15.8 on
  the other (1.61 GB rendition, 25.5 GB resident)). It never falls below the fixed 1 GB of
  before, which a machine with less free memory already got; that fixed limit assumes 16 GB free
  (`DEFAULT_MEMORY`), and `Limits::DEFAULT` says so.
- `Limits::for_machine()`: free memory from `CADCRAFT_MEMORY_GB` (gigabytes; for machines whose
  free memory CADCraft can't read, or to assume less), else `MemAvailable` from `/proc/meminfo` on
  Linux (the memory a program can take without swapping; no platform API, no `unsafe`, no new
  dependency), else the fixed default. macOS and Windows get the default until a probe without
  FFI exists; the variable covers them.
- The limit message names what it assumes: "… (the limit); it assumes 16.0 GB of free memory at
  16 bytes per byte of drawing data (CADCRAFT_MEMORY_GB sets what to assume); …".
- The group-code limit of a rendition follows its size (`dxf_read::read_with_limit`, a quarter
  of the bytes: a code and a value take two lines of at least two bytes), so a rendition the size
  limit allows isn't refused by the fixed 50 million group codes meant for files of unknown
  origin. Plain DXF files keep that fixed limit.
- Docs: file-format-parity (DWG paragraph, revision row), gaps FF6, ROADMAP, README's variable
  table.

So a damaged or hostile DWG can make the reader take what the machine has free and no more, and

title: DXF/DWG save: kept render settings take the declared version's class-version form (one of the two reasons BricsCAD refuses our DWGs)
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

One of the two reasons BricsCAD refuses CADCraft's DWGs (#907), the one on CADCraft's side.

Render settings store their `AcDbRenderSettings` class version (the first group 90 after that marker) in
the form of the file's version: a 2013+ file stores it one higher, and a 2013 file stores a rapid RT one
one lower, as acadrust reads and writes them (`class_dxf_render_settings`, `read_render_settings`). A kept
`RENDERSETTINGS`, `MENTALRAYRENDERSETTINGS` or `RAPIDRTRENDERSETTINGS` object carried the form of the file it
was read from into whatever file it was written to. The DWG bridge is an R2000 DXF for a 2018 DWG: a 2018
drawing's render settings went in with the 2018 form, acadrust took it at face value (the DXF said R2000)
and raised it once more for the 2018 DWG, and BricsCAD refused the DWG for an object of class version 3:

```
Objekt nicht ordnungsgemäß gelesen: <AcDbMentalRayRenderSettings> (1D10A)
```

- `dxf_raw::render_settings_versions`: after `finish`, the kept render settings objects take the declared
  version's form (source form → logical → declared form), for DXF saves at another version as well as the
  bridge. `save_version_of` gives the drawing's source version (`$ACADVER`), `None` for a new drawing.
- Docs: file-format-parity revision row, ROADMAP progress log.

The other reason is in acadrust: an `ASSOC2DCONSTRAINTGROUP` without nodes is written 9 bits short of the
registry layout BricsCAD reads (hakanaktt/acadrust#146, fix in hakanaktt/acadrust#147). With both, the
corpus file of #1592 (`02-ahu-schema-a.dwg`, BricsCAD V26 parametric blocks, 28 networks, one constraint
group, mental ray settings) saved by `cadcraft-cli convert` opens in BricsCAD V26 with every block intact;
with this PR alone it still fails on the constraint group, with the acadrust fix alone on the render
settings (bisected both ways).

title: REVCLOUD: arcs use the bulge readers need to recognise a cloud (follow-up to #1605, #1570)
author: SBaksa
body:
Follow-up to #1605 (part of #1570). **Depends on #1605**: this branch is built on it. Until #1605 lands, the diff also shows its commit. Once it merges, this PR is just the one commit on top.

#1605 adds the `RevcloudProps` xdata. That is half of what readers check. ezdxf's `is_revcloud`, which the issue uses to reproduce the bug, also requires **every arc's bulge to be within 0.02 of 0.520567**. CADCraft draws cloud arcs with bulge 0.5, which is 0.0206 off. So with #1605 alone, the issue's repro still prints `[False]`. I ran ezdxf 1.4.5 to confirm this; results are below.

### Change
- `cloud_vertices` uses `CLOUD_BULGE = 0.520567050552` instead of 0.5. That is an arc of about 110° instead of 106°, the shape other programs draw. Reversed clouds use the negative value, as before. This covers every way of making a cloud: JSON and interactive Rectangular/Polygonal/Freehand, and Object.
- `docs/file-format-parity.md`: the LWPOLYLINE row, the status line and the revision history now record that clouds are saved so readers recognise them.

`crates/engine/tests/revcloud_recognised.rs` tests what a reader checks: a closed polyline, `RevcloudProps` (`1070 0`, `1040` arc length) and every bulge at 0.520567.
- `every_way_of_drawing_a_cloud_is_recognised` covers all six ways of drawing a cloud (three JSON forms, `{handle}`, typed Rectangular, the Object pick) and a reversed cloud.
- `a_saved_cloud_reads_back_as_a_cloud` saves to DXF, checks that `RevcloudProps` is in the APPID table, then reopens the file and finds a cloud.

Both tests fail with bulge 0.5 and pass with this change. #1605's `revcloud_saves_revcloudprops_xdata` still passes. `cargo xtask ci` is green (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm) on Windows.

title: DXF: save pre-2007 text in the file's code page instead of all \U+ escapes
author: ffishman
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ffishman"} -->
_Requested by **Rodrigo**_

Before: saving a drawing as DXF 2000 or 2004 wrote every non-ASCII character as a `\U+XXXX` escape, so a Portuguese drawing had layers, blocks and text such as `El\U+00E9trica` and `A\U+00E7\U+00E3o` in the file, even though the header declares `ANSI_1252`, which has those characters.

After: the text is written in the code page the header declares, as the DXF Reference describes for pre-2007 files: `Ação` is the ANSI_1252 bytes `41 E7 E3 6F`. Characters the code page lacks (CJK in an ANSI_1252 file, emoji) are still `\U+XXXX` escapes, and a code page CADCraft doesn't know still gives pure ASCII.

This keeps #169's goal (correct text for every code-page-aware reader) while writing the file the way other pre-2007 writers do; readers that don't decode `\U+` in symbol table names now get the right layer and block names.

## How
- `cadcraft_dxf::write_ascii_in` / `write_binary_in` take the `$DWGCODEPAGE` value; `codepage::encode_char` encodes one character with `encoding_rs` or the DOS tables, and refuses any result that would be ASCII, NUL, CR or LF (a Shift-JIS trail byte may be ASCII, as `表` = `95 5C`; the reader decodes before unescaping, so that stays safe).
- `cadcraft_io::write_with` uses them for DXF before 2007, with the code page `dxf_write::code_page` already declares (the file's own when known, else `ANSI_1252`).
- `write_ascii`, `write_ascii_as`, `write_binary` and the DWG bridge are unchanged.

## Tests
- `crates/dxf/tests/code_page_write.rs`: ANSI_1252, ANSI_1251, ANSI_932, DOS850, astral characters and an unknown code page, ASCII and binary, written and parsed back.
- `crates/io/tests/codepages.rs` `saving_writes_text_in_the_code_page`: Portuguese and Cyrillic layer, block and text names saved at R2000/R2004, ASCII and binary, as code page bytes, read back the same.

title: DXF/DWG: keep a file's own arrowhead blocks with standard names (_Dot, _DotSmall)
author: ffishman
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ffishman"} -->
_Requested by **Rodrigo**_

Before: a drawing whose dimension style uses `_Dot` or `_DotSmall` arrowheads lost the file's own arrowhead blocks on open. On save, CADCraft wrote its own geometry in their place, a disc of 24 SOLIDs, instead of AutoCAD's `_Dot` (a closed polyline with width) or the user's redefinition. This applied to DXF and DWG.

title: Diameter dimensions: the *D block's text keeps the sign as %%c, so SHX styles plot it (fixes #1645)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #1645.

A diameter dimension's `*D` block got its text from `DimGeometry::value`, which has the `%%` codes already decoded, so `%%c` arrived as `⌀` (U+2300). No SHX font has that character. Other programs drew the block in an SHX style (the issue uses `romans.shx`) and plotted "60" with no sign. EXPLODE had the same problem: the MTEXT it leaves held U+2300 too.

### Change
- New `DimGeometry::mtext_contents()`. It returns `value` as MTEXT contents, with the diameter sign written as `%%c`. If a `%` would run into a code, it's written `%%%`. Everything else is unchanged, so a radius stays `R30`, and `°` and `±` stay as they were.
- The `*D` block writer (`io/src/dxf_write.rs`) and EXPLODE (`engine/src/cmd/modify.rs`) use it. DWG goes through the same writer.
- `docs/file-format-parity.md`: the DIMENSION row, the status line and the revision history.

What CADCraft draws on screen is unchanged, since that comes from the dimension's own MTEXT (#1608 / #1632 cover screen drawing).

**Why `%%c` and not U+2205 `∅`:** `%%c` is how CADCraft already keeps the sign in TEXT and MTEXT, as the issue notes. Every program's fonts draw it: SHX fonts elsewhere, and CADCraft's stroke and TrueType text through `decode_controls`. CADCraft's stroke font has no U+2205, so writing `∅` would have turned exploded dimension text into a missing glyph here.

### Tests
- `render::dim` `mtext_contents_write_the_diameter_sign_as_a_code`: checks the contents for `⌀60`, `2x ⌀8.5 THRU`, `R3.0`, `° ±`, `50%`, `5%⌀6`, `%%` and an empty value. For each one, decoding the contents gives the value back exactly, and no U+2300 is left.
- `crates/engine/tests/dim_diameter_sign.rs` uses the issue's drawing: an SHX style `R`, dimension style `D`, and `dimdiameter` on a circle of radius 30.
  - The `*D` block's MTEXT in the saved DXF is `%%c60`. Read back, CADCraft shows `⌀60`.

title: fix(snap): keep an arc's sweep for TAN and PER snaps
author: william-wwh
body:
Fixes #1697.

## Problem

An arc was snapped as its full circle. TAN and PER solutions on that circle were offered even when they fell outside the arc's sweep, so a snap marker could appear in the arc's gap and a line could point into blank paper. A deferred tangent stored only the center and radius, losing the sweep.

## Fix

- `SnapCurve` gains an `Arc { center, radius, start, end }` variant, so a deferred snap keeps the sweep and resolves onto the arc later.
- **TAN** filters its solutions with `Arc::contains_angle`. A tangent in the gap is dropped.
- **PER** returns both antipodes (`SnapCurve::perpendiculars`) and filters them with `Arc::contains_angle`, so a gap solution is discarded and the valid opposite antipode is found (rather than clamping to a non-perpendicular endpoint).
- **Deferred pairs**: any operand that is an arc is normalized to its carrier circle for the math, then the sweep filter is applied to the result. This restores arc-to-circle TAN-TAN and TAN-PER pairs.
- The viewport projection maps the new variant.

## Tests

`crates/engine/src/snap.rs` gains four cases against a quarter arc:

- `arc_tangent_only_on_the_arc_not_its_circle`: a tangent in the gap is not offered; the one on the arc is.
- `arc_perpendicular_clamps_to_the_arc`: the perpendicular from below finds the valid opposite antipode on the arc (aperture 5.5, with a margin).
- `arc_deferred_tangent_keeps_its_sweep`: a deferred TAN keeps the arc and resolves onto it.
- `deferred_tangent_pairs_with_arcs`: a TAN-TAN pair between an arc and a circle keeps only the tangent on the arc.

`cargo test --workspace` passes (2207 tests, 0 failures); `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

title: Dynamic blocks: array actions, polar and XY parameters (stacked on #1098)
author: codyvogt
body:
A dynamic block reference now repeats its arrayed objects the way AutoCAD does, and polar and XY parameters show in Properties and as grips.

> Stacked on #1098 (and through it on #1030 and #967). The first commits on this branch are those PRs; the change here is the last commit.

## What changes
- **Array actions** (`BLOCKARRAYACTION`): read with their four connections, row offset (140) and column offset (141). Each change to a reference rebuilds its arrays from the first copy of each arrayed object, using the parameter's current value:
  - along a linear or polar parameter: one copy for each whole column offset in its distance, at least the object itself;
  - across an XY parameter: a whole number of columns along X by rows along Y, toward the end point. If either count is short of one, only the object remains;
  - the objects follow the parameter's base point (dragging the base or a corner grip moves the whole array, as AutoCAD's Origin shows).

  Every copy but the first carries AutoCAD's `AcDbBlockArrayActionTag` xdata. Without it, AutoCAD reads the saved reference but refuses to change it again ("Invalid input").
- **Polar parameters**: Distance1 and Angle1 in Properties (editable, value sets applied; the angle is absolute, shown through ANGBASE/ANGDIR like the rotation parameter's), square grips at the base and end.
- **XY parameters**: X Distance1 and Y Distance1 in Properties, square grips at the base, the end and the two other corners (`basex-endy`, `basey-endx` in `blocks.reference.grip`). A distance below the value set's minimum is refused, as AutoCAD refuses it. In DXF, 305/306 are the Y and X labels and the Y value set comes first (97, 146–149, then 96, 142–145 for X).
- Changes are recorded in the reference's history as drags of the base and end grips.
- Hostile values: arrays over 100,000 copies, NaN or infinite distances, and zero column offsets are refused or ignored before any copy is made.

title: Storeys and the blueprint
author: Alex-BB44
body:
Branch `pr/storeys` · one commit on `main` (0b32c2e)

## What it does

A drawing can be a stack of **storeys**: the floors of a building, or any other stack (versions of
a product, variants of a layout). Each model-space object belongs to one storey; the **current**
storey is the one shown, selected and changed. Layers stay drawing-wide and independent of storeys:
"Plumbing off" hides plumbing on every storey.

Any other storey can lie beneath the current one as the **blueprint**:
drawn first, in one colour, snapped to, and never selected or changed, by a command, a grip or a
script. It is never plotted.

This is 2D drafting with storeys, not BIM: nothing else about the drawing changes.

## How it works

- **doc** — `Storeys` (ids are never reused; the start storey is number 0, those above count up,
  those below down). Each object's storey is xdata of the registered application `CADCRAFT_STOREY`,
  and the storey list is the XRECORD `CADCRAFT_STOREYS`. Both survive DXF and DWG round trips.
  Other programs keep them and show every storey at once.
- **engine**
  - The `storey.*` commands, `STOREYCOPY`/`STOREYMOVE`, and `storey.import` (another office's plan
    as a storey of its own).
  - A guard after every command takes back any change to another storey, except the commands that
    act on the drawing's tables.
  - No associativity across storeys.
  - LISP and selection filters.
  - A start setup for new drawings and for drawings without storeys.
- **render / snap** — the blueprint is drawn first in its colour and snapped to. Optionally without
  its hatches.
- **ui**
  - A **Storeys** palette: numbers, rename in place, and a right-click menu with go to, blueprint,

  - Storey and blueprint choosers, and Format ▸ Storeys.

title: Layer states as a quick switcher in the Layers palette
author: Alex-BB44
body:
Branch `pr/layer-states` · one commit on `main` (0b32c2e)

## What it does

The field below the layer list in the Layers palette has so far been a painted
"Unsaved Layer State" placeholder. It is now a working switcher for the drawing's layer states
(the same states the Layer Properties manager saves).

- **Choose** a state: the layers switch at once, on/off, frozen and locked only. Colours, linetypes

author: Alex-BB44

## What it does

This adds **Options ▸ Selection ▸ "Objects on locked layers can't be selected"**, kept in the

When it is on:

- picks, windows, fences and polygons leave objects on locked layers out;

This goes well with #1505 (LAYLOCKFADECTL fades locked layers on screen) and with #1372 (LAYISO
locks and fades). It touches neither: fading is how the layer looks, this is whether it can be
picked.

title: Reject doubled minus sign in parse_distance
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/units.rs:138-160` (no existing issue): parse_distance accepts a doubled minus sign and returns a positive distance.

## Cause
`parse_distance` strips one leading '-' and passes the rest to `parse_mixed`. `parse_mixed` parses its input as an f64, which accepts its own '-'. So `--5` parsed as -(-5) = +5.

## Fix
After the leading '-' is stripped, `parse_distance` returns None if the remainder starts with '-' or '+'. Single-signed inputs such as `-5` and `-3/4` still parse as before.

## Verified
- Regression test `units::tests::parse_distance_rejects_doubled_minus`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib parse_distance_rejects_doubled_minus`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The feet-and-inches path (`1'-6"`) and its separator handling are unchanged. Plain unsigned and single-signed inputs behave as before.

title: Read DXF sections and records as slices instead of copies
author: MadsHolten
body:
Found while reading large DWGs through `dwg_to_dxf` + `read_dxf` on a server with 8 GiB: an 83 MB DWG (a 0.6 GB DXF) peaked at 8.6 GB of live memory inside `read_dxf`, almost all of it group codes.

## Cause
The reader held the group codes three times over:
- `cadcraft_dxf::parse` builds the stream, growing a `Vec<Tag>` by doubling. A `Tag` is 40 bytes, so 25 million tags are 1 GB, and the last doubling holds the old and the new buffer at once and can leave up to half of the capacity unused.
- `sections()` copies every section out of the stream (`to_vec`) while the stream is still held (the image, mline and raw passes read the sections at the end).
- `records()` copies each record out of a section again (BLOCKS, ENTITIES, OBJECTS, TABLES).

## Fix
- `cadcraft-dxf` gets borrowing variants: `section_slices` (returns `SectionRef { name: &str, tags: &[Tag] }`) and `record_slices` (returns `(String, &[Tag])`). Sections and records are contiguous runs of the stream, so they are slices of it. `sections` and `records` stay as they are for their other callers (tests, `dxf_raw`).
- `dxf_read::read` and the OBJECTS, image, mline and raw passes take the slices; `parse_entities` takes `&[(String, &[Tag])]`.
- `parse_with_limit` already counts the file's lines for `MAX_TAGS`, so the ASCII stream is made with that capacity (`parse_ascii_sized`), which is capped by the limit like before.
- A string value is copied for `\U+`/`\M+` unescaping only when it contains such an escape (`unescape_unicode` returned a copy of it unchanged otherwise), and the EOF check uses a new `Tag::str_ref` instead of allocating a `String` per code-0 tag.

What the reader produces is unchanged.

## Verified
- New tests in `cadcraft-dxf`: `borrowed_sections_and_records_match_the_copies` (the slices equal what `sections`/`records` copy, including tags before the first record) and `a_sized_parse_holds_no_more_than_it_was_sized_for`.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: Control server: wait after a failed accept instead of retrying at once
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

The control server's accepting thread (`apps/cadcraft/src/control_server.rs`) read `listener.incoming().flatten()`, which drops a failed accept and asks again at once. When accepting keeps failing, for example while the process has run out of file descriptors, that thread keeps a core busy until it recovers.

It now waits 100 ms after a failed accept. Accepted connections, the limits and everything after the accept are unchanged. The loop goes through a small `accepted` helper, so the wait can be tested without exhausting file descriptors.

The same change is open in PdfCraft as storytold/pdfcraft#3631, where the single-instance listener already waits like this.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft -j 3 --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test -p cadcraft -j 3 control_server`: 9 passed

**Test.** New `a_failed_accept_waits_before_the_next` feeds the helper two connections around three failed accepts and checks that both come through and that it waits three times. With the old `flatten()` put back into the helper it fails: `left: 0`, `right: 3`.

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

There is no log line on a failed accept: while accepting keeps failing that would be ten lines a second. Happy to add one if you prefer.

title: ATTDEF: justify and style parameters, as TEXT and MTEXT take them (fixes #1658)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #1658.

`attdef` had no way to set a justification or a text style. Every attribute definition came out left/baseline in the current style, and a centred or right-aligned title-block field needed an `entmod` afterwards.

### Change
`attdef` takes two optional parameters, used the same way `text` and `mtext` use them:
- `justify`: the codes `text` accepts (`L`, `C`, `R`, `M`, `TL` … `BR`), parsed by the same `draw::justify`. As with TEXT, any justification but Left keeps `at` as the alignment point.
- `style`: a text style name in any case, stored as the style table spells it. The default is still the current style (TEXTSTYLE).

An unknown code or style is refused with an error, as `text` and `mtext` refuse them, and nothing is added. `A` (Align) and `F` (Fit) are refused too: they run between two baseline points, and `attdef` takes one, so they would give a zero-length span. title: Dynamic blocks: scale and polar stretch actions (stacked on #1699)
author: codyvogt
body:
Stacked on #1699 (array actions, polar and XY parameters); the first commits are that PR's. Part of #185.

Dynamic block references now apply the two actions CADCraft read but ignored, so every parameter it can change drives every action AutoCAD attaches to it.

## Scale actions
- Read: the base point (it follows the parameter's base point, at an offset, or stays put) and the connections (`Scale`, `XScale`, `YScale`).
- Applied: the action's objects scale about the base point by the ratio of the parameter's new distance to its old one. For a linear or polar parameter that is its distance. For an XY parameter it is the base-to-end diagonal; AutoCAD scales by the diagonal too (X 10 → 20 with Y 5 gives ×1.8439).
- The parameters in the selection are carried, as rotate and flip actions carry them.
- AutoCAD can also scale by an XY parameter's X or Y distance alone. It keeps that choice only in DWG data that its own DXF output doesn't show (an X-only scale action's DXF is identical to an XY one's), so this uses the diagonal.
- Factors below 1e-9 or above 1e9, and a scale from a distance of 0, are refused with an error, and the reference is left as it was.

## Polar stretch actions
- Read: the frame, the stretched objects' vertex lists, the objects it only rotates, and the multiplier and angle offset.
- Applied as measured in AutoCAD:
  - Every object in the selection turns about the polar parameter's base by the change of its angle.
  - Listed vertices inside the frame, and selected objects with no vertex list, then move with the end point along the new direction.
  - Rotate-only objects outside the selection only turn. An object in both lists is stretched, as AutoCAD does.
- Parameters in the selection are carried: they turn, and the ones whose points are in the frame follow the end.

## Stretch and move on polar and XY parameters

title: DWG: scale actions keep the byte AutoCAD reads after their connections (acadrust 0.6.5)
author: codyvogt
body:
## Problem
Saving as DWG a drawing that has a dynamic block with a scale action gave a file AutoCAD refuses to open ("Error Decrypting Data"), even when nothing was changed. DXF save of the same drawing was fine.

## Cause
AutoCAD's DWG scale action (`BLOCKSCALEACTION`) ends with one byte after its three connections, a field DXF doesn't have. Comparing the object's bits in an AutoCAD DWG with acadrust 0.6.4's rewrite shows they match up to the end of the third connection; AutoCAD's then has 8 more bits (0 in every sample). acadrust 0.6.4 neither read nor wrote them, so AutoCAD read past the object. Every other dynamic block action in the samples, polar stretch included, reads to its end exactly.

acadrust 0.6.5 keeps the byte (`BlockBasePointAction::dwg_tail_byte`, 0 from DXF, as AutoCAD writes it).

## Change
- acadrust 0.6.4 → 0.6.5 (`cadcraft-dwg`, and `cadcraft-io`'s dev-dependency).
- 0.6.5 maps the dimension flags byte's bit 0 to `text_user_positioned` both ways itself, so the bridge's inversion (#1094) would now invert twice; it is removed. The bridge still sets bit 1 (DXF group 70 bit 32), which acadrust doesn't keep from DXF.
- Regression test: a scale action's byte reaches the DWG, and a scale action from DXF is written whole at 2004 and 2018.
- docs/file-format-parity.md row.

## Checked in AutoCAD
- A drawing with a uniform scale action on a linear parameter, saved as DWG from CADCraft: AutoCAD opens it, and changing the reference's Distance1 from 942 to 1500 scales the block uniformly (942 × 949 → 1500 × 1511).
- A polar stretch block (Length 1.25 → 2, Angle 180° → 90°) edits as expected once the drawing opens.
- The second drawing still doesn't open from CADCraft's DWG for an unrelated reason (2D constraint groups, `ACDBASSOC2DCONSTRAINTGROUP`, through CADCraft's DWG bridge); that's a separate follow-up.

`cargo fmt`, clippy, and the dwg, io and cli tests pass; `cargo xtask wasm` and `cargo xtask layers` pass.

title: Read SVG arc flags as single characters in path data
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/io/src/svg_read.rs:892-894 (arc flags read via Numbers::next_num, 675-709)` (no existing issue): SVG path arc flags written without separators make the whole SVG fail to import.

## Cause
`parse_path` read the large-arc and sweep flags of `A`/`a` with the general number scanner. For minified paths such as `a20 20 0 01 20 20` or `0120 20`, the scanner took `01` as 1 and `0120` as 120. That swallowed a coordinate, and the import failed with "path command is missing coordinates".

## Fix
Added a flag reader to the path tokenizer that takes exactly one `0` or `1` character, with no separator needed after it. `parse_path` now uses it for arguments 4 and 5 of every arc, including repeated implicit arcs. In that case it rewinds the already-tokenized number first. A regression test covers the compact and spaced forms.

## Verified
- Regression test `svg_read::tests::compact_arc_flags_read_as_single_characters`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-io --lib svg_read::tests::compact_arc_flags_read_as_single_characters`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Number scanning for all other path arguments is unchanged. A flag that is not `0` or `1` still gives the existing "missing coordinates" error.

title: DWG: constraint groups keep their nodes (AutoCAD opened no DWG with parametric blocks)
author: codyvogt
body:
Stacked on #1725 (its commit is the first one here; review only the last commit). Related to #1687, which does the same kind of version-form fix for kept render settings and may touch the same writer files; happy to rebase after either lands.

AutoCAD refused CADCraft's DWG of a drawing with parametric blocks (e.g. a dynamic blocks sample drawing): "Error Decrypting Data".

**Cause.** A 2D constraint group (`ACDBASSOC2DCONSTRAINTGROUP`) is kept with its tags as read. From AutoCAD 2013 on, a constraint node's status (group 70) comes after its connections; before 2013 it comes right after the node id. acadrust reads it according to the DXF's `$ACADVER`. The DWG bridge's DXF declares R2000, so for a 2013+ drawing acadrust read every node's status and connections from the wrong groups and wrote garbage nodes into the DWG. (CADCraft's plain DXF export opened fine because it declares the drawing's own version.) A DXF saved at a version on the other side of 2013 from the source had the same mismatch.

**Fix.** After the kept objects are written, `dxf_raw::constraint_node_order` walks each group (actions, root node, node registry), finds every node header in either order and moves its status to where the written version expects it. If it can't find all of a group's nodes, the group is left as it is. The header search is bounded (hostile input).

**Tests**
- `crates/io/tests/constraint_group_dwg.rs`: a synthetic group, read from 2018 and 2010 DXF and saved as 2018/2010/2004 DWG and 2018/2013/2010/2000 DXF. acadrust reads back each node's id, status and connections. Without the fix, every 2018 → older case fails (connections come back empty).
- `hostile_constraint_groups_never_panic`.
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-io` and clippy `-D warnings` pass.

**Checked in AutoCAD.** The dynamic blocks sample, opened in CADCraft and saved as DWG, now opens in AutoCAD. Dynamic block edits work there: Tag Length 1.25 → 2 with Angle 180° → 90°, Door Size 2.5 → 3, Road Section Width 13.33 → 20 …

body:

title: Close hatch boundaries where a line ends just short of a flattened ellipse (#1690)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1690.

**Cause.** To trace a boundary, HATCH first turns curves into straight chords (tolerance `(width + height) / 20000` of the drawing extents). On a convex curve such as an ellipse, the chords run inside the true curve. A line that ends on the true ellipse, or just a little inside it like the verticals in the reported drawing, can therefore stop above the chord below it. It never touches the chord, so the strip stays open and HATCH reports "Valid hatch boundary not found." This also explains the workaround in the report: making the lines a little longer lets them cross the chords.

**Fix.** New `region::snap_ends` in `crates/geom/src/region.rs`. When an open curve end is no farther than the flattening tolerance from another curve, and it does not already touch a curve, the end moves to the nearest point on that curve. That curve also gets a vertex at the same point, so the two meet exactly. Ends farther away than the tolerance stay where they are, so a real gap is still a gap (HPGAPTOL still handles those). Both places that trace boundaries from flattened outlines now call it:
- `loops_at` in `cmd/hatch.rs` (Pick points),
- the associative refill in `cmd/hatch/assoc.rs`. Without it, a hatch made with the fix would stop being associative at the next edit of its boundary.

The tolerance formula now lives in one place, `outline_tol`, which both paths use.

**Tests.**
- `region::tests::line_ending_just_short_of_a_chord_is_joined_to_it`: without snapping there is no loop, with it the 2 x 10 strip is found. An end farther away than the snap distance stays unchanged.
- `hatch_options::lines_ending_on_an_ellipse_close_a_boundary`: an ellipse, two verticals that end exactly on the true ellipse, and a top line. HATCH picks the strip, and the loop's sources are all 4 objects. Sliding the top line keeps the hatch associative, which tests the refill path. The ends lie about half the tolerance above the chords, so `hatch` returns the error without the fix.

title: STRETCH moves only the multiline vertices inside the area (#1712)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1712.

`stretch_entity` had no arm for `EntityKind::MLine`, so a multiline fell into the generic fallback. That fallback moves the whole entity when its first grip is inside the area and leaves it alone otherwise. So a polygon or window over the last vertex reported `{"stretched":1}` and changed nothing, and one over the first vertex moved the whole multiline.

The new arm moves each vertex inside the area, the same way the `Line`, `LwPolyline` and `Solid` arms already do. It matches what dragging an MLINE vertex grip does (`grips.rs` sets the vertex `p` and touches nothing else). The JSON command, the typed/interactive STRETCH and its preview all go through `stretch_entity`, so this one change covers all of them. A fence still moves what it crosses whole, as before.

Test (`crates/engine/tests/stretch_select.rs`): the issue's repro. A crossing polygon over the last vertex gives `(0,0) (3000,0) (3610,2000)`, and then a window over the first vertex moves only that vertex: `(610,0) (3000,0) (3610,2000)`. Without the fix, the first check fails (nothing moves) and so does the second (every vertex moves).

title: REVCLOUD: ask maximum arc length and Reverse direction for Object (#1714)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1714.

The issue reports two prompt-flow gaps in interactive/script/LISP REVCLOUD (`RevcloudM` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/draw2.rs`). This PR fixes both:

**(a) Arc length takes one value.** After "Specify minimum length of arc", REVCLOUD now asks "Specify maximum length of arc" (default: the remembered maximum, never below the minimum), as AutoCAD does. So `"_A" "200" "800"` keeps 800, and the next REVCLOUD reports `Minimum arc length: 200.0000   Maximum arc length: 800.0000`. A maximum below the minimum is rejected and the prompt is asked again. The maximum is remembered in the drawing header as `CADCRAFT_REVCLOUDMAXARCLEN` (CADCraft-only state, hidden from SETVAR and not written to DXF, like `CADCRAFT_LAYERP`), so no new AutoCAD-looking system variable is invented. The cloud geometry still uses the minimum arc length, as before; this PR only fixes the prompt flow and the reported values.

**(b) Object has no "Reverse direction" prompt.** After Object picks the closed object, REVCLOUD now asks "Reverse direction [Yes/No] <No>:" before it converts it. `Yes` builds the cloud with reversed arcs (the same `reverse` flag the JSON `revcloud` command already takes); `No` or Enter keeps the direction. An extra `"_N"` / `"_Y"` from an AutoCAD routine is no longer run as a command.

The JSON `revcloud` command is unchanged (it already takes `arcLength` and `reverse`).

Tests: new `revcloud_arc_length_asks_max_and_object_asks_reverse` in `draw2_tests.rs` sends `a 200 800`, checks the reported minimum/maximum on the next run, and checks that Object asks "Reverse direction" and finishes on `n`. It fails on main (the 800 lands on the first-corner prompt and the maximum reads 200; Object finishes without the prompt). `revcloud_command_line` was updated for the two extra prompts.

This stays clear of #1605 (RevcloudProps xdata) and #1692 (bulge values): it touches only the prompt state machine, not the cloud geometry or the entity data.

title: Report DWGPREFIX, DWGTITLED, FILEDIA, CMDECHO and more from GETVAR (#1715)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Part of #1715: `(getvar ...)` returned nil for several variables that ordinary LISP routines read.

**What changes**

`sysvars::get` now reports, read-only (added to `READ_ONLY`, next to `DWGNAME`, `CMDNAMES` and `DBMOD`):
- `DWGPREFIX`: the folder of the drawing file, made absolute, with a trailing separator. `""` for a drawing that has no file yet.
- `DWGTITLED`: 1 when the drawing has a file path, 0 for an unnamed drawing.
- `CMDACTIVE`: 1 while a command is running, else 0 (from the same state as `CMDNAMES`).
- `TILEMODE`: 1 in model space, 0 on a layout (from the same state as `CTAB`).
- `PLATFORM`: the OS name (`std::env::consts::OS`).
- `LOGINNAME`: `USERNAME` (Windows) or `USER` (Unix), `""` when neither is set.

`FILEDIA` and `CMDECHO` go into the sysvar table as 0/1 choices with default 1. GETVAR now returns 1 before any SETVAR, SETVAR checks the value, and the value round-trips like `HPDLGMODE`. No command reads them yet, and a comment in the table says so.

**Test**

`lisp::tests::getvar_drawing_and_session_variables` checks a new drawing (`DWGPREFIX` `""`, `DWGTITLED` 0, `FILEDIA`/`CMDECHO`/`TILEMODE` 1, `CMDACTIVE` 0, a `FILEDIA` SETVAR round-trip). It then gives the drawing a file path and checks that `DWGPREFIX` is its folder with a trailing separator and `DWGTITLED` is 1. Without this change every one of those variables reads nil.

**Not in this PR**

- `CDATE`, `DATE` and `TDUPDATE` need the local date and time. The standard library has no time zone, and the workspace has no date crate. Whether to add one, or to report UTC, is the maintainers' choice.
- `LASTPROMPT` and `VISRETAIN` need state the engine does not keep yet (the last prompt text, and xref layer retention).

These can follow in another PR once the date question is settled.

title: LISP: tblsearch BLOCK reports xref flags and path (#1716)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1716.

`tblsearch "BLOCK"` and `tblnext "BLOCK"` returned `(70 . 0)` and no path for every block, so a routine could not tell an attached or overlaid xref from an ordinary block.

Both functions build their records in `table_records`, so the change is made there once. For a block with an `xref_path`, group 70 now has:

- plus 8 when it is an overlay,

title: Reject repeated leading '#' in Rgb::parse_hex
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/lib.rs:24` (no existing issue): Rgb::parse_hex accepts repeated leading '#' characters.

title: A quick right-click is Enter between commands too: it runs the typed command or repeats the last one (fixes #1387)
author: Sladrian
body:
Fixes #1387.

**Problem.** With the time-sensitive right-click on (the default), a quick right-click was Enter only while a command ran, and it sent a bare Enter even when something was typed. Between commands every right-click opened the shortcut menu: typing `rec` and right-clicking opened the menu instead of starting RECTANG (the report and the two comments after it), and at an empty prompt it didn't repeat the last command as AutoCAD does.

**Change.** A quick right-click now does what the Enter key does (`cmdline::submit`):

- between commands it runs the typed command, or repeats the last one when nothing was typed;
- while a command runs it enters the typed input (`@10,0`), or ends the input as before.

**What stays the same.**

- Holding the button (250 ms) opens the command menu while a command runs, and the shortcut menu between commands.
- A right-click on a grip with options keeps its grip menu; Shift/Ctrl+right-click is still the object snap menu.
- With the time-sensitive right-click turned off in Options, every right-click opens the menu.
- With nothing typed and no command run yet, a quick click opens the shortcut menu (there is nothing to enter).

The first comment on the issue suggested keeping the menu on an empty prompt; this repeats the last command there instead, as AutoCAD does with the time-sensitive right-click and as the later comments ask. The menu stays one held click away.

**Tests.** `time_sensitive_right_click` (real pointer events in an egui context) also checks that a quick click between commands repeats LINE, a held one opens the menu with Repeat LINE and repeats nothing, a typed `circle` starts CIRCLE and a typed `5,5` enters its centre. title: Convert px/unitless SVG root size to mm when a viewBox is present
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/io/src/svg_read.rs:576-593 (parse_length_mm), used at 605-612 (viewport)` (no existing issue): SVG import treats unitless or px root width/height as millimetres when a viewBox is present.

## Cause
`viewport` took the root `width`/`height` from `parse_length_mm`, which returns bare and `px` numbers unchanged. With a `viewBox` present, `width="800"` was therefore treated as 800 mm instead of 800 CSS pixels (about 211.67 mm), so the drawing came out 3.78 times too large.

## Fix
`viewport` now scales a bare or `px` root width/height by 25.4/96 mm per pixel before computing the viewBox scale. Other units are unchanged. A regression test covers `800` and `800px` with a viewBox.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::svg_viewbox_with_px_or_unitless_root_size_uses_reference_pixel`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-io --lib svg_viewbox_with_px_or_unitless_root_size_uses_reference_pixel`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`parse_length_mm` is unchanged. `num` also uses it for element attributes, where a bare number is a user unit that the root matrix already scales.

title: feat: add ETRANSMIT drawing packages
author: campbellcody
body:
CADCraft currently has no ETRANSMIT command, so sharing a drawing requires collecting xrefs, images and linked CSV files by hand. This adds native drawing ZIP packages with portable relative paths and a manifest of missing dependencies and drawing warnings.

- Adds `ETRANSMIT` and File ▸ eTransmit..., with the same JSON command available through scripts, CLI, control and MCP.
- Packages the current drawing snapshot and explicitly approved recursive xrefs, validated PNG/JPEG images and UTF-8 CSV table links. Sources are deduplicated, cycles reuse existing entries and colliding filenames receive unique archive names.
- Requires caller-provided `allow` entries for dependency source files or directories. No dependencies are authorized by default. Canonical paths enforce folder boundaries, including symlink escapes; exact-file approval does not approve siblings. The interactive command asks for source approval separately, and programmatic calls never open dialogs.
- Validates image format, decoding limits and CSV text before archiving their original bytes. Validation is performed for each declared reference kind and does not replace export authorization.
- Rewrites drawing copies, preserves the open drawing and source files, stages archives before no-overwrite publication, and provides strict mode to refuse incomplete packages. Traversal, file sizes and decoding are bounded.
- Preserves valid filename extensions when shortening long stems. Published ZIPs use ordinary-save Unix permissions respecting the process umask, while ZIP data remains private during staging.
- Documents the API and remaining limits, provides function documentation and the required Ukrainian menu translation, and updates ROADMAP.md, M7 and F23 without changing parity estimates.

author: codyvogt
body:
Dynamic block references now act on the last parameters CADCraft read but ignored: base point and alignment parameters. Lookup tables can also set and read every parameter value AutoCAD puts in them. Everything here was measured in AutoCAD on blocks authored there, and each change was checked by having AutoCAD edit the saved file again.

## Base point parameters
- AutoCAD's BSAVE moves a block's objects so its base point parameter is at the block's base point, so an unchanged reference already draws in the right place.
- When an action moves the base point parameter (a stretch frame holds it, or a move or rotate selection lists it), AutoCAD moves the reference's insertion point by that move and moves the block's objects and parameters back. CADCraft now does the same. In AutoCAD, Distance1 10 → 15 moved the insertion point from (100, 100) to (105, 100) and the block now runs from −15 to 0. CADCraft gives the same result, and a turned reference moves along its own axis. Attributes stay where they were.
- AutoCAD reads CADCraft's file and takes further changes (Distance1 20 → insertion point (110, 100)).
- Known limit: a rotate or scale action with a fixed base point stays where the dynamic block has it after the base point parameter has moved. CADCraft changes references step by step, while AutoCAD replays the whole history.
- AutoCAD shows no grip of its own for a base point parameter: the reference's insertion grip sits on it, so no new grip is added.

## Alignment parameters
- The type flag (`AcDbBlockAlignmentParameter` 280: 1 perpendicular, 0 tangent) is read. The grip is drawn at the base point as a small pentagon pointing to the left of the alignment direction, as AutoCAD draws it.
- Dragging the grip next to an object (within the aperture, the reference itself excluded, objects inside other blocks included) works as measured in AutoCAD:
  - the reference moves so the alignment's base point lands on the nearest point of the object;
  - it turns so the alignmen…

title: Let LISP entnext reach an INSERT's ATTRIBs and SEQEND
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1660

## Cause
`entnext` only walked top-level entity handles. An INSERT's attributes are stored inside the insert with no handles of their own, and the entity codec only returned an entity's first DXF record, so LISP had no way to name, list or change an ATTRIB.

## Fix
io gets `entity_sub_groups`, which returns the records written after an entity's own (an INSERT's ATTRIBs and SEQEND), exposed through a new `sub_groups` field on `EntityCodec`. The LISP env now names these sub-entities with entity names counting down from the top of the handle range. With that, `entnext` from an INSERT goes through its ATTRIBs and SEQEND before the next entity, `entget` lists them with their owner (330), and `entmod` on an ATTRIB updates the insert's attribute (tag, value, text placement, flags, properties).

## Verified
- Regression test `lisp::tests::entnext_walks_an_inserts_attribs`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib entnext_walks_an_inserts_attribs`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`entdel` and `entupd` on an ATTRIB/SEQEND name return nil, and `handent` does not resolve them, because they have no drawing handles. POLYLINE VERTEX records are not reached by `entnext`, since 2D polylines are stored as LWPOLYLINEs.

title: geom: exact ellipse intersections and closest points (conic kernel)
author: DVLUGI
body:
Addresses item 1 of "What to do first" in `docs/geometry-parity.md` (and top-10 row 3 of `docs/gaps.md`) for ellipses: line–, circle– and ellipse–ellipse intersections were tessellated, and `Ellipse::closest` sampled a polyline. This PR adds an exact conic kernel to `crates/geom` (L0, no new dependency) and makes `Ellipse::closest` exact. Commands (snaps, TRIM, EXTEND, BREAK) are **not** switched over yet; that is a follow-up in `engine`.

### What's new (`crates/geom/src/conic.rs`)

- `Conic`: general conic `ax² + bxy + cy² + dx + ey + f = 0` with `from_ellipse`, `from_circle`, `from_line_pair`, `eval`, `det`, `discriminant`, `add_scaled` (pencil member), `normalized` and `to_ellipse`.
- `line_ellipse(line, ellipse) -> Vec<(point, line_param, ellipse_param)>`: the ellipse is mapped to the unit circle by its affine frame (line parameters are preserved), then the existing `line_circle` does the work.
- `circle_ellipse` and `ellipse_ellipse(e1, e2) -> Vec<(point, t1, t2)>` (up to 4 points), plus `ellipse_arcs` / `on_ellipse_arc` to filter by the arcs' sweeps.
  - The rounder ellipse is mapped to the unit circle, which keeps coefficients of order one at any coordinates (tested at 1e6–1e7).
  - The pencil `C + λQ` has degenerate members where `det(C + λQ) = 0`, a cubic. Each real root's member is split into two lines (Richter-Gebert, *Perspectives on Projective Geometry*, §11.3: adjugate + cross-product matrix). The lines are intersected with the unit circle.
  - Candidates are polished by 2×2 Newton on both equations and kept only when both residuals are below 1e-8 (normalised). Coincident ellipses return no points, as `circle_circle` does for coincident circles.
- `ellipse_closest_param` (full ellipse): robust bisection after D. Eberly, "Distance from a Point to an Ellipse, an Ellipsoid, or a Hyperellipsoid" (2013). Our own implementation of the published method.

title: Fix ACI grey entries 8, 9 and 250-254 RGB values
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/lib.rs:153-154,174` (no existing issue): ACI grey entries 8, 9 and 250-254 use wrong RGB values.

## Cause
build_palette hard-coded ACI 8 as (128,128,128) and ACI 9 as (192,192,192), and used 51,91,132,173,214 for the 250-254 grey ramp. These differ from the AutoCAD values, so those indices rendered too light and nearest_aci mapped true-colour greys to the wrong index.

ACI 8 is now (65,65,65) and ACI 9 is (128,128,128). The grey ramp for 250-255 is now 51,80,105,130,190,255. A regression test checks these entries and the nearest_aci mapping for greys 65 and 128.

title: Fall back to decimal for huge architectural/fractional distances
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/units.rs:27-31 and 44-46` (no existing issue): Architectural/fractional distance formatting saturates at i64 for huge values and prints a wrong number.

## Cause
`format_distance` for LUNITS 4 and 5 computes `(a * denom).round() as i64`. For large finite values the cast saturates at `i64::MAX`, so the feet and inches come from a clamped number and the output is wrong. For example, 1e30 printed as `48038396025285290'-7 15/16"`.

## Fix
The scaled value is now checked before the integer cast. If it is 9.0e18 or more, which is near the i64 limit, `format_distance` returns the decimal format used for LUNITS 2. Values that fit keep the exact feet/inch and fraction arithmetic. A regression test covers ±1e30 for both modes, plus 1e15 and 12.5 for normal values.

## Verified
- Regression test `units::tests::huge_architectural_and_fractional_distances_do_not_saturate`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib huge_architectural_and_fractional_distances_do_not_saturate`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The LUNITS 3 (engineering) path is unchanged. Its `ft as i64` cast was not part of this report. Angle formatting is also unchanged.

title: AutoLISP: handent and entget reach table records, layouts and dictionaries; tblobjname, namedobjdict, dictsearch, dictnext (fixes #1661, #1659)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #1661. Fixes #1659.

AutoLISP could only reach graphic entities. `handent` returned nil for a layer's or layout's handle, and `namedobjdict`, `dictsearch`, `dictnext` and `tblobjname` weren't defined, so a routine had no way to reach layouts, dictionaries or table records.

### Change
- **`handent`** returns an entity name for table records, BLOCK records, layouts, dictionaries and the other objects a DXF file holds, as well as graphic entities. **`entget`** lists them: `(-1 . name)`, `(0 . type)`, then the record's groups as the file has them, including group 5 or 105, 330 and the subclass markers.
- **New:** `tblobjname`, `namedobjdict`, `dictsearch` (with `setnext`) and `dictnext` (with `rewind`). Keys and names match in any case.
- `entmod` and `entdel` still refuse these names (they return nil), as before for anything that isn't an entity.

### Where the handles come from
CADCraft keeps no handles for table records and objects. A save numbers them as it writes the file, starting at the drawing's handle seed (#495). So LISP sees these objects exactly as a save would write them now: the engine's `EntityCodec` gets an `objects` function, implemented in io by `object_records` (it writes the drawing with `dxf_write::tags` at its save version and keeps the TABLES records, BLOCK records and OBJECTS). The result is cached until the drawing changes, keyed on the document and its revision, so a layer a command adds during the same LISP run is found.

As a result:
- `handent` of a handle read from a file CADCraft saved finds that object after reopening, which is the issue's case (layer "0" `112C`, Layout1 `1123`).
- The handles hold while the drawing is unchanged, but they can move once objects are added, because the next save numbers the records above the new handle seed. `docs/autolisp.md` says so, and the gaps.md FF7 row now notes it.

title: AutoLISP: entmake defines blocks with BLOCK … ENDBLK (fixes #1662)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #1662.

`entmake` had one path: turn the list into an entity and add it to the current space. A BLOCK list isn't an entity, so it returned nil, the entities after it went into model space, and ENDBLK returned nil. Routines that build blocks with `entmake` (a common way to make or redefine a block from LISP) got nothing.

### Change
`entmake` now defines blocks, as AutoLISP does:
- A **BLOCK** list (2 name, 70 flags, 10 base point, 4 description) begins a definition and returns the list.
- **Entities** made while it's open go into the block instead of the drawing and return their lists as usual. A layer they name is created, as `entmake` does elsewhere.
- **ENDBLK** adds the block to the drawing, gives its entities handles, and returns the block's name. A block of the same name (any case) is redefined and keeps its existing spelling, as BLOCK does.
- **Anonymous** blocks (flag 1 with a `*U` name) get the next free `*U…` name at ENDBLK, which is what ENDBLK returns.
- **Refused (nil):** ENDBLK with nothing open; a BLOCK while a definition is open (the open one goes on); an xref (flag 4); an invalid or empty name; a block that inserts itself (checked with BLOCK's own `references_block`, so nested references count too). A definition takes at most 1,000,000 entities.

The definition is kept in the LISP environment until ENDBLK, and nothing is added to the drawing before then. `valid_block_name` and `references_block` in `cmd/blocks.rs` became `pub(crate)` so `entmake` uses the same rules as the BLOCK command. The tests reuse `lisp::tests::session` (now `pub(super)`). `docs/autolisp.md` describes it.

**Together with #1764** (`handent` and the dictionary functions, #1661 and #1659): both PRs add a field to the LISP environment, a test module in `lisp/mod.rs` and a paragraph to `docs/autolisp.md`, so whichever lands second needs a keep-both merge there. title: DXF: keep foreign objects whose handles are above 2^48 (fixes #1773)
author: philipp-tch
body:
Fixes #1773.

## What

`crates/io/src/dxf_raw.rs` believes the whole 64-bit handle range for foreign objects. Before, it only believed handles ≤ 2^48 (`MAX_HANDLE`, added with #545 against hostile files). Null handles are still refused. Modelled entities and table records already accepted any 64-bit handle; now foreign objects do too. Drawings that AutoCAD saved with handles around 2^51 therefore keep their dynamic blocks and all other unmodelled objects.

The handle values are only looked up in hash maps and are renumbered on write (`seed(tags).max(max_handle(tags) + 1)`), so a large value does not grow anything. `hostile_raw_data_never_panics` (with a `FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` handle) still passes.

## Test

New test `a_dynamic_block_with_handles_above_2_pow_48_is_kept` (`crates/io/tests/dynblock_read.rs`). It takes the DOOR fixture with every handle moved by `0xDAD1000000000` and checks that the dynamic block is read and survives a save. It fails without the change and passes with it.

Run locally on Linux:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-io --tests -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-io`: 310 passed

I did not run the full `cargo xtask ci`, because the wasm target is not installed here. Over the whole workspace, the same change on top of v0.8.0 passes 2043/2043 tests.

## Related, separate

The planner on our side noticed this while testing; it is not caused by this change. If a file's handles reach the end of the 64-bit range (for example all shifted to `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFF000`), handle allocation saturates (`saturating_add`), and new or carried objects all get `FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`. Real AutoCAD drawings don't get there; damaged or hostile files can. Refusing loudly or renumbering on read would avoid the duplicates. I can open a separate issue for it if you like.

body:

title: Write a layout's paper-space viewport (id 1) first, so DWG keeps the viewport ids
author: philipp-tch
body:
Fixes #1781.

## What

`crates/io/src/dxf_write.rs` writes a layout's paper-space viewport (id 1) ahead of the layout's other entities (`sheet_first`), for the first layout (ENTITIES section) and the others (their `*Paper_Space` blocks). DWG stores no viewport ids and readers number a layout's viewports in order, so a sheet viewport that the draw order had put behind a model viewport no longer comes back as id 2 with the model viewport as the sheet.

The order of everything else is unchanged. The paper-space viewport draws nothing of its own, so moving it to the front changes no drawing. Layouts without an id-1 viewport keep the existing `paper_views` path.

## Test

New test `a_paper_viewport_behind_a_model_viewport_stays_id_1_through_dwg` (`crates/io/tests/dwg_roundtrip_losses.rs`). It adds a model viewport (id 2) before the sheet viewport (id 1) in every layout and saves through DWG. It fails without the change (`(Some(1), Some(2))`) and passes with it.

Run locally on Linux:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-io --tests -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-io`: 310 passed

I did not run the full `cargo xtask ci`, because the wasm target is not installed here. On three real AutoCAD drawings (two of them with swapped pairs before), all viewports keep their id and twist through a DWG save with this change (14/14, 14/14, 29/29).

title: BOX, CYLINDER and EXTRUDE build 3D solids as groups of 3D faces
author: WladmirJunior
body:
First step toward F24, as proposed in #1783: commands that create 3D geometry, with no dependency on #1005 or #1675.

## What

- `crates/geom/src/mesh.rs` (new): pure face generation. `extrude` (closed profile, ear-clipped caps), `box_faces`, `cylinder` (fan caps) and `circle_segments`. Faces are 3DFACE-style quads (a triangle repeats its last corner), wound outwards, with the diagonals of triangulated caps and the radial edges of cylinder caps marked invisible via the hidden-edge bits.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/modeling.rs` (new): `BOX`, `CYLINDER` and `EXTRUDE` under Draw > 3D Modeling, each with a JSON form and a prompt sequence.
- Each solid is one group of `Face3d` objects, created in one undo step. Faces take the layer, colour and linetype of the profile (EXTRUDE) or the current ones (BOX, CYLINDER).
- EXTRUDE takes closed polylines (arcs by chord tolerance) and circles, along +Z from the profile's elevation. The profile is kept unless `erase: true`.
- No new entity type and no render changes. 3DFACE already round trips in DXF and DWG.

## Input handling

Profiles with fewer than 3 points, open, without area, folded back or self-touching are refused with a message, and nothing is added to the drawing when any profile of a call is bad. Sizes, tolerances and handles are checked; point counts (4096), sides (1024) and faces (50,000) are capped. Zero height or radius is an error.

title: Interface Language dialog: list the languages alphabetically by their own name
author: nikolainyegaard
body:
The Interface Language dialog listed the languages in registry order, which is the order they were added, so the list was hard to scan.

## Change

English stays first, as the source language and the fallback (Auto or System Language stays ahead of it where offered). The rest sort by their own name with Latin accents folded, so Čeština is under C and Magyar under M rather than after Z. Names in other scripts follow the Latin ones in code point order, which puts Cyrillic, then the CJK languages at the end without a special rule. `Preference::for_picker` holds the order and sorts by the registry's native name, so Korean keeps its place whether the dialog shows 한국어 or, without a Hangul face, Korean. `Preference::ALL` keeps its own order. A test checks the properties rather than a fixed list.

The same rule is in PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#8203) and the launcher (storytold/craft-launcher#720), so the suite's pickers read the same way.

title: Use chrono instead of hand-rolled UTC conversion
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Fixes #1785.

## Summary
- Adds `chrono` (0.4.45, `default-features = false, features = ["std"]`) as a workspace dependency. chrono is already used across the suite (deckcraft, pdfcraft, filmcraft, the launcher, services), so I picked it over jiff.
- Replaces the hand-rolled Hinnant `civil_from_days` copies in:
  - `apps/cadcraft/src/logging.rs`: `timestamp` → `2026-10-08T07:59:17.728Z`
  - `crates/ui-egui/src/autosave.rs`: `utc` → `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`
  - `xtask/src/parity.rs`: `today` → `YYYY-MM-DD`
- Output formats are unchanged. A pre-epoch clock still clamps to the epoch, and nothing panics.
- `AGENTS.md`: time goes through chrono, and nobody hand-rolls calendar math.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/file/omni.rs` belongs to unmerged #1146 and should switch to chrono there.

## Testing
- Existing format tests pass unchanged: logging (leap days, 2000/2100, pre-epoch clamp), autosave `utc_dates`, parity `civil_dates` (rewritten against `date()`).
- `cargo clippy -D warnings` on the changed crates and `cargo xtask layers` pass.
- Not run locally: `cargo xtask wasm` (no wasm32 target in my toolchain). chrono with only `std` builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown, and CI will confirm.

title: AutoCAD parity for #1321: DWG layouts, dynamic block fields, double-click and grip editing
author: LastSkywalk
body:
Addresses #1321: a production DWG (columns, layouts, constraint-driven dynamic blocks with field attributes) looked and behaved differently in CADCraft than in AutoCAD. This branch fixes how the drawing is displayed, keeps its dynamic block data and fields through read, edit and save, and makes double-click and grip editing work as they do in AutoCAD.

## What changed and why

### Display parity (report items 1–15)
- **Viewports:** the view target is read and the view centre is taken relative to it. A georeferenced drawing's layout viewports showed an empty spot; its tables looked empty for the same reason.
- **Annotative objects:** `ACDB_ANNOTATIONSCALES` context data is read. Annotative MTEXT, dimensions, multileaders, hatches and block references are drawn at the size AutoCAD gives them for the viewport's scale.
- **Line weights and LWDISPLAY:** read and drawn. The status bar and the canvas use one source, the drawing.
- **Layouts:** the sheet frame and plot origin come from the page setup. Exporting PDF, PNG or SVG while a layout is active plots that layout.
- **Entities:**
  - ATTRIB/ATTDEF vertical alignment;
  - dimension definition points and point marks;
  - zero-width LWPOLYLINE segments (no longer drawn doubled);
  - `\C256+` colour codes in MTEXT;
  - the multileader text attachment point.
- **Fonts:** `CADCRAFT_FONTPATH` and a `fonts` folder beside the settings file are searched first, so a font a drawing asks for can be supplied.
- **DWG:** records the reader had to skip are reported (`drawing.inspect`, `cadcraft-cli info`) as `readNotes`.

### Dynamic blocks and attribute fields
- **Attribute fields are read, saved and evaluated.** Rebar marks, lengths and counts are fields that read the reference's parameters. They used to be dropped, so a grip edit left stale values and a save lost them.

title: MEASUREINIT: choose the units of new drawings, kept in the profile
author: aussieboer61
body:
Part of #1182.

Today NEW, Cmd+N and the drawing CADCraft opens at startup are always imperial (INSUNITS 1, MEASUREMENT 0, Standard dimension style) unless you pass a template or `{"metric": true}`, and nothing keeps a metric choice across restarts: QNEWTEMPLATE is a session variable, not a profile one. Anyone working in millimetres has to remember "New (metric)" on the start page every time, and the startup drawing is always in inches.

This adds **MEASUREINIT**, under the same name AutoCAD uses for the setting: the units of a new drawing made without a template.

- `0` imperial (the default, so nothing changes for anyone who doesn't set it), `1` metric. Only 0 and 1 are accepted.
- It is a **profile variable** (`PROFILE_VARS`), so it is saved and restored like PICKBOX or OSMODE.
- `new` without `metric` or a template follows it; the app's startup drawing follows it (the profile is restored before that drawing is made). An explicit `metric`, a `template`, or a set QNEWTEMPLATE still wins.
- Options ▸ Files gets a "Units of new drawings" row (Imperial (inches) / Metric (millimetres)) with a hint that QNEWTEMPLATE takes precedence. Ukrainian strings are added for the reference-language check.

It doesn't touch the start page design discussed in #1182 (the visible default template and template picker); it gives that work a persisted default to show and change. The headless `Session::new()` used by the CLI and `cadcraft-cli mcp` is unchanged and still starts imperial, since there is no profile there.

Validation (Linux x86_64, rust 1.99.1 in the `rust:1` container):
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test measureinit`: new tests for the imperial default, NEW following MEASUREINIT (INSUNITS 4, MEASUREMENT 1, ISO-25) and an explicit `metric: false` still winning, values other than 0/1 refused, and the setting surviving a profile save and restore

title: EXTRUDE with holes and a 3DFACE command
author: WladmirJunior
body:
Stacked on #1784 (branch `extrude-box-cylinder-3dfaces`): the diff against it is only this PR's commit.

## What

- EXTRUDE cuts holes. `holes: [handles]` takes closed polylines and circles that lie fully inside a profile. With several profiles, each hole goes to the profile that contains it. `erase: true` also erases the holes. The prompt sequence gets a Holes option at the height prompt (a second selection).
- `crates/geom/src/mesh.rs`: `extrude_with_holes` and `profile_with_holes`. The caps are cut by ear clipping after joining every hole to the outline with a two-way bridge (right-most hole first, reflex-vertex rule for the visible vertex). Bridge edges and cap diagonals are marked invisible, so only the real outline and hole edges show on the caps.
- 3DFACE (Draw > 3D Modeling > Meshes > 3D Face, alias `3F`): `{points: [3 or 4 points], invisible?: [edge numbers]}` and the prompt sequence with the Invisible option. A triangle repeats its third point; its closing edge is bit 8. Faces with no area are refused.

## Input handling

Holes that touch or cross the outline, touch or overlap each other, lie inside another hole, or lie outside the profile are refused with a message naming the problem, and the drawing is left untouched. Caps: at most 256 holes and 4096 points in total; the ear cutter has an operation budget, so a hostile polygon returns an error instead of hanging.

## Tests

- `geom::mesh::tests`: volume of a square with a hole, several holes in a concave outline, a ring from two circles (both hole orientations), a bridge that has to bend around a notch, a 10x10 grid of holes, a 900-tooth comb, and every refusal.
- `crates/engine/tests/solids3d.rs`: holes through JSON and through the prompts, holes assigned to the right profile, erase, refusals that leave the drawing untouched, DXF round trip of a holed solid including the invisible edge flags, 3DFACE (quad, triangle, invisible edges, hostile input, prompts).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: WEDGE, CONE, PYRAMID, SPHERE and TORUS 3D primitives
author: WladmirJunior
body:
Stacked on the EXTRUDE holes and 3DFACE branch (`extrude-holes-3dface`, PR for #1793), which is stacked on #1784. The diff against that branch is only this PR's commit.

## What

Five more primitives under Draw > 3D Modeling, built exactly like BOX and CYLINDER (a JSON form and a prompt sequence each, one group of `Face3d` objects, one undo step):

- WEDGE: same inputs as BOX; the tall end is at the first corner's X and it slopes down to the other end.
- CONE: `radius`, `height`, optional `topRadius` for a truncated cone, `segments` or a chord `tolerance`.
- PYRAMID: `radius` to the corners, `height`, `sides` (3 to 1024, default 4), optional `topRadius`. At the prompt, the Sides option changes the count.
- SPHERE: `radius` and `segments` (slices around Z, half as many rings) or `tolerance`.
- TORUS: `radius` (centre to the middle of the tube), `tubeRadius` (smaller than `radius`), `segments`, `tubeSegments`.

`crates/geom/src/mesh.rs` gets `wedge`, `frustum` (cone and pyramid), `sphere` and `torus`. Convex solids are built and then oriented from an interior point, a torus from its tube centre, so every face winds outwards whatever the sign of the height. Triangle fans and apex triangles carry the invisible-edge bits.

CYLINDER's prompt machine is now the shared round-shape machine (same prompts and behaviour); BOX's is shared with WEDGE.

## Input handling

Zero or negative radii, a zero height, a tube as wide as the ring, sides or segments out of range, and non-finite numbers are refused with a message and add nothing. Sphere and torus refuse a segment count whose face count would pass 50,000 before building, and the defaults taken from the tolerance are capped (sphere 256, torus 256 by 128).

- `geom::mesh::tests`: exact volumes for pyramids, cones and frusta (upwards and downwards), wedge volume and tall end, sphere (octahedron and 96 slices) and torus volumes, flipping keeps invisible edges on their edges, every refusal.

title: AutoLISP: namedobjdict, dictsearch, dictnext, tblobjname; handent and entget of non-graphic objects (#1659, #1661)
author: tyrel
body:
Fixes #1659. Fixes #1661.

## What changed

AutoLISP routines can now reach the drawing's non-graphic objects: layouts and their plot settings, dictionaries and symbol table records.

- **New functions:** `namedobjdict`, `dictsearch` (keys in any case, optional `setnext`), `dictnext` (optional `rewind`) and `tblobjname` (for the BLOCK table it gives the BLOCK entity).
- **`entget` of a non-graphic object** lists it as a DXF file of the drawing holds it. Pointers (groups 320–369, 390–399, 480–481) are entity names, and group 5 is the object's own name, so `(handent (cdr (assoc 5 l)))` leads back to it.
- **`handent`** finds these objects too, including by the handles of the file the drawing was read from (#1661: `(handent "112C")` for layer `0` in a saved `h.dxf`).

### How it works

CADCraft writes these objects from its own model and only gives them handles in a file. So the records come from the DXF writer:

- **`cadcraft_io::object_records`** returns the TABLES records, the BLOCK records and the OBJECTS records, each with the role the existing `dxf_raw::identities` gives it (layer name, `NOD`, `NOD/ACAD_LAYOUT` entry and so on). The engine reaches it through a new `EntityCodec::objects` hook, the same way `entget` already reaches `entity_groups`.
- **Stable names:** each object gets a name that stays the same for the drawing's LISP session, keyed by its role, so it survives edits. An object read from a file keeps that file's handle as its name. The reader now records the roles of all the file's table, block and dictionary handles in `Foreign::handles`, which is not part of `Foreign::is_empty`, so saving is unchanged. An object the file didn't have gets a name from `7F00000000000000` up, skipping any name already taken.
- **Cache:** the records are cached per drawing revision, so repeated calls on an unchanged drawing don't rewrite it.

### Not in this PR

title: The keypad's decimal key types a point, also with a decimal-comma layout
author: Alex-BB44
body:
Branch `pr/numpad-decimal` · one commit on `main` (7fef8cb)

## What it does

With a keyboard layout that uses a decimal comma (German, French, Czech and many more), the
numeric keypad's decimal key sends a comma. In CADCraft a comma separates coordinates, so `2,5`
typed on the keypad became the point (2, 5) instead of the number 2.5. Now the keypad's key types
a point; the comma on the main keyboard stays the coordinate separator.

## How

`numpad_decimal_point` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` runs over the raw input events before the
frame. The keypad key is told apart by its physical key: egui-winit maps none for it, while the
main comma key has one. A comma key event without a physical key, followed by a typed comma, is the
keypad's, and only that comma becomes a point.

Measured on Linux (X11) with a real key event (the keypad decimal key under a German layout). On
Windows and macOS this rests on the same egui-winit mapping and has not been measured there.

## Tests

`cargo xtask ci` is green. The new test is `crates/ui-egui/tests/numpad_decimal.rs`: the keypad
comma becomes a point while the main comma stays, only the comma right after the keypad key
changes, and a layout that already sends a point is left alone.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Properties palette: several objects of one type show what they share, *VARIES* where they differ
author: Alex-BB44
body:
Branch `pr/properties-varies` · one commit on `main` (7fef8cb)

## What it does

With several objects of the same type selected, the Properties palette now shows their own
values too, not only the general ones (colour, layer, linetype …):

| Type | Values |
|---|---|
| Line | length, angle |
| Circle | radius, diameter, circumference, area |
| Arc | radius, start and end angle |
| Text | height, rotation, width factor |
| MText | text height, defined width |
| Polyline | global width, closed |
| Hatch | pattern, scale, angle |
| Dimension | dimension style, text height, arrow size, overall scale |
| Block reference | rotation, scale |

A value they share is shown once; one they don't share shows `*VARIES*`. A value typed there is
set for all of them in one `properties.set`. Positions and contents stay per object: one centre or
one text for all would wreck the drawing.

The selection is checked for one type before anything is copied, since a large selection is
looked at every frame. A mixed selection shows the general values only, as before.

## Tests

`cargo xtask ci` is green. The new test is `crates/ui-egui/src/palettes/several_tests.rs`: three
circles of different radii show `*VARIES*` in the four boxes, and 7 typed into the radius sets all
three to 7.

title: Plot: JIS B4/B5/B6 and Japanese paper sizes (はがき・封筒・四六判)
author: midasdf
body:
## What this fixes

Japanese drafting uses the **JIS** B series — B4 257×364 mm, B5 182×257 mm, B6 128×182 mm — but the paper table only had the ISO sizes (B4 250×353, B5 176×250), so a JIS B5 sheet plotted about 7 mm short in each direction (the audit measured 7–12 mm across the B series). The Japanese postcards, envelopes and 四六判 could not be selected at all.

## Changes

- **Paper table** (`crates/render/src/paper.rs`): `B4`/`B5`/`B6` are now the JIS sizes (728.50×1031.81, 515.91×728.50 and 362.83×515.91 pt). The ISO sheets stay reachable as `B4 (ISO)`/`B5 (ISO)`.
  - Added: Japanese Postcard (はがき, 100×148 mm → 283.46×419.53 pt), Japanese Double Postcard (往復はがき, 148×200 mm), Japanese Envelope #3 (長形3号, 120×235 mm), Japanese Envelope Kaku #2 (角形2号, 240×332 mm) and 四六判 (Shirokuban, 127×188 mm). A6 was already an ISO sheet.
  - Names resolve case-insensitively and ignore spaces, hyphens, underscores and parentheses (`B5 (JIS)`, `b5-jis`, `b5jis`); the Japanese spellings are aliases too.
- **Plot/PDF output** uses the resolved sheet for the PDF `/MediaBox` and the PNG preview; the built-in plotter devices and the Page Setup/Plot paper combo iterate `PAPER_SIZES`, so the new sizes appear there automatically. The `pagesetup`/PLOT parameter docs list the new names.
- **Backward compatibility:** a drawing that stored the ISO sheet keeps its stored canonical name and dimensions; only the bare `B4`/`B5` alias changed meaning. Callers that mean ISO now say `B4 (ISO)`/`B5 (ISO)` — called out in `docs/plotters.md` and the ROADMAP revision row.
- **Docs:** `docs/plotters.md` (standard sizes, margins, name resolution), ROADMAP progress log + revision history, dated 2026-10-21.

title: Find installed fonts where fontconfig looks: XDG dirs, fontconfig <dir> entries, Flatpak host fonts
author: mbolling
body:
Part of #674 (CJK fonts not supported well on Linux).

## Problem

On Linux and the BSDs `cadcraft_fonts::ttf::scan()` only walked `/usr/share/fonts`,
`/usr/local/share/fonts`, `~/.fonts` and `~/.local/share/fonts`, and `ui-egui/theme.rs` looked
for the UI, CJK, Japanese, Korean and Arabic fonts at hard-coded `/usr/share/fonts/...` paths.
Distributions and sandboxes that keep fonts elsewhere got nothing:

- **NixOS** (verified on a NixOS 25.11 laptop): `/usr/share/fonts` does not exist. fontconfig
  finds fonts through `/etc/fonts/conf.d/00-nixos-cache.conf`, one
  `<dir>/nix/store/...-dejavu-fonts-2.37</dir>` per font package, plus
  `<dir prefix="xdg">fonts</dir>` in `/etc/fonts/fonts.conf` (which fontconfig expands to
  `$XDG_DATA_HOME/fonts` and every `$XDG_DATA_DIRS` entry + `/fonts`: `~/.nix-profile/share/fonts`,
  `/etc/profiles/per-user/$USER/share/fonts`, `/run/current-system/sw/share/fonts`). Home-manager
  adds `~/.config/fontconfig/conf.d/10-hm-fonts.conf` with more `<dir>`s and `<include>`s.
  `fc-list` sees 156 TrueType/OpenType files there; our scan found 0, so TEXT with Chinese
  characters drew the stroke font's missing-glyph boxes although Unifont was installed, and the
  interface kept egui's bundled font.
- **Guix**: `~/.guix-profile/share/fonts` and `/run/current-system/profile/share/fonts`, reached
  the same way (`$XDG_DATA_DIRS`).
- **Flatpak**: the sandbox has no host `/usr/share/fonts`; flatpak bind-mounts the host's system,
  local and user font directories at `/run/host/fonts`, `/run/host/local-fonts` and
  `/run/host/user-fonts`, and writes `/run/host/font-dirs.xml` (`<dir>` + `<remap-dir>`
  elements) which the freedesktop runtime's `/etc/fonts/fonts.conf` includes. (Relied on from
  flatpak's documented font handling, not tested in a sandbox here.)

## Design

`crates/fonts/src/ttf/dirs.rs` (new, `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))`): a Linux/BSD font
