author: mbolling
body:
Fixes #1608. Crate: `cadcraft-fonts` only.

## What the tester saw, reproduced on Linux

`%%c` becomes U+2300 (`decode_controls`, `crates/fonts/src/lib.rs`). A text style whose
TrueType font has no U+2300 glyph then draws the font's own missing-glyph shape: the glyph the
face maps `.notdef` to, an empty rectangle in Arial-class fonts. Most Latin text fonts lack
U+2300: Arial, Times, Calibri and, on Linux, Liberation Sans/Serif (the metric-compatible Arial
and Times substitutes every distribution ships, and what a drawing whose style names `arial.ttf`
realistically gets on Linux). Every Latin font has Ø (U+00D8). Only wide-coverage fonts
(DejaVu, FreeSans, Noto Sans Symbols...) have U+2300, and only when one is installed did the
per-character fallback rescue the symbol, in a different font and size than the surrounding
text.

Headless reproduction (`cadcraft-cli run --metric --cmd 'style {"name":"T","font":"LiberationSans-Regular.ttf"}' --cmd 'text {...}' --export out.png`, HOME pointed at a scratch directory whose `.local/share/fonts` holds only the fonts named), text height 5, lines `%%c50 ABC`, `Ø50 (U+00D8)`, `∅50 (U+2205)`, `⌀50 (U+2300)`, MTEXT `%%c50`:

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| (a) style font Liberation Sans, no other font installed | `%%c`, U+2205 and U+2300 are empty boxes (TEXT and MTEXT); only the literal Ø line reads | all four lines show Liberation Sans' own Ø, same size and weight as the digits |
| (b) Liberation Sans + DejaVu Sans installed | `%%c` and U+2300 are DejaVu's small ⌀ (x-height sized), U+2205 DejaVu's large ∅: readable but visibly another font | identical to (a): the style's own Ø; DejaVu is no longer consulted |
| (c) stroke font (default style) | `%%c`, Ø, ⌀ are the stroke diameter sign; U+2205 is a box (or, with DejaVu installed, DejaVu's ∅) | U+2205 is the stroke diameter sign too |
| (d) symbols-only style font (Symbols Nerd Font: no Latin at all), no other font | every character is a box | every character is drawn by …

title: i18n(ja): Japanese interface, first step
author: midasdf
body:
## What this adds

A Japanese interface for CADCraft, first step — the app had the catalog infrastructure and
thirteen languages but no Japanese `ja` catalog, so Japanese users saw an English interface.

- **`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/ja.tsv`: 856 rows** — the collected menu, command-label, tool,
  object-snap and marked-UI strings (848 rows), the two single-count templates, and six labels for
  the Options tabs that the UI reads dynamically. The catalog covers, among others: all menu
  headings and command labels, ribbon/tool groups and tooltips, object snaps, status bar and
  property labels, the Options dialog, main dialogs (Drafting Settings, Blocks, Layers, Quick Select,
  Parameters, Command Reference, About, Interface Language), start page, file/model tabs, drawing
  utilities and the About window controls.
- **A `ja` preference** in `i18n::Preference` and `LANGUAGES`, selectable in Edit → Interface
  Language, the Options language page and `ui.language` / `ui.set` (`{"interfaceLanguage":"ja"}`),
  saved with the other preferences, with Auto following the system locale (`ja-JP`,
  `ja_JP.UTF-8` → `ja`). Missing rows fall back to English.
- **A single count form** (`@plural` with `{n}`), like Korean and Hungarian: a Japanese noun is not
  pluralised after a number.
- **A Japanese font gate.** The interface only switches when a font covers every kana, kanji and
  Japanese punctuation mark in the catalog: the installed Japanese face already used for drawing

title: Dynamic blocks: author linear and point parameters with stretch and move actions (BPARAMETER, BACTION)
author: codyvogt
body:
Part of #185 (dynamic blocks; `docs/gaps.md` F3, the remaining alpha blocker): the first slice of **authoring** dynamic blocks in the Block Editor.

## What it does

While a block is open in the Block Editor (BEDIT):

- **BPARAMETER** adds a **linear** or **point** parameter.
- **BACTION** adds a **stretch** or **move** action that follows one.

Both have AutoCAD's command-line prompts and a JSON form:

```
BPARAMETER  Enter parameter type [Alignment/Base/pOint/Linear/Polar/Xy/Rotation/Flip/Visibility/looKup]: L
            Specify start point or [Name/Label/Chain/Description/Base/Palette/Value set]:
            Specify endpoint:   Specify label location:   Enter number of grips [0/1/2] <2>:
BACTION     Select parameter:   Enter action type [Array/Move/Scale/sTretch]: T
            Specify parameter point to associate with action or enter [sTart point/Second point] <Second>:
            Specify first corner of stretch frame or [CPolygon]:   Specify opposite corner:
            Specify objects to stretch / Select objects:   Specify action location or [Multiplier/Offset]:
```

```json
{"command":"bparameter","params":{"type":"linear","start":[0,0],"end":[10,0],"labelAt":[5,-2]}}
{"command":"baction","params":{"parameter":"Distance1","type":"stretch","frame":[[8,-1],[12,6]],"handles":["102"],"at":[12,-2]}}
```

The Block Editor draws what was added:
- a linear parameter as a dimension with its label and arrow grips;
- a point parameter as a marker with its label;

title: Apply a block reference's linetype scale to the objects inside the block
author: philipp-tch
body:
Fixes #1829.

## What

`sub_ctx` in `crates/render/src/lib.rs` multiplies `lt_factor` by the reference's own linetype scale (group 48, when finite and positive). The objects inside a block reference are then drawn with LTSCALE × reference scale × their own scale. The same applies to a dimension's block, which goes through `sub_ctx` too. Nothing else changes; a reference at scale 1 draws as before.

## Test

New `crates/render/tests/block_ltscale.rs`: a DASHED line in a block, inserted at linetype scale 1 and 2, with the line's own linetype DASHED and BYBLOCK. It fails without the change (dashes stay 0.5 at scale 2) and passes with it.

Run locally on Linux: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-render --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p cadcraft-render` (143 passed). Not the full `cargo xtask ci` (no wasm target here). In our fork on top of 0.10.0 the whole workspace passes (2234).

## Please check in AutoCAD, if you can

I can't verify AutoCAD's behaviour here. This makes the same drawing as the test, as DXF (ezdxf):

```python
import ezdxf
d = ezdxf.new("R2018", setup=["linetypes"])
b = d.blocks.new("B"); b.add_line((0, 0), (100, 0), dxfattribs={"linetype": "DASHED"})
m = d.modelspace()
m.add_blockref("B", (0, 0), dxfattribs={"ltscale": 1})
m.add_blockref("B", (0, 10), dxfattribs={"ltscale": 2})
d.saveas("block_ltscale.dxf")
```

If AutoCAD draws both rows with the same dashes, the expectation is wrong and I'll close this.

title: DXF read: fewer allocations on the per-group and per-entity paths (#1076)
author: mbolling
body:
Part of #1076 (large drawings are slow to open, and take many times their size in memory). A profile of `cadcraft-cli info` on the DXF rendition of the #1076 sample (276 MB, 16.7 million groups, 1.1 million entities) put 23% of the reader's time in malloc, free and memmove, and showed where the needless allocations come from. This PR removes the ones that are local changes: six commits, each measured on its own, no change to what is read.

Test file, as #1076 asks: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cyfung1031/uploads/9126f172518fc3b0ba6cda72ac4d8be9e1fa1fd1/cad-samples/CADCraft_Heavy_Engineering_sample.dwg` (the DXF used below is `cadcraft-cli convert` of it, so the DXF reader can be measured without the DWG bridge).

## Commits

- `Key the raw reader's entity map by handle, not hex text`: `dxf_raw::read` kept a `HashMap<String, bool>` keyed by every entity's `handle.hex()` and probed it with freshly formatted text once per entity: 1.1 million String allocations and SipHash over strings. Keyed by `Handle` now; the lookups use the handle the record already parsed. An entity with a null or absurd handle, which the map could never match before either, is treated the same. Measured −0.36 s.
- `Skip the raw reader's head scan for records without 102 groups`: `head()` ran three times per entity, allocating two to four Strings each, to find reactors and extension dictionaries that only a `102` group can introduce; most entities of a large drawing have none. Guarded by a scan for a `102` group. Measured −0.25 s.
- `Unescape DXF text only when it holds a backslash`: the ASCII parser allocated every string value twice, once in `typed()` and once in `unescape_unicode()`, which copied its input even with nothing to unescape; and the end-of-file check cloned the text of every record's type group. Measured −0.15 s.
- `Size the DXF tag list from the line count`: `parse_with_limit` already counts the lines for its limit check; the count now sizes the tag list once instead of letti…

title: Spline extents: evaluate on the stack and sample relative to the spline (#1076)
author: mbolling
body:
Part of #1076 (large drawings are slow to open): a third of the time the reference drawing took to open was spent computing its extents, and nearly all of that was spline evaluation. `open_drawing` computes the extents of every drawing it opens, so the GUI pays this on every open; it is probably part of what #738 and #754 saw as the app frozen after opening a large DWG.

Profile of `cadcraft-cli info` on the DXF rendition of the #1076 sample (276 MB, 985,250 entities, 3,072 splines): `cadcraft_geom::spline::basis` 13.7% of samples, `Spline::eval` 6.8%, `calloc` 5.8%. Three causes, one commit each, only `crates/geom/src/spline.rs` changes:

- `Evaluate spline basis functions on the stack`: `basis()` allocated three `Vec`s per evaluated point. `eval` now uses stack arrays for degrees up to 10 (the cap the DXF reader and the SPLINE command apply; a programmatic spline above it takes the heap path as before). `basis()` keeps its signature for `spline_fit`. A test keeps the previous `basis` and `eval` verbatim as the reference and checks the new ones match them bit for bit: degrees 1 to 11, clamped and uniform unclamped knots, unit and random weights, 1,041 parameter values including some outside the domain.
- `Validate a spline once per tessellation`: `tessellate` called `eval`, which ran `is_valid` (a walk over the knot vector) and `domain` for every sample; both now run once.
- `Size spline bounds sampling relative to the spline`: `bounds()` tessellated at an absolute tolerance of 1e-3, so in a drawing in millimetres every spline hit the 4,000-sample cap (12.3 million evaluations for this file). It now samples at 1e-3 of the spline's own control-box diagonal, with at least four samples per knot span for dense fit splines and the same cap, folded straight into a `Bounds2` without an intermediate `Vec`; a degree-1 spline is its control polygon, so its control box is returned as exact, and a degenerate spline gets its control box, which contains the curve. A typical spli…

title: DWG open: stream the DXF rendition into the tag parser (#1076, #57)
author: mbolling
body:
Part of #1076 (and #57, the first report of a large DWG failing after minutes): opening a DWG held its whole DXF rendition in memory before any of it was parsed. For the #1076 sample (47.8 MB, AC1032) that is 300 MB of text, plus the buffer's doubling as it grows and the header-variable splice that moves the whole buffer once, all alive next to the 20 million tags parsed from it. This PR streams the rendition into the tag parser as acadrust writes it, so the text never exists as a whole.

Test file, as #1076 asks: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cyfung1031/uploads/9126f172518fc3b0ba6cda72ac4d8be9e1fa1fd1/cad-samples/CADCraft_Heavy_Engineering_sample.dwg`

## Commits

- `dxf: parse a file as it is written, through a Write sink`: `cadcraft_dxf::TagStream` (`new(max_tags, max_bytes)`, `impl std::io::Write`, `finish() -> Result<Vec<Tag>>`) builds the tag list from DXF fed in chunks, ASCII or binary (the sentinel decides). Same result as `parse` for the same bytes: the binary record decoder is now shared with `parse_binary`; ASCII strings are decoded line by line, UTF-8 when valid else in the declared `$DWGCODEPAGE`, which is what `decode_ascii_file` decides for a whole file. A line or record cut by a chunk boundary waits for the rest, bounded by `MAX_RECORD` (1 MiB) so a hostile stream cannot grow the carry buffer; the group-code limit and a new byte limit (`DxfError::TooLong`) fail the stream for good. Tests feed the same files whole, one byte at a time and in mixed chunks, split a code page switch and a string across chunks, and cover the limits, dangling records and bad code lines.
- `dwg: write the rendition straight into a sink`: `cadcraft_dwg::dwg_to_dxf_stream_noted(bytes, limits, sink)` hands acadrust's text to any `Write` as it is produced (through a 64 KiB `BufWriter`, since acadrust writes every group on its own), within the same size limit and with the same message as `dwg_to_dxf_noted`, and returns beside it what the text leaves out, as values rather tha…

title: security: enforce HTTPS on curl downloads (SonarCloud S6506)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Enforces HTTPS on `curl` downloads flagged by SonarCloud rule **S6506** (`shell:S6506`, `docker:S6506`, `githubactions:S6506`, Security).

These `curl` calls use `-L`/`-fsSL` (follow redirects). A redirect could transparently downgrade to plaintext HTTP, exposing the download to MITM tampering. Adding `--proto '=https'` forces curl to refuse any non-HTTPS protocol, including across redirects, without changing behavior for the legitimate HTTPS endpoints already in use.

## Change
`curl <args>` → `curl --proto '=https' <args>` on each flagged line.

🤖 Generated to address SonarCloud findings.

title: security: write files atomically through an exclusive temp file (CWE-59)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Save, export, plot, autosave, and the audit log each wrote output by putting bytes in a **predictable sibling temporary path** and then renaming it over the real file:

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs` — `<path>.cadcraft-tmp` (save)
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/exchange.rs` — `<path>.cadcraft-tmp` (export)
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/layout.rs` — `<path>.cadcraft-tmp` (plot)
- `crates/engine/src/autosave.rs` — `<recovery>.tmp` (autosave)
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/audit.rs` — companion `.adt` (audit log)

Opening a pre-existing temporary path for a truncating write **follows a symlink** planted there by another local user, letting them redirect the write onto any file the victim can write, before the subsequent rename (CWE-59).

## Fix
New shared helper `crates/engine/src/atomic_write.rs`:
- creates a **fresh** temporary file with `create_new` (`O_CREAT|O_EXCL`) in the destination directory, so an existing entry (symlink or not) makes the create fail instead of being followed;
- writes through the **retained handle**, flushes and `sync_all`;
- atomically renames the temp into place, cleaning up on any error.

All five write sites are routed through it. The macOS CI cert importer (`packaging/macos/import-cert.sh`) wrote the decoded PKCS#12 to a fixed name in a possibly-shared temp dir (CWE-377); it now uses a private per-run `mktemp -d` directory and `noclobber` create.

## Tests
- `atomic_write::tests::replaces_contents_atomically`
- `atomic_write::tests::does_not_follow_a_planted_temp_symlink` (unix)
- `cargo check`, `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib`, and `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-engine` pass (no new warnings).
- `bash -n` on the edited script passes.

Addresses security findings rows 1, 25, 40 (CWE-59) and 19 (CWE-377).

title: security: confine craft-fonts manifest paths and reject newline Cargo directives (CWE-22, CWE-74)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
The optional `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` build input lets a font manifest (`fonts/manifest.txt`) choose the file each face is embedded from. `crates/fonts/build.rs` had two issues:

1. **Path traversal (CWE-22):** it canonicalised `dir.join(file)` with **no containment check**, so an absolute path, a `..` traversal, or a symlink inside the checkout could make the generated `include_bytes!` read an arbitrary readable file on the build host and expose its bytes through `CRAFT_FONTS`.
2. **Cargo directive injection (CWE-74):** it printed the resolved path straight into Cargo's newline-delimited build-script protocol (`cargo::rerun-if-changed=…`). A path with an embedded newline (reachable via a crafted symlink target) could inject a second directive such as `cargo::rustc-env=OUT_DIR=…`, redirecting the generated-source include to attacker Rust.

## Fix
- `resolve_font`: reject absolute and `..` manifest paths, and require the **canonicalised** result to stay inside the **canonicalised** checkout root (also catches symlink escapes).
- `rerun_if_changed`: refuse any path containing CR/LF before emitting the directive.
- `one_line`: collapse CR/LF in checkout-derived diagnostics printed via `cargo::error`/`cargo::warning`.

## Tests
- `cargo check -p cadcraft-fonts` passes.
- Standalone harness confirms: legit relative file allowed; `../../etc/passwd`, `/etc/passwd`, a symlink escaping the checkout, and a CR/LF path are all rejected.

Addresses security findings rows 5 (CWE-22) and 14 (CWE-74).

title: security: bound Lisp callbacks, native comparisons, and local file reads (CWE-400, CWE-407)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Several unbounded paths in the command and scripting engine let supplied LISP source (or a client-selected path) monopolise the thread or exhaust memory:

| Finding | Sink | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **row 2** | `lisp/eval.rs` `call_sync` ran callbacks with `u64::MAX` fuel | drive in bounded slices, abort past a hard step cap |
| **row 33** | `lisp/builtins.rs` `wcmatch`/`glob` exponential `*` backtracking; `lisp/value.rs` `equal` re-traverses shared subtrees | charge a shared work budget, stop when exhausted |
| **row 39** | `lisp/drawing.rs` `setvar` `to_json` unbounded expansion of a shared cons DAG | depth/element-bounded conversion, reject with a LISP error |
| **rows 21, 34** | `fs::read` with no cap in `read_text_file` (OPEN/LOAD/APPLOAD), SCRIPT, and native open (`read_file`/`run_open`) | new `capped_read` helper: reject non-regular files, cap bytes (read `max+1`) |

## Details
- **call_sync**: a `Need::Yield` (slice budget exhausted) is retried up to `SYNC_CALL_CAP`; a comparator with `(while t)` now errors instead of hanging and bypassing the blocking cap.
- **wcmatch/equal**: `glob` and `equal_depth` take a `&mut u64` budget; exhaustion is treated as no-match (ssget filters) or a LISP error (`wcmatch`). The budget is sized so the existing pathological-but-bounded test pattern still succeeds.
- **setvar**: `to_json_bounded` caps elements and depth; over-budget values are rejected.
- **capped_read**: opens once, requires a regular file, reads through `take(max+1)`.

## Tests
- `synchronous_callback_loop_is_an_error_not_a_hang`
- `setvar_rejects_an_oversized_shared_structure`
- `capped_read::tests::{reads_within_limit_and_rejects_oversize, rejects_non_regular_file}`
- Full `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib` (326 tests) passes; `cargo clippy` adds no new warnings.

Addresses security findings rows 2, 21, 33, 34, 39.

title: security: submit XATTACH picked path as literal text, not a command line (CWE-74)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
The External References palette's `XATTACH` handler (`crates/ui-egui/src/xrefs.rs`) passed the file picker's result to `app.cmdline(&path)`. `cmdline` interprets command-line syntax, so a selected filename beginning with an apostrophe — e.g. a file literally named `'closeall` — was executed as an engine command instead of naming the file, closing every open drawing **without the UI's unsaved-change confirmation**.

The picked path is attacker-controlled: the picker returns whatever the user selected, and `relative_to_host` can reduce it to a bare basename, making a crafted name easy to trigger.

## Fix
After `start("xattach")`, submit the path through `Session::input(Input::Text(path))`. `input()` delivers the value straight to the running command's prompt (`input_to_command`) and never goes through the `cmdline`/`typed` apostrophe-command branch, so the filename is always treated as literal text. This matches the existing picker/dialog bridges (`palettes/patterns.rs`, `dialogs.rs`, `mtext_editor.rs`).

## Tests
- `cargo check -p cadcraft-ui-egui` and `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-ui-egui` pass with no new warnings.
- Verified in `crates/engine/src/lib.rs` that `Input::Text` routes via `input_to_command` (the command's prompt), bypassing command interpretation.

Addresses finding row 26 (CWE-74).

title: security: authenticate the local control server with a per-session token (CWE-306)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
The optional `--control PORT` server (`apps/cadcraft/src/control_server.rs`) listens on `127.0.0.1` and dispatched any JSON request **without authenticating the peer**. Loopback TCP does not distinguish OS users, so another local account could connect and drive the desktop user's command and file authority — e.g. reading files through native Lisp, or create/truncate writes.

## Fix: per-session token
- **New `cadcraft_mcp::control_token`**: `issue(port)` generates a 256-bit random token (via `getrandom`) and writes it to `cadcraft-control-<port>.token` in the per-user runtime dir with **owner-only** permissions (`0600` on Unix; per-user `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on Windows). `read(port)` reads it; `matches` compares in constant time; `revoke(port)` removes it.
- **Server**: issues the token at startup (logs its path) and requires every request to carry a matching `token` field. Requests without a valid token get `{"ok": false, "error": "unauthorized…", "state": "not-run"}` and the connection is closed **before dispatch**.
- **MCP bridge** (`Remote`): reads the token from the owner-only file — which needs the desktop user's own filesystem access — and attaches it to every request. The bridge keeps working unchanged for the legitimate user; a different local user cannot read the token, so cannot authenticate.

This keeps the existing TCP transport and is cross-platform; authority is bound to filesystem ownership of the token file.

## Docs
`docs/control-protocol.md` now documents the required `token` and where the file lives.

## Tests
- `control_token`: `issue_then_read_round_trips`, `matches_is_exact`, `token_file_is_owner_only`.
- `control_server`: `a_request_without_the_token_is_unauthorized`, `a_request_with_the_token_is_dispatched`, plus the existing suite updated to send the token.
- `cadcraft-cli` MCP `--connect` integration tests still pass.
- `cargo clippy` adds no new warnings (mcp forbids unsafe / denies unwrap in non-test code).

Addresses finding row 4…

title: security: do not follow directory symlinks in cargo xtask stats (CWE-400)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
`xtask/src/stats.rs` `walk` descended with `Path::is_dir()`, which **follows symlinks**, and kept no record of visited directories. A small acyclic graph of directory aliases planted in a workspace package (e.g. via a contribution a developer inspects) caused exponentially repeated enumeration and file reads, burning the developer's CPU and I/O far beyond the repository's real size.

## Fix
- Inspect each entry's own `file_type()` and **skip symlinks** before descending or reading, so a directory alias is never re-scanned as a fresh directory.
- Add a traversal budget (`MAX_ENTRIES = 2_000_000`) as defense in depth.

## Tests
- `walk_does_not_follow_directory_symlinks` (unix): a directory symlink pointing back at a real dir is not followed, so its single `.rs` file is counted once.
- `cargo test -p xtask` and `cargo clippy -p xtask` pass (the one remaining clippy warning is pre-existing in `layers.rs`).

Addresses finding row 4.

title: security: bound native DXF/SVG/PDF import allocation and quadratic work (CWE-400/407/789)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Six native import paths in `crates/io` let a crafted drawing cause quadratic CPU work or unbounded allocation:

| Finding | Where | Fix |
|---|---|---|

title: security: guard the DXF->DWG conversion input and document decoder limits (CWE-789)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
`crates/dwg` wraps the third-party `acadrust 0.6.4` decoder, which allocates tables and section buffers from sizes a file declares and cannot be interrupted once it starts (an allocation failure aborts the process; `catch_unwind` cannot recover that).

The **DWG→DXF read** path is already hardened: input-size limit before decode, `CappedWriter` output cap, `catch_unwind`, failsafe mode. The **DXF→DWG `convert`** path had **no input-size guard**, so a very large DXF went straight into the dependency's reader.

## Fix
- `convert` now rejects DXF input larger than `Limits::max_dxf_bytes` before calling `DxfReader::read`, symmetric with the read path, keeping the existing `catch_unwind` around reader and writer.
- Documented the residual risk and the recommended upstream fix in the crate docs.

## Scope / honesty note
Rows 3, 23, 27 describe allocations driven by **internally declared** table/section sizes inside the unmodified dependency. A *small* file declaring a huge table can still make the dependency allocate before any size is known — that can only be fully fixed by patching/upgrading `acadrust` to validate declared sizes against a decoded-memory budget, or by running the decode in a separate worker with an OS memory limit (`acadrust` is used unmodified, and this crate is `forbid(unsafe_code)`). This PR bounds the reachable **input and output size** and documents the residual clearly rather than claiming a complete fix.

## Tests
- `dxf_to_dwg_rejects_garbage_without_crashing` plus the existing suite; `cargo test`/`cargo clippy -p cadcraft-dwg` pass.

Addresses findings rows 3, 23, 27.

title: Linux: native Wayland by default, with in-app window buttons on GNOME
author: bmh129
body:
On a Wayland desktop, CADCraft forces winit's X11 backend (XWayland) whenever `DISPLAY` is set (#159). The deb and rpm only recommend the X11 libraries. Without `libxkbcommon-x11`, winit panics at startup:

```
Library libxkbcommon-x11.so could not be loaded
```

This PR ports WordCraft's fix for the same crash (storytold/wordcraft#3359) and its GNOME window buttons (storytold/wordcraft#3361). The two changes go together: GNOME draws no frame for native Wayland windows, so switching to Wayland without the window buttons would leave a window with no way to move, resize or close it.

## Changes

**1. Native Wayland by default; `CADCRAFT_X11=1` for XWayland**
- The app runs natively on Wayland: sharp at fractional scales, with working input methods.
- `CADCRAFT_X11=1` runs it through XWayland, but only if the X11 libraries load (libX11, libXcursor, libX11-xcb, libXi, libxkbcommon-x11). If they don't, the app logs what is missing and stays on Wayland, so it no longer crashes at startup.
- The deb and rpm also recommend `libxkbcommon-x11`, and the rpm recommends `libX11-xcb`.

**2. GNOME Wayland: window buttons and resize edges drawn by the app**
- GNOME's compositor offers no `zxdg_decoration_manager_v1`. When that protocol is missing, the window opens without winit's frame and CADCraft draws a title row like GNOME's header bar:
  - the drawing's name, centred;
  - minimize, maximize and close, in the order GNOME's `button-layout` sets (read once through the XDG Desktop Portal).
- Thin zones along the window's edges resize it.
- KDE, Sway, Hyprland, COSMIC and X11 keep the desktop's own frame.
- **Options ▸ Display ▸ Use system title bar** (OPTIONS key `systemTitleBar`) brings back winit's frame immediately. It is saved in `workspace.json`, which is now read before the window opens.
- `CADCRAFT_TITLEBAR=app` or `=system` overrides the detection.
- The icons are drawn in code; the new strings are translated in all 15 catalogs.

title: DXF: proxy objects and entities keep their class through a save (#1812)
author: tyrel
body:
Fixes #1812.

## What changed

A proxy record (`ACAD_PROXY_OBJECT`, `ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY`) names its class by number in group 91. Per the DXF Reference, that number is 500 plus the class's position in the CLASSES section. When CADCraft saves, it rewrites CLASSES: its own classes first, then the kept ones. But kept proxies were written with the numbers they were read with, which then named a different class. In #1812's R14 files, AutoCAD's visual styles came back as SCALE, TABLESTYLE or MLEADERSTYLE, and numbers past the last class stayed in the file.

- **Read** (`dxf_raw::read`): when a file has proxy objects or entities, the reader keeps the file's class order (`Foreign::class_order`, upper-case names) and the CLASS records its proxies name. Before, only classes whose name matched a kept record's type were kept, and a proxy's type is `ACAD_PROXY_OBJECT`, so a class like VISUALSTYLE was lost.
- **Write** (`dxf_raw::finish`): it numbers the written CLASSES the way they are written (the writer's own, then the kept ones it appends) and gives each kept proxy object and planned proxy entity its class's new number. A proxy whose number names no class is dropped. A dropped proxy object takes what it owns and its dictionary entry with it, through the existing liveness walk.
- **Copies:** the mapping goes by the read file's class order, not by handle, so copies of a proxy entity follow it too.

Docs: `docs/file-format-parity.md` (the proxy entity and object rows, plus its status line and revision history) and the ROADMAP progress log (also its status line and revision history). The fix is described for DXF save. DWG save already drops proxy entities (acadrust), and I didn't check proxy objects through DWG, so the docs don't claim it.

## How it was tested

- **New test** `proxies_keep_their_class_when_classes_are_rewritten` in `crates/io/src/tests.rs`. It builds a synthetic file (no third-party sample files used): a CADCraft-written DXF with VISUALSTYLE and WIDGETX injected f…

title: DWG read: keep a polyline's vertex order when handles are not ascending
author: nicholasgower
body:
Fixes #1856.

## Root cause

`crates/dwg` is a byte-level bridge over `acadrust`. In acadrust 0.6.4 the DWG builder sorted object record handles (`handles.sort_unstable()`) and appended each `VERTEX_3D` record to its owner's pending vertices in that order. It read the polyline's `owned_count` but discarded the owned vertex-handle list, so a vertex inserted into an existing polyline (and therefore given a higher handle) came back at the end of the outline — wrong shape, self-crossings, longer length.

acadrust 0.6.5 reads the owned vertex-handle list (`read_owned_vertex_handles`) and orders each polyline's collected vertices by it before the DXF illustration is written.

## Change

- Bump `acadrust` 0.6.4 → 0.6.5 in `crates/dwg` and `crates/io` (dev-dependency), with a comment recording why.
- Add `crates/io/tests/dwg_polyline_vertex_order.rs`: writes a DWG containing one 6-vertex 3D polyline whose second vertex has the highest handle, reads it through the real DWG bridge (`cadcraft_io::read`), and asserts the order for AC1018 and AC1032. On 0.6.4 it fails with exactly the reported reorder; on 0.6.5 it passes.

## Verification

- The reporter's gist DWG (SHA-256 `bfdfb7f4e311bb85f42114481b4db8bdd08d7ace155cafa544de02dda1be3750`): `cadcraft-cli convert` now emits the vertices in order — (0,0,0), (10,0,1), (10,10,2), (0,10,3), (0,20,4), (10,20,5).
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-io --lib` (86 tests), the four `dwg_*` integration test files, and `cargo test -p cadcraft-cli` pass.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p cadcraft-io -p cadcraft-dwg --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo check -p cadcraft-io --all-targets` and `cargo check -p cadcraft` are clean.

Note: the upstream fix covers R2004+ polylines (the reported AC1018/AC1032 files). Pre-R2004 DWGs still fall back to handle order because acadrust does not use the first/last-vertex chain there.

title: find, dimstyle: prompt for their parameters instead of erroring
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong

Clicking **Edit ▸ Find...**, or typing `FIND`, returned `invalid parameters for 'find': find is required`, and nothing could be found or replaced from the UI. `DIMSTYLE` (Format ▸ Dimension Style... and Dimension ▸ Dimension Style...) failed the same way with ``name` is required`, as reported in the issue comments.

## Root cause

Both commands are registered with a JSON `run` function that requires parameters (`run_find` needs `find`, `run_dimstyle` needs `name`) but had no `.interactive(...)` prompt machine. Menu items and typed command names go through `Session::start`, which for a command without an interactive machine calls `execute(id, Value::Null)`; the required parameter is therefore missing and the command errors before it can ask for anything. This was a wiring bug, not a parameter-validation bug: the JSON forms themselves were fine.

## Fix

* **FIND** now has an interactive prompt machine (`crates/engine/src/cmd/utility.rs`): *Find what* → *Replace with (Enter to only find)* → *Search options* with `Match case` / `Whole word` toggles and `Done` (Enter). It calls the existing `run_find`, so behaviour is identical to the JSON form (including selecting matches when there is no replacement). `execute("find", {...})` is unchanged and still never prompts.
* **DIMSTYLE** now has an interactive prompt machine (`crates/engine/src/cmd/props.rs`), wired to both `dimstyle` and `dimstyle.dimension`: it prints the current dimension style, `?` lists the styles, and a name makes that style current. Unknown names are refused, not silently created. `execute("dimstyle", {...})` is unchanged.

No new dependencies, no dialogs, no panics (all new code returns `Result`; the interactive steps run under the existing `catch_unwind` guard).

title: Plot paper units follow the drawing's length unit (INSUNITS), not MEASUREMENT
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong

A 10 mm line in model space, plotted to ISO A4 at 1:1, came out 254 mm long — wider than the whole sheet. The page itself was A4 (595.28 × 841.89 pt); the geometry was 25.4× too large.

## Root cause

`cadcraft_render::paper::paper_unit_mm` decided the drawing's paper units from `MEASUREMENT`: 1 → millimetres, 0 → inches. `MEASUREMENT` does not describe the drawing's length unit — it only chooses the imperial or ISO hatch/linetype libraries (as noted in #1649/#1826). The drawing's length unit is `INSUNITS`.

CADCraft's UNITS command (and Drawing Units dialog) sets `INSUNITS` only. So a drawing started imperial and switched to millimetres had `INSUNITS` 4 but `MEASUREMENT` 0; model-space paper units were taken as inches, and a "1:1" plot mapped 1 drawing unit to 1 inch of paper. Many AutoCAD metric drawings also have `MEASUREMENT` 0, so the same happened to files that were never touched by UNITS.

## Fix

`paper_unit_mm` now follows `INSUNITS`: inch-based units (inches, feet, miles, microinches, mils, yards, US survey units) → 25.4 mm; metric units (mm through km, angstroms through parsecs) → 1 mm. Unitless drawings (`INSUNITS` 0/absent, e.g. files without `$INSUNITS`, #1209) keep the old `MEASUREMENT` fallback. This covers both model-space plots and layouts whose page setup has plot paper units 0.

## Tests

- New `crates/io/tests/plot_model_metric_units.rs`: exact geometry of a 10-unit line at 1:1 on ISO A4 portrait (595.28 × 841.89 pt, line 28.3465 pt) for
  - a metric drawing (`INSUNITS` 4, `MEASUREMENT` 1),
  - a drawing switched to millimetres (`INSUNITS` 4, `MEASUREMENT` 0) — failed before the fix at 720 pt,
  - a layout in that drawing with an A4 page setup and plot paper units 0,
  - an imperial drawing (`INSUNITS` 1), which still plots 10 units as 10 inches (720 pt).
- New unit test `paper_units_follow_the_length_unit` in `crates/render/src/paper.rs`.

title: UI: a visible close button on every panel header
author: nicholasgower
body:
Closes #1838.

## What was wrong

A dockable panel could only be closed from its tab context menu, so closing the
External References, Layers, Properties or Tool Sets palettes was hidden. Nothing
on the panel header hinted that closing was possible.

## The change

Every closable panel header now shows a visible X beside its title. It queues the
same `Action::Close` as the context menu's "Close panel", so visibility, saved
workspace state, and reopen behaviour are unchanged.

- Tab groups and floating groups draw the button through the docking surface's
  group-header callback (`group_header_width` / `group_header` in
  `crates/ui-egui/src/docking.rs`), reserving width so the tab titles are fitted
  beside it and never underneath it.
- Accordion title bars (the default Layers/Properties stack) have no header
  callback in `craft-ui`, so the same button is placed over the title bar, left of
  the stock collapse control, using that title's rendered rectangle.
- The icon is the existing code-drawn `Icon::Close`; the hover fill uses
  `theme::Tokens`; the tooltip is "Close panel".
- The accessible name includes the panel ("Close Layers", "Close External
  References", ...) so headers stay distinguishable and the context menu's
  "Close panel" label is not duplicated.
- The drawing canvas is protected and gets no close button.

## Tests

New regression test `every_panel_header_has_a_close_button_that_closes_like_the_context_menu`
in `crates/ui-egui/tests/docking_workflows.rs` covers:

- a close button on the Tool Sets tab header;

title: Autosave: a new autosave folder is owner-only on Unix
author: oracola91
body:
## What and why

Autosave files are unsaved drawings. When the autosave folder (SAVEFILEPATH, by default `<settings dir>/autosave`) doesn't exist yet, the autosaver makes it with `create_dir_all`: in `write_file` before the first autosave, or in `heartbeat` for the lock file (`crates/engine/src/autosave.rs`). On Unix it got the default mode (usually `0o755`) and the files in it the default file mode, so other accounts on the same machine could read the drawings, unless a folder above blocks them. That is common on Linux, where home folders are often readable by other accounts.

Both places now use one helper that creates the folder with mode `0o700` on Unix (`DirBuilder` with `DirBuilderExt::mode`). A folder that already exists keeps its mode, since SAVEFILEPATH can point at any folder the user picked. Windows and the web build are unchanged.

PdfCraft and VectorCraft made the same change for their recovery folders (storytold/pdfcraft#3320, storytold/vectorcraft#3406).

#1840 also changes `write_file`, a few lines below this change (the temporary file). The two don't overlap: this branch and #1840 merge cleanly, and the result keeps both.

Not changed: an autosave folder that already exists, for example the default one an earlier version made, keeps its mode, so the files in it are as readable as before. Making the autosave files themselves owner-only would cover that case and a picked SAVEFILEPATH. That belongs with the temporary file #1840 creates, so I left it out here.

## How it was tested

- New test `a_new_autosave_folder_is_owner_only` in `crates/engine/tests/autosave.rs` (Unix only). The first autosave write makes a missing folder and its missing parent `0o700`. A folder that exists keeps `0o755`. With main's `autosave.rs` it fails (`0o755` instead of `0o700`). The lock file path uses the same helper; it has no test of its own because it reads the process-wide SAVEFILEPATH, which another test in the same binary sets.

title: web: report the open drawing in the viewport title
author: nicholasgower
body:
The web build never sent `ViewportCommand::Title`, so an embedding host (pi-agent-dashboard, sandboxed iframe) could not tell which document opened or whether it had unsaved changes; a refused drop looked like the default `Drawing1`. title: OFFSET uses a single preselected object
author: nicholasgower
body:
Fixes #1610.

**What was wrong:** OFFSET cleared the selection on start, so drawing a rectangle, selecting it and running OFFSET still asked "Select object to offset" after the distance. AutoCAD behaves the same (parity), but users coming from other tools expect the selection to be used.

title: CLI: a --cmd can act on a handle an earlier --cmd returned ({last})
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong

`cadcraft-cli run`'s `--cmd` steps were independent. `mview` answered `{"viewports":["100"]}`, but the next step could not use that handle, so the issue's sequence failed:

```
$ cadcraft-cli run --metric --cmd 'layout.set {"name":"Layout1"}' --cmd 'mview {"p1":[20,20],"p2":[200,150]}' --cmd 'viewport.set {"scale":1}'
{"viewports":["100"]}
`handle`: "..." is not an object handle   # or: no viewport given (pass `handle` or select a viewport)
```

## Mechanism chosen: a `{last}` placeholder

The batch runner now remembers the last object handle a `--cmd` returned, and a parameter value of **exactly** `"{last}"` is replaced with it before the command runs. It works for any parameter and at any depth (e.g. `"handles":["{last}"]`), so it is not tied to `viewport.set`.

```
$ cadcraft-cli run --metric \
    --cmd 'layout.set {"name":"Layout1"}' \
    --cmd 'mview {"p1":[20,20],"p2":[200,150]}' \
    --cmd 'viewport.set {"handle":"{last}","scale":1}'
{"viewports":["100"]}
[{"handle":"100","scale":1.0,...}]
```

- Handles are read from a result by checking the strings against the active drawing, so counts and names (even a hex-looking layer name) are never mistaken for handles; `{"viewports":["100"]}` works like `handle`/`handles`.
- The most recent returned handle stays available across later commands that return none.
- Every other string, and `--script` text, is passed unchanged: normal JSON semantics are untouched.
- `{last}` with no earlier returned handle fails the run with a clear error (`--cmd viewport.set: `{last}` needs an earlier --cmd in this run to have returned a handle`) instead of handing the token to the command as a bad handle.

Documented in `cadcraft-cli --help` (`--cmd chaining`), README and `docs/customization.md`.

## Tests

- `apps/cadcraft-cli/tests/handle_chaining.rs` (new integration test against the built binary, the issue's sequence):
  - `viewport_set_after_mview_uses_the_returned_handle` — failed before the fix with `` `hand…

title: DWG: write AutoCAD's drawing variable dictionary (AC1018 output)
author: nicholasgower
body:
**What was wrong.** An AC1018 (AutoCAD 2004) DWG written from a drawing with no `AcDbVariableDictionary` is read as empty by Vectric Aspire 10.5 ("No data was imported from the DXF / DWG file"), while the same drawing as DXF — and as an AC1032 DWG — imports. AutoCAD always writes that dictionary in the named object dictionary; CADCraft's DXF writer (like ezdxf's) does not, so the bridge converted a DXF without one.

**Fix.** `crates/dwg/src/lib.rs`: before writing a DWG older than AC1032, the bridge adds `AcDbVariableDictionary` to the named object dictionary when it is missing, with the variables AutoCAD keeps there: `CMLEADERSTYLE`, `CTABLESTYLE`, `CANNOSCALE` (from the drawing header), and `DIMASSOC`, `HIDETEXT`, `LAYEREVAL`, `LAYERNOTIFY` (no DXF header variable). AC1032 output is unchanged, and a dictionary a drawing already has keeps its own entries and values. `AcDbVariableDictionary` is AutoCAD's own spelling (the DXF Reference calls it the ACDBVARIABLEDICTIONARY; keys are case-insensitive).

**Tests.** New `crates/io/tests/dwg_required_dictionaries.rs`:
- an AC1018 DWG of a rectangle whose DXF has no dictionary gets one, with the expected variables' values, and CADCraft still reads the rectangle back;
- an AC1032 DWG still has no added dictionary;
- an existing dictionary (ezdxf-style, one `CMLEADERSTYLE` entry) is left exactly as it was.
The first test failed before the fix (`AC1018 DWG: the named object dictionary has an AcDbVariableDictionary`) and passes after it.

Targeted tests (cadcraft-dwg unit tests; cadcraft-io lib and the DWG/round-trip suites: dwg_header_vars, dwg_layout_owner, dwg_roundtrip_losses, followups_626, mleader_roundtrip, acad_interop, roundtrip_audit, dxf_versions) all pass: 143 tests, 0 failures. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and clippy (`-D warnings`) on cadcraft-dwg and cadcraft-io are clean.

title: dim: apply the style's DIMPOST to angular dimensions (#1653)
author: nicholasgower
body:
Fixes #1653.

## What was wrong
A dimension style with DIMPOST `<>` (e.g. `<> m`) reached linear dimensions but not angular ones (2-line and 3-point): CADCraft drew and wrote `36.9°` into the `*D` block, while AutoCAD rebuilds the same dimension as `36.9° m`. The same drawing therefore read differently in the two programs.

## Root cause
`crates/render/src/dim.rs`, the `DimKind::Angular | DimKind::Angular3P` branch called `format_angle` and passed the result straight to the text override, deliberately not applying DIMPOST since #376 (the Dimension Style Manager shows Prefix/Suffix only for linear dimensions, but AutoCAD applies the style's DIMPOST to angular dimensions anyway: both its own 2-line and vertex+2-point dimensions read `36.9° m`).

## Fix
The angular branch now wraps `format_angle(...)` in the same `post(&st.post, ...)` helper the linear branch uses, before the dimension's text override. Nothing changes for a style with an empty DIMPOST (the default): `post` returns the measurement unchanged.

## Tests
- `crates/render/tests/dim_text_format.rs`: renamed and deliberately changed the #376 test to `dimpost_applies_to_angular_dimensions_too` (suffix and prefix forms; the override case now wraps the posted angle, matching linear dimensions).
- `crates/engine/tests/dim_vars.rs`: `dimpost_applies_to_angular_dimensions` covers the command path for a 3-point (vertex + 2 points) and a picked-two-lines angular dimension.
- `crates/io/tests/dim_block_text.rs`: two new tests check the text written into the anonymous `*D` block for a 3-point and a 2-line angular dimension, in both DXF and DWG (`write_with` → `dwg_to_dxf`): `90.0° m` / `45.0° m`.

Results with the fix: `cargo test -p cadcraft-render --test dim_text_format` (2 passed), `-p cadcraft-io --test dim_block_text` (3 passed), `-p cadcraft-engine --test dim_vars` (8 passed). title: DXF/DWG: angular, diametric and radial dimensions get DIMASSOC (#1651)
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong

`dimangular`, `dimdiameter` and `dimradius` create associative dimensions (CADCraft follows their geometry and `dimreassociate` counts them), but the DXF/DWG writer only emitted a `DIMASSOC` for linear/aligned and ordinate dimensions. In AutoCAD the angular, diameter and radius dimensions were therefore unassociated and stayed at their old measurement after edits.

## Root cause

`std_assoc_refs` (`crates/io/src/dxf_write.rs`) had name slots only for `p13`/`p14` (linear/aligned) and `p13` (ordinate); every other kind fell through to `&[]`, so `plan` created no `AssocObj` and no `DIMASSOC` object (and no `ACAD_DIMASSOC` extension dictionary) was written.

## Fix

- **Writer** (`crates/io/src/dxf_write.rs`): write the references AutoCAD writes for each kind.
  - Angular: all four definition points (`p13`, `p14`, `p15`, `p16`); the 3-point angular created by `dimangular` gets its three (`p13`, `p14`, `p15`), including an intersection reference for the vertex.
  - Diameter and radius: one centre reference to the circle/arc with associativity flag `2`, as AutoCAD 2026 writes radial and diametric dimensions (confirmed against AutoCAD-produced DXF samples: one `AcDbOsnapPointRef`, osnap `3`, flag `2`). One reference is enough: it names the geometry whose radius/diameter the dimension follows.
  - Arc length (saved as an aligned dimension) gets its two arc-end origins.
  - Curve start references now use osnap `13` (end stays `1`), as AutoCAD writes them; this also lets a stored point of `0,0,0` resolve to the correct end.
- **Reader** (`crates/io/src/dxf_read.rs`): read the same standard references back, reconstructing radial/diametric definition points on the circle, so AutoCAD files associate those kinds too. Curve refs use osnap `13`/`1` semantics instead of guessing from the (often `0,0,0`) stored point.

CADCraft's own exact links still travel in xdata; the standard objects are the AutoCAD-facing layer.

title: feat(fonts): add context-aware legacy Vietnamese transcoding (TCVN3 & VNI)
author: vantruong-dang
body:
### Summary

In Vietnamese AEC and civil engineering drawings, legacy 8-bit encodings (**TCVN 5712 / TCVN3 / ABC** and **VNI Windows**) are ubiquitously embedded in text entities under `$DWGCODEPAGE: ANSI_1252`. Opening these drawings on modern systems causes widespread mojibake unless users locate and install dozens of legacy 1990s font packs into the operating system. Furthermore, legacy 8-bit fonts (such as `VHELVCN.TTF`, `VAVON.TTF`, `.VnTime`) lack Unicode CMAP tables, causing character advance collisions (such as acute accents having near-zero advances and collapsing into adjacent glyphs).

This PR introduces an idiomatic, zero-allocation legacy Vietnamese transcoding module to `cadcraft-fonts` along with automatic legacy font resolution to clean modern Unicode outline faces.

### Key Changes

1. **Zero-Allocation Transcoder (`cadcraft-fonts::vietnamese`)**:
   - Linear-time, deterministic transcoding for **TCVN3** (single-byte lowercase and composite uppercase) and **VNI Windows** to Unicode NFC.
   - Utilizes `Cow<'a, str>`: Returns `Cow::Borrowed` with zero heap allocations and 0 nanoseconds overhead for ASCII and standard Unicode text.
   - **Context-Aware Fallback Chain**: Inspects font hints (`.Vn*`, `VNI*`), falling back to heuristic byte signature detection (`detect_vietnamese_encoding`) when styles use generic or default names (`Standard`, `simplex.shx`, `Arial`).
   - **False-Positive Prevention**: Strict validation guard (`is_already_unicode_vietnamese`) ensuring existing modern Unicode strings are never corrupted.

2. **Legacy 8-bit Font Resolution (`cadcraft-fonts::TextFont::resolve`)**:
   - Detects legacy Vietnamese font stems (`vni`, `vhelv`, `vtime`, `vavon`, `.vn`) and resolves them to clean modern Unicode TrueType outline faces (`Arial` for Sans, `Times New Roman` for Serif).
   - Prevents floating tone-mark collisions and advance-width collapse caused by non-Unicode legacy font files.

title: Reject a leading '+' in ACI indices and RGB triples in Color::parse
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/lib.rs:115 and 126` (no existing issue): Color::parse accepts a leading '+' in ACI indices and RGB triples.

## Cause
Color::parse turned ACI indices ("5", "color 5") and RGB parts ("1,2,3") into numbers with Rust's integer `str::parse`, which accepts a leading '+'. Inputs like "+5", "color +5" and "+1,+2,+3" were therefore accepted as valid colours.

## Fix
Added a small `parse_digits` helper that returns None unless the text is non-empty and made only of ASCII digits, and only then parses it. All three numeric paths in Color::parse (the "color N" form, the bare ACI index and each RGB part) now use it.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::parse_rejects_plus_sign`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p cadcraft-color parse_rejects_plus_sign`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Hex colour parsing (`Rgb::parse_hex`) already rejected signs and is unchanged. Whitespace around RGB parts ("1, 2, 3") is still accepted.

title: fix(canvas): keep the OS cursor visible over menus and panels
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong

Over the drawing area CADCraft hides the OS cursor (`CursorIcon::None`) and draws its own
crosshair. Moving the pointer to the menus left the cursor invisible, so menu titles and items
could not be seen while pointing at them (reported on Ubuntu 24.04, #1701; the same symptom as
photocraft#6569).

## Root cause

`canvas::show` decided the pointer was over the drawing with

```rust
let inside = hover_pos.is_some_and(|p| rect.contains(p)) && resp.hovered();
```

egui reports a widget as `hovered` when no *widget* is above it, but an open menu's frame (the
padding between its items and its border, and its separators) is not a widget: it belongs to the
popup's own layer. With a menu open over the drawing, the canvas therefore stayed `hovered`, kept
requesting `CursorIcon::None`, and hid the cursor over the menu. A dialog's padding or a floating
palette over the canvas did the same. Over the bare menu bar the cursor was already restored, which
is why only some spots looked broken.

## Fix

`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`: the pointer counts as inside the drawing only when the topmost layer
under it *is* the canvas's layer (`ctx.layer_id_at(p) == Some(ui.layer_id())`). Menus, tooltips,
dialogs and floating panels now keep the visible pointer, and the crosshair stays put under them
instead of following the pointer behind the popup. The hide still applies over the drawing itself,
and `Show System Cursor` still keeps the OS crosshair there.

## Tests

New `crates/ui-egui/tests/cursor_over_menus.rs` (headless `egui_kittest`):

- the canvas hides the OS cursor (`None`);
- the menu bar shows it again (`Default`);
- an open menu over the drawing keeps it — including the case that failed before this change: the
  pointer over the menu's frame, which is an area above the canvas and inside the canvas rect;
- docked palettes keep it;
- `Show System Cursor` shows the OS crosshair over the canvas and the arrow off it.

Results: `crates/ui-egui/tests/cursor_over_menus…

title: web: post cadcraft:opened when a hub-supplied drawing is loaded (#1666)
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong

Embedded in the SCC Space Creative Hub (`?host=parent`), CADCraft accepted `cadcraft:open { name, bytes }` from the parent page but never replied. The hub's host agent waited out its 5 s timeout on every launch with a file (~5 s of needless "Opening…"), and could not tell a failed open from a slow one.

## Fix

- `apps/cadcraft-web/src/host.rs`, `upload.rs`: the inbox remembers which queued files came from the embedding page. After `drain` opens them, the shell posts **once per open**, to the parent on `location.origin`:
  - `{ type: 'cadcraft:opened', name }` once the drawing is loaded and the frame that shows it is drawn;
  - `{ type: 'cadcraft:open-failed', name, error }` when it could not be opened (bad drawing, too large, unreadable) — including the "too large to copy" refusal, which is now answered too.
- `CadApp::open_bytes` now returns the error OPEN reported (OPEN's own failure or the size limit) and `opened` passes it on, so the failure reply carries the real reason. Existing callers that don't report anything ignore the result; the `open_bytes` test now also checks the returned error.
- The message shapes live in a pure `OpenReply` helper in `apps/cadcraft-web/src/main.rs` (compiled for wasm and tests), so they are unit-tested natively without a browser. It is wasm-only wiring; no new dependencies, no panics.

No reply is sent for files picked through File › Open or dropped on the window — only hub-supplied drawings, as the issue asks.

title: Right-click at a command prompt with options opens the shortcut menu (#1366)
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong

The issue's screenshots show AutoCAD's **Command shortcut menu** at the ARRAY prompt ("Enter array type" with Rectangular / PAth / Polar at the cursor). CADCraft only listed those options in the command line: a normal right-click at a prompt was Enter, and the menu appeared only if the button was held for 250 ms. So the reporter never saw the options menu, and the selected object's menu looked absent too.

CADCraft also defaulted `timeSensitiveRightClick` to on, while AutoCAD's initial values are time-sensitive right-click **off** and Command mode **"enabled when command options are present"** (`SCMCommandMode = acEnableSCMOptions`; Autodesk's VBA reference notes the initial value, and SCMTimeMode's initial value is false).

- `timeSensitiveRightClick` now defaults to **off**, as in AutoCAD. The option still gives the old behaviour when enabled: quick click = Enter, hold 250 ms = menu.
- `context_menu::in_command` follows AutoCAD's default command mode: a right-click opens the command menu at the cursor when the prompt has options (Enter, Cancel, Recent Input, the prompt's options, Snap Overrides, Pan/Zoom); at a prompt without options it is still Enter.

title: Fix LISP getangle subtracting ANGBASE in degrees from radians
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/lisp/input.rs:256-258 (lisp_angbase, used at :127 and :183); cause is crates/engine/src/sysvars.rs:141` (no existing issue): LISP getangle subtracts ANGBASE in degrees from an angle in radians, giving wrong angles whenever ANGBASE is not 0.

## Cause
LISP getangle subtracts ANGBASE in degrees from an angle in radians, so answers are wrong whenever ANGBASE is not 0. `Session::lisp_angbase` is documented to return radians, but it read ANGBASE through `sysvars::get`, which returns degrees (`crates/engine/src/sysvars.rs:141`). The helper is used for picked points (`crates/engine/src/lisp/input.rs:127`) and typed angles (`:183`). There is no existing issue for this.

## Fix
`lisp_angbase` now reads the drawing header's ANGBASE directly, which is stored in radians. The regression test `lisp::tests::getangle_is_relative_to_angbase` sets ANGBASE to 90 and checks a picked `getangle` answer, a `getorient` answer (which ignores ANGBASE) and a typed `getangle` answer. It fails on `main` without this change; run it with `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --lib getangle_is_relative_to_angbase`. The full CI run is left to the pipeline.

title: agents: add an issue-solver OpenCode agent
author: nicholasgower
body:
Adds a project-level OpenCode agent that orchestrates the batch issue-solving workflow used in this session: select N unclaimed issues, prepare one worktree and branch per issue, serialize builds and tests, drive one subagent per issue through a failing test and minimal fix to a PR, replace issues that cannot be reproduced, and follow up on CodeRabbit docstring coverage.

This is project tooling rather than application code, but it should speed up contributors who use OpenCode for maintenance work.

## What it adds

- `opencode.json` — defines the `issue-solver` primary agent, with permission to launch `general` subagents and to use the question tool (for the one contributor-credit question).
- `.opencode/issue-solver.md` — the workflow prompt:
  - **Selection:** recent, unclaimed issues; excludes `in progress`, `needs info`, `duplicate`, issues with an open PR, issues the author is already implementing, platform-specific cases, translations, asset/licence work, and large multi-part feature requests.
  - **Isolation:** one `git worktree` and `fix/<issue>-<slug>` branch per issue under a configurable temporary work root (`CADCRAFT_ISSUE_WORKROOT`, defaulting to the system temp directory).
  - **Build serialization:** a per-issue `cargo.sh` wrapper that acquires a process-owned shared lock (holder PID, reclaimed only when that process is gone), retries every 30 seconds, keeps a private `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` with debuginfo/incremental off, and is deleted immediately after its final test run.

title: MCP: the open tool description names DWG as well as DXF
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong

`tools/list` advertised the MCP `open` tool as `"Open a DXF file."`, but `open` (`app.open` → the engine's `open` command → the io layer) reads DWG as well, without a warning. ```

title: Drafting Settings: expose POLARMODE bit 8 (Shift to Acquire)
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong

`POLARMODE` bit 8 (`SHIFT_ACQUIRE`, "Points are acquired by holding Shift, not by resting the cursor on them") worked in the engine (`crates/engine/src/snap/tracking.rs`, `TrackConfig::relative_to` and `Tracker::hover`), and `POLARMODE` accepts the full `0..=15` range, but Drafting Settings had no control for it. title: usage: a read-only cross-reference of layers, blocks, styles and linetypes
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was missing

PURGE finds unused named objects, but only as an interactive cleanup. An agent about to edit a drawing had no read-only way to learn which layers, blocks, text styles and linetypes are used, where, or which are empty/unused (#1439, part of #1377).

## Fix

New `usage` command in the inquiry family (`crates/engine/src/cmd/inquiry/usage.rs`), registered beside `shapes` with a full `params` contract and `noundo`:

```json
{"type?": "layers|blocks|textstyles|linetypes|all", "limit?": 200, "offset?": 0}
```

It returns `schema: 1` with:

- `items`: per named object, `type`, `name`, `entities` (objects in model space/layouts that use it), `blockEntities` (objects in block definitions), `references` (named-object references such as a layer's linetype or a text style's dimension/multileader styles), `used`, `insideBlocksOnly`, `empty`, `unused`, and `current` where a current name exists;
- `summary`: `{total, used, insideBlocksOnly, empty, unused}` per kind;
- `unused`: PURGE's own candidate names per kind, in table order (capped at 5,000 names with `truncated`; counts complete);
- `count`/`returned`/`offset`/`truncated` paging like `shapes`.

The scan is shared with PURGE rather than duplicated: `purge::candidates` (including its built-in keep-list for `0`, `Defpoints`, the current layer/style/linetype, `ByLayer`/`ByBlock` and `Continuous`) and `purge::used_blocks` are now `pub(in crate::cmd)`. PURGE's behaviour is unchanged — only visibility and doc comments changed there. Nothing is created, deleted, selected or undone: `usage` is read-only.

## Tests

`crates/engine/tests/usage.rs` builds a synthetic drawing with a used layer, an empty layer, a layer used only inside a block, a block referenced only inside another block, an unreferenced block, an unused text style and an unused linetype, then asserts:

title: analysis: report found/analysed/skipped counts, caps and implausibility
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong

Agents reading CADCraft's analyses saw only the objects an analysis chose to report. A skipped entity, a paged result or a capped pass was indistinguishable from "nothing there", so an agent could treat an incomplete analysis as complete.

## Root cause

`shapes` built a `skipped` map internally, but no analysis result carried a uniform coverage record. `count`, `countlist`/`counttable` and `massprop` silently dropped objects they did not measure. Caps (`limit`, `MAX_CROSSING_SEGMENTS`, `MAX_WORK`, `MAX_HANDLES`, `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH`) were not reported (or only as a bare `truncated` flag), and no analysis checked its own values.

## Fix

- Added a shared, schema-versioned `SelfCheck` helper in `crates/engine/src/cmd/inquiry.rs`: `found`, `analyzed`, `skipped` (per type with reasons), `caps` (name → value actually hit) and `implausible` flags. It is add-only: the top-level `schema` and every existing key of each command are unchanged.
- `shapes`: reports found/analyzed/skipped (the existing `skipped` map is now derived from the same helper); `limit` when paging truncates; `crossingSegments` when a shape has more than 4000 edges; and flags a perimeter > 10× the bounding-box diagonal or an area larger than the drawing extents.
- `count`/`countlist`/`counttable`: reports the top-level objects scanned, block references counted, non-block objects skipped by type, and the `work`, `handles` and `blockDepth` caps when hit. Counting objects like a picked one reports the same-type comparisons and skips other types.
- `massprop`: reports the regions found, skipped non-regions, and the same perimeter/area implausibility flags.
- Documented the field in `docs/mcp.md` and in the commands' parameter docs.

## Tests

- `crates/engine/tests/shapes.rs`: unsupported entity types (`Line`, `Text`, `3D Face`) with per-type reasons; a paging `limit` cap and the `crossingSegments` cap; a sawtooth whose perimeter exceeds 10× its box diagonal and an invisible 100×100 shape who…

title: Double-clicking a block reference edits it in place (REFEDIT)
author: nicholasgower
body:
Double-clicking a block reference in the drawing now starts REFEDIT on that reference, like AutoCAD's default DBLCLKEDIT: its objects become ordinary objects in place, the rest of the block is faded, and the drawing stays visible. The Block Editor (which hides the drawing) is still reachable from the context menu, the menu bar, the palette and `BEDIT`; nothing there changed.

## What was wrong

The canvas had double-click handlers for text (TEXTEDIT), hatches (Hatch Edit dialog) and layout viewports (MSPACE/PSPACE), but none for block references. A double-click on an INSERT fell through to the ordinary click path (selection) with no in-place edit gesture, so the only way to edit a block was the separate Block Editor.

## Root cause

`canvas::show` never inspected the picked object for `EntityKind::Insert` on a double-click. There is no DBLCLKEDIT-equivalent routing for block references.

## Fix

- `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`
  - New `insert_at` helper: the top object under the pick aperture (same `pick_at` the TEXTEDIT double-click uses), when it is a block reference.
  - With no command running (`session.running.is_none()`), a primary double-click on a reference sets it as the selection and runs `refedit {handle}` — the programmatic form that needs no prompts.
  - This case runs *before* the layout-viewport double-click, so a reference on a paper-space sheet is edited rather than being swallowed by the MSPACE fallback. It also covers model space.
  - The click is consumed (`refedit_dbl`): it cannot also start a grip edit, a selection window, TEXTEDIT, the hatch dialog or MSPACE. A refused reference still consumes it and leaves the command line echo.
  - Refusals go through `CadApp::run`, which echoes the engine error (unequal X/Y scale, an xref, generated `*`/array geometry, an edit already in progress). No panic, no new `unwrap`/`expect`.
- `crates/ui-egui/tests/block_double_click.rs` (new): drives real pointer events through the egui_kittest harness.

title: render: cull block contents to the viewport window
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong

`contents()` (the code that draws model space through a layout viewport) culled top-level model-space entities against the viewport's model window with 10 % slack, but an `INSERT` whose bounds reached the window was handed to `insert()` and expanded whole. Every entity in the block (and in nested blocks) was built and then clipped away. In the report, one model-space INSERT of a ~470 000-object site/building block shown through 13–15 m viewports allocated about 9.3 GB transiently to keep ~0.2 GB of visible display list.

## Root cause

The viewport window lived only in `contents()`, as a closure used by the top-level `seen` filter. Block sub-contexts created by `insert()` carried the transform, layers and linetype scale but no window, so block entities could not be culled.

## Fix

`crates/render/src/lib.rs`:

- `contents()` computes the same window in paper units (the space a context's `xf` maps model/block coordinates to) and puts it in the new `Ctx::cull: Option<Bounds2>`.
- `sub_ctx()` propagates `Ctx::cull` into block sub-contexts, so nested blocks cull recursively.
- `insert()` checks each block entity with `reaches_window()`: its `entity_bounds` (at the matching block depth), through the accumulated insert transform, must intersect the window. Entities that miss it are skipped before taking an expansion budget unit; the check is only made where bounds are known, so text/dimension approximations keep the existing slack, empty bounds (rays, xlines, unknown) are always drawn, and a hostile/unbounded window or transform turns culling off rather than dropping content.

`MAX_BLOCK_EXPANSION` is unchanged and still bounds expansion of what does reach the window. No new dependencies and no panics in non-test code.

## Tests

Added to `crates/render/src/tests.rs`:

- `viewport_expands_only_block_entities_that_reach_it`: a block of 500 separated LINEs plus a nested block of 300 more, shown through a 20×20 viewport. Asserts `DisplayList::expanded` sta…

title: PLOTWINDOW: pick both corners even with ORTHO on
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong
With Plot ▸ Plot area = Window, the **Window <** button starts PLOTWINDOW. With ORTHO MODE on, the second pick was bent onto the nearest axis, so the two corners always shared an X or Y: the window had no width or height, `set_plot_window` refused it ("the window needs a width and a height"), and the plot area could not be set.

## Root cause
`PlotWindowM::prompt` used `Prompt::base(a)` for "Specify opposite corner". The canvas snaps the cursor through `Session::snap_cursor`, which applies ortho whenever the prompt has a base and `Prompt::corner` is false. The engine already has the flag for exactly this case: `Prompt::corner` (ZOOM Window #787, RECTANG, ARRAYRECT's unit cell) sets the base *and* tells the snap pipeline not to bend the opposite corner. PLOTWINDOW just was not using it.

## Fix
One line in `crates/engine/src/cmd/plotters.rs`: `.base(a)` → `.corner(a)`. The base is unchanged, so the rubber-band rectangle and direct distance entry still work; only ortho projection is skipped for this prompt. ORTHO itself is untouched (and with ORTHO on, polar tracking is already off in `TrackConfig::relative_to`, so the pick is free of both constraints). `Prompt::corner`'s doc now lists PLOTWINDOW.

## Tests
New regression test `plotters.rs::plotwindow_picks_both_corners_with_ortho_on`:
- sets ORTHOMODE 1, OSMODE 0;
- starts the interactive `plotwindow` machine, snaps two non-axis-aligned corners (10,20) and (40,5) through `Session::snap_cursor` exactly as the canvas does (`CursorQuery { corner: prompt.corner, .. }`);
- asserts the opposite corner is where the cursor is, the machine finishes, and the stored window is 10,5–40,20 with both extents;
- then asserts an ordinary point prompt (LINE's next point) still snaps to the horizontal axis under ORTHO.

## Commands and results
- `cargo test -p cadcraft-engine --test plotters --test zoom_window_ortho` — 8 passed (new test fails before the fix with the corner bent to (40,20)).
- `cargo xtask ci` — all 6…

title: RECTANG: add a Center Rectangle construction mode
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong

`RECTANG` only ever treated its first point as a corner. There was no way to build a rectangle symmetrically about a centre (an origin, a guide intersection, a snap point), so users had to calculate half-dimensions by hand or add construction geometry.

CIRCLE already has its alternate construction modes (Centre+Radius, Centre+Diameter, 2P, 3P, TTR) in `crates/engine/src/cmd/draw.rs`; this PR completes the rectangle side of issue #1127. No circle modes were reinvented.

## Root cause

`run_rectang2` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/draw2.rs`) and the `RectM2` prompt machine always passed the first point straight to `rect_kind` as the rectangle's local origin, and measured the size from it. `rect_kind` itself was already general (it draws from a local origin with a signed width and height), so only the interpretation of the first point and of the second point's distance had to change.

## Fix

- **Interactive**: a `Center` keyword at the first rectangle prompt (`Specify first corner point or [Chamfer/Center/Elevation/Fillet/Thickness/Width]`). After it, the prompt reads `Specify center point for rectangle`. `Chamfer` keeps the `c` shortcut exactly as before (`Center` matches `ce` or the full word), so existing command-line scripts are unaffected. The option can come before or after the other options.
- **JSON**: `center: true` on `rectang`; `p1` becomes the centre (keeping `p1`/`p2` meaning in the default mode). Works with `p2`, `dimensions`, `area` + `length`/`breadth`, and `rotation`.
- **Geometry**: the second point is a corner mirrored across the centre, so centre `(10,10)` with `p2 (14,16)` gives corners `(6,4)`–`(14,16)`. Dimensions and area describe the full rectangle, still centred; rotation turns about the centre.
- **Options preserved**: chamfer, fillet, width, elevation and thickness behave exactly as in corner mode, and the rubber-band preview shows the centred rectangle.
- `rectang`'s `params` documentation now lists `center?`.

## Tests

Added…

title: calibrate: scale a drawing by a known distance
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong

Scaling a survey drawing to a known distance only worked through SCALE ▸ Reference: a user has to know the option, pick a base point and two reference lengths. There was no discoverable command that says “this distance is 1250 long” and no way to say what the calibration applies to. The issue asked for a clear name and an apply target.

## Root cause

No such command existed. SCALE Reference itself was already correct (`5 → 1250` gives `1250.0000`); the gap was entirely discoverability and target selection.

## Fix

Add `CALIBRATE` (label **Calibrate Scale**, `Modify ▸ Calibrate Scale`, alias `cali`):

- Pick two points, type the true length between them, then choose **Everything**, **Selection** or **Underlay**.
- The factor and transform are SCALE's own (`Mat3::scale_about` + `transform_entities`); the second point lands the true distance from the first, which becomes the base point.
- “Everything” scales every object in the active space; “Selection” uses the current selection and, with none, asks to select objects. Locked layers stay untouched, as in every other modify command.
- “Underlay” is accepted but reports clearly that raster/PDF underlays are not available yet (they don't exist in CADCraft until #560), rather than silently doing nothing.
- JSON form: `{p1, p2, length, apply?: "all"|"selection"|"underlay", handles?} → {factor, measured, length, base, apply, scaled}`. `apply` defaults to `all`, or to `selection` when handles are named, so naming objects never scales the whole drawing by accident.
- One undo step, interactive and JSON; the calibrated factor is offered to the next SCALE, and the command line reports the lengths and how many objects were scaled.

Guards, all as clear errors (never a panic or a division by zero):

- coincident points (`measured ≤ 1e-12`);
- a measured distance that overflows with finite coordinates (`hypot` of ±1e308);
- a zero, negative, non-finite or unreadable true length;
- a scale factor that overflows;…

title: SVG export: write TEXT and MTEXT as <text> elements
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong

`EXPORT`/`SAVEAS` to `.svg` always drew TEXT and MTEXT in an installed outline font as filled glyph geometry (`<path>`/`<polyline>`). The display list only recorded the font glyphs it stands for for **plots** (`DisplayList::texts` was populated from `Builder::plotting`), so the SVG writer had nothing to turn back into text. The result was not searchable or editable in Inkscape/browsers.

## Root cause

`cadcraft_render::Builder::shaped` recorded `PlotText` glyphs only when building a plot, and `cadcraft_io::svg` had no text mode: it wrote every primitive's geometry. `EXPORT` also had no way to pass format options to the host writer.

## Fix

- **render**: new `Options::text_glyphs` (default `false`) asks a normal build for the outline-font glyph records. Plots are unchanged (they already record them). When SVG text is requested, glyphs are recorded even if `TEXTFILL` is off, so the text path is independent of the fill setting.
- **io/svg**: new `TextMode` (`Text` default, `Geometry`) and `export_window_with_text` / `export_list_with`. Consecutive glyphs of one object, font, colour and baseline are grouped into a run and written as one `<text>` with:
  - `font-family` from the face's family (falling back to `sans-serif`),
  - `font-size` = world em size,
  - a `matrix(...)` carrying position, rotation, width factor, obliquing and the SVG y-flip,
  - `text-anchor="start"`,
  - the run's colour/opacity.
  Words are reconstructed from the glyph advances (whitespace has no outline glyph), and MTEXT lines become separate `<text>` elements. The glyph outline primitives the text replaces are skipped.
  `text: "geometry"` keeps the previous exact outline output.
- **io**: `export_with(drawing, name, json)` parses `text?: "text" | "geometry"`; other formats ignore it. SVG plots honour the same option.
- **engine/apps**: new optional `ExportWithHook` (like the existing `WriteAsHook`) so `EXPORT` forwards its JSON parameters; the desktop, CLI and web hosts in…

title: fix(engine): use tight glyph bounds for MText hit-test and clear selection on empty click
author: vantruong-dang
body:
### Summary

The CADCraft Selection Engine currently diverges from behavior in two critical UX interactions, causing severe frustration during daily drafting:

1. **MText Phantom Hit-Testing:** Clicking in the empty whitespace of an `MTEXT` entity's `wrap width` selects the MText instead of what is visually underneath it. The engine uses the entire bounding box (`width x height`) for hit-testing, ignoring the actual text strokes.
2. **Sticky Selection on Empty Pick:** Clicking in empty space or dragging an empty selection window (without holding `Shift`) fails to clear the existing selection. AutoCAD standard dictates that an empty click/window should deselect all objects.

### Key Changes

1. **MText Tight Bounds (`crates/engine/src/select.rs`)**:
   - Removed `EntityKind::MText` from the `filled` entities list (which relied on `entity_bounds`).
   - Updated `hit_polylines` and `in_text` to calculate distance and hit-tests against the actual `layout_mtext_entity(...).strokes` glyph outlines. Clicking in the wrap width whitespace now correctly misses the MText.

2. **Empty Pick Deselect (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`)**:
   - Updated `idle_click`: When a selection window resolves to an empty handle list (`hs.is_empty()`) and the `Shift` key is **not** held, the engine now calls `self.set_selection(Vec::new())` to clear the selection, matching AutoCAD's `PICKADD=2` default behavior.

### Testing & Quality Gates

- Added **8 comprehensive regression tests** covering:
  - MText empty wrap width and masking (phantom hits).
  - MText rotated bounds and multiline (`\P`) ragged right spaces.
  - Empty MText strings (Never Crash / no panic).
  - Empty window deselect (with and without `Shift` key).
- All **322 unit and integration tests** in `cadcraft-engine` pass 100%.
- `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` are clean.
- Architecture layering (`cargo xtask layers`) remains compliant.

title: appload: load a .lsp file from a path or the file picker
author: nicholasgower
body:
## What was wrong

`appload` existed as an engine command and a menu item (Tools ▸ Load Application…), but invoking it showed no file browser: `app.start("appload")`/the menu fell through to the engine's interactive prompt and typed `appload` was never routed to any UI. There was no `.lsp` picker, no remembered folder, and the JSON form did not report which commands the file defined.

## Root cause

- The UI knows about file pickers only through `Services` (`pick_open`, `pick_save`), and no `.lsp` picker was injected by the desktop app.
- Typed/menu commands are routed in `menus::run_ui_command`; `appload`/`ap` had no arm there, so it went to the engine's text prompt (and on a menu click only the prompt, which the report experienced as "no visible result").
- `run_appload` returned `{value, output, error?}` only; nothing listed the newly defined `c:` commands, and `{path}` did not check the extension (a `.txt` was read and evaluated).

## Fix

- **Desktop picker:** new `Services::pick_lisp: Option<Box<dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<String>>>`. The desktop implements it with `rfd` (same pattern as `pick_open`/`pick_save`), filtered to `lsp` plus an All files filter.
- **Routing:** `menus::run_ui_command` handles `appload`/`ap` when called with no parameters (typed, menu, toolbar, short `AP` alias): it opens the picker, then runs the engine's JSON form `appload {path}`. A cancelled picker is a no-op. JSON calls (`engine.execute`, `app.run(id, {path})`, scripts, control channel, MCP) carry parameters and never reach the picker. Where there is no native dialog (the web host injects no `pick_lisp`), the arm returns `None` and the existing engine prompt asks for the file name — the wasm build is unaffected.
- **Remembered folder:** `UiState::last_lisp_dir`, saved in `prefs_json` as `lispDir` and restored by `load_prefs`; the picker starts there, and a successful pick updates it to the chosen file's folder.
- **Engine:** `appload {path}` refuses anything that is not a `.lsp` file …
